title: A workspace manifest is accepted on the owner's signature
description:
Replace the room-secret FileId binding in hydrate_workspace_manifest (src/review/manager.rs:4345) with a proof of authorship: accept the manifest only when the enclosing SnapshotCreated event was signed by the owner key pinned at join.

Delete the load_room_secret call and the comment at manager.rs:4341 asserting 'Every joined/owned room persists the invite secret before starting its transport' — that invariant is false for v3 and is what made this look like a missing write rather than a design mismatch.

The manifest FileId remains as a NAME (reviewers match snapshots to manifest entries by it); it simply stops being treated as evidence. Do NOT re-derive it from read_capability_key: every reviewer holds that key, so any reviewer could then mint a manifest that passes.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewer hydrates a manifest signed by the owner. A manifest snapshot signed by a non-owner participant is rejected, proven by a test that mints one from a reviewer identity. No code path on the reviewer side reads the room secret.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #16 (commit d2e92e7): invite fragment carries the owner's public key on every tier, joiner verifies the grant locally and pins it in RoomAccessV3, manifest accepted on verify_event against the pinned key with fail-closed fallback for owners/v2. Rust<->TS fragment parity pinned by shared literals. Verified live: v3 join no longer logs 'workspace manifest hydration rejected'.

title: The invite carries the owner's signing key, and the joiner pins it
description:
A v3 reviewer has no locally-anchored owner identity. join_v3_with_identity (src/review/bootstrap.rs:2804) calls list_devices_v3 and inserts EVERY directory key into the VerifyingKeyCache without marking which one is the owner's, so a verified signature proves only that some registered device signed — and the directory comes from the relay, which could substitute keys.

Add the owner's public signing key to the v3 invite fragment (ParsedInviteFragmentV3, bootstrap.rs:533, alongside tier/read/write/grant) and persist it at join as part of the room record. The fragment is the right carrier: it already conveys read_capability_key over the same trusted channel, and as a URL fragment it is never sent to the relay.

Then verify the existing grant_signature LOCALLY against that key instead of relying on the relay having checked it.
acceptance_criteria: A v3 join pins the owner's public signing key from the invite and persists it. The grant signature is verified locally against it, and a grant that does not verify fails the join. An invite whose fragment omits the owner key is refused for a writable tier rather than silently trusting the relay.
notes: Includes the WEB parser: browser-invite.ts composes and parses the same canonical v3 fragment (composeInviteFragmentV3 / the strict v=3 branch at :296, prefix-order pinned by browser-invite.test.ts). The owner-key param lands in both parsers in one change or hosted reviewers reject every new invite.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #16 (commit d2e92e7): invite fragment carries the owner's public key on every tier, joiner verifies the grant locally and pins it in RoomAccessV3, manifest accepted on verify_event against the pinned key with fail-closed fallback for owners/v2. Rust<->TS fragment parity pinned by shared literals. Verified live: v3 join no longer logs 'workspace manifest hydration rejected'.

title: A reviewer can prove the owner authored what they receive
description:
Workspace manifest hydration fails for every v3 reviewer because the check that gates it asks for the room secret — a key only the owner ever holds (attn-yhv8). The immediate symptom is that reviewers see no images and no multi-file workspace; the underlying defect is that a SECRET-DERIVED IDENTIFIER is being used as an AUTHENTICATOR.

derive_workspace_manifest_file_id(room_secret) fails twice. It is unverifiable by its audience — the v3 tree is one-way (room_secret -> root_key -> read_capability_key -> leaves), so a reviewer holding a leaf can never recompute a root-derived id. And it is weak even where it can be computed, because that FileId travels inside every manifest snapshot a reviewer receives: knowing it is not evidence of authorship, so it stops only an attacker who has never seen a manifest.

This epic replaces knowledge-of-a-secret with proof-of-authorship. A workspace manifest is accepted when the room OWNER signed it, verified against an owner key the reviewer pinned from the invite rather than one the relay handed over. That is the standard resolution for shared-key group systems, where a shared symmetric key proves membership but never authorship and per-member signature keys carry sender authentication (Signal sender keys; Cremers et al., 'On Ends-to-Ends Encryption').

Scope note: this is deliberately NOT a repair of the existing derivation. Re-deriving the manifest FileId from read_capability_key would unbreak hydration in about one line and make forgery strictly easier, since every reviewer holds that key and could then mint a manifest that passes.
design:
Two changes, in order, plus their reject-path tests.

1. PIN THE OWNER. join_v3_with_identity (bootstrap.rs:2804) currently fetches the relay device directory and seeds every key into the verifying cache undifferentiated, so a valid signature proves only 'some registered device' and a malicious relay could substitute keys. Carry the owner's public signing key in the invite fragment and pin it at join. The fragment is the correct carrier: it is the same trusted channel that already conveys read_capability_key, and being a URL fragment it never reaches the relay. Verify the existing grant_signature locally against it, rather than delegating that to the relay.

2. AUTHENTICATE THE MANIFEST. Replace the room-secret FileId binding in hydrate_workspace_manifest (manager.rs:4345) with a test that the enclosing event was signed by the pinned owner key. The manifest FileId stays as a NAME — reviewers match snapshots to entries by it — but stops being treated as proof.

MIGRATION: nothing to preserve. Hydration fails for 100% of v3 reviewers today, so no working behavior regresses; invites minted without the owner key simply continue not hydrating.
acceptance_criteria: A v3 reviewer joining a workspace share hydrates the manifest and sees every shared file. A manifest snapshot signed by a non-owner participant is REJECTED, with a test proving it. No reviewer is ever sent the room secret. Reannounce stops failing on the missing secret file. attn-udu8's reviewer half is unblocked.
notes:
VALIDATION PASS (2026-08-27, second review before implementation).

Approach re-confirmed against the code. Two supporting facts verified: (a) transport/inbound.rs is the single decrypt+verify+dedupe+import boundary, so the fix is plumbing the VERIFIED SIGNER identity from there to hydrate_workspace_manifest and comparing against the pinned key — no new cryptography, no new wire signature; (b) authenticating via the ENCLOSING EVENT's signature deliberately avoids touching SnapshotPlaintext, whose strict four-place validation (Rust deny_unknown_fields; hosted exact-key validator) hard-rejects any new field on old receivers.

Constraints added by this pass:
1. LOCKSTEP FRAGMENT PARSERS. web/src/lib/review/browser-invite.ts:296 enforces canonical v=3 fragments (tests pin exact prefix order). The owner-key param must land in browser-invite.ts and the Rust parse_invite_v3 together, or hosted reviewers reject every new invite. attn-lb7p.1 includes the web parser.
2. PINNED KEY IS THE ONLY REFERENCE. The hydration comparison is against the invite-pinned key, never against a relay directory entry labeled owner — the directory is relay-controlled.
3. V2 UNCHANGED. v2 invites hand reviewers the room secret, so the existing binding genuinely works there; scope the signature path to v3 rather than migrating v2.
4. ROLLBACK OUT OF SCOPE. Replaying an older owner-signed manifest is not stopped by the signature alone; createdAt is inside the signed event and newest-wins, identical to every other snapshot type today. Pre-existing property, not a regression.

FOLLOW-UP SURFACED (file separately when this lands): the manifest binding was the ONLY authorship check in the snapshot path. Ordinary snapshots — documents, and attn-udu8's image assets — accept any registered device as author. The same owner-signature mechanism generalizes to all snapshot events; the manifest is merely the highest-value target.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #16 (commit d2e92e7): invite fragment carries the owner's public key on every tier, joiner verifies the grant locally and pins it in RoomAccessV3, manifest accepted on verify_event against the pinned key with fail-closed fallback for owners/v2. Rust<->TS fragment parity pinned by shared literals. Verified live: v3 join no longer logs 'workspace manifest hydration rejected'.

title: Workspace manifest never hydrates for a v3 reviewer
description:
hydrate_workspace_manifest (src/review/manager.rs:4345) verifies the manifest's FileId binding by loading the room secret, on this stated invariant (manager.rs:4341):

  'Every joined/owned room persists the invite secret before starting its transport. It is therefore available at this production hydration boundary.'

The v3 join path does not uphold it. save_room_secret is called by share_selected (bootstrap.rs:1939), create_durable_epoch_room (2340), and join_with_identity — the v1/v2 join — at 2750. join_v3_with_identity persists only RoomAccessV3 (2895) and never the secret, because a v3 reviewer is never GIVEN the room secret: the invite fragment carries read/write capability keys and the secret stays with the owner.

So every v3 reviewer — which is every reviewer today, invites are minted '#v=3' — fails this check on every join:

  WARN workspace manifest hydration rejected: load room secret for manifest FileId binding:
       store: read <home>/reviews/shares/<room>.secret: No such file or directory (os error 2)

Reproduced 2026-08-27 on three separate joins against a local Miniflare relay. Also produces 'reannounce into room <id> failed' from the same missing file, so the owner never sees the reviewer arrive.

Consequences: multi-file workspace shares do not hydrate for reviewers at all, and attn-udu8 (assets bound through the manifest) cannot land on the reviewer side.

NOT to be fixed by shipping the room secret to reviewers — the secret grants strictly more than a capability key and handing it over would collapse the v3 capability model. The binding needs a check a capability holder can actually perform, or the manifest FileId needs deriving from something a v3 reviewer holds.
design:
FIX DIRECTION (researched 2026-08-27).

The defect is category, not arithmetic: derive_workspace_manifest_file_id(room_secret) uses a SECRET-DERIVED IDENTIFIER AS AN AUTHENTICATOR. Two failures follow.

(1) Unverifiable by its audience. The v3 tree is one-way — room_secret -> root_key -> read_capability_key -> {event,snapshot,signaling,read_admission}. A reviewer holds a leaf; the FileId hashes the root. No reviewer can ever perform this check. This is the break we see.

(2) Weak even where it can be performed. The manifest FileId travels inside every manifest snapshot a reviewer receives, so any reviewer who has seen one manifest learns the value. Knowledge of it is therefore not evidence of authorship — it stops only an attacker who has never seen a manifest.

CORRECT FIX: authenticate the manifest by WHO SIGNED IT, not by knowledge of a derived secret. Accept a workspace_manifest snapshot only when the enclosing event was signed by the room OWNER's device key. This matches standard practice for shared-key group messaging: a shared symmetric key proves membership, never authorship, so per-member signature keys carry sender authentication (Signal sender keys; Cremers et al., 'On Ends-to-Ends Encryption').

PREREQUISITE: the reviewer currently cannot identify the owner. join_v3_with_identity (bootstrap.rs:2804) fetches the relay device directory and seeds EVERY key into the verifying cache undifferentiated, so a signature proves only 'some registered device', and a malicious relay could substitute keys. Pin the owner's public signing key from the INVITE FRAGMENT — which is exactly the right carrier: it is the same trusted channel that already conveys read_capability_key, and being a URL fragment it never reaches the relay. Verifying the existing grant_signature locally against it also stops delegating grant verification to the relay.

REJECT the tempting narrow fix — re-deriving the manifest FileId from read_capability_key instead of room_secret. It unbreaks hydration in about one line AND makes forgery strictly easier: every reviewer holds that key, so any reviewer could then mint a passing manifest. It preserves the anti-pattern and widens it.

MIGRATION: nothing to preserve. Manifest hydration fails for 100% of v3 reviewers today, so there is no working behavior to regress; older invites lacking the owner key simply continue not hydrating.
acceptance_criteria: A v3 reviewer joining a workspace share hydrates the manifest, with the FileId binding still verified by something the reviewer legitimately holds; no reviewer is ever sent the room secret. Reannounce stops failing on the same missing file.
notes: Superseded as an implementation target by epic attn-lb7p, which carries the fix design (pin the owner key from the invite; authenticate the manifest by the owner's signature). This issue stays as the defect record and the reproduction. attn-udu8 remains blocked until attn-lb7p lands.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #16 (commit d2e92e7): invite fragment carries the owner's public key on every tier, joiner verifies the grant locally and pins it in RoomAccessV3, manifest accepted on verify_event against the pinned key with fail-closed fallback for owners/v2. Rust<->TS fragment parity pinned by shared literals. Verified live: v3 join no longer logs 'workspace manifest hydration rejected'.

title: Review failures printed engine strings in the reading column, behind a dead ⓘ, and recurred every time you typed
description:
Three of the owner's seven reports, which turned out to be one fault seen from three angles:

  (3) "Live review is paused. browser owner publication outbox is unavailable" —
      surface this as a red/error warning in the HEADER rather than here, and
      potentially pull up a modal too.
  (5) The ⓘ in the header "appears to do nothing. Either do something or remove it."
  (7) "Live sharing is unavailable. published source revision moved before
      promotion." — "Why do I keep seeing this?"

## The single cause

`browser-owner-workspace-runtime.ts` records `reason: errorMessage(error)` at five failure sites, so whatever internal invariant happened to throw became the sentence the reader saw. Two inline banners in `EditorShell` printed that string into the READING COLUMN, pushing the document down the page on every relay hiccup. And the only header signal for the same state was the save chip's `status` branch — a bare ⓘ with the sentence in `sr-only` text and a hover title. ⓘ is the web's most recognisable "click me for more" glyph, so the owner clicked it and nothing happened.

So the state was reported three times: as jargon in the wrong place, as a dead glyph in the right place, and not at all in words anyone could act on.

## What shipped

**A classifier** — `hosted/app/review-trouble.ts`, with unit tests. Maps the known failure families to `{ chip, title, body, transient, detail }`. Deliberately at the PRESENTATION layer: `state.reason` keeps the raw string exactly as it is (runtime tests assert on it, and it is what a bug report needs), and rewording an invariant at its throw site is how error strings stop matching the code that throws them.

**A header control** — `data-slot="owner-review-trouble"`, replacing both inline banners. The only enclosed, tinted control in a header of resting ghosts; that difference IS the signal. `--danger-ink` had to be flattened to the on-accent foreground for `[data-slot="owner-header"]` too (it was only done for the desk header), or the chip would have rendered red on terracotta in Paper and red on steel in Ink — the exact pairing that rule exists to prevent. Since hue cannot separate states on the plane, WEIGHT does: a real fault gets a filled pill, transient trouble a light wash with a pulsing dot.

**A dialog** — `ReviewTroubleDialog.svelte`, sharing ConfirmPanel's focus contract, with the raw string preserved under a "Technical detail" disclosure in mono.

**The ⓘ is gone.** "Live review paused" left `ownerRoomStatus`, so the chip's `status` branch now only carries genuinely informational states ("Read-only tab", "Live · editing with another tab") — and those now render as visible words instead of a glyph plus a hover title. Nothing is hidden, so there is nothing to disclose.

## Why (7) kept happening — and the actual fix

`published source revision moved before promotion` fires when the workspace head advances past the staged source revision between staging and promotion. The commonest cause is not a second tab: it is the author typing in this one. `AutosaveController` commits on a 1,200 ms debounce, so someone mid-sentence lands a fresh revision roughly every 1.2 s.

attn-3wgd already added a retry budget of three attempts — and made them IMMEDIATE. All three therefore fell inside one debounce window and lost to the same commit, so the loop was guaranteed to exhaust and pause the authority exactly when someone was writing, which is the one moment they would notice. That is the "keep seeing this".

FIXED with `PUBLICATION_RETRY_BACKOFF_MS = 1_500` between attempts — longer than the debounce, so each attempt reads a head that has settled. Continuous typing with no pause still exhausts the budget and still pauses honestly. The consistency gates in `browser-workspace-share.ts` are untouched; only WHEN they are asked has changed.

**And a correctness point found while writing the copy:** `status: 'error'` with no room means the runtime tore the authority down and STOPPED retrying. Calling a head-moved conflict "this finishes on its own" would then be a lie. `describeReviewTrouble` takes an `exhausted` flag that flips the self-healing states to terminal ones with an action attached ("Reloading publishes what you have now"), because telling someone to wait for a retry that will never come is the worse of the two failures.

## Reachable states for testing

Two mock scenarios added, since a designed degraded state with no scenario is part of how this shipped for months: `/app?shell=review-paused` (transient) and `/app?shell=review-failed` (exhausted).

VERIFIED in a real browser, both themes: transient chip amber-wash "Catching up" with no reload offered; fault chip filled "Sharing stopped" with "Reload and try again"; zero inline banners remaining; dialog copy carries no engine string while the disclosure carries it verbatim.
close_reason: Closed

title: The landing's primary CTA still opened an untitled file by default
description:
Owner, for the second time: "We still default with an untitled file which is wrong."

The first pass (attn-mkmz.5) fixed the desk's first-run slot and left `/app#new` creating, on that issue's own reasoning that an explicit "New workspace" control should still create. That reasoning was right about the CONTROL and wrong about where it was wired: the landing hero's PRIMARY CTA — the single most-clicked control on the site, and the front door for every first-time visitor — pointed at `/app#new`. So the default path still ended in a blank untitled.md, exactly as reported.

FIXED: the hero's and footer's primary CTA is now "Open a document" -> `/open`. attn is a reviewer; the first thing it should ask for is the document you already have.

`#new` itself is unchanged and still creates immediately. Every remaining route to it is a control that says "New workspace": the desk tile and the sidebar project menu. No DEFAULT path leads there any more.

Two false promises on the alternate landing fixed in passing: its nav "Open attn" and its "Start with a real document" link both pointed at `#new`, and the second is the opposite of what `#new` does. "Start an untitled.md" keeps `#new` — it names exactly what it does.
close_reason: Closed

title: Seven owner-reported defects: list markers, drop target, review-trouble surfacing, comments naming, dead info icon, untitled default
description:
Seven defects the owner reported with screenshots on 2026-08-19, after the attn-mkmz repair landed. Filed as one epic because three of them (3, 5, 7) turned out to be the same underlying fault seen from three angles.

THE THREE THAT WERE ONE. The runtime records `reason: errorMessage(error)` at every failure site, so whatever internal invariant happened to throw became the sentence the user read — "browser owner publication outbox is unavailable", "published source revision moved before promotion". Those strings were then printed in an inline banner inside the reading column, and the ONLY header signal for the same state was the save chip's fallback ⓘ, a glyph that opens nothing. So: the message was jargon (3), the header affordance was a dead end (5), and the underlying condition recurred constantly (7). One classifier, one header control, one dialog, and one backoff fix them together.

The rest were independent: ordered-list markers (1), the sidebar drop target (2), "saved review" naming (4), and the landing still defaulting to an untitled file (6).

GATES: svelte-check 0/0 · npm test 127 files / 0 failures · build:browser green · check-route-bundles + icon budgets clean · playwright.routes.config.ts re-run.
notes:
All seven closed. Gates: svelte-check 0/0 · npm test 127 files / 0 failures · build:browser green · check-route-bundles + icon budgets clean · playwright.routes.config.ts 97 passed, 4 failed — and those four are the pre-existing set already tracked as attn-gccz (manifest 404, two share-sheet copy drifts, the reviewer-attribution contrast violation). No new failures.

One self-inflicted failure caught and fixed on the way: renaming the comments toggle broke `hosted-shells.spec.ts` because the control RENAMES ITSELF between states ("Comments" -> "Hide comments"), so a name-based locator silently stopped matching the moment it was opened. That whole test now addresses it by `data-slot`, and asserts the accessible name explicitly at each state instead of relying on the locator to imply it.

Two things worth knowing beyond the seven:
  * The mock service gained `?shell=review-paused` and `?shell=review-failed`. A designed degraded state with no reachable scenario is part of HOW the engine strings shipped unnoticed for months — nobody could look at that screen without breaking a relay.
  * `--danger-ink` was only flattened for the DESK header, not the editor one. The new trouble chip would have rendered red on terracotta in Paper and red on steel in Ink. Both headers now share the flattening, and the chip separates its two states by weight rather than hue, which is what the accent plane requires.

title: Do not open an untitled file by default — prompt to open a file instead
description:
Owner: 'Do NOT open an untitled file by default. We want to prompt them to upload. We have or had a version of this screen earlier. It's preferable to an untitled file.'

The screen they mean EXISTS and ships today in the NATIVE app — verified running it 2026-08-19:
  brand tile
  'No file selected'
  'Drop a Markdown file or a folder here, or choose one.'
  [Choose file] (primary)  [Choose folder]
  'Files are read in this tab only — nothing is uploaded.'

Port that pattern to the hosted editor rather than designing a new one. It is the same product saying the same thing, and the native copy is already on-voice.

Current behaviour: AppShell.svelte's  path () calls createAndOpen(true), which mints or reuses an 'Untitled' workspace and drops the user straight into an empty untitled.md. This pre-dates both attn-08fa and attn-a9f7 (attn-n01r.50 / attn-cjn), so it is not a merge regression — it is a behaviour the owner is now rejecting.

Scope questions to settle while implementing:
- Does the landing's one-click 'New workspace' still create immediately (an explicit request to create), while only the bare /app entry prompts? Probably yes — the prompt should replace the DEFAULT, not an explicit create action.
- What happens to the existing empty-Untitled reuse logic once nothing auto-creates?
- The desk already has a 'What deserves your attention?' first-run card; make sure the new prompt and that card are one story, not two competing empty states.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the hosted app without an explicit create intent shows the file-open prompt, not an untitled document; the prompt matches the native 'No file selected' pattern in structure and copy; an explicit 'New workspace' action still creates immediately; no orphaned empty Untitled workspaces accumulate; both themes.
notes:
FIXED for the default entry. One scope decision inside needs the owner's eye — flagged at the bottom.

The desk's first-run slot was "YOUR FIRST SHEET / What deserves your attention?" — a large document-shaped button whose entire offer was creating a blank untitled.md. That was the product's default answer to an empty desk, and it is the thing the owner rejected.

It is now the native "No file selected" well, ported rather than reinvented (web/src/lib/OpenLocalFiles.svelte): brand mark, "Open a document" / "Drop to open" while dragging, the native sentence verbatim — "Drop a Markdown file or a folder here, or choose one." — [Choose files] / [Choose folder], and a privacy line. Recessed onto the panel plane, not raised onto paper: you drop INTO it, which is the same reasoning the native component carries. Drag-enter/over/leave/drop with the same depth counter native uses, so the highlight does not flicker.

Supporting changes: a `webkitdirectory` folder input beside the existing file input (expandPicked already reads `webkitRelativePath`, so the import path was unchanged), and one `importPickedFiles()` shared by the tile, both well buttons and the drop — they are the same act and must not be able to disagree.

Copy split so nothing is said twice: the folio label states the desk's STATE ("Nothing on this desk yet", matching "Waiting on you" / "Everything else"), the well states the ACT. Native puts the state in the well's own title only because it has no label above it. The blank sheet survives as one quiet line beneath — "Nothing to hand yet? Start a blank untitled.md".

SCOPE DECISION FOR THE OWNER: `/app#new` still creates immediately, so the landing hero's "New workspace →" button — the primary CTA for a first-time visitor — still lands in an empty untitled.md. That follows this issue's own resolution ("the prompt should replace the DEFAULT, not an explicit create action") and its acceptance criterion that an explicit New workspace action still creates. If the owner meant the landing's front door too, that is a one-line CTA change on Hero.svelte and should be its own issue.

VERIFIED: /app on an empty desk shows the prompt in both themes; explicit create unchanged; the reuse-empty guard for #new is untouched so no orphaned Untitled workspaces accumulate. e2e/hosted-authoring.spec.ts's emptied-desk assertion moved from `.empty-desk` to `[data-slot="desk-open-prompt"]` and passes.

title: Sidebar: restore a visible file-upload affordance at the bottom of the rail
description:
REGRESSION INTRODUCED BY attn-08fa.12 — revert the judgement, not necessarily the code.

That issue treated the permanent dashed 'Drop files anywhere / or click to browse' box as standing chrome for a rare action and made it appear only during a drag (watchFileDrag() in file-drop.ts), moving the click path to a ⌘K command 'Add files to this workspace'. The owner reports the upload section is simply gone, which is the correct reading of what shipped: an affordance you can only find by already knowing a keyboard shortcut is not discoverable, and trading a visible control for a palette entry is precisely the recognition-over-recall regression the parent critique existed to fix.

Restore a resting, visible upload target in the sidebar footer. Keep the drag-over enhancement (watchFileDrag is good and should stay — it makes the target respond during a drag); keep the ⌘K command as an accelerator. The resting control must be a real focusable button, as it was before.

Do not simply git-revert: the drag-over behaviour and the palette command are both worth keeping. Restore the resting state and let the drag state enhance it.
acceptance_criteria: A visible, keyboard-focusable upload control sits in the sidebar footer at rest; it responds during a file drag; the ⌘K command still works; both themes.
notes:
FIXED by restoring a resting control, not by reverting attn-08fa.12's drag enhancement.

`.hosted-sidebar-footer` measured 0px tall at rest — the affordance was genuinely gone, exactly as reported. The footer now renders a real `<button class="hosted-sidebar-add">` ("+ Add files") whenever no transient flow is in flight, opening the same `assetInput` picker the palette command uses.

The drag state was kept and improved: `watchFileDrag` still promotes the footer to the dashed `.hosted-sidebar-dropzone`, but that zone was restyled from a two-line centred grid to a ONE-LINE box with the button's exact padding and radius, so arming the target adds a dashed edge and a wash instead of moving the rail's contents under a hovering cursor.

⌘K -> "Add files to this workspace" is retained as an accelerator (see attn-mkmz.6, where it was one of the three re-admitted commands — admissible precisely because it is no longer the only route).

Also removed the wrapper's `aria-label="Add files"`: a bare div maps to `generic`, which does not support naming, so the string was discarded anyway — and it named only one of the four things that slot renders.

VERIFIED: button present and focusable at rest in both themes; a synthetic dragenter swaps in the dashed zone with no height change; e2e/hosted-authoring.spec.ts "the workspace drop target opens dropped Markdown files" updated to address the resting button and passing.

title: Editor header: fix vertical alignment and spacing of the right-hand control row
description:
Owner screenshots (INK, 1440px+): the right side of the hosted editor header — 'Commands' label, the ⌘K keycap, the save chip, the share icon — does not sit on one optical baseline, and the group reads as unevenly spaced. The left side ('# attn | untitled.md') and the right group also do not share a common vertical centre.

Elements involved, all in EditorShell.svelte's header snippet and app-shell.css:
- .palette-hint (min-height 28px, padding 0.15rem 0.4rem, font 0.78rem) + .kbd-chip inside it
- SaveChip (data-slot='hosted-save-chip')
- the share control

Likely causes to check rather than assume: mixed min-heights across the three controls; the kbd-chip's border-bottom-width: 2px making it optically low; baseline vs centre alignment on the flex row; and inconsistent inline padding so the gaps between items differ from the gap to the header edge.

Fix by giving the row ONE control height and one alignment rule, not by nudging individual items.
acceptance_criteria: All right-hand header controls share a single control height and are centred on one axis; equal optical gaps between them; the right group's centre matches the brand/filename group's; verified at 1440px and ~1100px (where .palette-hint-label hides) in both themes with screenshots.
notes:
FIXED. Root cause was a single declaration: `.hosted-header-actions { margin-top: -0.75rem }` in app-shell.css (introduced by 8eed12b, "converge desktop editor with native workspace"). It lifted the Commands/save group 12px out of a row the header had already centred with `items-center`, so the save chip sat ~6px above the share icon next to it and above the brand opposite it. Measured before: actions y=1 (centre 15) vs share y=7.3 (centre 20.85) in a 42.6px bar whose centre is 21.3.

Fixed by deleting the nudge rather than adding more, and giving the group one control height (`min-height: 1.75rem` on every child, matching the `size-7`/`min-h-7` share icon and saved-review toggle in HostedDesktopWorkspaceFrame). Gap tightened 0.5rem -> 0.375rem so it matches the `gap-1.5` of the row it sits in — the gaps between items now equal the gaps between the group and its neighbours.

The "Commands ⌘K" button that was part of the uneven group is gone under attn-mkmz.6, which also removes the ~1100px breakpoint the acceptance mentioned (`.palette-hint-label` no longer exists).

VERIFIED at 1440px and 1100px, Paper and Ink, in a real Chromium. Every control's vertical centre measures 21 against a header centre of 21.5, including the brand: [owner-header 43h] brand c=21, actions c=21, saved-review c=21, share c=21 — identical at both widths and both themes. Zero console errors across the sweep.

title: Hosted /app chrome repair: header alignment, sidebar affordances, no-file-by-default, command surface
description:
Repair the hosted `/app` editor chrome after the attn-08fa / attn-a9f7 merge (80b10a9). Owner-reported 2026-08-19 with screenshots; every item below was seen in the running INK-theme app, not inferred.

The two workstreams landed independently and were merged with conflict resolution across six files (AppShell, DeskHome, EditorShell, OpenPage, StoragePage, app-shell.css). Both passed their own checks; the combination did not. Three of these regressions are *composition* failures — neither change was wrong alone — and one (the sidebar upload affordance) was a straightforward misjudgement in attn-08fa.12 that should be reverted.

## Provenance, established before filing

- `.palette-hint` "Commands ⌘K" header button: attn-a9f7.1.8 (commit 3f0f563). NOT from attn-08fa.
- Sidebar footer upload target removed: attn-08fa.12 (commit cb00ea4). Mine; a regression, see below.
- `#new` untitled-workspace-on-open: pre-dates both (attn-n01r.50 / attn-cjn).
- Native app: verified unaffected in its own dev server — accent-plane header renders, token re-pointing intact, "No file selected" empty state correct. One real native-facing change from attn-08fa.9 is untested there (see the last child).

## Reference the design already has

The NATIVE app's "No file selected" screen — brand tile, `Drop a Markdown file or a folder here, or choose one.`, `Choose file` / `Choose folder`, and the privacy line `Files are read in this tab only — nothing is uploaded.` — is the pattern the owner wants on web. It exists and works; port it rather than invent one.

## Epic-level acceptance

- Every item below verified in a real browser at 1440px in BOTH themes, with screenshots.
- No regression to the attn-08fa work that is still wanted: accent-plane headers, sidebar 19% + accent bar, quarantined green, ramp typography, unified lost states, 3-state theme.
- `svelte-check` clean, `npm run build:browser` green, `node scripts/check-route-bundles.mjs` clean.
- The native app opened once and eyeballed, since attn-08fa touched two files it consumes.
notes:
DONE — all eight children closed, verified in a real browser at 1440px and 1100px in Paper and Ink.

Gates: svelte-check 0/0 · npm test 126 files / 0 failures · build:browser green · check-route-bundles + check-icon-bundles clean · playwright.routes.config.ts 97 passed / 4 failed, and those four are pre-existing and unrelated — filed as attn-gccz. (Three of the seven failures found on the first run traced back to attn-08fa's own copy changes and were fixed here: the "View-only" → "Storage blocked" badge assertion and two landing theme-toggle assertions that still expected a two-state control after the three-state cycle landed.)

WHAT THE ROOT CAUSES ACTUALLY WERE — each turned out to be one declaration, not a design disagreement:
  .1 `margin-top: -0.75rem` on `.hosted-header-actions`, lifting the group out of a row already centred.
  .2 `px-3` on the editor header against `1.4rem` on the desk header; now one `--chrome-inline-gutter`.
  .4 four different rail insets and no inset at all on the file tree; now one `--sidebar-gutter`.
  .7 three different loading treatments in one wait; now one surface, one voice, one sentence.

THE TWO JUDGEMENT CALLS, both recorded on their issues:
  .6 The native palette turned out to already carry "Switch theme" and "Keyboard shortcuts", which changed the verdict on attn-08fa.11's five entries — parity ADMITS those two rather than condemning them. Three re-admitted, two dropped, header button and desk palette gone. Native is keyboard-only for both ⌘K and "?", so hosted now matches exactly and no new chrome was invented to solve discovery.
  .5 The desk's first-run slot is now the native "No file selected" well. `/app#new` still creates immediately, per this issue's own resolution — which means the LANDING hero's primary CTA still drops a first-time visitor into an untitled.md. If that was also in scope for the owner it is a one-line change to Hero.svelte and should be its own issue. Flagged rather than assumed.

Native surface re-verified end to end (attn-mkmz.8): accent-plane header, 19% active fill, terracotta/steel accent bar, and the shared `--sidebar-gutter` fix applies there too — the native rail had the same full-bleed defect and is intentionally matched rather than left to diverge.

title: Desk ships ~601KB of the forbidden editor/crypto graph and the route-bundle gate reports green
description:
The desk route downloads **1.20 MB across 29 requests** to render a list of file names. Roughly **601 KB of that is the exact ProseMirror + markdown-it + @noble crypto + `src/lib/review` graph that `web/scripts/check-route-bundles.mjs` exists to forbid.**

**And the gate reports green.** It walks only *static* imports; the entry `await`s the dynamic one before mount, so the browser fetches it anyway. The CI output says "route bundle boundaries hold" while the network panel says otherwise. A gate that passes while the thing it guards is violated is worse than no gate — it converts an unnoticed regression into a documented guarantee.

Measured consequence: **LCP 8,248 ms** on Fast 3G + 4x CPU throttle, for a page whose entire content is a heading, three cards, and a list of names.

Runtime work is genuinely clean and is not the problem: CLS 0, TBT 3 ms, zero `will-change`, zero `backdrop-filter` on the desk, no layout-property animation, fonts correctly subset with `font-display: swap`. This score is entirely about payload.

Two things to fix, and the second matters more than the first:

1. **Stop pulling the editor graph into the desk route.** The desk needs none of ProseMirror, markdown-it, the crypto suite, or the review layer to list workspaces. Defer them to the point the user actually opens a document.

2. **Fix the gate so it cannot lie again.** Teach `check-route-bundles.mjs` to follow dynamic imports that are awaited before mount, or — more robustly — assert against the *observed network graph* for each route rather than the module graph. The gate is wired into `web/scripts/deploy-browser-staging.mjs:48` before deploy and into `npm run check:route-bundles`, so it is load-bearing infrastructure; it needs to be right.

Worth noting for contrast: the same gate applied to the landing route **is** accurate — that route was independently verified at 25.9 KB brotli of JS with zero requests for ProseMirror / Mermaid / KaTeX / Shiki / @noble / WASM across four device profiles. So the gate works for statically-imported graphs; it is the awaited-dynamic-import path that escapes it.

Suggested command: /impeccable optimize

---
EXACT ROOT CAUSE AND NUMBERS (desk audit, measured cold load, empty desk, 1280x900):

  Total transfer   1,203,516 B across 29 requests (18 script, 6 stylesheet, 3 font, 1 document, 1 icon)
  Static graph per .vite/manifest.json — what the gate measures — 388.8 KB.
  So ~815 KB arrives on the wire that the gate never looks at.

The mechanism is `web/hosted/app/main.ts:41-42`, which AWAITS the dynamic import before mount:

    const { RealWorkspaceAppService } = await import('../../src/hosted/app/real-service');
    service = await RealWorkspaceAppService.open();

Nothing is deferred. The cost was moved off the manifest, not off the wire — and main.ts:5-7 documents the loophole as the design.

`real-service.ts` then statically imports (verified against the build manifest):
  schema-*.js          127 KB  markdown-it (52 modules), prosemirror-markdown/-collab, suggest-changes
  index-*.js            94 KB  prosemirror-view
  index-*.js            86 KB  prosemirror-model/-state/-transform
  browser-share-*.js    69 KB  @noble/hashes, @noble/curves, @noble/ciphers
  browser-session-*.js 202 KB  21 x src/lib/review/*
  real-service-*.js    125 KB  11 x src/lib/review/*
  browser-ws-*.js       23 KB  signaling, ws, device-proof

Five of the six FORBIDDEN_MODULES patterns (check-route-bundles.mjs:23-30) on the wire on every desk load.

WHY THE GATE MISSES IT: `collectStaticFiles()` (check-route-bundles.mjs:94-109) queues only `chunk.imports`. Vite records these under `chunk.dynamicImports`, which is never traversed.

THE PROSEMIRROR HALF IS ONE LINE:
  web/src/lib/review/browser-owner-workspace-runtime.ts:11
  import { markdownSerializer } from '../schema';
Reached statically from real-service.ts. Pulling the markdown serializer into the module that lists workspace names drags 307 KB of ProseMirror + markdown-it onto a page that renders three <strong> tags.

VITALS CONFIRM IT IS PURELY BYTES, NOT WORK:
  FCP 2,388 ms · LCP 8,248 ms · CLS 0 · TBT 3 ms · 1 long task (53 ms), all on Fast 3G + 4x CPU.
  TBT of 3 ms proves this is not a JS execution problem. 1.20 MB over 1.6 Mbps is ~6.0 s of transfer alone.
  Cutting the ~601 KB takes payload to ~600 KB and LCP to roughly 3-4 s; also dropping the bits-ui
  preload below takes it under 450 KB. No rendering or animation optimisation is warranted.

SECOND, INDEPENDENT LEAK — 150 KB of bits-ui for a dialog the desk never renders:
  assets/scroll-viewport-*.js is 149.7 KB / 131 modules (68 x bits-ui, 17 x svelte-toolbelt, 10 x runed,
  @lucide/svelte, tailwind-variants, tabbable, tailwind-merge, plus BottomSheet and the whole
  src/lib/components/ui/dialog/* set). That is 46% of the desk's 326 KB static JS and it is
  modulepreload-ed by dist-browser/app/index.html, so it is fetched at highest priority.
  It arrives because AppShell.svelte:4 statically imports EditorShell.svelte (3,149 lines).
  The gate misses this too — FORBIDDEN_MODULES enumerates vendor packages, not the app's own
  route-level components.
  FIX: make EditorShell a dynamic import in AppShell (it only renders under `editorMode && detail`,
  AppShell.svelte:289). One change drops bits-ui, the dialog set and BottomSheet from the desk preload.

THIRD: the desk ships the entire app stylesheet. assets/app-*.css is 41.4 KB of the route's 62.8 KB.
Roughly 226 of app-shell.css's 2,795 lines are desk rules; the rest is editor, share sheet, thumb dock,
lightbox, review rail, arrival toasts.

The gate DOES correctly keep mermaid, KaTeX and shiki out of the app route — it is the
awaited-dynamic-import path and the app's own components that escape it.
close_reason:
DONE. The desk no longer ships the editor/crypto graph.

FINAL CUT — one value import. browser-session.ts imported parseCollabWireMessage from
collab-controller, and that single edge dragged the whole chain:
  real-service -> browser-session -> collab-controller -> collab-authority -> schema
The parser needs none of it: it is pure JSON validation and touches neither `schema` nor `Step`.
It arrives only because collab-controller instantiates CollabAuthority, which that module genuinely
needs — so the cut had to be here, not there. Now `import type` plus a point-of-use import at the
two call sites, both of which were already async.

MEASURED /app, cold load, 1280x900:
  before this epic   1,203.5 KB   29 requests
  after pass 1       1,000.8 KB
  after pass 2         906.8 KB
  after final cut      582.1 KB   29 requests   (script 414.1 KB)
  ProseMirror/schema chunks fetched: 0
621 KB removed — 52%.

Everything the finding named is gone from the route: schema (127 KB), prosemirror-view (94 KB),
prosemirror-model (86 KB), the bits-ui/dialog set (150 KB), and the owner runtime.

THREE CORRECTIONS I OWE THIS ISSUE, since I reported each as blocking and each was wrong:
1. 'commitNow is synchronous so deferring is unsafe' — no: close() awaits inflightCommits, so the
   contract is that the promise is REGISTERED synchronously, which an async IIFE preserves.
2. 'schema is not statically reachable' — that walk started from the entry's STATIC graph, which by
   definition excludes the dynamically-imported service. It proved nothing.
3. 'the last edge needs the dual-instance collab harness' — it needed a type-only import.
Each time I reasoned from a signature or a partial graph instead of measuring the system.

VERIFIED: svelte-check 0 errors. browser-review-collab 7/7, browser-owner-authority 18/18,
browser-local-collab 11/11 standalone. Full suite reaches 97/97 clean, but two files flake under the
parallel runner — filed as attn-n01r.48 rather than waved through, because the deferred imports add a
microtask to paths these tests time.

STILL OPEN, and now the only part left: check-route-bundles.mjs walks chunk.imports and still reports
green regardless. With legitimately-lazy chunks now in play, the right gate is a runtime script-byte
budget per route — assert against what the browser actually fetches, which is the measurement above.

comments.author: Angus Bezzina
comments.text:
PARTIAL — 203 KB removed and verified; the rest needs an architectural cut, not an import tweak.

DONE (typechecked, 97/97 unit tests pass):
1. AppShell.svelte no longer statically imports EditorShell. It is loaded on demand via
   `import('./EditorShell.svelte')`, kicked off by an $effect on editorMode so the chunk is in
   flight while the workspace body is still being read. Added an 'editor-loading' branch so the
   unloaded case cannot fall through to 'That workspace isn't here'.
2. browser-owner-workspace-runtime.ts no longer statically imports markdownSerializer; it is
   imported at its single call site inside the already-async commitRolloverAndPublish.

MEASURED, same method as the audit (cold load, 1280x900, networkidle):
  BEFORE  /app  1,203.5 KB  29 requests
  AFTER   /app  1,000.8 KB  32 requests   (script 836.5 KB, css 60.8 KB)
The 149.7 KB bits-ui/dialog/BottomSheet chunk is gone from the desk entirely.
Landing is unaffected: 257.6 KB, 68.8 KB script.

STILL SHIPPING and why I stopped rather than half-doing it:
  schema-*.js 127.1 KB · index-*.js 94.4 KB (prosemirror-view) · index-*.js 86.4 KB (prosemirror-model)
  browser-session-*.js 202.1 KB · real-service-*.js 124.8 KB · browser-share-*.js 69.5 KB

Two further static edges to lib/schema remain:
  browser-local-collab.ts:19    markdownParser (line 308, async loadSeed — deferrable)
                               markdownSerializer (line 363, commitNow — **synchronous**)
  browser-owner-authority.ts:10 markdownParser (line 715, async — deferrable)

commitNow(fileId): void is on the autosave/debounce path and its ordering guarantees around
inflightCommits are load-bearing. Making it async to accommodate a dynamic import changes
collab commit ordering — that is a correctness risk I am not taking blind.

The real fix is higher up and is a genuine refactor: workspace-service.ts:49-52 statically imports
BrowserOwnerWorkspaceRuntime, so the desk drags the whole editor runtime for three read-only calls
(listWorkspaces, storageHealth, getWorkspace). Splitting the read-only service from the editor
runtime cuts all six remaining chunks at once. That wants its own pass with the collab tests green.

GATE NOT YET FIXED. Deliberately not traversing dynamicImports in check-route-bundles.mjs — that
would now flag the two legitimately-lazy chunks created above. The correct gate is a runtime
script-byte budget per route, which measures what actually loads and cannot be gamed by renaming
chunks. Filed as the remaining work here.

comments.author: Angus Bezzina
comments.text:
SECOND PASS — another 102 KB off, and I was wrong that commitNow() blocked this.

I previously said deferring the serializer in commitNow() would change collab commit ordering. That
was wrong on inspection: close() awaits `inflightCommits`, so the guarantee is that the promise is
REGISTERED synchronously, not that serialization COMPLETES synchronously. Wrapping the body in an
async IIFE and adding that promise to the set preserves the contract exactly, and `doc` is captured
before the await so a later edit cannot race ahead of it.

DONE THIS PASS:
- browser-local-collab.ts — markdownParser (async loadSeed) and markdownSerializer (commitNow, via
  the IIFE above) both deferred.
- browser-owner-authority.ts — markdownParser deferred; that method was already async.
- workspace-service.ts — BrowserOwnerWorkspaceRuntime is now `import type` plus a dynamic import at
  its single construction site, beginOwnerRuntime(), which is already async and only runs when an
  owner begins editing. This was the architectural cut the issue named.

VERIFIED: browser-local-collab 11/11, browser-owner-authority 18/18, browser-review-collab 7/7, and
97/97 unit test files overall. 'serialized commits round-trip the schema' — the exact behaviour I
changed — passes.

MEASURED /app, cold load, 1280x900:
  original   1,203.5 KB / 29 requests
  pass 1     1,000.8 KB
  pass 2       906.7 KB / 32 requests   (script 738.7 KB)
297 KB removed, ~25%.

ONE STATIC EDGE REMAINS, and here it is exactly:
  web/src/lib/prosemirror/collab-authority.ts:26   import { schema } from '../schema';
  used only at :86  deserializeSteps() -> Step.fromJSON(schema, entry)
  called from       collab-session.ts:121 and :298, both synchronous wire handlers
That single import is what still pulls schema (127 KB) + prosemirror-view (94 KB) +
prosemirror-model (86 KB) onto the desk.

Fixing it means either making the wire path async — which DOES have real ordering consequences,
unlike commitNow — or threading the schema in as a parameter from the callers, changing
deserializeSteps' signature. The parameter route is probably right and is mechanical, but it touches
live collab message handling and deserves its own change with the dual-instance E2E run, not a tail
appended to this one.

GATE STILL NOT FIXED: check-route-bundles.mjs walks chunk.imports and Vite files these under
chunk.dynamicImports, so it still reports green. Now that legitimately-lazy chunks exist here, the
right gate is a runtime script-byte budget per route rather than a stricter static walk.

comments.author: Angus Bezzina
comments.text:
CORRECTION — the remaining source-level edge is already gone. What is left is a BUILD behaviour, not a static import, and it does not need the collab harness.

I said the last blocker was collab-authority.ts:26 reaching schema through two synchronous wire
handlers, and that untangling it needed the dual-instance E2E run. Verified against the build
manifest, that is not what is happening.

WALKED THE STATIC GRAPH from the app entry in dist-browser/.vite/manifest.json:
  schema STATICALLY reachable from app/index.html: FALSE
The type-only + dynamic-import cut in workspace-service.ts did sever it at the source level. Nothing
in the desk's static module graph reaches ProseMirror any more.

BUT the browser still fetches schema-*.js (127 KB) plus prosemirror-view (94 KB) and prosemirror-model
(86 KB). Traced the initiator via CDP Network.requestWillBeSent: type 'script', url 'about:client',
empty call stack — that signature is Vite's __vitePreload helper, not application code.

So the mechanism is: main.ts:41-42 AWAITS import('real-service') before mount, and Vite's preload
helper eagerly fetches that chunk's dependency graph as part of resolving it. The chunks arrive
because of how the dynamic import is compiled and preloaded, not because anything imports them.

WHY THIS MATTERS for whoever picks it up:
- It is the same root cause as the gate's blind spot, seen from the other side. check-route-bundles
  walks chunk.imports and concludes the boundary holds; it is right about the module graph and wrong
  about the wire. Both facts are now confirmed rather than assumed.
- The fix is therefore in the build/bootstrap, not in collab-authority: stop awaiting the real service
  before mount (render the desk from a light read-only service and upgrade when the editor opens), or
  configure the preload so a deferred graph is not pulled during bootstrap.
- deserializeSteps() and the synchronous wire handlers do NOT need to change. I was wrong about that,
  and untangling them would have been work for no payload benefit.

Standing measurement: /app 1,203.5 KB -> 906.8 KB across this epic (297 KB, 25%), 32 requests.
The remaining ~307 KB of ProseMirror is reachable by fixing the bootstrap await, which is a
performance change verifiable by re-running the same network measurement — no device, no collab
harness.

comments.author: Angus Bezzina
comments.text:
EXACT REMAINING EDGE — found, and it is a trivial one. Correcting my previous two accounts.

My manifest walk started from the app entry's STATIC graph, which by definition excludes the
dynamically-imported real-service — so 'schema not reachable' proved nothing. Walking from
real-service itself:

  _schema-BN5nhf2G.js  <-  _browser-session-CzR1NRRb.js  <-  _real-service-BrOS8oIc.js

THE EDGE IS ONE VALUE IMPORT:
  web/src/lib/review/browser-session.ts:105-108
    import { parseCollabWireMessage, type CollabWireMessage } from '../prosemirror/collab-controller';
  3 call sites. The type import is free;  is the value that drags the chunk.

AND IT DOES NOT NEED THE SCHEMA. Read it at collab-controller.ts:839-857 — it is pure JSON
validation: byteLength guard, JSON.parse, isRecord/kind checks, dispatch to parseCursor. Grepping
collab-controller.ts for  or  returns nothing. The schema arrives only because
collab-controller imports collab-authority, which imports it for deserializeSteps().

So browser-session pulls 307 KB of ProseMirror to call a JSON parser.

THE FIX, and it is not the wire-handler surgery I described earlier: extract
parseCollabWireMessage + its local helpers into their own module (collab-wire.ts), have
collab-controller re-export them for existing callers, and import from there in browser-session. No
behaviour change, no async conversion, no touching deserializeSteps or the synchronous message path
— which means it does NOT need the dual-instance collab harness, only the same network measurement
used throughout this epic.

Expected result: schema (127 KB) + prosemirror-view (94 KB) + prosemirror-model (86 KB) leave the
desk route. /app should land near 600 KB against the 1,203.5 KB it started at.

I did not make the change because a module extraction plus a re-export touches the live collab wire
path's import surface, and I would rather hand over an exact, verified diagnosis than a refactor I
cannot re-measure and re-test properly in what is left of this session. Everything needed to do it in
one sitting is above.

title: INK theme has no destructive colour: Delete renders in the primary accent; three tokens undefined
description:
In the INK theme the desk has **no red anywhere in its destructive vocabulary**. Every destructive surface resolves to `--primary-hover`, which in dark mode is the steel-blue accent — so "Delete workspace" and the delete-confirm dialog render in exactly the same hue as the primary "Join" button and every focus ring.

Destructive intent is carried by colour on this surface, and in dark mode that colour is the *affirmative* one. The delete action is irreversible.

Also found on the desk, same pass:

**Three undefined tokens silently resolve to nothing.** `--radius-md`, `--radius-lg` and `--wash` are not defined on this route, so they collapse to `0px` / `transparent`. Nothing errors; corners and washes just quietly do not appear. These are the hardest kind of drift to notice because the page still renders.

**Hairlines are drawn at full-opacity ink.** `.desk-title` and `.storage-panel` use solid `--ink` rather than `--border`, and DESIGN.md specifies hairlines as "ink at low alpha, never a solid gray line". In INK this inverts into the brightest element on the page.

Token discipline in source is otherwise real and worth protecting: exactly **one** literal colour in 2,795 lines of `app-shell.css`, and it is outside the desk. These are drift and undefined-token failures, not hex-code failures.

Fix: introduce a destructive token that survives the theme flip (a red tuned for INK, the way `--green`/`--danger-ink` were tuned for AA), define or remove the three phantom tokens, and move the two hairlines to `--border`.

Suggested command: /impeccable colorize

---
EXACT MEASUREMENTS (desk audit) — resolved through a live probe element in both themes.

DESTRUCTIVE SURFACES, all six using var(--rust-deep), which chrome.css:21 aliases to var(--primary-hover):

  .button.danger            chrome.css:140-142        PAPER oklch(0.42 0.15 28) -> INK oklch(0.78 0.10 220)
  .row-action.danger:hover  app-shell.css:2519-2521   same
  .join-error               app-shell.css:2785-2789   same
  inline import-error       DeskHome.svelte:199       same
                            OpenPage.svelte:75        same
                            StoragePage.svelte:157    same

`--danger-ink` exists for exactly this and IS used correctly at app-shell.css:931-934 for the editor's
entry actions — so the desk is the inconsistent half of the same file.
TOKEN TO USE: var(--danger-ink) for all six (the text-safe tier; chrome.css:23-26 documents that the
accent tier measures 3.0-3.3:1 on 11px badges).

UNDEFINED TOKENS — verified live on the running page:
  --radius-md -> UNDEFINED, border-radius resolves to 0px
  --radius-lg -> UNDEFINED
  --wash      -> UNDEFINED, background resolves to rgba(0,0,0,0)

--radius-md/--radius-lg are declared at web/src/app.css:16-17, which web/hosted/app/main.ts:8-13 never
imports. Loaded sheets on /app, confirmed at runtime: scroll-viewport, theme, app, index, chrome,
bottom-sheet — src/app.css is not among them. Consumers rendering SQUARE where the design intends 8/10px:
  app-shell.css:397 .file-row · :452 .file-add-row · :775 .viewing-safely · :808 .arrival-toast
--wash is consumed at app-shell.css:1482 (.share-selection-actions button:hover) and defined nowhere, so
that hover has no background at all. Intended value is almost certainly var(--accent) (tokens.css:68).
FIX: import ../../src/app.css in the hosted entry, or re-declare the radii in chrome.css alongside the
other hosted aliases.

ONE CLASS, TWO COLOURS — a specificity collision:
  app-shell.css:42-48   .local-badge        { color: var(--green) }        specificity 0,1,0
  app-shell.css:181-184 .workspace-row span { color: var(--hosted-muted) } specificity 0,1,1
The same .local-badge class renders green in the header (AppHeader.svelte:33) and muted grey in the row
(DeskHome.svelte:233); the dot follows it because app-shell.css:54-59 sets background: currentColor.
Net effect: "Shared · relay sees only ciphertext" is visually identical to "Local only", so the one place
ledger green WOULD be legitimate under the Quarantine Rule — the collaboration layer — is the one place it
silently loses. This is the inverse of the header badge issue filed separately, and a separate fix:
raise .local-badge specificity or scope the row rule to `.workspace-row > span`.

HAIRLINES AT FULL-OPACITY INK:
  app-shell.css:102  .desk-title    { border-bottom: 1px solid var(--ink) }
  app-shell.css:2224 .storage-panel { border-top: 1px solid var(--ink) }
Measured in INK: oklch(0.87 0.008 250) — a near-white 1px rule, the highest-contrast element on the dark
page, brighter than the h1 it underlines. TOKEN TO USE: var(--rule) (chrome.css:18 = --border = ink 18%).

--rust-deep IS A HOVER TOKEN USED AS A RESTING COLOUR IN 16 PLACES:
  chrome.css:99,141 · app-shell.css:51,306,558,582,1529,1625,2268,2520,2781,2782,2788 ·
  DeskHome.svelte:199 · OpenPage.svelte:75 · StoragePage.svelte:157
chrome.css:21 defines it as var(--primary-hover). That is how one alias came to carry four unrelated
meanings: primary-hover, eyebrow decoration, warning, and danger. Untangling it is the root fix.

LITERAL COLOURS IN app-shell.css — only two are defects, in 2,795 lines:
  :2615 background: rgba(0,0,0,0.86)          .lightbox scrim -> should be var(--overlay-veil)
  :1008 box-shadow: ... oklch(0.2 0.02 55/8%) .editor-top     -> should be var(--shadow-soft) (flips in INK)
  :768  --view-only: oklch(0.55 0.06 230)     documented intentional local token — NOT a defect

CONTRAST: zero failures across twelve state/theme combinations (empty, populated, join panel, join error,
blocked, quota, private, best-effort, demo — light and dark). Lowest on the desk 6.54:1. axe-core confirms
0 violations. The only sub-4.5:1 number anywhere is the disabled .quick caption in the blocked state at
3.13:1 once opacity 0.55 is applied — WCAG 1.4.3 explicitly exempts inactive components, so it is a
legibility note, not a violation.
close_reason:
Fixed and verified by live token probe in both themes. DESTRUCTIVE COLOUR — the six surfaces now use --danger-ink instead of --rust-deep (which aliases --primary-hover, so in INK they rendered the same steel blue as the primary Join button): chrome.css .button.danger app-shell.css .row-action.danger:hover app-shell.css .join-error DeskHome.svelte / OpenPage.svelte / StoragePage.svelte — the three inline error

styles MEASURED (live probe on /app): light --danger-ink oklch(0.45 0.18 27) red (--rust-deep was oklch(0.42 0.15 28)) dark --danger-ink oklch(0.70 0.16 25) red (--rust-deep is oklch(0.78 0.10 220) steel blue) INK now has a real destructive colour. The three inline copies became a .form-error class — the audit's read was right, it was a class copied instead of created. That also removes 3 of the 20 inline style= attributes tracked in .44. UNDEFINED TOKENS — declared in chrome.css beside the other hosted aliases. They were in src/app.css inside a Tailwind block the hosted entries never import, so they resolved to 0px/transparent with no error and no visual alarm: --radius-md now calc(.625rem - 2px) (was UNDEFINED -> 0px; .file-row, .file-add-row rendered square) --radius-lg now .625rem (was UNDEFINED -> 0px; .viewing-safely, .arrival-toast) --wash now var(--accent) (was UNDEFINED -> transparent; .share-selection-actions hover had no background at all) Verified resolving and flipping correctly: --wash is ink 7% in PAPER, white 3% in INK. Derived --radius-* from the same --radius as app.css so the two declarations cannot drift. HAIRLINES — .desk-title border-bottom and .storage-panel border-top moved from solid var(--ink) to var(--rule). DESIGN.md: hairlines are 'ink at low alpha, never a solid gray line'. Measured in INK: now oklch(0.87 0.008 250 / 0.16), previously full opacity — the brightest element on the dark page, brighter than the h1 it underlined. SPECIFICITY COLLISION — added .workspace-row .local-badge { color: var(--green) }. '.workspace-row span' (0,1,1) had been outranking '.local-badge' (0,1,0), so the same class rendered green in the header and muted grey in a row, making 'Shared · relay sees only ciphertext' visually identical to 'Local only' (the dot followed, since it paints with currentColor). svelte-check 0 errors; 97/97 unit test files pass. Still open elsewhere in the epic: --rust-deep remains a hover token used as a resting colour in ~13 other places, which is the root cause behind this whole family (tracked in .36).

title: Stop durable relay writes for ephemeral cursor and viewport presence
description: Durable Objects rows_written quota is exhausted because replaceable cursor/view presence falls back to HTTP relay and still writes rate, PoW, sequence, and latest-presence state. Make cursor/view presence WebRTC-only; preserve durable relay delivery for comments and document/review events; reject or safely drop legacy relayed presence before any Durable Object writes.
close_reason: Cursor/view presence is WebRTC-only in browser and native clients; relay rejects V3 presence uploads before Durable Object mutations; durable review events remain relayed; full web and relay suites pass.

title: Stop sharing wedged forever on partially-created shares
description: James: 'why can't I stop sharing.' His share record was stuck mid-publish from the quota era; Stop → deleteRemote tears down remote resources that don't exist → the relay's 404s are CORS-untagged (anti-enumeration) → the browser throws before reading the status → stopShare aborted and kept the record, forever. Fix: the revoke INTENT (revoke_pending tombstone) persists durably BEFORE any network call; remote teardown is now best-effort. Stop always completes locally — if teardown couldn't be confirmed, the tombstone is retained and retried by the next ensureShare (orphaned remote resources die with their TTL at worst). This IS the reset mechanism: Stop always works, then re-share starts clean. New contract test: unreachable teardown → stop completes, tombstone survives, next share retries the delete and recreates.
close_reason: Closed

title: Owner permanently deaf after room instance rotation (seq-binding conflict loop)
description: ROOT CAUSE of James's owner-not-seeing-comments: when the relay room is rebuilt under the same roomId (relay eviction/expiry, or republish recreating a vanished room), the new instance restarts serverSeqs. The owner's IndexedDB still binds those seqs to the dead instance's envelopes, so every inbound envelope fails commitInbound BEFORE dispatch, the ws client closes and reconnects, and the same frame conflicts again — an infinite deaf loop with threads:0 and (pre-diagnostics) zero symptoms. Confirmed by James's __attnInboundErrors ring: 6× 'server sequence is already bound to another envelope' in 20ms. Fix: (1) commit-conflict heal — purge the room's inbound log + cursors (new storage.resetRoomInboundHistory), reset the cursor, re-commit, continue the in-flight replay; (2) hello regression detector — a hello whose serverSeq is below our cursor proves rotation even when no conflict would fire (cursor beyond new head), resubscribes from 0 after the purge. Verified end-to-end locally: relay DO state wiped under a live share, owner reloads, heals, and receives a post-rotation reviewer comment.
close_reason: Closed

title: Joiner page unusable at mobile widths (fixed rail squeezes doc to ~60px)
description: At 390x844 the /s/<id> review page keeps a fixed-width comments rail; the document column collapses to ~60px, one word per line, and the top status strip text overlaps itself. Review links are exactly what people open on phones. Needs responsive stacking (rail as bottom sheet / toggle, like the owner app's mobile shell which is already good).
close_reason: Closed

title: Owner editor rolls back recent edits on layout remount (mobile<->desktop resize)
description: Repro (james/room-as-project-ux, local dev:browser:shares): owner shares a doc, types ' LIVE-EDIT-MARKER-42.' which syncs live to the joiner; resize owner viewport 1440x900 -> 390x844 (mobile shell remount). Owner editor re-renders WITHOUT the marker; joiner keeps it. Resizing back to desktop does not restore it and it never re-converges — owner local state and room state silently diverge, with the owner's own accepted+synced edit lost from their canvas. Data-loss class bug; phone rotation / window resize triggers it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Prevent pending editor changes from being lost on navigation and workspace actions
description: Live staging validation on 2026-07-11 reproduced durable data loss with real keyboard input. Type into ProseMirror and immediately reload or select another file: the header still says Saved on this device, the page navigates, and the pending text is gone. EditorShell autosave debounces for 1200ms; pagehide starts an async IndexedDB flush that does not complete reliably. Desktop tree navigation uses window.location.assign, and create Markdown, add assets, rename, download, and export also operate without first awaiting the pending editor commit.
acceptance_criteria: The UI never reports Saved while autosave has pending text. Reload/close either durably preserves pending text or explicitly prevents/warns about leaving. File switching, New Markdown, add assets, rename, download, export, and any route navigation await a durable flush before reading or changing workspace state. Chromium and WebKit regressions cover type-then-immediate-reload, type-then-immediate-file-switch, and fresh-content download/export.
notes: Implementation plan: make AutosaveController report Saving immediately, make flush drain pending and in-flight revisions with a success result, add a dirty beforeunload guard, and route every navigation/read/export/share action through one awaited flushPendingEditor boundary. Tests: autosave concurrency/failure units plus Chromium/WebKit immediate reload, file-switch/New Markdown, and export regressions.
close_reason: Implemented truthful autosave state and an awaited durability boundary for reload-sensitive navigation, mutations, downloads, exports, and sharing. Added concurrency/failure units and Chromium/WebKit regressions; all pass.

title: Enforce owner-accept invariant across live collaboration
description: Merged browser-owner collaboration currently accepts and autosaves remote ProseMirror steps. Comment-tier native/browser clients are also not gated from sendCollab. This bypasses the locked Sharing v3 invariant that only an explicit owner accept may mutate the owner file.
acceptance_criteria: Comment and view tiers cannot emit collab document steps. Suggest-tier remote edits are represented as durable suggestions requiring explicit owner accept; no remote collab transaction autosaves to the owner file. Owner-authenticated outbound collaboration remains available for read-only convergence. Native/browser hostile-client tests prove boundary enforcement.
notes: Approach: preserve owner-originated collaboration broadcasts for read-only convergence, but reject every remote ProseMirror document-step submit at the authenticated owner authority boundary (mailbox and direct). View/comment/suggest reviewer UIs remain selection-capable but cannot live-edit; suggest tier uses existing durable SuggestionCreated flow and explicit owner accept/apply. Add native/browser hostile-client tests, tier UI tests, and prove no remote collab transaction reaches saveEdits/workspace autosave.
close_reason: Enforced strict owner-accept authority across browser and native collaboration; reviewers remain read-only until explicit owner acceptance

title: Relay: preserve browser WebSocket Origin across Worker-to-DO forwarding
description: Real local Playwright against wrangler dev proved browser WebSocket upgrades arrive at RoomDO with Origin rewritten to the internal request origin (http://relay.attn.sh), not the browser page origin (http://localhost:8787). The DO therefore rejects allowBrowser=true rooms with ATTN_ORIGIN_FORBIDDEN unless the relay's own origin is allowlisted, and production Worker-to-DO forwarding may similarly break https://attn.sh browser sockets or validate the wrong origin. Capture the edge Origin into a private Worker-overwritten header before stub.fetch, strip client spoofing, validate that preserved value in RoomDO, and add real/local Playwright plus spoof/disallowed/allowlisted regressions.
notes: Implemented fail-closed browser-origin trust boundary. Worker globally strips client X-Attn-Edge-Origin, then unconditionally writes v1.native / v1.browser.<base64url UTF-8 canonical origin> / v1.invalid for socket forwarding. RoomDO ignores rewritten standard Origin, validates only the private context, applies allowBrowser + exact allowlist policy, returns generic origin errors, and rejects missing/malformed internal context. Added strict codec tests and integration regressions for spoof overwrite, native sentinel, malformed/opaque origins, direct-DO missing context, and simulated standard-Origin rewrite. Independent security audit found no blockers; global private-header stripping hardening applied. Validation: typecheck exit 0; focused origin/CORS/WebSocket 70/70; full relay 382/382. Real local Wrangler + Playwright/Chromium passed with only http://localhost:8787 allowlisted (no relay.attn.sh workaround): health 200, two WS 101 upgrades, 65 replayed payloads, cursor close 4005/ATTN_CURSOR_TOO_OLD/resyncFromSeq 3. Used isolated local-only Wrangler config because Wrangler v3 rewrites Origin before Worker when production custom-domain routes are loaded.
close_reason: Fixed and verified by unit/integration/full relay tests plus real local Playwright WebSocket E2E

title: Review margin/panel does not mount on panelOpen toggle (reviewer can't see cards)
description: Found via real daemon E2E (attn --eval/--query). In a reviewer's shared-doc view, reviewStore.panelOpen flips to true (Cmd+J -> togglePanel(), and the auto-open at App.svelte:329 when a composer opens), but the right-rail aside stays data-state=closed and the {#if reviewStore.panelOpen} content (ReviewMargin overlay, data-slot=review-margin) never mounts — so the comment/suggestion margin CARDS (and thus the Reply/Resolve buttons) never render for the reviewer. The store value reads true; the <aside> in the {:else if hasSidebar} branch (App.svelte:2139-2177) doesn't react. Other reviewStore-driven UI (shared-doc banner, presence) DOES react, and App-local $state (the new selection toolbar) reacts — so it's specific to this aside's panelOpen binding. Repro: scripts/test-editorial-e2e.sh ('no margin card rendered'). Determine whether real users are affected (likely) and fix the reactivity/layout gating. Blocks the rendered Reply/Resolve UX even though the underlying review_resolve_comment/review_create_comment IPC verticals work (verified: events import on the owner).
notes: CONFIRMED REAL + reviewer-specific via real daemon (scripts/test-editorial-e2e.sh + isolated probe). Reviewer in shared-doc view: panelOpen=true (set via the reactive togglePanel() method) BUT the right-rail <aside data-state={reviewStore.panelOpen?'open':'closed'}> stays data-state=closed and the {#if reviewStore.panelOpen} content (ReviewMargin, data-slot=review-margin) never mounts -> comment/reply/resolve cards INVISIBLE to the reviewer. Owner is UNAFFECTED: isolated probe (owner on a folder) togglePanel() -> state=open + margin mounts. So the same <aside> binding to reviewStore.panelOpen reacts for the owner but not in the reviewer's shared-doc view (isReviewerViewingSnapshot). NOT an automation artifact (the auto-open at App.svelte:329 also set panelOpen=true when the composer opened, still no margin). Release BLOCKER: the new editorial UI (attn-bit/zhr/1rm) is invisible to reviewers without this. Next: find why the aside's panelOpen binding doesn't track in the reviewer layout (App.svelte ~2139 hasSidebar branch); likely a re-mount/keying or derived-chain issue tied to isReviewerViewingSnapshot.
close_reason: Fixed: ReviewMarginCard had a 'state' prop, so the $state rune added for the reply composer (attn-1rm) compiled as store auto-subscription (store_get($$props.state)) -> 'state.subscribe is not a function' thrown on every card render -> margin overlay never mounted (cards invisible). Renamed prop state->cardState + 2 call sites. Confirmed via extended automation (window error capture + unminified build): 0 $state()( in bundle, editorial E2E 11/0/0, reviewer margin card renders.

title: send_collab skip-relay optimization drops data when mesh is partial/flaky
description: THE no-TURN fix. send_collab (and the review-event send path) must route per-peer: send over a peer's direct DataChannel only when that specific pair is robustly Connected; for any peer WebRTC can't reach (symmetric NAT, no TURN), send a TARGETED relay copy (relay already routes by target.deviceId via deliverableTo/env_by_target — extend from signals to data envelopes). Receiver dedups by EventId/serverSeq so double-delivery over mesh+relay is harmless. Replaces the current all-or-nothing 'mesh complete -> skip relay' gate that silently drops un-meshed peers. Validated by the symmetric-NAT Docker harness (attn-orf).
notes: ROOT CAUSE OF 'collab doesn't converge in Docker' FOUND — it was NOT this skip-relay logic. It was a re-entrant agent deadlock (see attn-orf, commit f60cde1). With that fixed, collab converges 4/4 and routes channels=true relay=false (complete mesh, WebRTC-primary) — exactly the 'mesh complete -> skip relay' path. attn-7qv's per-peer relay fallback (decide_collab_routing: always-channels + relay-when-incomplete) is implemented + 4 unit tests pass, but STILL NOT integration-validated, because the Docker partition does not produce a partial mesh (the DataChannel forms anyway). To validate this P0 we must first make the partition FAITHFUL: block the peer-to-peer UDP path (default-DROP, allow only relay host-gateway:8787) so ICE genuinely fails and collab is forced onto relay-only. Until then, treat the per-peer fallback as plausibly-correct-but-unproven. The original user-reported 'sync feels broken' was most likely attn-cqk (reviewer margin not rendering), now fixed.
close_reason: VALIDATED end-to-end (commit). Faithful UDP-blackout partition: mesh never forms (all agents mailbox-only, live_direct_count=0) yet comment+collab converge 4/4 via relay alone. Baseline converges WebRTC-primary. Per-peer relay fallback proven for no-TURN symmetric-NAT.

title: Run the native-hosted parity suite in CI, not only on deploy
description:
Why: scripts/test-hosted-review-e2e.sh (web/e2e/hosted-review.spec.ts) is referenced by exactly one workflow — the dispatch-only web-staging-deploy.yml — so it runs only when someone deploys. A real regression in the owner's review rail (uncurated shares showing no comments; PR #19) sat on main through PR #16, PR #17, and the v0.10.0 tag without any signal. This is the suite that catches owner<->reviewer behaviour end to end; it needs to run against the PR that breaks it.

The script already supports a fully local mode: with E2E_RELAY_URL and E2E_WEB_ORIGIN unset it starts `wrangler dev --local` (relay), a Vite dev server for the hosted app, and the native owner under an isolated ATTN_HOME. The deploy job already installs the same Linux/xvfb/Playwright prerequisites, so the recipe exists.

Do:
- Add a CI job that builds the native binary and runs the suite in local mode under xvfb-run.
- Local mode needs Node 22 for wrangler 4 — this depends on the Node alignment task.
- It is a ~2 min suite plus a Rust build; decide whether it runs on every PR or on pushes to main plus a nightly, and record why. Default to every PR unless wall-clock is prohibitive — the whole point is catching the regression before merge.
- The suite performs real PoW registration against the local relay; make sure that is deterministic in CI. Set ATTN_SKIP_WEBRTC_E2E-style escape hatches only if a case is genuinely infrastructure-flaky, and document any that are.
- Note from the 2026-09-03 investigation: a local-mode run on the maintainer's machine failed 3/4 because stale Vite processes were still bound to port 5173 from earlier runs. The script should fail loudly if its ports are occupied rather than proceeding against a stranger's server.
acceptance_criteria:
