- The suite runs in ci.yml (or a workflow triggered on pull_request) and is green on main.
- Reverting the PR #19 fix (restore the early `selected_paths.is_empty()` return in local_owner_display_path) on a branch makes that CI job fail on the 'native share opens in hosted reviewer' case.
- The script refuses to start when its relay or web port is already bound.

title: Run one Node version: align ci.yml with the deploy job and declare it
description:
Why: ci.yml runs all four jobs on Node 20; web-staging-deploy.yml runs Node 22 because web/ depends on wrangler ^4.110, which refuses anything older (commit 5fa404f). Different Node means different bundled npm, so CI never exercised the combination the deploy actually runs — the npm 10 arborist crash was invisible to CI for weeks. Nothing declares the requirement either: root package.json says engines.node >=18 and there is no .nvmrc, so a contributor on 20 gets a green local build and a red deploy.

Do:
- Set node-version to "22" in every setup-node step in ci.yml (four occurrences: lines ~57, 119, 172, 211).
- Add a .nvmrc (or .node-version) at the repo root pinning 22.
- Set engines.node to >=22 in web/package.json; decide whether the root package.json (the attnmd npm CLI wrapper) should also move or genuinely still supports 18 for end users — record the answer.
- Confirm relay/ (wrangler ^3.80) is happy on 22; it should be.
- Consider whether the single input should live in one place (a workflow-level env or a reusable step) so the two files cannot drift apart again.

Stay on 22 rather than jumping to 24: it matches the deploy job and the maintainer's local machine (22.14), and this task is about removing a split, not choosing a new floor.
acceptance_criteria:
- `grep -n node-version .github/workflows/ci.yml .github/workflows/web-staging-deploy.yml` shows one value.
- .nvmrc present; `nvm use` / fnm picks 22.
- web/package.json engines.node is >=22; `npm ci` on Node 20 fails fast with an engines error rather than a late wrangler error.
- CI is green on 22 (all four jobs) before merge.

title: Vendor the icon packs and drop the three git dependencies
description:
Why: web/package.json pulls eyecons, catppuccin-vsc-icons, and vscode-icons straight from GitHub (git+ssh:// in the lockfile). npm has to clone each and resolve that project's own floating package.json against the live registry on every install, so an upstream publish can break our install with no change here — which is exactly what happened on 2026-09-03. None of the three has a usable registry package (eyecons on npm is a 0.0.1 placeholder; the other two are unpublished), so the only hermetic option is to carry what we consume ourselves.

What the generator actually reads (web/scripts/generate-vscode-icon-map.mjs): eyecons icons/files + icons/base + data/file-icons.ts + data/base-icons.ts; catppuccin icons/latte; vscode-icons icons/ + its manifest. Its output (src/lib/icons/vscode-generated ~13 MB / 2,777 SVGs, vscode-icon-packs ~620 KB, vscode-icon-map.generated.ts) is gitignored and regenerated on every `npm run build` and `npm run check`.

Do:
- Add a refresh script that fetches each pack as an https tarball at an explicitly pinned commit (the three SHAs currently in web/package-lock.json are the starting pins) and copies only the consumed files into web/vendor/icon-packs/<pack>/. No git+ssh, no npm resolution of upstream package.json.
- Each vendored pack carries its upstream LICENSE and a PROVENANCE file (repo URL + commit + fetch date) so the pin is auditable.
- Point the generator at web/vendor/ instead of require.resolve('<pack>/package.json').
- Remove the three deps from web/package.json and regenerate web/package-lock.json.
- Keep material-icon-theme and seti-file-icons as they are — both come from the registry.

Design decision to make and record here: vendor the SOURCES and keep running the generator at build time, or vendor the GENERATED output and make generation a manual dev command. Both cost ~13 MB in git; committing the output additionally removes the generator from the CI/build critical path and is the simpler contract. Recommendation: commit the generated output, keep the generator as `npm run refresh:icons` for upgrades.

Also worth checking while here: the memory 'fresh attn git worktrees need their own web/node_modules, and plain npm ci FAILS there: a git-sourced puppeteer dep tries to download a browser' — confirm whether that puppeteer comes in via one of these three and whether it goes away.
acceptance_criteria:
- `grep -c 'git+' web/package-lock.json` is 0.
- In a fresh clone, `npm ci` in web/ succeeds under BOTH npm 10.9.x (Node 22's bundled npm) and npm 11 — the npm 10 case is the one that failed on 2026-09-03 and must be exercised explicitly.
- `npm run build` and `npm run check` succeed with the registry as the only network dependency.
- The rendered icon set is byte-identical to what the git-dep build produced at the same pins (diff the generated dir before/after).
- Each vendored pack directory contains LICENSE and PROVENANCE.
- A documented command refreshes a pack to a new pinned commit.

title: Hermetic web builds and one Node version across CI and deploy
description:
Why: the web staging deploy was blocked on 2026-09-03 by two build-infrastructure failures that had nothing to do with product code, and the fix that unblocked it (pinning npm 11 in the deploy job, PR #18) is a workaround, not a resolution. Each will recur.

1. Non-hermetic installs. web/package.json depends on three icon packs straight from GitHub — eyecons, catppuccin-vsc-icons, vscode-icons — resolved as git+ssh:// in the lockfile. The lockfile pins each repo's commit, but npm still has to clone the repo and resolve THAT project's own floating package.json against the live registry on every install. A registry publish upstream (eslint 10 landing in eyecons' devDependencies next to plugins capped at 9) walked npm 10's arborist into "Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')" with no change in this repo. Switching to registry packages is not an option: eyecons on npm is a 0.0.1 placeholder, and the other two are not published.

2. Two Node versions. ci.yml runs every job on Node 20; the deploy job runs Node 22 because wrangler 4 (web/) refuses anything older. Different bundled npm, so the deploy is the only job that ever saw failure 1, and CI stayed green throughout. Root package.json still declares engines.node >=18 and there is no .nvmrc.

3. No CI coverage for native<->hosted parity. scripts/test-hosted-review-e2e.sh runs only inside the dispatch-only deploy workflow. That is how a real owner-side regression (uncurated shares rendering an empty review rail, fixed in PR #19) sat on main through two merges and a version bump.

Scope: make `npm ci` in web/ reproducible from the lockfile alone, run one Node version everywhere, retire the npm pin, and get the parity suite in front of PRs. Out of scope: the attn.sh apex still being served by a stale Vercel deploy (only staging.attn.sh runs the worker) — separate issue.

Done when: a fresh clone installs and builds web/ with no network beyond the npm registry, `grep 'git+' web/package-lock.json` is empty, ci.yml and web-staging-deploy.yml use the same Node input, the deploy job has no npm upgrade step, and a regression in the native review rail fails CI on the PR that introduces it.

title: Diagnose and repair hosted HTTPS image rendering end to end
description: Reproduce the external-image fallback with the current Pexels fixture in a newly imported workspace, then trace authored Markdown through approvedExternalImageUrl, EditorShell resolveLocalAssetUrl, the ProseMirror image NodeView, hosted CSP, and the actual browser request. Separately verify whether the reported workspace is displaying an older persisted copy of the fixture. Repair the failing owner path without weakening reviewer consent, scheme restrictions, credential rejection, referrer policy, or missing-file fallback behavior.
acceptance_criteria: A new workspace imported from current tests/fixtures/images.md visibly loads the exact Pexels JPEG for the owner. A newly shared review shows a placeholder until Load images is chosen, then loads the same HTTPS image; reload returns to the safe default. Missing local files remain placeholders and unsafe/non-HTTPS URLs remain rejected. The stale-workspace case has a reproducible diagnosis and an explicit user-facing or smoke-test refresh path. Focused policy, node-view/CSP, and hosted-browser tests cover the fixed failure.
close_reason: Closed

title: Hosted workspace: reliable external images, unified import, and truthful folder disclosure
description: Resolve the remaining hosted-workspace failures observed on /app/w/Z5fiNc8wUUZa7wXYYypKKg/tests/fixtures/images.md. The external HTTPS image still renders the fallback card; the sidebar exposes separate file and folder import controls; and folder disclosure chevrons do not accurately communicate collapsed state or use the requested motion curve. The screenshot contains the pre-Pexels fixture copy, so investigation must distinguish a stale persisted workspace document from a current-source fetch, CSP, resolver, or node-view failure.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh import of tests/fixtures/images.md renders https://images.pexels.com/photos/35227957/pexels-photo-35227957.jpeg for the workspace owner, and the shared reviewer flow retains its explicit per-session Load images privacy gate. Existing stale workspaces are diagnosed and the product or smoke instructions provide an unambiguous refresh/re-import path. The sidebar presents one visible, keyboard-accessible Add files control that lets a user choose files or a folder while preserving relative paths and drag/drop. Every folder chevron points right while closed and down while open, including independent nested folders, and its rotation uses an explicit cubic-bezier curve with reduced-motion support. Automated coverage and a documented owner/reviewer smoke test prevent regressions.

title: Expose folder selection from the hosted Add files control
description: Expose the existing directory input from the desktop Add files well so users can choose a whole folder, while retaining multi-file picking and drag-and-drop.
acceptance_criteria: Desktop Add files surface exposes Add files and Add folder actions; both inputs remain wired to importFiles; focused hosted-shell checks pass.
close_reason: Desktop Add folder action now exposes the existing directory picker; focused browser checks pass.

title: Support HTTPS images in hosted workspaces and reviewer shares
description: Allow standard HTTPS image URLs in an owner's hosted workspace while requiring an invited reviewer to explicitly opt in for the current review session. Keep local assets automatic, missing assets graceful, and block unsafe schemes.
acceptance_criteria: Owner workspaces render approved HTTPS images; reviewers start with external images blocked and can enable them per session; image requests use no-referrer; HTTP, data, javascript, protocol-relative, credentialed, and missing paths remain blocked or graceful; automated and live hosted-share coverage passes.
close_reason: Implemented and validated HTTPS image support with session-only reviewer consent.

title: Add end-to-end compatibility coverage for hosted image shares
description: Exercise hosted Markdown and HTML image shares in real browsers across owner, live reviewer, follower tab, reload, and durable owner-offline replay. Prove rejected and oversized inputs retain the existing fallback, Blob URLs are revoked on replacement and teardown, and a reader-first rollout remains compatible before asset-emitting writers are enabled.
close_reason: Real browser coverage now proves hosted Markdown and HTML images across owner, reviewers, reload, and owner-offline durable recovery.

title: First-class document images in hosted shares
description:
## Problem

Images are a core part of a document, but the hosted share path currently treats them as inert metadata. Browser publication can emit asset snapshots, while live reviewer hydration discards verified bytes, durable log replay ignores assets, durable share snapshots omit them, and neither hosted editor supplies an asset resolver. Current-file shares also do not automatically include referenced image dependencies, and the native 8 MiB per-image and 32 MiB aggregate policy conflicts with the relay 5 MiB snapshot and 25 MiB durable-share ceilings.

## Outcome

Hosted owners and invited reviewers see the same document images across local editing, live review, follower tabs, reloads, and owner-offline durable review, without weakening encrypted scope, manifest integrity, sandboxing, or bounded resource use.
design: Treat images as first-class encrypted share dependencies. Add a room-scoped, per-tab asset registry that activates bytes only after signature, base hash, path, media type, size, and signed workspace-manifest binding checks; render verified bytes through Blob URLs with acquire/release cleanup; and keep decrypted bytes and object URLs out of persisted review state. Compute referenced-image dependency closure for file and selected-document scopes, extend live and replay hydration plus versioned durable snapshots to carry assets, and roll out compatible readers before writers. Preserve the opaque-origin HTML sandbox and rewrite only verified local image attributes through parsed DOM rather than string replacement. Align Rust, browser, and relay limits with shared conformance fixtures; prefer a versioned binary asset payload over base64-in-JSON wire inflation.
acceptance_criteria: Hosted Markdown images render for the local owner, a live invited reviewer, a follower tab, and an owner-offline durable reviewer after reload. Workspace, selected-document, and current-file shares include only in-scope referenced local images; remote, missing, rejected, corrupt, out-of-manifest, and oversized images retain the existing honest fallback. Supported raster formats and SVG render only in image context, with allowlisted types, content and dimension validation, per-image/count/aggregate limits, no unintended network fetches, and no executable SVG or HTML escalation. HTML img src and picture/source srcset references resolve inside the existing sandbox. Image replacement, file switching, room rotation, share stop/expiry, and component teardown revoke obsolete Blob URLs without breaking duplicate references. Rust, TypeScript, relay conformance tests and hosted Playwright coverage prove live, replay, durable, mobile, nested-path, Unicode, tamper, limit, and resource-lifecycle behavior.
close_reason: Hosted document-image sharing is implemented and validated across Rust, TypeScript, production bundles, and the real browser lifecycle.

title: Only the manifest checks who authored a snapshot
description:
attn-lb7p made workspace-manifest acceptance depend on proof of authorship: a manifest hydrates only when the room OWNER signed the event carrying it, verified against a key pinned from the invite (validate_workspace_manifest_binding, src/review/manager.rs). While doing that it became clear the manifest was the ONLY place in the snapshot path where authorship is checked at all.

Every other snapshot — the documents a reviewer reads, and now the image assets attn-udu8 publishes — is accepted on the strength of a signature from ANY device in the room's directory. InboundPipeline verifies that the signing key is one it knows (src/review/transport/inbound.rs seeds every relay-directory key into the VerifyingKeyCache without distinguishing the owner), so the property actually enforced is 'some registered participant signed this', not 'the owner published this'.

Concretely: a reviewer holding a comment- or suggest-tier grant is a registered device with a valid signing key. Nothing in rehydrate_snapshot_event stops them minting a SnapshotCreated for an arbitrary fileId and having other reviewers render it as the owner's document — or, since attn-udu8, as one of its images.

The mechanism to fix it already exists and is proven: RoomAccessV3.owner_public_signing_key is pinned at join, and crate::review::crypto::signing::verify_event is a full local re-verification that is valid on replay.
design:
Extend the owner-signature check from the manifest branch to the general snapshot path in rehydrate_snapshot_event, reusing the pinned key and verify_event exactly as validate_workspace_manifest_binding now does.

Two things to establish BEFORE tightening, because getting either wrong breaks live collab:
1. Are non-owner snapshots ever legitimate? Owner saves go through republish_snapshot_for_path; a reviewer's contributions are EVENTS (comments, suggestions), not snapshots. Confirm no live-collab or agent path publishes a snapshot as a non-owner before refusing them.
2. Keep the same fail-closed fallback shape attn-lb7p used: rooms with no pinned key (v2, and v3 rooms joined before the owner key existed) must retain today's behavior rather than losing their documents.

Bound the blast radius: a wrong tightening here does not degrade an image, it makes the shared document itself refuse to render.
acceptance_criteria: A snapshot signed by a non-owner participant is rejected on the reviewer side, proven by a test that mints one from a reviewer identity — the document case, not just the manifest. Rooms with no pinned owner key keep working. No live-collab or agent flow regresses.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #17 (draft): snapshot authorship generalized beyond the manifest; wire paths mint for shares with no curated list. Verified live plus mutation-checked forgery tests.

title: Prove a reviewer hydrates, and that a forged manifest does not
description:
End-to-end coverage for the epic, because the failure it fixes was invisible from the terminal: the join reported success while the daemon logged 'workspace manifest hydration rejected' and the reviewer window quietly showed nothing.

Two surfaces:
- Rust: a v3 reviewer joining a workspace share hydrates the manifest and lists every shared file; a manifest minted and signed by a REVIEWER identity is rejected by hydrate_workspace_manifest.
- Harness: extend scripts/test-webrtc-e2e.sh or the dual-instance suite so a reviewer joining a multi-file share asserts the shared file list is non-empty, and that no 'hydration rejected' line appears in the reviewer daemon log.

The log assertion matters as much as the positive case — this bug shipped because a WARN was the only evidence and nothing failed on it.
acceptance_criteria: Both the positive and the forged-manifest cases are covered by Rust tests. The harness fails if a reviewer's daemon log contains 'workspace manifest hydration rejected' after a successful join.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #16 (commit d2e92e7): invite fragment carries the owner's public key on every tier, joiner verifies the grant locally and pins it in RoomAccessV3, manifest accepted on verify_event against the pinned key with fail-closed fallback for owners/v2. Rust<->TS fragment parity pinned by shared literals. Verified live: v3 join no longer logs 'workspace manifest hydration rejected'.

title: Reviewers receive the images a shared document references
description:
A reviewer opening a shared markdown file sees the 'Image didn't load' card for every relative image src. Correct given what is sent — src/review/share_lifecycle.rs:632 restricts a share to md/markdown/html/htm, so image bytes never leave the owner's machine — but a document arriving without its figures is a broken document.

The primitives already exist: DocType::Asset carries media_type + base64url content inside the encrypted payload (src/review/model.rs:284), WorkspaceManifestEntryKind::Asset exists, the BROWSER owner already publishes assets this way (web/src/lib/review/browser-owner-workspace-runtime.ts:1244), and Editor.svelte gained a resolveAssetUrl prop in attn-cgev that the reviewer-snapshot editor deliberately does not pass. Nothing about the relay or the crypto changes; the relay stays content-blind.

Consent decision (owner, 2026-08-27): images referenced by a SELECTED markdown file are auto-included and DISCLOSED in the Share dialog — 'images.md + 3 images referenced', expandable to per-file names and sizes, with a combined byte total. Silent inclusion was rejected: the dialog promises 'the exact files reviewers will receive' and that must stay true. Per-image ticking was rejected: forgetting one ships a broken document.
design:
Owner: for each selected markdown file, parse its image srcs, resolve each against the file's own directory (the resolveImageSrc rules from attn-cgev), and publish the ones that resolve to real regular files as DocType::Asset snapshots plus Asset manifest entries. Reviewer: build authored-src -> asset map from the manifest and pass a resolveAssetUrl to the snapshot editor that yields a blob:/data: URL.

Bounds are part of the feature, not a follow-up: an image extension allowlist, a per-asset size cap, a total-payload cap, a refusal to follow symlinks, and confinement to the share root — a markdown file can reference ../../../.ssh/id_rsa.png and must not exfiltrate it.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewer opening a shared document that references local images sees the images. The Share dialog names every extra file it will send, with sizes and a total. An src that escapes the share root, is a symlink, exceeds the size cap, or is not an allowlisted image type is not sent, and the reviewer sees the placeholder card for it.
close_reason: Implemented in PR #16 (commit 654f1d4). Owner publishes referenced images as encrypted asset snapshots with manifest entries; daemon emits a SnapshotCreated update per asset after BlobRef re-verification; reviewer resolves authored srcs against share wire paths and renders data: URLs. Verified live: reviewer decodes 96x64, 96x64, 64x64, 120x64 from tests/fixtures/images.md. Native only — hosted zeroes asset bytes by design.

title: attn review join reports success it never verified
description:
run_join_via_daemon (src/cli_review.rs:501) writes the invite to the daemon socket and, on a successful WRITE, prints 'join request sent to the running attn daemon' and exits 0. The daemon parses and acts on the invite asynchronously, so every failure after the write is invisible: a rejected grant, a room the daemon cannot hydrate, a relay with no such room.

The comment at line 476 already documents this for malformed invites (which is why validate_invite_for_join exists). The same silence covers joins the daemon accepts and then fails.

Observed 2026-08-27: the CLI printed success and exit 0 while /tmp/attn-collab-reviewer/attn.log recorded 'workspace manifest hydration rejected: load room secret ... No such file or directory' and 'reannounce into room ... failed'. The user had no way to know from the terminal that the join had not taken.
acceptance_criteria: A join that the daemon fails to complete is reported as a failure by the CLI with a non-zero exit, within a bounded timeout; the success line is printed only once the daemon confirms it joined the room.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #16 (commit 13a4aee): port guard + EADDRINUSE detection in start_relay, ReviewJoinWait so the join CLI reports real outcomes, invite retry loop.

title: dev-collab start_relay mistakes a foreign relay for its own
description:
start_relay in scripts/dev-collab.sh waits for GET /health to return 200 on port 8787. Any process already bound to that port answers it, so when the harness's own `wrangler dev` dies with EADDRINUSE the script still concludes its relay is healthy and continues.

Observed 2026-08-27: a stray relay from another session held 8787. The harness relay logged 'Fatal uncaught kj::Exception: ::bind(): Address already in use; 127.0.0.1:8787' and 'The Workers runtime failed to start', but the script proceeded. Both daemons then used the foreign relay, whose Durable Object state knew nothing of their rooms — producing a 409 on reviewer device registration and a missing <room>.secret. The visible symptom was 'the reviewer window never opens the shared doc', which points nowhere near a port clash.
acceptance_criteria: start_relay fails loudly when its own wrangler child exits or when 8787 is already bound by a process the script did not start; the health probe alone can no longer satisfy it.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #16 (commit 13a4aee): port guard + EADDRINUSE detection in start_relay, ReviewJoinWait so the join CLI reports real outcomes, invite retry loop.

title: file-drop: reject on readEntries/entry.file errors instead of importing a partial tree
description: web/src/hosted/app/file-drop.ts ~L90: readAllEntries maps the readEntries error callback to resolve([]), which is indistinguishable from end-of-directory. A failure after the first batch returns the accumulated subset, readDroppedFiles resolves normally, and the drop handler calls onFiles with an incomplete tree — the exact silent-truncation failure the module header says it exists to prevent. Same class of bug at entryFile (~L80): entry.file() errors resolve null and the file is silently skipped.
design: Make readAllEntries reject on the error callback (wrap the DOMException in an Error with a user-facing message consistent with DropLimitError copy: 'Nothing was imported'). Make entryFile reject likewise, or at minimum count skipped files and reject if any were skipped. walkEntry already propagates throws; readDroppedFiles then rejects and fileDrop's onDrop routes to opts.onError. Keep the no-entries-API fallback path unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: New cases in web/src/hosted/app/file-drop.test.ts: (1) readEntries errors after one successful batch → onError called, onFiles not called; (2) entry.file() error → onError, onFiles not called; existing DropLimitError tests still pass. Module header comment stays true.
close_reason: Fixed: readAllEntries and entryFile now reject with a new DropReadError instead of resolving empty/null, so a partial walk reaches onError rather than importing a truncated tree. file-drop.test.ts +4 cases including the full drop-surface path; verified A/B (old behaviour imports 1 of 2 files and reports success).

title: Surface failed lazy EditorShell chunk loads instead of hanging on the Opening spinner
description: web/src/hosted/app/AppShell.svelte ~L222: loadEditorShell() chains .then().finally() on the dynamic import('./EditorShell.svelte') with no rejection handler. If the chunk fetch fails (stale deployment cache, offline, 404 after a redeploy), EditorShell stays undefined, editorShellPending resets to false, and nothing re-triggers the $effect (it only depends on editorMode). The user sits on the 'Opening {name}' LoadingLine forever with an unhandled rejection in the console.
design: Add a .catch that routes to the existing error surface: set phase = 'error' (see the existing handler around L200) with a message that offers reload, or attempt one reload-on-chunk-failure (common SPA pattern for stale hashed chunks). Keep editorShellPending semantics so a later editorMode change can retry. Decide whether retry should be manual (button) or automatic (one reload guarded by a sessionStorage flag to avoid loops).
acceptance_criteria: Simulated import rejection (mock the dynamic import in a vitest) leaves the app on the error/retry surface, not the spinner. No unhandled rejection. Retry path re-invokes loadEditorShell and succeeds when the import resolves.
close_reason: Fixed: loadEditorShell now has a .catch. One automatic reload (chunk-reload.ts, sessionStorage-guarded, ceiling of one), then a dedicated error surface — 'The editor didn't finish loading' — with Reload attn / Go to your desk and a collapsed technical detail. Tests: chunk-reload.test.ts (6 cases, incl. no-storage never reloads) + e2e in hosted-shells.spec.ts aborting the EditorShell chunk in both dev and built shapes, asserting exactly 2 fetch attempts. Verified A/B: original code hangs on the spinner past 20s.

title: Codex branch review follow-ups: drop integrity, editor-chunk recovery, stale join intent, hover after re-render
description: Four confirmed findings from the Codex review of branch angus/comment-card-redesign against main (2026-08-20). All verified against the code; none are false positives. Ranked: editor-chunk recovery first (user-visible hang), drop integrity second (contract violation in a module written to prevent exactly this), the remaining two are polish.
acceptance_criteria: All four child tasks closed; web unit tests pass (cd web && npm test); no unhandled rejections from the lazy editor path; file-drop tests cover the readEntries error path.
close_reason: All four children closed. web: 134 unit test files green, svelte-check 0 errors, route-bundle gate clean, hosted-shells e2e 26/26. Four pre-existing failures elsewhere in the routes suite (hosted-offline manifest, 2x hosted-share-sheet, landing-review-demo) were confirmed identical on stashed baseline — not caused by this work.

title: Invalidate pending beginEditing session when workspace changes in place
description: web/src/hosted/app/AppShell.svelte ~633-640 / EditorShell ownerSessionOpening. Desktop in-place navigation keeps the same EditorShell; ownerSessionOpening is neither cancelled nor tagged with a workspace id, so selecting B while beginEditing(A) is pending lets A's promise resolve and install A's runtime/session into B. Autosave then commits B's active path through A's session. Fix: tag the acquisition with the workspace id (or a generation counter) and discard/close the result if the workspace changed before it resolved; start a fresh beginEditing(B).
acceptance_criteria: Switching workspace while beginEditing is pending never installs the previous workspace's session; autosave targets the correct workspace; test covers the race.
close_reason: Fixed on angus/comment-card-redesign. .1: import pipeline extracted to web/src/hosted/app/import-into-workspace.ts — workspace id is a parameter, live reads (placeholder/name/navigation) gated on still-on-screen; 5 unit cases. .2: acquisition tagged with its workspace in owner-session-gate.ts, stale grants discarded and their runtime closed; 6 unit cases. .3: BrowserWorkspaceService.closeOwnerRuntime + WorkspaceAppService.closeEditingRuntime, called from EditorShell's workspace teardown; 2 service tests (lease handed back, no runtime accumulation). .4: review-counts folds lifecycle last-writer-wins via the exported compareEventKeys, cross-checked against reconstructThreads in 5 new cases. .5: the folder walk throws DropLimitError past the file/depth ceilings; drop surfaces show it (FileDropOptions.onError is required); 4 cases.

title: Import continuation must capture workspace id before awaiting storage
description: web/src/hosted/app/EditorShell.svelte ~865-870. A folder/zip import into workspace A awaits storage; if the user switches to B before it resolves, the continuation reads the now-current workspace.id (B) while 'placeholder' was computed for A. It deletes B's untitled.md, then renames/refreshes B. Fix: capture the workspace id at import start, and after each await bail out if it is no longer the active workspace (or route the remaining work to the captured id only). Add a test that switches workspace mid-import.
acceptance_criteria: Mid-import workspace switch never deletes/renames files in the newly active workspace; regression test covers it.
close_reason: Fixed on angus/comment-card-redesign. .1: import pipeline extracted to web/src/hosted/app/import-into-workspace.ts — workspace id is a parameter, live reads (placeholder/name/navigation) gated on still-on-screen; 5 unit cases. .2: acquisition tagged with its workspace in owner-session-gate.ts, stale grants discarded and their runtime closed; 6 unit cases. .3: BrowserWorkspaceService.closeOwnerRuntime + WorkspaceAppService.closeEditingRuntime, called from EditorShell's workspace teardown; 2 service tests (lease handed back, no runtime accumulation). .4: review-counts folds lifecycle last-writer-wins via the exported compareEventKeys, cross-checked against reconstructThreads in 5 new cases. .5: the folder walk throws DropLimitError past the file/depth ceilings; drop surfaces show it (FileDropOptions.onError is required); 4 cases.

title: Codex review fixes: workspace-switch isolation, reopen counts, folder-drop limits (angus/comment-card-redesign)
description:
Codex review of branch angus/comment-card-redesign against main (2026-08-20) surfaced five defects. Two P1s: in-place workspace switching lets a pending folder/zip import or a pending beginEditing() continuation from workspace A land on workspace B (deleting/renaming B's files, or installing A's runtime into B so autosave commits B through A's session). Three P2s: the departed workspace's owner runtime (lease, heartbeat, collab hub, review transport) is never released on switch; review-counts.ts folds comment_resolved/comment_reopened by arrival order instead of last-writer-wins, so the Desk openComments count disagrees with reconstructThreads; and file-drop.ts returns a silently truncated list when a dropped folder exceeds 5000 files / depth 24 and the import reports success.

Done when: all five child issues closed, npm --prefix web run check passes (it currently exits 1 on this branch — fix as part of this epic if the failure is in touched files), and a manual test of switching workspaces mid-import / mid-open no longer cross-contaminates.
acceptance_criteria: All child issues closed; web check passes; workspace switch mid-import and mid-beginEditing verified isolated; review-counts has a unit test for out-of-order resolve/reopen; folder drop over limits aborts with a visible error.
close_reason: All five children fixed and closed. Gates: npm --prefix web run check = 0 errors (it was already green at branch HEAD — the reported exit 1 no longer reproduces); npm --prefix web test = 132 files, 0 failures (including the 4 new/extended unit suites); npm run build:browser + check:route-bundles clean; routes e2e 105 passed / 4 failed, all four pre-existing and unrelated (filed as attn-cx3z, attn-ius0, attn-s662). Manual verification is now a spec: e2e/hosted-workspace-switch.spec.ts drives real in-place switching in the real app (each workspace keeps its own text across A->B->A and reloads; a workspace this tab left is writable from a second tab), stable over 3 repeats.

title: [P1] Cancel pending in-workspace file reads when navigate() switches workspace
description:
Where: web/src/hosted/app/AppShell.svelte — `applyEntry` (209-229) vs `navigate`/`openWorkspaceRoute` (239-335).

Bug: `applyEntry` guards only against newer `applyEntry` calls via `applyGeneration`. `navigate` bumps `navGeneration` but never touches `applyGeneration`. Sequence: user selects file X in workspace A (read in flight, captured `detail.id === A`) → clicks workspace B in the sidebar/desk/palette → `openWorkspaceRoute` resolves first and sets `detail=B`, `activePath`, `bodyText`, route, URL → A's read resolves, passes its stale generation check, and overwrites `activePath`/`bodyText`/`route`/URL with A's path and A's content while `detail` is B. The URL now reads /app/w/B/<A-path>, the editor shows A's content, and the next autosave writes A's body into workspace B at a path that may not exist there.

Fix: unify the two generation counters (or have `navigate` also `++applyGeneration`), and additionally capture `const workspaceId = detail.id` at the top of `applyEntry` and bail if `detail?.id !== workspaceId` after the await — generation alone is the mechanism, the id check is the invariant stated in code. Audit the other await-then-mutate sites in AppShell (line ~142/153 bootstrap replaceState, 409 rename path) for the same hazard and apply the same guard where a workspace switch can interleave. Consider extracting a tiny pure helper (e.g. `web/src/hosted/app/navigation-guard.ts`) so the race is unit-testable without mounting the component.

Tests: vitest with a controllable `service.readBodyText` (deferred promises): start applyEntry(A,x), then navigate to B, resolve A's read → assert state/URL remain B's. Add alongside web/src/hosted/app/workspace-service.test.ts or a new navigation test file.
acceptance_criteria: Stale file read from a previous workspace never mutates activePath/bodyText/route/history after a workspace switch (unit test with deferred reads). Rapid same-workspace selection ordering still correct (existing behaviour). No autosave can target workspace B with workspace A's body.
close_reason: Unified transition counter in web/src/hosted/app/navigation-guard.ts (begin/current/isCurrent) + workspace-identity invariant via canApplyWorkspaceRead. Applied to applyEntry, navigate, openWorkspaceRoute, load, createAndOpen, onWorkspaceChanged, refreshActiveBody. 6 regression cases in navigation-guard.test.ts; confirmed the pre-fix logic fails case 1.

title: [P1] Restrict Unresolve to comment-rooted threads — accepted/rejected suggestions must stay terminal
description:
Where: web/src/lib/ReviewMargin.svelte:1199-1220 (expanded-resolved branch) and web/src/lib/ReviewMarginCard.svelte:616-622 (Unresolve button renders whenever `onUnresolve` is passed).

Bug: `stateFor(t)==='resolved'` is true for suggestion threads that were accepted or rejected (their terminal events are recorded via `noteLifecycle(suggestionId, …)` in web/src/lib/review/selectors.ts:171-180). The expanded-resolved card passes `onUnresolve` unconditionally, so clicking Unresolve on a decided suggestion calls `unresolveThread(t.id)` → mints `comment_reopened { threadId: <suggestionId> }`. In `reconstructThreads`, `isClosedByLifecycle` treats the latest lifecycle event as the winner, so the reopen beats the accept/reject and the suggestion reappears as live with accept/reject actions (and `restoreThreadLocally` does the same optimistically). selectors.ts:178 already documents the intent: 'only comment threads can reopen'.

Fix (layered — do all three):
1. UI: in ReviewMargin.svelte only pass `onUnresolve` when `kindFor(t) === 'comment'` (i.e. root event is `comment_created`). ReviewMarginCard then naturally hides the button. Check the collapsed-rail / gutter chip paths too — grep for every `onUnresolve=` and `unresolveThread(` call site and gate each.
2. Store/selectors: make `noteLifecycle` (or `isClosedByLifecycle`) ignore a `comment_reopened` whose threadId refers to a thread rooted by `suggestion_created`, so a stray/replayed event from an old client or a peer can't resurrect a terminal suggestion in passive tabs either. Also guard `reviewStore.restoreThreadLocally`.
3. Backend (defense in depth): in `reopen_comment` (src/review/manager.rs:1908) and the browser-owner equivalent (grep `comment_reopened` / `reopenComment` under web/src/lib/review/browser-*.ts), reject the command with an ATTN_REOPEN_COMMENT error when the thread id belongs to a suggestion. Keep this cheap — if thread lookup isn't available at that layer, note it and rely on 1+2.

Tests: add cases to web/src/lib/review/selectors.test.ts (suggestion_accepted followed by comment_reopened on the same id → thread stays closed, kind suggestion) and to margin-integration.test.ts or a component test (expanded-resolved suggestion card has no data-testid=review-margin-card-unresolve; resolved comment card still has it).
acceptance_criteria: Unresolve button absent on accepted/rejected suggestion cards in every rail state; present on resolved comment cards. `comment_reopened` targeting a suggestion id is a no-op in `reconstructThreads` (test). Rust/browser reopen path rejects suggestion ids or the task notes why not. Existing Unresolve-on-comment E2E/unit tests still pass.
close_reason: UI gate (ReviewMargin canUnresolve + ReviewMarginCard kind check), projection drop in reconstructThreads + review-counts, and a durable Rust guard (ReviewStore::is_suggestion_thread wired into reopen_comment). Browser owner has no event-log access at the authoring layer, so the projection drop is its durable half. Tests: 5 new selectors cases, 2 review-counts cases, 2 Rust store cases.

title: Codex review follow-ups: review lifecycle + hosted /app navigation fixes (branch angus/comment-card-redesign)
description:
Address all four findings from the Codex review of angus/comment-card-redesign vs main (2026-08-20). Two P1 regressions (terminal suggestions can be reactivated via Unresolve; cross-workspace file-read race) and two P2 hosted /app correctness gaps (unencoded route segments; Enter shortcut hijacks focused controls).

Each child task is independently shippable. Every fix must land with a regression test (vitest) — none of the four bugs is currently covered.

close_reason: All four findings fixed and verified. web: 130 test files 0 failures, svelte-check 0 errors, both builds green. rust: 563 lib tests pass, clippy clean. Review E2E unchanged vs baseline (43 PASS / 4 PEND / 13 pre-existing FAIL). Changes are uncommitted on angus/comment-card-redesign pending review; codex re-review of the criterion needs a commit first.

title: Blank route: invitation resurrected itself a second after typing; rail missing
description:
REPORTED 2026-08-20 after attn-rjuo landed, with screenshots: 'start a blank untitled.md' showed the Open-a-document invitation ON TOP of already-typed text, with no file rail — while the import route was correct.

TWO STATE RESETS, both fired by the same-workspace refresh that follows every autosave commit:

1. createIntent. AppShell clears it beside isNewDraft on the refresh path (AppShell ~L405), so a second after the first keystroke the blank route stopped being 'blank' and showCanvasInvite went true. FIX: EditorShell reads the DURABLE origin (readWorkspaceOrigin, persisted at create time by attn-rjuo.1.2) instead of the prop; the prop stays as the same-session fallback for browsers that refuse localStorage.

2. canvasInviteEdited. It was a boolean reset by an $effect keyed on activeEntry?.path. That effect re-ran whenever activeEntry RECOMPUTED — the derived produces a new object for the same path each time AppShell hands down a fresh workspace — so the answered latch cleared and the invitation reappeared over live typing. FIX: hold the answered PATH and derive the flag, so the reset is structural and no effect can undo it.

RULING REFINED: the rail is hidden exactly while the invitation is up. Two states, not three — the import route is the invitation screen and drops the rail, the blank route is an ordinary editor and keeps it (rail, file row, Add files, from the first frame). This retired the sticky per-workspace flag that had to guess when a bare workspace stopped being bare. No mid-word jump remains, because the invitation withdraws on pointer-down, so a click restores the rail before the first character.
notes:
Verified 2026-08-20 at 1440 dark, dev server:

CASE2 on arrival      | invite: 0 | rail: 1 | rows: [untitled.md] | addfiles: 1
CASE2 after typing+4s | invite: 0 | rail: 1 | rows: [untitled.md] | addfiles: 1   (past the autosave refresh that used to resurrect it)
CASE2 after reload    | invite: 0 | rail: 1 | rows: [untitled.md] | addfiles: 1
CASE1 on arrival      | invite: 1 | rail: 0 | rows: []            | addfiles: 0
CASE1 after import    | invite: 0 | rail: 1 | rows: [brief.md]    | addfiles: 1
EDGE type-on-import   | invite: 0 | rail: 1 | rows: [untitled.md] | addfiles: 1

Case 2 now matches the screenshot the user asked for; case 1 is untouched. Suites: 67/67 hosted, 128 unit files, chrome-dialect, bundle guards, and 105 passed on the built worker with only the 4 pre-existing failures (attn-gccz).
close_reason: Closed

title: Drop the untouched empty placeholder when an import supersedes it
description:
In the shared import path (EditorShell.importFiles, ~L740, used by invitation pickers, canvas drop, sidebar Add files, palette), after addAssetFiles succeeds: if the workspace held exactly the placeholder before the import — one entry, untitled.md, empty body, no pending autosave text (drain first, same as export does) — delete it via the existing entry-delete service call, then navigate to the imported doc as today.

GUARDS: never delete when body text or pending edits are non-empty; never delete when the import itself contains untitled.md (the import wins the name — dedupe or replace, do not double); a failed import leaves the placeholder untouched. Prefer this post-import removal over not creating the file up front: an editable file on arrival is what keeps the type-through path and the caret alive.

ALSO: when the superseded workspace is still auto-named 'Untitled', adopt the import's name (importName/prepareImport already compute it on the desk path — reuse, don't fork).
acceptance_criteria: Import-first flow ends with only imported files in the tree; typed-in or non-empty untitled.md always survives; failed import changes nothing; 'Untitled' workspace takes the import name
notes:
Two bugs found in verification, both fixed:
1. The emptiness guard read collabSeed.markdown — the text the editor was HANDED at mount, which for a local workspace is '' and stays '' however much you type. It would have called every placeholder untouched and deleted real work. Now asks editorRef.getMarkdown() for the live document, with the seed chain only as the pre-editor fallback.
2. The palette's 'Add files to this workspace' clicked assetInput, which was bound inside the rail footer and the invitation — both unmounted on a bare typed-into workspace, so the command silently did nothing. One pair of pickers now mounts at the component root and every affordance clicks it (also retires the double-binding hazard the old comments warned about).
close_reason: Closed

title: Import into a bare workspace leaves a stray empty untitled.md
description:
REPRO: desk → 'Import files' → choose slack-acceptance.md. The tree now lists slack-acceptance.md AND untitled.md — an empty placeholder the user never asked for. Screenshot 2026-08-20.

ROOT CAUSE (verified): both desk routes mint the workspace via createAndOpen → service.createWorkspace(), which always creates untitled.md; the subsequent import (EditorShell.importFiles → service.addAssetFiles) only ADDS. The placeholder survives every import route: the invitation's Choose files / Choose folder, a canvas drop, the sidebar's Add files, ⌘K → add.

TARGET: an import that supersedes an untouched empty placeholder removes it in the same operation. The rule is written once, on the import path, so all five routes inherit it. A blank-intent workspace (explicitly requested untitled.md) is untouched by imports arriving LATER only if the file has content or edits — emptiness+untouched is the guard, not intent. Never delete a file with content.
close_reason: Closed

title: Inline the rename input at the picker trigger's position in the owner header
description:
In HostedDesktopWorkspaceFrame's header, when a rename is in flight the [data-slot=owner-doc-name] / picker-trigger slot renders an input instead of the trigger: same geometry (min-w-0 shrink, truncation bounds), header type step, on-plane colours (the accent header re-points tokens — a raw input here rendered near-black on terracotta/steel, which is the reported frame). Wire it to the existing renamingTitle/titleValue/commitTitleRename state in EditorShell — likely by lifting the rename UI into the frame via a snippet or callback prop, since the state owner and the name's position are currently in different components.

Remove the .hosted-title-input placement from desktopHeaderActions (~L3256). Escape restores focus to the trigger (focusSidebarAnchor('.owner-project-trigger') already targets it). Reconcile the mobile masthead rename (~L3512) to the same component/treatment so there is ONE inline-rename, not two.
acceptance_criteria: Rename input appears where the name was, styled for the plane; Enter/Escape/blur semantics unchanged; no input in the actions cluster; mobile and desktop share the treatment
notes: Mobile already renamed in place (.doc-name swaps .mobile-workspace-title for .mobile-title-input); only desktop was detached. The two now share the behaviour but keep separate classes deliberately — the mobile masthead is on the paper plane and the owner header on the accent plane, so one class cannot serve both.
close_reason: Closed

title: Workspace rename must edit the name in place, not open a floating input
description:
REPRO: picker menu → 'Rename workspace' (or ⌘K → rename). An unstyled dark input appears at the RIGHT edge of the header, in the actions cluster next to Share — detached from the name it renames, wrong plane (raw input colours on the accent header), and reads as a rendering bug. Screenshot 2026-08-20.

ROOT CAUSE (verified): the desktop rename renders {#if renamingTitle} <input class='hosted-title-input'> inside the desktopHeaderActions snippet (EditorShell.svelte ~L3256) — a leftover from when workspace identity lived in the sidebar project row. The name itself now lives at the header's left as the ProjectPicker trigger (moved 2026-08-20), so the input edits a name that is nowhere near it.

TARGET: renaming swaps the name AT ITS OWN POSITION for an input — same spot, same type step (--text-meta, sans, 500), accent-plane styling — Enter commits, Escape cancels, focus returns to the trigger. The mobile masthead variant (~L3512) already inlines over the title; align both on one treatment.
close_reason: Closed

title: Ruling: what chrome frames the bare canvas while the invitation is up
description:
Two 2026-08-20 rulings now collide: 'remove the nav entirely when no file/folder has been selected' (the rail is dropped whole on a bare workspace) versus the same-day report 'there is no sidebar nav like there used to be here' filed as part of 'the untitled experience is broken'.

Today: rail hidden while bare AND after the first keystroke (sticky per workspace id — deliberate, to avoid a mid-word 248px document jump); it returns only when a second file lands.

Options to rule on:
(a) Status quo, sold better: keep the rail out until a second file exists; the invitation fix (attn-rjuo.1 siblings) may be what actually cures the 'broken' read.
(b) Rail returns on commitment: first keystroke/caret placement schedules the rail's return at a non-jarring moment (idle, blur, or animated slide) so the typing surface regains its nav without the mid-word jump.
(c) Rail always mounts, with a purpose-built bare state (no filter, no list, picker gone to the header already) — nav presence constant, content honest.

Blocks the implementation task; record the ruling here.
acceptance_criteria: One option chosen and recorded; implementation task unblocked
notes:
RULING (2026-08-20): option (a) — the rail stays out until a second file exists.

Reasoning. The nav's absence was ruled twice today and in plain terms ('I don't even think we should see this nav when a file/folder hasn't been uploaded'; 'remove the nav entirely when no file/folder has been selected'). The report that reopened it lists three symptoms of one screen — a couple of seconds of nothing, then a pop-in, and no rail — and only the first two are defects. A bare workspace genuinely has nothing to navigate: a filter over one row, and that row is the document already open.

What actually made the screen read as broken is the arrival, not the missing rail: the invitation was nested inside the lazily-loaded editor chunk, so the first paint was a lone caret on black for the length of a dynamic import. Fix that (attn-rjuo.1.1) and the caret/overlay overlap (attn-rjuo.1.3) and the screen is meaningful from the first frame.

Option (c) — always mount the rail with a bare state — is the fallback if the complaint survives an instant arrival. It is a one-line flip of hideFileRail plus the bare-state markup, so it stays cheap to reverse.

Option (b) — return the rail on commitment — is rejected outright: every variant of it moves the document sideways while a caret is live, which is the defect the sticky flag exists to prevent.
close_reason: Closed

title: Withdraw the invitation on pointer-down into the canvas, not only on the first keystroke
description:
Click-through currently places a caret while the invitation stays centred (it withdraws on doc change only — noteCanvasEdited via the change watcher). A person who clicked the canvas has answered the invitation; the overlay lingering over their caret is the 'broken' frame in the report.

Withdraw on pointer-down that lands in the ProseMirror (not on the invite's own buttons), same one-way latch as typing. Keyboard path: focusing the editor and typing already withdraws; make plain focus-by-click sufficient.

ACCEPTANCE: click empty canvas → invitation gone, caret where you clicked, before any keystroke. Clicking Choose files/folder does NOT withdraw it. Update e2e 'the bare canvas invitation withdraws on the first keystroke' to cover both withdrawal triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Pointer-down in canvas withdraws invite; invite buttons do not; e2e updated
close_reason: Closed

title: Persist create-intent so a blank workspace stays blank across reload
description:
createIntent lives in AppShell component state; F5 loses it, so an explicitly blank workspace re-greets its owner with the import invitation. Persist the intent where the workspace already lives (workspace-service metadata written at createWorkspace time, e.g. origin: 'blank' | 'import'), read it on load, and thread it to EditorShell in place of the session value. Session value stays as the same-session fast path.

Default for workspaces that predate the field: bare + unknown origin → invitation (import-first ruling). The mock service needs the same field so ?shell= scenarios stay honest.

ACCEPTANCE: desk → 'start a blank untitled.md' → reload: still a plain blank editor, no invitation. Desk → 'Import files' → reload before importing: invitation still there.
acceptance_criteria: Blank survives reload with no invitation; import-intent survives reload with invitation; mock + real service agree
close_reason: Closed

title: Render the canvas invitation without waiting for the editor chunk
description:
Move the invitation out of the {#if EditorComponent} branch (EditorShell.svelte ~L3108-3160) so it mounts with the shell: render it whenever showCanvasInvite holds, alongside the 'Opening editor…' placeholder branch rather than inside the loaded-editor branch. The overlay is static DOM + two pickers; it needs no ProseMirror.

Keep: pointer-transparency except the buttons; the suppressed-placeholder rule in app-shell.css (:has(.canvas-invite)) must still match in the pre-editor state — verify the selector's ancestor exists before the editor mounts.

ACCEPTANCE: throttled to Slow 3G, a bare workspace shows the invitation before the editor chunk resolves; no frame shows the bare caret alone; once the editor mounts, click-through and typing behave exactly as today.
acceptance_criteria: Invitation visible pre-editor-chunk on slow network; no caret-only frame; existing invite e2e still green
close_reason: Closed

title: Bare-workspace arrival: invitation renders late and the wait reads as a hang
description:
REPRO: desk → 'Import files' (or /app#new, or reload a bare workspace URL). The canvas shows a bare blinking caret at the top-left for roughly the editor-chunk load time; the 'Open a document' invitation then pops in. Screenshot 2026-08-20 22:0x.

ROOT CAUSES (verified):
- The invitation markup is nested inside {#if activeEntry?.presentation === 'editable' && EditorComponent} (EditorShell.svelte ~L3108), so a pure-DOM overlay that needs nothing from ProseMirror waits for the lazily imported editor chunk (Editor.svelte + prosemirror-state + decorations).
- createIntent ('blank' | 'import') is session memory in AppShell; a reload of the same workspace URL arrives with intent undefined, so even an explicitly-blank workspace greets its owner with the invitation again.
- While the invite is up, a click into the canvas places a caret under the overlay (click-through is intended) but the invitation only withdraws on the first DOC CHANGE — so caret + centred invite coexist, which is the exact frame the report calls broken.

ACCEPTANCE: a bare workspace's first paint after the shell mounts already shows the invitation (no editor-chunk wait, no caret-only frame); an explicitly blank workspace never shows it, including after reload; caret and invitation are never on screen together.
close_reason: Closed

title: First-run workspace flows: bare-canvas arrival, in-place rename, clean import
description:
Three user reports (2026-08-20, screenshots) against the new bare-workspace experience shipped on angus/comment-card-redesign:

1. The untitled experience reads broken: a bare workspace paints a lone caret for a couple of seconds before the 'Open a document' invitation appears, and the chrome around it (no rail, nothing to anchor the wait) makes the delay read as a hang.
2. Workspace rename opens a floating unstyled dark input at the right edge of the header, detached from the name it renames. Renaming should edit the name in place.
3. Choosing import first still leaves an empty untitled.md beside the imported files — a placeholder the user never asked for and now has to delete.

INVARIANTS this epic restores (rulings 2026-08-20):
- Import-first: the default offer on any bare surface is bringing a document in; a blank untitled.md happens only on explicit request.
- A blank page requested in so many words STAYS blank — no invitation over it, on arrival or on reload.
- No stray files: the untitled.md placeholder never survives an import that supersedes it.
- The chrome is coherent in every state: nothing unstyled, nothing floating detached from what it edits, no seconds of unexplained blank.

Fix surfaces: web/src/hosted/app/EditorShell.svelte, AppShell.svelte, DeskHome.svelte, HostedDesktopWorkspaceFrame.svelte, workspace-service.ts, app-shell.css; e2e in web/e2e/hosted-{shells,authoring,a11y}.spec.ts.
close_reason: Closed

title: Sidebar lost the standing drag-and-drop space (only a text button remained)
description:
Owner: "we used to have a space to drag and drop here", with a screenshot of the sidebar footer showing only a small "+ Add files" text button.

MY REGRESSION, one step removed. attn-08fa.12 deleted the standing drop box entirely; attn-mkmz.3 restored the click path but restored it as a LABEL. A word is not a target you can aim a drag at, so the rail still had no place that said "things go here" — the affordance was back and the space was not.

FIXED: the resting control is a dashed well again — 74px, glyph over "Add files" over "or drop them here". Still exactly one `<button>`, so the keyboard path is one Tab stop and the pointer path is one click; the box is simply the size and shape of the target.

The drag state now occupies the SAME box: identical height, padding and radius, so arming the target changes only its edge and fill. Nothing shifts under a cursor that is already mid-drag, which is the one moment a layout jump costs the user the drop.

VERIFIED both themes: resting well 74x232, drag state identical, e2e drop test passing against the resting button.
close_reason: Closed

title: Two Vite dev servers shared one dep-optimizer cache and corrupted each other
description:
Two Vite dev servers shared one dependency-optimizer cache, so starting the second one broke the first.

SYMPTOM (owner-reported): the browser app 500s on every import with
  The file does not exist at "web/node_modules/.vite/deps/chunk-RIHC7GL6.js?v=8872dd31"
  which is in the optimize deps directory. The dependency might be incompatible
  with the dep optimizer. Try adding it to `optimizeDeps.exclude`.

The suggestion in that message is a red herring — no dependency is incompatible with anything.

CAUSE: neither vite.config.ts (native frontend, `task dev` / `npm run dev`) nor vite.browser.config.ts (hosted app, `npm run dev:browser`) set `cacheDir`, so both defaulted to `web/node_modules/.vite/deps`. They describe different apps — different entries, different plugins (viteSingleFile only on native), different `optimizeDeps.include` — so each server re-optimizes on startup and rewrites the prebundled chunk hashes. Whichever started second replaced the chunk files the first server's already-loaded page still referenced by name, and every subsequent import 500'd. A `.vite-temp` directory was left behind from the interrupted swap.

Reproduced exactly: it happened while running the hosted server on 5173 and the native server on 5199 together to verify attn-mkmz.8 on both surfaces.

FIX: each config gets its own cache directory — `node_modules/.vite/native` and `node_modules/.vite/browser`. Running the two side by side is an ordinary thing to do (CLAUDE.md documents both commands, and the two surfaces are meant to be compared), so the answer is separate caches rather than a rule against it.

Recovery for anyone who hits the stale state on an older checkout: stop the dev servers, `rm -rf web/node_modules/.vite web/node_modules/.vite-temp`, restart. No reinstall needed.

VERIFIED: both servers up simultaneously; hosted desk, hosted editor, hosted landing and the native frontend all return 200, mount, and log zero console errors and zero 4xx/5xx. svelte-check 0/0; npm test 126/0; `npm run build` and `npm run build:browser` both green; check-route-bundles clean. The web unit tests are tsx child processes rather than vitest, so nothing else was reading that directory.
acceptance_criteria: vite.config.ts and vite.browser.config.ts have distinct cacheDir values; both dev servers run concurrently with all surfaces loading error-free; builds and gates green.
close_reason: Fixed: distinct cacheDir per config (node_modules/.vite/native and /browser). Verified both dev servers running concurrently with all four surfaces error-free; svelte-check, npm test, both builds and route-bundles green.

title: Four pre-existing e2e failures in the hosted routes suite
description:
Four Playwright specs in `playwright.routes.config.ts` fail on this branch for reasons unrelated to attn-mkmz. Found while running that suite as part of the attn-mkmz repair (94 passed, 7 failed; 3 of the 7 traced to attn-08fa and were fixed there). These four did not, and each needs a decision rather than a mechanical selector update.

1. **e2e/landing-review-demo.spec.ts:36 — a real WCAG failure, not a stale assertion.**
   axe reports `color-contrast`, impact "serious", on `span[data-author-kind="reviewer"]` in the landing review demo. That attribute comes from the comment-card redesign (e787653) on this branch, so the reviewer attribution line is shipping below AA. This is the only one of the four that is a live defect rather than a test lagging the code — treat it as P1 and fix the colour, not the test.

2. **e2e/hosted-offline.spec.ts:61 — manifest 404.**
   `manifest describes an installable standalone app` gets 404 instead of 200 for the webmanifest under `wrangler dev` against `dist-browser`. Either the build stopped emitting it or the worker stopped routing it; find out which before touching the test.

3. **e2e/hosted-share-sheet.spec.ts:30** expects the Advanced summary to contain "Hybrid delivery"; it now reads "Advanced settings · Live + resumable".

4. **e2e/hosted-share-sheet.spec.ts:48** expects "Select at least one Markdown file"; it now reads "Select at least one Markdown or HTML document to create a review." — the HTML half arrived with attn-61t.

3 and 4 look like deliberate copy changes the specs never followed, but confirm that against the commits that made them before rewriting the assertions: a test asserting the OLD words is the only remaining record that the words changed.

Fixed in attn-mkmz and NOT part of this issue, listed so nobody re-finds them: the `.local-badge` "View-only" → "Storage blocked" assertion (attn-08fa.8) and two landing theme-toggle assertions that still expected a two-state "Switch to dark theme" control after attn-08fa made it a three-state Paper/Ink/System cycle.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the four is either fixed or explicitly closed with a reason; the reviewer-attribution contrast failure is fixed in the design, not silenced in the test; playwright.routes.config.ts runs clean.

title: Loading states: centre them and bring them into sync
description:
Owner: 'loading states are out of sync and not centered.' Reported alongside the header/sidebar issues in the hosted /app editor.

Two distinct defects to reproduce and fix:
(1) NOT CENTRED — a loading indicator is not optically centred in the region it covers. Identify which surface: AppShell's phase==='loading' desk/editor state, the EditorShell chunk-loading window (EditorShell is dynamically imported), and the workspace-body read each have their own.
(2) OUT OF SYNC — several regions resolve at different times, so the shell, the sidebar and the document area appear to load in visible stages rather than as one. AppShell.load() awaits getWorkspace, then readBodyText, then listWorkspaces, while the EditorShell chunk is fetched in parallel via a separate  — so the sidebar can be populated while the editor is still a blank region, or vice versa.

Reproduce with a throttled network profile before changing anything; a stage that is invisible on a fast local server is exactly what the owner is seeing. Decide whether the surfaces should resolve together (one gate) or stagger deliberately with a shared skeleton — either is defensible, but it must be a decision.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduced under throttling with before/after captures; the loading indicator is centred in its region; the editor route presents ONE coherent loading story rather than independently-resolving areas; no layout shift when the real content arrives; both themes.
notes:
FIXED — both defects, and they turned out to be one story.

NOT CENTRED: AppShell's two loading branches each rendered `<main class="desk">` with a left-aligned `.eyebrow` at the top of the page. So the indicator sat in the top-left corner of a region it was standing in for, and — worse — opening a DOCUMENT drew a desk-shaped page first and then snapped to a three-column editor.

OUT OF SYNC: a single wait crossed up to three different treatments in sequence — that left-aligned desk eyebrow, then `.hosted-shell-loading` (centred, but 0.85rem MONO), then `.hosted-editor-loading` (600-weight sans, left-aligned inside the content column). Three materials, three positions, one wait.

Resolved by making them one surface rather than by adding a gate. `.app-loading` and `.hosted-shell-loading` now share one rule — centred, `--muted-foreground`, 500/0.85rem sans — and `.hosted-editor-loading` takes the same voice centred in its own column. The two shell branches drop `grid-template-rows` to `1fr` so the single centred child owns the viewport instead of the 64px masthead band they have no header to put in.

They also say the same thing at every stage: AppShell's editor branch says "Opening {name}…" and EditorShell's frame-loading branch now says "Opening {workspace.name}…" instead of "Opening workspace…", so the handover between chunks does not read as something restarting.

Deliberately NOT done: gating first paint on both the data and the EditorShell chunk. One gate would make the stages agree by making the whole thing slower. Making every stage identical achieves "one coherent loading story" at zero cost — a stage the user cannot distinguish from its neighbour is not a stage.

VERIFIED under a 120ms-per-request throttle: one box, text "Opening Product direction…", measuring 1440x900 at 0,0 — centred in the viewport. Both themes, zero console errors.

title: Restore the command palette to its introduced design; justify additions individually
description:
Return the hosted command palette to its introduced design, then justify every addition to it individually. This is a RESTORATION, not a redesign — the palette is not the problem.

## Who introduced it, and what it was

The ⌘K palette is James's feature, authored and committed by him:

    c810cb9  feat(hosted): ⌘K command palette
    James Lal <james@littlebearlabs.io>  2026-07-12

His stated reason was native parity — "The hosted app had no command palette (native App.svelte has one; hosted did not)" — and `web/src/App.svelte` does import and use `CommandPalette`, so this is a product-level pattern across both surfaces, not a hosted experiment.

What he shipped was deliberately narrow, and the shape IS the design:

- **Document-scoped.** Share for review, Edit/Stop editing, New Markdown file, Export workspace, and one `Open <path>` per other workspace entry. Every command acts on the document or its workspace.
- **One entry point.** ⌘K (⌃K) from a window keydown. No button, no header slot, no second palette.
- **Self-contained**, styled with the hosted chrome tokens, focus restored on close.
- Validated in Playwright at the time.

## What we added on top, eight hours apart, neither aware of the other

- `3f0f563` (attn-a9f7, 2026-08-18 23:31) — the persistent `Commands ⌘K` **header button** (`.palette-hint`, rationale attn-a9f7.1.8: "⌘K was reachable and advertised nowhere"), plus a **second, desk-level palette** in AppShell.svelte with a different command set.
- `cb00ea4` (attn-08fa.11, 2026-08-19 06:28) — five palette entries (Appearance, Keyboard shortcuts, Add files to this workspace, Go to your desk, Storage & recovery) and a ShortcutsSheet on `?`.

Merged in `80b10a9`. The composite the owner rejected: two palettes with different contents behind one keystroke, ten mixed-purpose commands in a flat unranked list, a labelled header button competing with Share in a header whose entire argument was one visible action, and four separate surfaces advertising the same feature.

## The work

1. **Restore the introduced shape first.** Remove the header button and the second desk-level palette. One palette, ⌘K, document-scoped.
2. **Then re-admit additions one at a time, each with a reason to be in a DOCUMENT-scoped palette.** Do not batch this. On the current evidence:
   - `Add files to this workspace` — acts on the workspace; plausible. But see attn-mkmz.3: it must not be the ONLY route to upload.
   - `Keyboard shortcuts` / the `?` sheet — help, not a document action. If the palette is the discovery surface, `?` may be the better home and the palette entry redundant.
   - `Appearance`, `Go to your desk`, `Storage & recovery` — app settings and navigation. These are the three that broke James's model; they need the strongest justification or a different home.
3. **Whatever survives, keep one advertised entry point.** The a9f7 concern (⌘K advertised nowhere) is legitimate — the editor placeholder is the only hint and it vanishes on first keystroke — but a persistent labelled header button was the wrong answer to it. Solve discovery without spending the header's single-action budget.

Do not git-revert `3f0f563`: it is ~1,495 lines across 12 files, of which the command surface is a small slice (EditorShell +20, CommandPalette 10, part of AppShell). The desk rewrite, ConfirmPanel.svelte, chrome-dialect.test.ts and the export-zip work in that commit are wanted. Cut surgically.

Check the outcome against the native palette (`web/src/lib/CommandPalette.svelte`, used by App.svelte) — parity was the reason this feature exists, and the two should not have drifted apart.
acceptance_criteria: One palette, ⌘K, document-scoped — the header button and the second desk-level palette are gone. Every command remaining in it acts on the document or its workspace, with a recorded reason if it was re-admitted. Exactly one advertised entry point for commands, and it does not occupy the header's single-action slot. Hosted and native palettes are in deliberate parity. Verified in both themes; svelte-check, build:browser and check-route-bundles clean.
notes:
DONE — restored to James's introduced shape, then each addition re-admitted or dropped on its own evidence.

REMOVED
  - The `.palette-hint` "Commands ⌘K" header button (attn-a9f7.1.8). Its premise was true — ⌘K was advertised nowhere — but it answered that by spending the header's single-action budget on a labelled control beside Share.
  - The second, desk-level palette in AppShell (attn-a9f7.3.4), with its own command set. Also removed the `HostedCommand` import, `deskCommands`, `onShellKeydown`, `openPalette` and the `<svelte:window onkeydown>` that carried it. Cut surgically; 3f0f563 was NOT reverted.

EVIDENCE THAT DECIDED THE RE-ADMISSIONS — the native palette's actual contents (App.svelte:3283):
  Comment on selection · Suggest an edit · Share this file for review… · Toggle review panel ·
  Switch theme (Paper / Ink / System) · Settings · Keyboard shortcuts

That changes the reading of attn-08fa.11's five entries. Theme and Keyboard shortcuts are NOT foreign to this surface — native has carried both since before the hosted palette existed, and parity with native is the stated reason the hosted palette was built. So:

  KEPT  Appearance          — native has "Switch theme (Paper / Ink / System)". Parity.
  KEPT  Keyboard shortcuts  — native has it. It is also the advertised entry point (below).
  KEPT  Add files…          — acts on this workspace; no longer the ONLY route, since attn-mkmz.3
                              restored the sidebar footer button. That was the real objection.
  DROP  Go to your desk     — app navigation, no native counterpart (native has no desk), and the
                              sidebar project menu already offers "All workspaces" visibly.
  DROP  Storage & recovery  — app settings, no native counterpart, reachable from the desk header.

ADVERTISED ENTRY POINT: exactly one, and it costs no header space — the shortcut sheet, opened with "?" and listed inside the palette as "Keyboard shortcuts". This is precisely what native does: keyboard.ts binds ⌘K/⌘P to the palette and "?" to KeyboardShortcutsDialog, with no visible control for either. Hosted now matches. The a9f7 discovery concern is answered by pointing at the same place native points, rather than by inventing hosted-only chrome.

VERIFIED in a real browser: `.palette-hint` count 0; ⌘K on the desk opens nothing; ⌘K in the editor opens one palette listing Share for review · New Markdown file · Rename workspace · Export workspace · Appearance · Keyboard shortcuts · Add files to this workspace · Download <file> · Open <each other entry> — every one of which acts on the document or its workspace. "?" opens the sheet. Both themes; svelte-check, build:browser and check-route-bundles clean.

title: Sidebar: add horizontal padding around the nav items
description:
Owner screenshot of the rail: the project header ('UNTITLED'), the 'Filter files' field and the file rows run flush to the rail's left and right edges — the active 'untitled.md' row's fill touches both edges, so the row reads as a full-bleed band rather than a contained item. DESIGN.md specifies tree rows at 9px radius, which a full-bleed row cannot show on the sides it touches.

Add consistent inline padding to the rail's content column so rows, the filter field and the section label share one gutter, and the active row's radius is visible on both sides.

Check this against the native sidebar, which uses the same tree components via app.css — the fix should not make the two diverge.
acceptance_criteria: Rail content has one consistent inline gutter; the active row's 9px radius is visible on both sides; the filter field and section label align to the same gutter; native sidebar unchanged or intentionally matched; both themes.
notes:
FIXED in the shared component, so the native rail is intentionally matched rather than left to diverge.

The rail had FOUR different insets and the file tree had none: `.sidebar-controls` 12px, `.sidebar-outline-wrap` 10px, `.sidebar-outline-empty` 10px (whose own comment claimed it lined up with "the filter and the file list"), and `.sidebar-tree-menu` 0. Now one `--sidebar-gutter: 12px` on `.project-sidebar` (spacing.md on DESIGN.md's scale), consumed by all four. Verified hosted AND native: active row x=12 w=223, exactly matching the filter field's box.

TRAP WORTH KNOWING, and it cost a round: the reset `[data-sidebar] ul { padding-inline-start: 0 }` in app.css is UNLAYERED, so the first attempt — a rule inside `@layer components` — lost on the start side only and produced 12px right / 0 left, which is worse than the full-bleed it was fixing. The gutter rule for the tree must be unlayered too (`ul.sidebar-tree-menu[data-sidebar]`), and it now sits directly beneath the reset with that reason written next to it. title: Editor header: give the header row consistent horizontal padding to the window edges
description:
From the same screenshots: the share icon sits very close to the right window edge while the brand tile has a different inset on the left, so the header is not symmetrically padded. Related to the alignment bug but a separate fix — that one is about the items relative to EACH OTHER, this is about the row relative to the WINDOW.

Note the hosted editor header is a different element from AppHeader.svelte's .app-header (desk/open/storage), which uses padding: 0.5rem 1.4rem. Decide whether the two headers should share one padding token; DESIGN.md's 'one grammar, one plane' argument for the accent plane applies to the geometry too.

notes:
FIXED, and the two headers now share one token rather than agreeing by coincidence.

Measured before: the editor header carried Tailwind `px-3` (0.75rem = 11.6px) while `.app-header` on desk/open/storage carried 1.4rem (21.7px). Both sides of the editor bar were symmetric, so the owner's "share icon very close to the right window edge" was really about the ABSOLUTE inset being half the desk's — the controls sat 11.6px off the window edge, and crossing from desk into a document slid the brand 10px left.

Resolved in favour of matching, not diverging: `--chrome-inline-gutter: 1.4rem` declared once at the top of app-shell.css, consumed by `.app-header` and by the editor header (`px-[var(--chrome-inline-gutter)]` — it has to stay a utility, since a Tailwind utility on the element would outrank any layered rule).
