title: Hosted app: design-system & copy alignment (impeccable critique 2026-08-19)
description:
Bring the hosted browser app (web/src/hosted + shared web/src/lib components it renders) into line with DESIGN.md and the product voice, per the dual-agent impeccable critique of 2026-08-19 (snapshot: .impeccable/critique/2026-08-19T01-36-32Z__web-src-hosted.md). Critique score: 32/40 (Good) — strong core loop (landing → desk → editor → share → review lifecycle), with drift concentrated at the edges.

## Source findings (summary)

Consistency & Standards scored 2/4 and Help & Documentation 2/4; everything else 3–4. Every P1 is a case where DESIGN.md and the shipped pixels disagree:

1. **Accent budget violations (One Pencil Rule).** `web/styles/base.css:226` colors every `ul li::marker` at 80% `--primary` (verified live in both themes) — DESIGN.md's labelling exceptions are a closed enumeration that excludes them. The ShareSheet "CURRENT" pill also spends the accent (rust tint + rust-deep text). The base.css comment calls the bullets deliberate, so this is a doc-vs-code conflict, not a plain bug.
2. **Quarantine Rule violation.** `.status-box strong { color: var(--green) }` (web/src/hosted/app/app-shell.css:2494) paints Storage's "Protected from automatic cleanup" green; `--green` is defined free-standing in web/src/hosted/chrome.css:42/62 — the only hosted token bypassing tokens.css. AppHeader.svelte's own comment says storage state cannot claim green.
3. **Read/Do violations.** Storage prose at 0.72rem mono (StoragePage.svelte:219); ShareSheet meta ("1 file selected · 125 B", "Hybrid delivery", "Markdown · 125 B") in Source Code Pro (app-shell.css:1844–1877). The in-page detector independently flagged the same text as tiny-text (11.2–11.5px).
4. **StoragePage escapes the system wholesale**: inline style= attributes, off-ramp sizes (0.92/0.88/0.72rem), glyphs inside heading strings (● ◐ ◌ ▲ ⊘ — announced by screen readers), spacer-span layout, raw error.message passthrough.
5. **Terminology drift**: "review link" (share sheet, lifecycle) vs "Paste an invite link" (DeskHome.svelte:307) vs "Copy invite command" (landing); "View-only" is both a share tier and the storage-unavailable header badge (AppHeader.svelte:29); "Your Desk" title-case outlier (BrowserReviewApp.svelte:1543); sentence-initial "Attn" in lifecycle errors.
6. **Sidebar active row off-spec**: DESIGN.md says 19% ink fill + 2px accent bar; live is 10% ink fill + ink-colored bar.
7. **Three lost-state designs**: global 404 (brand header, two buttons, clamp type — Fixed-Scale violation), workspace-not-found (AppShell.svelte:369 — no header; muted underlined link matching neither link rule), review lifecycle errors (accent links). Punctuation differs. Detector adds ~142–148-char line lengths on Open and workspace-not-found.
8. **Power-user gaps**: no in-app theme control (landing-only toggle), no shortcut reference, ~6-command palette, 4 inline actions per desk row with no overflow menu, permanent dashed drop-zone in the sidebar, storage-health badge invisible inside the editor.

## Structure

Three decision beads (accent budget, desk header plane, hero privacy claim) gate only their own implementations; all task beads are otherwise independent and parallelizable. Each child carries its exact file:line targets and acceptance criteria.

## Epic-level acceptance

- Re-run `/impeccable critique` on web/src/hosted: Consistency & Standards ≥ 3, no P1 findings remain, total ≥ 35/40.
- `node .claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/detect.mjs --json web/src/hosted` stays clean (currently clean; no regressions).
- In-page detector on /, /app, /app/storage, /open, and a bogus workspace route reports no tiny-text and no line-length findings.
- DESIGN.md and shipped CSS agree on every named rule touched (One Pencil enumeration, Quarantine, Read/Do, sidebar active state) — whichever direction each decision bead ruled.
- Both themes (PAPER/INK) verified for every visual change.
notes: CITATION NOTE (2026-08-19): .impeccable/critique/ is now gitignored and its 13 previously-tracked snapshots were untracked, so the path quoted in this issue's description resolves only on the machine that ran the critique. This is not a dangling reference in practice — the 'Source findings' section below restates every finding the epic acts on, with file:line, so the issue stands on its own. Treat the path as provenance, not as the record.

title: Resolved comment redesign: Lucide check, Unresolve action, full-width badge
description:
Three changes to the resolved-thread rendering (screenshots 2026-08-15).

(1) Lucide check icon replaces the literal check glyph: ReviewMarginCard.svelte:526 (.rmc-meta-tick — keep the tick+sr-only design, no "resolved" word, per notes :503-510 and :9-13 / attn-bw2h.3), ReviewMargin.svelte:1022 (gutter icon variant) and :1224 (label chip). (2) Unresolve action: the resolved card footer is INTENTIONALLY empty (ReviewMarginCard.svelte:596-600, attn-42y — that decision is now reversed). Add an Unresolve button + onUnresolve prop, gated like resolve (readOnly/reviewerAuthoring at :595; prop doc :140-141 — hosted reviewer may reply/resolve but never apply/re-anchor). ReviewMargin.svelte: unresolveThread() beside resolveThread (:531-542), including an inverse of the optimistic dismissThreadLocally dim (:537), wired through the card mounts (~:1056,:1094,:1174). DEPENDS on the CommentReopened protocol bead.

(3) Resolved badge spans the full comment rail width: the label-variant resolved chip (ReviewMargin.svelte:1201-1227, CSS :1386-1437 — currently a content-hugging 28px pill with inline author border-color) becomes full-width of the expanded rail. Harmonize with the new 2px author-border card language. The 48px-gutter icon-variant chips (:1010-1024, CSS :1443-1456) are likely retired along with the gutter by the rail-hide child of attn-is2m — coordinate. Keep the stacked/mobile variant (:1117-1119) and the show-all-resolved count pill (:1230-1235, threshold :257-276) coherent. Expand/collapse interactions preserved: expandResolved/collapseResolved (:945-967), Escape collapses (:679-687), mid-selection click guard (ReviewMarginCard.svelte:392-400).

Acceptance: every resolved indicator uses the Lucide check; resolved cards offer Unresolve (owner + attested reviewers) that reopens the thread live on all surfaces; the collapsed resolved badge spans the full rail width; a11y preserved (sr-only "resolved", aria-labels/aria-expanded on chips); both themes checked.
close_reason: Implemented. Lucide check replaces the literal glyph in all three places (card meta tick, labeled resolved chip, gutter icon chip) — first icon import in the rail; 'check' confirmed present in the pinned @lucide/svelte 0.561 and imported by deep path per the bundle-guard convention. Unresolve: the deliberately-empty resolved footer branch (attn-42y) now carries one action, gated like resolve (readOnly/reviewerAuthoring); ReviewMargin.unresolveThread() mirrors resolveThread including optimism — new store.restoreThreadLocally() is the inverse of dismissThreadLocally, plus collapseResolvedThread so the reopened card leaves read-only presentation. Wired natively (reviewReopenComment IPC) and on both hosted surfaces (reopenBrowserComment / reopenReview). Full-width badge: the labeled chip now spans the rail (left+right 12px, matching card insets) instead of hugging its content; the 48px gutter icon variant explicitly opts back out, and the stacked/mobile variant uses align-self stretch.

title: Protocol: CommentReopened event (unresolve) across Rust + web
description:
Unresolve is unsupported today by design: CommentResolved { thread_id, resolved_by } is a one-way marker (src/review/model.rs:1385-1388; web mirror types.ts:992-996), the manager comment says "Reopening is a future CommentReopened event (not yet modeled)" (src/review/manager.rs:1846-1847), and the web projection is add-only (selectors.ts:144-145, Set.add with no delete).

USER DECISION 2026-08-15: authorization mirrors resolve — owner or attested reviewer, self-attributed (reopened_by == event author), agents never (pattern at src/review/transport/inbound.rs:720-729).

Rust: add ReviewEventBody::CommentReopened { thread_id, reopened_by } beside CommentResolved (model.rs:1385); authz arm in inbound.rs:724 area; event-name map manager.rs:4562 ("comment_reopened"); mint fn reopen_comment beside resolve_comment (manager.rs:1848-1878) + IPC command wiring + error code (e.g. ATTN_REOPEN_COMMENT); signing test vector following signing.rs:677-689.

Web: CommentReopenedBody + event-body union (types.ts:992 area); projection must become order-sensitive last-writer-wins per thread — resolve -> reopen -> resolve must land on resolved; verify the event-log ordering guarantees in browser-review-log.ts before a naive add/delete pass (selectors.ts:144; also browser-ws.ts:1083 decode and review-counts.ts:96). browser-session.ts: reopenComment() with the grant-tier check mirroring resolve (:1150-1159 — view grant cannot).

COMPATIBILITY: old receivers (<= 0.9.0) will not know the new event variant — assess ReviewEventBody serde behavior for unknown variants on the Rust side and the web validators (same deny_unknown_fields family as attn-mz25 / attn-mz25.1); document the rollout implication (old native peers in a room where someone reopens a comment).

No UI in this bead — the Unresolve button lands in the resolved-state redesign child.

Acceptance: reopen event minted, signed, authorized, and projected on both stacks; ordering/replay covered by tests (incl. resolve/reopen/resolve); compat impact documented in the bead on close.
close_reason: Implemented across the stack. Rust: ReviewEventBody::CommentReopened{thread_id,reopened_by}, authz arm in inbound.rs mirroring resolve (non-agent, self-attributed), ReviewCommand::ReopenComment + reopen_comment() minting via the outbox, IPC review_reopen_comment, command/event name maps, stub arm. Web: CommentReopenedBody + union, browser-session.reopenComment() with the view-tier guard, browser-ws eventAllowedForRole mirror, review-counts fold, and reopenComment mirrored through the whole session facade chain (share-session, share-production, owner-authority, owner-workspace-runtime, hosted EditingSession, real/mock services). Projection: reconstructThreads now folds resolve/reopen LAST-WRITER-WINS by compareEvents instead of a one-way Set — array order is not log order, so out-of-order delivery was the real trap. Test vector 6 (comment_reopened) added to the shared signing corpus and replayed green. Tests: 3 selector cases (reopen, resolve/reopen/resolve, out-of-order), 3 count cases, 2 Rust authz cases.

title: Hover linking for HTML annotations (shell <-> sandboxed frame)
description:
Extend card <-> segment hover linking to HTML documents (annotation runtime injected into the sandboxed opaque-origin iframe).

Card -> frame (small): the machinery already exists as dead code — bridge setAnchorState (html-annotation-bridge.ts:331-338) and runtime handler (doc-runtime/index.ts:769-776, dispatch :827-828) are implemented but no shell ever calls them; state is only baked into renderAnchors (App.svelte:536-560 sends resolved|default, never active). Do NOT reuse the 'active' state for hover (it is the focus tier and setAnchorState mutates persistent state — un-hover must restore resolved/default). Instead add 'hovered' to AnchorRenderState (doc-protocol.ts:37). Runtime: repaintHighlights (index.ts:646-662) is a TWO-bucket model (attn-text / attn-text-active, buckets :43-44) — add a third bucket + ::highlight(attn-text-hover) style in doc-runtime/styles.ts:40-46; element overlays/pins get [data-state="hovered"] variants (styles.ts:50-101). Shell: $effect on reviewStore.hoveredEventId -> bridge.setAnchorState(threadId,...) with pre-hover state tracked for restore, in all three mounts (App.svelte ~:562-567, EditorShell.svelte ~:858+, BrowserReviewApp.svelte ~:1010+).

Frame -> shell (needs a NEW protocol message): no hover over committed anchors is reported out today (scopeHover is the authoring scope chain, not committed anchors; the only committed-anchor interaction is anchorActivated from the element pin click, index.ts:695-702 — text-range anchors have no handlers at all). Add doc->shell anchorHover { anchorId: string | null } to doc-protocol.ts:96-118 PLUS a parseDocMessage validator arm (unvalidated messages are dropped silently). Additive is safe: both sides ignore unknown types, DOC_PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 1 (doc-protocol.ts:20-21). Runtime detection: element anchors — overlay fill is pointer-events:none by design so text stays selectable (styles.ts:52-56); hit-test instead of naive listeners (pins are interactive already). Text-range anchors — CSS Custom Highlight ranges are not DOM nodes and receive no events: throttled mousemove + caretPositionFromPoint / Range.getClientRects hit-test. Bridge: new onAnchorHover in AnnotationBridgeEvents (html-annotation-bridge.ts ~:146) + #dispatch arm (:233-274); shell maps anchorId -> thread -> reviewStore.setHoveredEventId, mirroring the onAnchorActivated handlers (App.svelte:673-676, EditorShell.svelte:965, BrowserReviewApp.svelte:1127).

MUST regenerate the runtime artifacts after any doc-runtime/ change (web/src/doc-runtime/runtime.generated.js, web/src/lib/review/doc-runtime.generated.ts — npm run build:doc-runtime; guarded by html-annotation-inject.test.ts).

Acceptance: hovering a card lights the HTML element/text-range in the frame (visually distinct from focus and resolved; correct restore on un-hover); hovering an annotated element or text range lights up its card; works for native owner, hosted owner, and browser reviewer; generated artifacts rebuilt; covered in html-annotation-runtime e2e.
close_reason: Implemented both directions. Card->frame: added 'hovered' to AnchorRenderState (distinct tier from 'active', which means focused) plus a third ::highlight(attn-text-hover) bucket in repaintHighlights and [data-state=hovered] overlay/pin styles. The restore-on-unhover problem is owned by the bridge, not the shells: setHoveredAnchor() reads the retained #rendered specs for the base state, so a resolved anchor cannot be left painted as unresolved. Frame->shell: new additive doc->shell anchorHover{anchorId|null} message with a parseDocMessage validator arm (unvalidated messages are dropped silently), reported from onPointerMove BEFORE the inspect gate so hover linking works on a document whose click-to-comment mode is off. Element anchors hit-test via data-anchor-id chrome + element.contains (innermost wins); text ranges via Range.getClientRects since a CSS Custom Highlight is not a DOM node and gets no events. mouseleave clears. DOC_PROTOCOL_VERSION stays 1 (additive). Generated runtime artifacts rebuilt. Tests: 4 protocol validator cases + 2 Playwright E2E (real range geometry hit-test, and hovered-vs-active painting); the geometry test was verified to fail with the reporting call disabled.

title: Comment cards: full 2px author-color border replacing left accent strip
description:
USER DECISION 2026-08-15: every card gets a full 2px border in the comment AUTHOR identity color (the current left-strip color — NOT a fixed green; the screenshots looked green because that reviewer was assigned green). Keep the 6px radius. Exactly 2px.

Current implementation: the left accent is NOT a border — it is an absolutely-positioned ::before strip (ReviewMarginCard.svelte:804-818) with long rationale comments at :731-746 and :783-802 (miter/clipping regression fixes, attn-bw2h.1). The card box itself has border: 1px solid var(--review-card-border) + border-radius: 6px at :747-777.

Accent resolution today (keep the same semantics, just move to the border): inline style:--rmc-accent={authorAccent} at :466; authorAccent (:408-411) is undefined for stale/ambiguous so CSS state rules win — data-state stale -> var(--destructive) (:851-853), ambiguous -> var(--confidence-low) (:855-857); data-kind fallbacks :839-845.

Change shape: delete the ::before strip; border: 2px solid var(--rmc-accent, var(--review-card-border)). With a uniform full border the miter/taper concerns that motivated the pseudo-element vanish; the overflow warning (:741-743) becomes moot but retire the stale comments. Rebalance padding (:747 — the 13px left compensated for the 3px strip). Redefine the active/selected treatment (:825-831 currently overrides border-color to primary + adds a ring) so data-active remains clearly distinct from the ever-present 2px author border (e.g. outer ring only, or surface/elevation shift). Also reconcile hover treatment with the hover-linking child.

Verify contrast in both paper and ink themes (tokens at web/src/tokens.css:222-226 and :338-342). Shared component — change lands on native, hosted owner, and browser reviewer simultaneously.

Acceptance: all cards show a 2px full author-color border, 6px radius; stale/ambiguous keep their state colors; active state still visually distinct from the author border; no clipping regressions in the attn-bw2h.1 scenarios; both themes checked.
close_reason: Implemented: the 3px left ::before strip is replaced by a uniform 2px border in the author identity color (--rmc-accent), 6px radius kept, padding rebalanced to 9px/11px so content sits at the same inset. Active/selected no longer overrides border-color (that would erase identity) — it is an outer ring instead; hover gets a softer accent-colored halo. Stale/ambiguous keep their state colors. The pseudo-element, its isolate/z-index stacking context and the attn-bw2h.1 -1px offsets are gone with it; rationale comments rewritten rather than deleted.

title: Remove card excerpt; bidirectional hover linking (markdown docs)
description:
USER DECISION 2026-08-15: remove the quoted excerpt from normal cards and replace it with hover linking; STALE/orphaned cards KEEP their quote (they render no document highlight, so the quote is their only context).

Excerpt removal: .rmc-quote render at ReviewMarginCard.svelte:558-560, CSS :981-990; data via quotePreviewFor (ReviewMargin.svelte:913-915, t.anchor?.quote?.exact) passed at the five card render sites (~:1042,:1080,:1101,:1160,:1197). Keep the stale-quote block (ReviewMarginCard.svelte:540-552, CSS :994-1009) — stale/ambiguous resolutions produce no inline mark at all (review-decorations.ts:414-429).

Hover linking — the join key is data-event-id on the inline decorations (review-decorations.ts:237-252).

Doc -> card ALREADY WORKS: mouseover/out handlers (review-decorations.ts:571-597) set reviewStore.hoveredEventId (:281, setter :1195); ReviewMargin derives it (:179) and the card gets data-hovered (ReviewMarginCard.svelte:461). But the visual is only an opacity bump (:820-823) — strengthen so the card visibly lights up (ring/elevation in the hover flavor), distinct from data-active, coherent with the new 2px author border.

Card -> doc DOES NOT WORK: cards write hoveredEventId (ReviewMarginCard.svelte:431-441, wired :469-470) but nothing document-side reads it — the decoration rebuild deliberately excludes hover for perf (App.svelte:1840-1851; same note BrowserReviewApp.svelte:516). Implement per the existing "hover is CSS-only" intent: reflect hoveredEventId as an attribute on the editor container (e.g. data-hovered-event-id) and add a descendant rule like [data-hovered-event-id="X"] [data-event-id="X"] { stronger highlight } — do NOT trigger buildDecorations on hover. Highlight classes/CSS live at web/src/app.css:921-978 (attn-review-comment / attn-review-suggestion etc.).

Known limits (accepted): marks only exist for confidence >= inline cutoff; below-cutoff and stale threads get no doc-side hover effect (stale keeps its quote instead).

Acceptance: excerpts gone from normal cards, kept on stale; hovering a card highlights its segment; hovering a segment lights up its card; no decoration rebuild on hover (perf); behavior verified on native, hosted owner, and browser reviewer surfaces.
close_reason: Implemented: excerpt (.rmc-quote) removed from anchored cards and the quotePreview prop/quotePreviewFor helper deleted; stale cards keep .rmc-stale-quote as decided. Bidirectional hover: doc->card already existed (strengthened to a visible halo); card->doc added via applyReviewHoverHighlight(view, eventId) which toggles an is-hovered class straight on the mark DOM — no decoration rebuild, honoring the existing perf rule. Wired in all three hosts (App, BrowserReviewApp, EditorShell) in an effect separate from the rebuild effect, re-applied after PM redraws. Also implemented is-focused styling in app.css, which was emitted by the plugin but had no CSS anywhere.

title: Review rail toggle fully hides the rail (all surfaces)
description:
The rail toggle only narrows to a 48px gutter. USER DECISION 2026-08-15: binary expanded <-> fully hidden (0px). The marker gutter disappears when closed; the document re-wraps to full width — this supersedes the "gutter reserved for the life of the surface" rationale in planning/collab/review-band-stability.md (option A); update that doc.

Root cause: computeRailMode (web/src/lib/review/rail-mode.ts:107-118) returns only expanded|collapsed while in a room — hidden is unreachable with the toggle. Widths at rail-mode.ts:18-22 {hidden:0, collapsed:48, expanded:320}.

Changes:
- rail-mode.ts:107-118 — in-room mapping becomes panelOpen ? expanded : hidden. Decide whether the collapsed mode is retired entirely or kept for other callers; resolved icon-chips that render in the gutter (ReviewMargin.svelte:1010-1024) become unreachable — coordinate with the resolved-state redesign child of attn-bb6t.
- store.svelte.ts togglePanel :1026-1028 and railMode :365-368.
- Hosted: HostedDesktopWorkspaceFrame.svelte:86-99 — railVisible ORs in reviewHistoryAvailable and effectiveRailMode force-falls-back to collapsed, pinning a permanent 48px strip whenever review history exists (EditorShell.svelte:3115 passes durableReviewHistory || fixtureReviewHistory || replay failed); rework so the history affordance does not pin chrome open. Aside width/paint at :350-373 and :396-401.
- Reviewer page: BrowserReviewApp.svelte:1698-1714 hard-codes flex: 0 0 48px whenever desktopLayout with the toggle only swapping an overlay (railVisible :262, toggle :1596-1615, intent comment :1688-1697). Must also fully hide.
- Native already skips rendering at hidden (WorkspaceEditorFrame.svelte:278-281) — it just needs the mode to be reachable; verify the Cmd-J path.

Constraints to preserve: expanded width stays user-resizable and persisted (WorkspaceEditorFrame.svelte:107-254; only expanded resizable :176,:221); RAIL_WIDTH_MIN_PX 260 / MAX 640 (rail-mode.ts:59-61) are mirrored in src/prefs.rs and pinned by rail-width.test.ts — do not drift.

Acceptance: toggling the rail on hosted owner, browser reviewer, and native fully hides it (0px, no border/chrome); re-toggling restores the previous expanded width; no permanent 48px strip when review history is available; rail-mode/rail-width tests updated.
close_reason: Closed

title: Hosted header parity: icon save chip + compact share chip with hover titles
description:
Hosted editor header shows text chips where native shows icons + title tooltips.

(1) Share chip — one-flag parity: HostedDesktopWorkspaceFrame.svelte:309-316 mounts ReviewBar without compactShare; add compactShare={true}. ShareChip already supports it (ShareChip.svelte:46-57 prop, :108 iconOnly, :163-169 class fork, :207 label becomes sr-only; compact glyphs Zap/Wifi/CloudOff :190-196, pre-room Share2 :185, title composed at :179). Tests to update: web/src/lib/header-icon-states.test.ts:79-120, native-header-parity.test.ts (whole file, esp :35-38), save-state-copy.test.ts:62 (orphan-literal rule — the full sentence must survive in a title/sr-only slot), ShareChip.test.ts, and e2e text assertions at web/e2e/hosted-authoring.spec.ts:64,321,355,514, hosted-recovery.spec.ts:20,63,90, hosted-shells.spec.ts:67.

title: Hosted upload/drop should auto-open the imported file
description:
Uploading or dropping a file in the hosted app registers it in the nav but never activates it; user must click the nav entry.

Root cause: EditorShell.svelte importFiles() (web/src/hosted/app/EditorShell.svelte:623-639) calls onWorkspaceChanged() with NO path, so AppShell.onWorkspaceChanged (web/src/hosted/app/AppShell.svelte:188-206) resolves the target back to the currently active file. Sibling flows already do it right: createMarkdownFile passes the path (EditorShell.svelte:614), commitEntryRename too (:651).

Fix shape: service.addAssetFiles returns Promise<void> (types.ts:344, real-service.ts:540-561) so paths must come from the local input — hoist the toImportFiles(...) result (ImportFileInput[] with .path, import-files.ts:136-160, type types.ts:115-120) into a variable and pass the first imported document path to onWorkspaceChanged(path). If a batch mixes docs and assets, open the first viewable doc (md/html) else the first entry.

Do NOT move the auto-open decision into onWorkspaceChanged itself: the cross-tab structure-change path calls it argument-free on purpose (AppShell.svelte:241) and must keep current behavior.

Entry points that all funnel into importFiles: sidebar dropzone button (EditorShell.svelte:3025-3033), hidden file input (:3035-3043), fileDrop targets on desktop+mobile shells (:3098, :3213; web/src/hosted/app/file-drop.ts:43-96), mobile add button (:3420-3424).

Tests pinning old behavior to update: web/e2e/hosted-authoring.spec.ts:192-208 (drop asserts only nav button appears) and :560-570 (picker explicitly clicks pixel.png before asserting).

Acceptance: after upload/drop, the imported doc is active without any nav click, on desktop and mobile shells; rename/new-file auto-open unchanged; cross-tab refresh unchanged; e2e updated.
close_reason: Closed

title: Comment card redesign: 2px author border, hover linking, resolved state (native + hosted)
description:
Redesign of the review comment cards and resolved-state treatment across BOTH surfaces (native wry app and hosted browser app — the rail components are shared). Reported with screenshots 2026-08-15. User decisions locked in:

4. Replace the single left accent strip with a full 2px border in the comment author identity color (not a fixed green — the green in screenshots was the Anonymous reviewer color). Keep the 6px radius. Not thicker than 2px.
5. Remove the quoted excerpt from normal comment cards. Replace it with bidirectional hover linking: hovering a card lights up its highlighted segment in the document, hovering a segment lights up its card. Must work for markdown docs AND HTML-annotated docs (sandboxed frame — needs one additive doc-protocol message for frame->shell hover). Exception: stale/orphaned cards KEEP their quote block since they render no document highlight.
6. Resolved state redesign: Lucide check icon instead of the literal check glyph, an Unresolve action (requires a NEW protocol event — CommentReopened — resolve is currently one-way by design), and the collapsed resolved badge spans the full width of the comment rail. Unresolve authorization mirrors resolve: owner or attested reviewer, self-attributed, agents never.

Children carry exact file:line pointers from the 2026-08-15 code investigation. Protocol child has a compatibility note (old receivers vs new event variant — same family as attn-mz25).
close_reason: All five children implemented and verified. Cross-cutting notes for whoever picks up attn-is2m: (1) the 48px collapsed gutter still renders resolved icon-chips — attn-is2m.3 retires that gutter, so those chips go with it; (2) CommentReopened is a new event variant, so receivers on 0.9.0 and earlier reject it and will keep showing a reopened thread as resolved — same compatibility family as attn-mz25, worth folding into that bead's rollout note. Verification: 561 Rust tests, 125 web test files, 29 html-annotation E2E, svelte-check clean, clippy clean, production web build OK.

title: Hosted web app UX parity: upload autoload, header icons, rail close
description:
Three UX defects in the hosted browser app (attn.sh /app surface), reported with screenshots 2026-08-15. Scope is the hosted editor shell, though the rail-close child deliberately spans all surfaces because rail-mode state is shared.

1. Uploading/dropping a file adds it to the nav but does not open it — user must click it again.
2. The editor header still uses long text chips ("Changes autosaved", "Sharing - <doc title>") where the native app uses compact icons with a title tooltip. Parity: icons + title attribute + sr-only text.
3. The comments rail toggle only narrows the rail to a 48px gutter instead of closing it. User decision: toggle becomes binary expanded <-> fully hidden (0px); the marker gutter goes away when closed and the document re-wraps to full width (supersedes the review-band-stability option A rationale).

Children carry exact file:line pointers from the 2026-08-15 code investigation.
close_reason: Closed

title: HTML annotation: anchors were unclonable proxies, so no pin/geometry ever reached the frame
description: RenderableAnchor objects are assembled from the Svelte 5 review store, where every tracked object is a Proxy. postMessage serialises with structured clone, which throws DataCloneError on a proxy — so HtmlAnnotationBridge.renderAnchors threw on EVERY call and the document frame never received an anchor. Consequences: no numbered pin painted, no anchorsResolved, no geometry, and htmlAnchorTops permanently empty. Compounding it, ReviewMargin's HTML branch skipped any thread with no reported top, so the rail rendered EMPTY — a saved comment appeared lost. Found by reproducing the user's smoke test against a live daemon: 'DataCloneError: The object can not be cloned' in the webview log. Every prior e2e passed plain object literals through the bridge, which is exactly why none caught it.
design: Fixed in html-annotation-bridge.ts: plainAnchor() flattens to structured-cloneable data on the way in, so the retained replay copy is safe too. ReviewMargin now falls back to y=0 for anchored HTML threads with no geometry, matching what the resolved-chip branch already did — a card stacked at the top is a position problem, a missing card is a lost comment. Regression test posts PROXIED anchors through the real bridge and asserts both the resolution and the painted pin.
close_reason: Fixed and covered by e2e 'renders anchors that arrive as reactive proxies' (verified to fail when the fix is reverted).

title: Debug-only in-frame drive channel so E2E can exercise the annotation UX
description: The attn automation bridge (--eval/--click/--query) evaluates in the shell DOM and cannot cross into the sandboxed opaque-origin iframe, so every attn-z64t E2E assertion was shell-shape only — the entire in-frame interaction layer (pin, pill, hover, click) shipped with zero test coverage, which is how the self-hide bug and the silent-return bug reached smoke testing. Add a debug-build-only drive channel over the EXISTING MessagePort (html-annotation-bridge.ts): shell can send synthetic hover/click/select commands and query runtime UI state (visible chrome, current outline target, pending proposal); the runtime only honors these when the shell enables debug drive at init. Release builds compile it out / never enable it. Extend scripts/test-html-annotation-e2e.sh to drive hover->outline->click->composer and selection->pill->composer end to end. Security note: the channel must not add any inbound message that mutates review state (amendments.md #20) — drive commands emulate input, assertions read UI state only.
acceptance_criteria: E2E fails if the pin/chip hides on approach, if element click does not produce a proposal, or if the composer does not open; release bundle contains no drive path.
notes: DEVIATION from the filed plan, deliberate: no debug drive channel was added to the runtime. Playwright already drives a real mouse into the opaque-origin frame (frameLocator works cross-origin), so in-frame hover/click/pill coverage was added to web/e2e/html-annotation-runtime.spec.ts instead — 9 new cases, real events, testing the SHIPPED bundle. This is strictly better than the planned channel: no new inbound message, no release-build strip needed, no new surface on an untrusted frame (amendments.md #20 untouched). The shell half is covered by a read-only window.__attn_html_debug__ mirror in App.svelte plus a new assertion in scripts/test-html-annotation-e2e.sh that the owner's frame is annotatable AND connected. Both new guards verified to FAIL when their fix is reverted.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: 22 in-frame Playwright cases (real mouse, opaque-origin frame), 125 web test files, svelte-check clean, cargo build clean, and the two-daemon+relay html-annotation E2E green including a new owner-wiring assertion. Each new guard confirmed to fail when its fix is reverted.

title: Shell swallows annotation proposals silently on the owner side
description: App.svelte onProposal (:497) and the composer render gate (:4022, '{#if htmlComposer && reviewStore.currentRoomId}') both depend on reviewStore.currentRoomId, but the owner deliberately stays on their local doc (attn-0wa) so room focus may be unset — a pill/element click then returns with no feedback at all (matches smoke-test report 'nothing happens'). htmlAnnotatable (:423) has the same dependency. Fix: key annotatability and the composer gate off the room the file's snapshot belongs to (owner's own published snapshot for this path), not the focused room; every path that cannot open a composer must explain itself (existing toast pattern), never return silently. Verify the unshared-owner toast actually fires in the native app.
acceptance_criteria: Owner on a shared HTML file: element/selection click always opens the composer; unshared: always toasts; no code path in onProposal ends without visible feedback.
notes: Two root causes. (1) web/src/lib/HtmlViewer.svelte path-mode iframe was missing bind:this={frameEl}, so the OWNER's local HTML never completed the bridge handshake — the runtime said hello and nothing answered. (2) annotatability + composer gate keyed off reviewStore.currentRoomId, which an owner routinely lacks (attn-0wa). Now: htmlAnnotationSnapshot resolves by DISPLAYED path via new snapshotPublishesPath(); htmlComposer carries its own roomId; onProposal toasts a reason on every explicit refusal (share-first / not-in-share / preparing) and never returns bare. New protocol field 'explicit' stops a passive drag-select from opening a composer.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: 22 in-frame Playwright cases (real mouse, opaque-origin frame), 125 web test files, svelte-check clean, cargo build clean, and the two-daemon+relay html-annotation E2E green including a new owner-wiring assertion. Each new guard confirmed to fail when its fix is reverted.

title: Runtime chrome hides itself under the cursor; annotate clicks must not navigate
description: onPointerMove (web/src/doc-runtime/index.ts:282) hides the gutter pin/flyout whenever the hover target is not a SCOPE_TAGS element, and the runtime's own chrome (.attn-layer descendants: pin, flyout, pill, chips) is not excluded — so moving the cursor onto the pin hides the pin, making it structurally unclickable (the exact symptom from smoke testing). Fix: ignore mousemove/click targets inside the runtime layer, and add hover hysteresis/grace so chrome survives short traversals. Also, in the element-click annotation model, clicks on annotatable elements must preventDefault/stopPropagation so links and buttons in the document do not fire while the user is placing a comment (agentation behavior); page scripts otherwise run normally per the decided posture.
acceptance_criteria: Chrome elements can always be reached and clicked; hovering runtime chrome never dismisses it; clicking an <a> to comment on it does not navigate the frame.
notes: Fixed: onPointerMove returns early for targets inside .attn-layer (the self-hide); 160ms hide grace; chip hit box reaches 2px over the element it names plus a 6px corridor above so a cursor travelling to the chip never re-targets; leaving-the-chip-and-returning now disarms the hide timer (second wedge found in review); reflow drops chrome whose element left the DOM. Capture-phase click preventDefault/stopPropagation, but ONLY in inspect mode so an unshared page keeps its own links and buttons. Regression tests bite: reverting either fix fails the suite.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: 22 in-frame Playwright cases (real mouse, opaque-origin frame), 125 web test files, svelte-check clean, cargo build clean, and the two-daemon+relay html-annotation E2E green including a new owner-wiring assertion. Each new guard confirmed to fail when its fix is reverted.

title: Element-first hover/click annotation in the doc runtime
description: Replace the gutter-pin-and-flyout as the primary element path in web/src/doc-runtime/index.ts. Hovering any element draws the outline (existing outline()) plus a small label chip (scopeTitle/scopePreview, e.g. 'row 3 - Q3 - $1.2M'); clicking the element sends the proposal (existing proposalForElement/pickScope path) so the shell opens the composer pinned to it. Scope drilling (cell/row/table, li/ul, etc.) moves to a breadcrumb on the label chip instead of a margin flyout. Text selection -> Comment pill remains for ranges and suppresses element hover while a selection is live (logic exists at index.ts:285). Remove or demote the gutter pin. Persistent numbered pins for committed comments are unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Every SCOPE_TAGS element (and reasonable fallback for others) outlines on hover with a chip; click opens composer; breadcrumb drills scope; selection pill unaffected; no flyout-only path remains.
notes: Implemented: gutter pin + flyout removed; hover -> dashed outline + breadcrumb chip (outermost-first, e.g. 'table > row 2 > cell') naming the innermost element; chip segments pick any scope; SCOPE_TAGS broadened (headings h1-h6, dl/dt/dd, sectioning, media, a/button/label/form controls, code) plus fallbackScope() so unscoped markup is still commentable; selection pill retained for ranges. Element click commits only in shell-enabled inspect mode. Covered by web/e2e/html-annotation-runtime.spec.ts (real-mouse, in-frame).
close_reason: Implemented and verified alongside its blocker attn-yqun.2 (both live in the same file and were delivered together).

title: Agentation-style element inspection UX for HTML commenting
description: Smoke testing (2026-08-13) found the attn-z64t in-frame UX both mis-designed and broken. What shipped is text-selection-first plus a left-margin gutter pin with a scope flyout; the user expects agentation.dev's model: hover any element -> outline + label chip naming it -> click the element -> composer opens pinned to it -> numbered markers persist. Additionally the gutter pin hides itself when the cursor reaches for it (the document-wide mousemove handler in web/src/doc-runtime/index.ts:282 hides chrome when the hover target is not a scope element, and the pin/flyout are not excluded), and the shell swallows pill clicks silently when the owner's currentRoomId gate fails (App.svelte:497 onProposal silent returns; composer render gated on reviewStore.currentRoomId at App.svelte:4022). None of this was caught because the automation bridge evaluates in the shell DOM only and cannot reach inside the sandboxed iframe — all attn-z64t E2E assertions were shell-shape only. Scope: comment storage only (no agent actions), share-first rule unchanged, sandbox stays opaque-origin (allow-scripts, NEVER allow-same-origin), frame stays untrusted (proposes anchors / reports geometry only).
design: All required machinery already exists in the runtime: outline(), scopeTitle/scopePreview, anchorForElement, persistent pins. The work is re-fronting it as direct manipulation, fixing the self-hide bug, removing shell silent-returns, and adding a debug-only in-frame test drive channel over the existing MessagePort.
acceptance_criteria: Hovering any element in an annotatable HTML doc outlines it with a label chip; clicking it opens the shell composer; scope drill via breadcrumb on the chip; text-selection pill still works; no interaction path ends in silence; E2E can drive and assert in-frame hover/click in debug builds.
notes: Second review round (codex) found 11 items; 8 actioned, 2 filed as children, 1 declined. FIXED: (a) hover chrome now gated on inspect too — the chip is opaque and painted over the page, so on a merely-read document it occluded and swallowed clicks on the page's own links to offer an affordance that could only say 'share first'; one switch, not two. (b) only the chip cancels a pending hide — a comment pin or the pill used to hold a stale chip open forever. (c) a click commits only to the element the chip is NAMING (was: re-derived from the click target), which fixes the reachable case of dismissing a stale selection committing a comment, and also the double-click double-commit. (d) snapshotPublishesPath gained an exact shareRoot resolution; its heuristics accepted 'docs/a.html' for '/p/archive/docs/a.html' and cross-room root joins. (e) a snapshot published without the capability now says so instead of 'preparing' forever. (f) chip clamped at the right edge (was raising a horizontal scrollbar). (g) SCOPE_TAGS compared upper-cased so SVG matches. (h) security: reportHtmlResolutions keyed to the displayed snapshot, not the focused room, and the unavailable-toast given a fixed id so a hostile frame cannot stack them. DECLINED: chip padding occlusion is inherent to labelling above an element and is now confined to documents under review, where click interception is intended. Filed: attn-yqun.5 (mousedown-driven page behaviour under inspect), attn-yqun.6 (detached-element chrome).
close_reason: All four children delivered and verified.

title: Integration gate: real multi-role validation and repeat Impeccable review
description:
Integrate all hosted-web remediation and prove the result as a product flow, not a collection of component snapshots.

Run the real local owner/reviewer share loop with a minted authenticated invite: Desk count -> open workspace -> durable desktop/mobile history -> reviewer comment/suggestion -> owner resolution/acceptance -> offline/reconnect -> reload and multi-tab convergence. Exercise reviewer loading and every terminal state with fixtures. Verify strict routes at the response-status and rendered-state levels. Measure the desktop workspace network payload after the existing icon-catalog optimization.

Then run a bounded `/impeccable polish`, repeat `/impeccable critique` and `/impeccable audit`, and capture the required 320/390/1280/1440, 200%-text, PAPER/INK, keyboard, Axe, reduced-motion, and no-overflow evidence. Run Svelte checks, hosted unit/E2E suites, route-bundle checks, and production build. Record staging/device gaps honestly.

This gate is also the handoff contract for the later `site/` epic: document the shared brand/state vocabulary and identify the parity test or shared-token boundary that `site/` should adopt, without editing `site/` here.


## Required Skills
impeccable,svelte5-best-practices
design: Parent agent integrates subagent work, runs /impeccable polish in one bounded pass, and repeats independent critique/audit. Record local validation, staging acceptance, and device acceptance separately.
acceptance_criteria: A real authenticated owner/reviewer loop passes across Desk counts, durable history, comment/suggestion lifecycle, offline/reconnect, reload, and multi-tab convergence; strict route status/render matrix passes; connected plus all terminal reviewer states are browser-verified; desktop workspace first-open payload meets the pinned post-icon-split budget; 320/390/1280/1440, 200%-text, PAPER/INK, keyboard, screen-reader/Axe, reduced-motion, safe-area, and no-overflow matrices pass; Svelte checks, hosted unit/E2E suites, route-bundle gates, detector, production build, bounded Impeccable polish, and repeat critique/audit pass; remaining staging/real-device gaps are filed and stated; no site/ file changed.
close_reason: Integration gate passed: 125 unit files, Svelte check 0/0, production build, route/icon bundle gates, 55 hosted browser tests, 8 real reviewer lifecycle browser tests, and authenticated owner/reviewer local loop including multi-tab and durable mobile history. Repeat Impeccable review accepted the fixed rail and detector findings were source-context false positives. Staging/physical-device acceptance is explicitly filed as attn-cbvj.

title: Keep durable review history visible independently of live connection
description:
Owner review visibility currently conflates durable history with live connection state. The mobile demo falls back to `workspace.reviewCards`, while desktop mounts the rail only when `reviewRoomActive`; the real service initializes `reviewCards` empty. A Desk review obligation can therefore disappear after opening the workspace.

Implement the locked product contract: durable review history is visible in desktop and mobile whether peers are live, offline, or the live session has ended. “Live” adds connection, presence, and authoring capabilities; it does not gate history. Materialize owner workspace review state from the single durable projection (`attn-whdh`) rather than a mock-only side channel. Desktop rail/toggle, mobile sheet, Desk counts, resolution/acceptance, and reload/multi-tab behavior must derive from the same projection.

This task depends on the single-projection architecture and its final proof includes the real relay loop tracked by `attn-dalx`.


## Required Skills
impeccable,svelte5-best-practices
design: Use /impeccable clarify and /impeccable harden. Durable log/projection is the source of truth; live presence is ephemeral decoration and authoring capability. Do not promote mock reviewCards into a second production store.
acceptance_criteria: Owner desktop rail/toggle and mobile Review sheet expose the same durable threads and counts when the room is live, peers are offline, or the live session has ended; connection badges describe only connectivity; Desk counts, workspace counts, resolution/acceptance, and review history derive from one durable projection; real-service data replaces the mock-only fallback; reload and leader/follower tabs converge without duplication; an authenticated owner/reviewer relay test proves create, comment, suggest, resolve/accept, disconnect/reconnect, and reload behavior; empty and unavailable states are distinct and actionable.
close_reason: Durable history is now projection-driven rather than tied to live session state. The authenticated owner/reviewer browser loop verifies comment and suggestion creation, owner resolve/accept, reviewer disconnect, desktop and mobile reloads, and preserved resolved history.

title: Build a branded, recoverable reviewer lifecycle shell
description:
Invited-review loading and terminal states are nearly blank utilities. Invalid `/review` and fragmentless `/s` states expose internal strings such as “no invite fragment or remembered room,” have no semantic page heading, and offer no recovery controls. Bootstrap failures use a separate fallback, so the state grammar is fragmented.

Build one branded reviewer lifecycle shell for loading, invalid/missing capability, admission denied, expired, cursor expired, deleted, revoked, offline/network, and bootstrap failure. Each state gets plain-language diagnosis, only evidence-backed privacy reassurance, and state-appropriate actions. Missing-capability recovery should accept a complete invite through the existing validated parser without logging or exposing the fragment; other states provide Retry, request-new-link guidance, Home, or Desk as appropriate. Raw diagnostics remain console/log-only.

Preserve connected review rendering and keep valid review-domain failures distinct from malformed-route 404s.


## Required Skills
impeccable,svelte5-best-practices
design: Use /impeccable harden then /impeccable clarify. Reuse the normal attn brand/header and theme grammar without loading the editor for terminal states. State copy must be derived from verified state, never raw exception text or unearned security reassurance.
acceptance_criteria: Loading, invalid/missing capability, admission denied, expired, cursor expired, deleted, revoked, offline/network, and bootstrap failure render through one branded state system; every terminal state has a semantic heading, plain-language diagnosis, appropriate recovery action, keyboard route away, and honest privacy reassurance where evidence supports it; raw diagnostics are log-only; missing-capability recovery accepts a complete validated invite without persisting/logging/exposing its fragment; malformed paths remain 404 while valid-domain failures remain lifecycle states; component tests cover the full state matrix and browser checks cover desktop/mobile, PAPER/INK, screen reader, keyboard, and Axe.
close_reason: Implemented branded reviewer lifecycle states, safe complete-link recovery, and state-matrix tests.

title: Make homepage install-command overflow keyboard operable
description:
At 390x844 Axe reports `scrollable-region-focusable` for the horizontally overflowing install command in `CopyCode.svelte` / `landing.css`. Keyboard users cannot reach and scroll the full copyable command.

Make both install commands keyboard operable at narrow width and text zoom. Prefer semantic code content with an intentional focus state and arrow-key scroll behavior, or a wrapping solution that preserves the exact command and Copy behavior. This task follows homepage restructuring because both touch landing CSS.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build the hosted browser bundle and open `/` at 390x844.
2. Run Axe; note the serious `scrollable-region-focusable` violation on the long install-command span.
3. Navigate with the keyboard and confirm the overflowing command cannot receive focus or be horizontally scrolled.
design: Use /impeccable adapt after the homepage distillation lands. Keep the exact command text and existing Copy contract; use the shared focus vocabulary.
acceptance_criteria: Both install commands are fully perceivable and operable by keyboard at 320px, 390px, and 200% text; if overflow remains, the semantic command region is focusable, visibly focused, and arrow-key scrollable; Copy still copies the exact complete command; Axe reports no scrollable-region-focusable violation; no horizontal page overflow is introduced in PAPER or INK.
close_reason: Implemented keyboard-operable install command overflow; focused landing Axe and keyboard scrolling checks pass.

title: Recompose populated Desk rows for mobile scanning and touch
description:
The populated Desk row inherits a desktop grid that collapses at phone width. At 390x844 the sharing line overlaps the workspace title and file/recency/size metadata fragments into word-per-line columns. Recompose the mobile row as an explicit card instead of shrinking six desktop cells.

Target hierarchy: title plus one labeled administration/overflow action; wrapping file/recency/size metadata; open review counts; then sharing/backup state. The whole card remains the open target. Preserve desktop density, keyboard filtering/selection, accessible names, empty Desk quality, and truthful local/share/backup copy.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build the hosted browser bundle and open `/app?shell=demo` at 390x844.
2. Inspect the first `Product direction` workspace row.
3. Observe the share-status text overlapping the title and the file/recency/size metadata breaking into narrow word-per-line columns.
design: Use /impeccable adapt. Preserve the desktop grid at desktop widths; use an explicit mobile card composition under the mobile breakpoint. Do not hide review/share truth to make it fit.
acceptance_criteria: At 320px and 390px, long workspace names, active review counts, ciphertext share copy, backup state, and worst-case metadata neither overlap nor fragment into word-per-line columns; the entire card is the open target; administration is one labelled overflow action with Rename/Delete; keyboard filtering, arrows, Enter, Escape, focus rings, accessible names, and desktop row density remain intact; PAPER/INK and 200%-text screenshots, Axe, and no-overflow checks pass.
close_reason: Implemented responsive Desk cards; mobile scanning, management, overflow, and Axe coverage pass.

title: Strict hosted routing and branded not-found recovery
description:
Unknown and malformed hosted paths currently masquerade as successful pages: unknown roots render the homepage with HTTP 200; malformed `/app/*` renders Desk; malformed review/share paths render invite errors with HTTP 200. Introduce strict route recognition and a product-specific not-found state without breaking valid deep links.

Use one explicit routing contract across `web/src/lib/hosted/routes.ts`, the Cloudflare worker, Vite dev/preview middleware, and the app bootstrap. Keep route failure distinct from domain failure: a syntactically valid workspace absent on this device is not a 404, and a syntactically valid invite that is expired/revoked/denied belongs to reviewer lifecycle recovery.

Coordinate with `attn-n01r.45`, which tracks valid app deep-link serving. This task must not “fix” invalid paths by regressing valid cold navigation.


## Required Skills
impeccable,svelte5-best-practices
design: Use /impeccable harden. Add an explicit not-found route contract rather than another large entry bundle; share the smallest branded shell and theme preflight possible. Dev, preview, service worker, and Cloudflare worker must agree. Preserve valid deep paths and privacy boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: Unknown root and malformed /app, /open, /review, and /s path shapes return HTTP 404 and render a branded, keyboard-accessible not-found state with Home and Desk recovery; valid workspace-shaped paths absent locally retain the existing on-device recovery state; valid expired/revoked/denied invites retain reviewer lifecycle recovery; Vite dev/preview, Cloudflare worker, and service worker agree; route tests assert response status, selected entry, rendered state, attempted path handling, and valid deep-link non-regression.
close_reason: Implemented strict shared route contract and branded 404; build, route/SW tests, preview parity, and browser routing coverage pass.

title: Hosted web product: Impeccable audit remediation across home, Desk, review, and 404
description:
Fresh `/impeccable critique` and `/impeccable audit` of the hosted product in `web/`, covering the homepage `/`, Desk `/app`, owner workspace `/app/w/:workspaceId/:filePath`, invited-review routes `/review/:roomId` and `/s/:shareId`, and unknown/malformed paths.

This is refinement, not redesign. The steady-state product already has a specific and coherent “Lit Reading Room” identity. The work is to extend that quality through responsive layouts, lifecycle failures, durable review history, routing, accessibility, and bundle discipline.

Evidence archive: `.impeccable/critique/2026-08-12T18-21-40Z__web-hosted.md`. Method: isolated design assessment, independent detector/browser assessment, and a separate technical audit. Design score 27/40; audit score 13/20. Browser evidence spans 1440x900/1000 and 390x844 in PAPER and INK where available. Connected reviewer states still require a real capability/relay validation loop.

Decisions locked by the user:
- Keep a concise homepage security guarantee visible and put the full relay evidence behind an explicit “Read the threat model” disclosure.
- Keep review history available after live connectivity ends. “Live” is connection state only; it never decides whether durable review content is visible.

Out of scope: the separate `site/` marketing package. A later epic will audit it, but it must inherit `web/`'s typography roles, PAPER/INK materials, one-pencil accent, quiet voice, local-first terminology, CTA vocabulary, and loading/error/not-found grammar. Do not edit `site/` in this epic.

Existing exact-match work is linked rather than duplicated, especially `attn-7xl.7.8` (desktop icon bundle) and `attn-dalx` (live Desk review-count proof).
design:
Execution is deliberately multi-agent once implementation begins. The parent agent owns Beads mutations, dependency sequencing, integration, and publication; subagents never call `bd`. Assign one implementation subagent per unblocked child or compatible file lane. Serialize overlapping lanes: homepage tasks share landing CSS; Desk responsive and global hit-area work share app-shell CSS; reviewer lifecycle and review hit-area work share BrowserReviewApp.

Every UI implementer uses the repo-local `/impeccable` command named by its child plus `svelte5-best-practices`, reads the relevant PRODUCT/DESIGN/surface context, then loads `craft-floor.md` immediately before editing. Preserve incumbent identity and factual/security copy. Do not treat the detector’s pinned-paper `cream-palette` or blockquote side-rule findings as defects.

Implementation waves:
1. Independent root-cause fixes: routing/404, mobile Desk cards, homepage distillation, reviewer lifecycle shell, durable review projection, and the existing icon-bundle task.
2. Accessibility consolidation after the overlapping surface work lands: install-command overflow, coarse-pointer hit areas, and file-delete semantics.
3. Integration gate: real owner/reviewer relay loop, desktop/mobile/PAPER/INK browser matrix, `/impeccable polish`, repeat critique/audit, quality gates, and evidence-backed handoff.

Subagent code must be reviewed and integrated by the parent. Local tests are not live acceptance: final reporting distinguishes static/unit/build evidence, local real-browser evidence, and any unverified staging/device state.
acceptance_criteria: All scoped children and linked blockers are complete; /, /app, owner workspace, invited-review lifecycle, and malformed/unknown routes satisfy the recorded contracts in PAPER and INK at desktop/mobile and 200% text; durable review history remains visible independently of live connection; homepage security detail is accessible by explicit disclosure; real owner/reviewer local validation passes; repeat Impeccable critique/audit, Svelte checks, hosted tests, route/bundle gates, Axe, and production build pass; no files under site/ are modified.
close_reason: All scoped remediation is integrated: homepage security disclosure, strict branded 404, responsive Desk/owner workspace, reviewer lifecycle recovery, durable projection/history, a11y/touch/focus repairs, lazy icon bundles, and live authenticated browser proof. Local quality gates pass; independent staging/physical-device follow-up is attn-cbvj. No site/ files were changed by this epic.

title: Annotation bridge never re-sends anchors after a frame RELOAD, so a watched file loses every highlight on save
description:
Found while validating this epic. Latent today because only the reviewer annotates (content mode); becomes a first-order bug the moment the native owner annotates a local file, because local files are WATCHED and reload on every save — the owner's normal workflow.

Mechanism:
- HtmlAnnotationBridge.renderAnchors only stashes into #pending when there is NO port (html-annotation-bridge.ts:228-234). After the first successful render the port exists and #pending stays null.
- On a frame reload the runtime dies and re-boots, posts hello again, and #establish runs — but #pending is null, so it re-sends NOTHING (html-annotation-bridge.ts:140-143). The frame comes back with zero anchors.
- HtmlViewer's bridge effect reads renderedContent but NOT src (HtmlViewer.svelte:114-125), so a src change does not rebuild the bridge. Content mode is therefore safe (content changes rebuild the bridge and the app's render effect re-fires), and PATH mode is not.
- The native watcher sets htmlMtimeByPath on change (App.svelte:2650), and the viewer appends ?v=mtime to the src, so every on-disk save reloads the frame.

Net effect after the owner work lands: edit the HTML, it reloads, and every highlight and pin silently disappears until something unrelated changes the anchor list.

Also fix the comment at HtmlViewer.svelte:119-120, which claims the bridge is rebuilt whenever the frame or document changes — true only in content mode as written.

Fix shape: have the bridge remember the last rendered set (not merely the un-flushed one) and re-send it on every successful handshake, so a re-boot is idempotent. renderAnchors is already full-state by design, so this is a small change; the trap is asserting it.
acceptance_criteria: Reloading the document frame (src change or an in-frame reload) re-paints every anchor without the shell doing anything. Covered by a real-browser test that boots, renders anchors, forces a reload, and asserts the anchors come back.
close_reason: Bridge now replays retained anchors after iframe reload.

title: Extend the annotating-runs-page-scripts security sign-off to the native owner and hosted authoring surfaces
description:
attn-kio6 asks for sign-off on one surface: a hosted REVIEWER annotating someone else's shared HTML gets page scripts enabled. This epic extends the same posture to two more surfaces, so the sign-off has to be re-scoped rather than assumed to carry over.

The three cases are NOT equivalent and should be judged separately:
* Native owner, own local file — weakest threat: the user opened their own file, and the native app already runs local HTML with scripts today.
* Hosted authoring, own uploaded file — the user chose the file, but it now executes on the hosted origin inside an opaque-origin sandbox where previously it was never executed at all. That is the posture change the DOWNLOAD ONLY copy currently describes.
* Hosted reviewer, someone else's document — the original attn-kio6 case and the sharpest one.

Deliverable: a decision per surface recorded in html-annotation.md section 4, and whatever guard rails follow (for instance whether the hosted authoring case warrants a one-time confirmation before first execution). Depends on the spike, because option (b) there would change the native frame's origin from opaque to attn://localhost and that must be judged too.
acceptance_criteria: html-annotation.md section 4 states the posture for each of the three surfaces with its reasoning, attn-kio6 is either closed by it or narrowed to what remains, and any agreed guard rail is filed as its own issue.
close_reason: Documented native and hosted opaque-origin script posture.

title: Verification: E2E for the two new surfaces, and smoke-test instructions that match reality
description:
Prove the epic's acceptance bar automatically, and fix the guidance that sent a user down a path the app could not do.

Existing coverage stops at the reviewer: scripts/test-html-annotation-e2e.sh asserts an owner shares .html and a REVIEWER receives an annotatable document. Nothing asserts the owner's own window can annotate, and nothing covers the hosted authoring app at all.

Work: extend the dual-instance E2E so the OWNER, after sharing, has an annotation-capable HTML frame (shell-observable assertions only — the automation bridge cannot reach into the frame, so assert on the injected marker, the sandbox, the mounted margin and the compose availability, as the existing script already does). Add a Playwright case for the hosted path: upload an .html, confirm it renders as a document rather than a download card, and that it becomes commentable once shared. Update the smoke-test instructions and tests/fixtures/annotation-smoke.html usage so the documented flow is one the app supports on every surface named.

Regression guard: markdown review must be unaffected on all three surfaces. Baseline the review-surface suite before and after, as was done for the original epic — the merge-base comparison is what caught nothing regressing last time.
acceptance_criteria: task test:html-annotation covers owner-side annotation as a hard assertion, a hosted Playwright case covers upload-render-comment, and the documented smoke-test steps work as written on both surfaces. Markdown review shows an unchanged failure profile against the merge-base.
close_reason: Added native and hosted regression coverage plus smoke-test updates.

title: Hosted: render and annotate an HTML document in the authoring app
description:
Make an HTML entry a document you can read and comment on in the hosted app, replacing the DOWNLOAD ONLY card that prompted this epic.

The hosted authoring app does not import HtmlViewer at all today — only BrowserReviewApp does. EditorShell renders entries by presentation: editable goes to the markdown editor, preview shows an image, everything else falls to the download card (EditorShell.svelte:2673-2702).

Work: mount HtmlViewer for the html presentation with annotate/annotationEvents/onBridge, and give it the review margin so cards have somewhere to land. Per the owner decision, the frame runs page scripts — the annotation runtime requires allow-scripts, so allowScripts || annotating already yields the right sandbox; do not weaken htmlViewerSandbox, and note that html-viewer-sandbox.test.ts asserts a script-free sandbox for the non-annotating hosted case, which must stay true.

Gate commenting the same way hosted markdown is gated (share-first). Establish what that gating actually is in EditorShell before copying it — do not assume it matches the native rule.
acceptance_criteria: An uploaded .html renders as a document in the hosted app instead of a download card. Once shared, selecting text or an element opens the composer and the comment lands in the rail. Images and other genuine assets still show their existing preview/download behaviour.
notes: Validation finding: the hosted compose path is NOT adaptable — openOwnerCommentComposer (EditorShell.svelte:890-910) requires a ProseMirror view plus snapshot.anchorIndex, and comments route through session.createComment, not native IPC. HTML needs a PARALLEL compose path mirroring BrowserReviewApp's HtmlCommentComposer usage, routed through the hosted session API. Confirmed the hosted app already has the review machinery (ReviewMargin/CommentComposer lazily imported, EditorShell.svelte:155-165) gated by reviewRoomActive (:224), so share-first holds on that surface and the HTML path must join the same lazy-load flow.
close_reason: Hosted author renders annotatable HTML with an HTML comment composer and rail.

title: Hosted: HTML as a first-class workspace entry kind
description:
Give the hosted app a concept of an HTML document. Everything else in the hosted half depends on this.

WorkspaceEntryKind is markdown | asset (hosted/app/types.ts:21). kindForFile (import-files.ts:123) routes every non-markdown upload to asset, and toViewEntry (real-service.ts:606) then renders an asset inline only for an image media type, so text/html lands on download-only. The wire format is already ahead of the app here: WorkspaceManifestEntryKind is markdown | html | asset, so this is a local gap, not a protocol change.

Work: add html to WorkspaceEntryKind; classify .html/.htm into it; give it a presentation the viewer can switch on; update anywhere that counts or labels entries by kind (share scope labels, markdownCount/assetCount, the share sheet). Include a migration path for files ALREADY stored as kind asset with a text/html media type — decide whether to reclassify on read or with a storage migration, and say which and why.
acceptance_criteria: Uploading an .html produces an entry whose kind is html, distinct from asset, with the manifest/publish types agreeing. Existing .html files already stored as assets are reclassified. Unit tests cover classification and the migration. No behaviour change for markdown or for genuine assets.
close_reason: Added first-class hosted HTML entries and legacy asset read-time migration.

title: Native: owner compose-availability and anchor identity for shared HTML
description:
Decide WHEN the owner may comment on HTML, and stamp those comments correctly. This is the share-first parity work.

Markdown precedent, verified: the owner never flips to the snapshot view, but the room is selected by path (ownerRoomIdForActivePath) and currentFileId comes from ownerFileIdForPath, so once shared, composeAvailability goes ready and the anchor is stamped with the SNAPSHOT's fileId/snapshotId/baseHash (App.svelte:1437-1447) while offsets come from the local document. HTML must follow the same rule.

Work: compose-availability.ts currently treats snapshot.anchorIndex as the readiness signal; HTML has no anchorIndex and instead declares annotation === html_selectors_v1, so it needs an HTML branch that yields the same honest absent/pending/blocked/ready copy rather than silently rendering nothing. htmlAnnotatable in App.svelte is snapshot-derived and reviewer-shaped; it needs an owner variant keyed on the room selected for the active path plus a published HTML snapshot for that file. HtmlCommentComposer already takes fileId/snapshotId/baseHash, so wire the owner's resolved snapshot in.

Also correct the ShareDialog copy: the file picker labels .html entries Read-only, which stops being true the moment this lands.

Known and accepted: if the owner edits the file after sharing, offsets are authored against the local DOM but labelled with the published snapshot's baseHash. Markdown has the identical trade-off; the client-side resolver reconciles. Do not invent new drift machinery here — just do not make it worse.
acceptance_criteria: Before sharing, the owner sees the same honest unavailable state markdown gives (not silence). After sharing an HTML file, the owner can comment on it from their local view; the event carries the snapshot's fileId/snapshotId/baseHash and the comment appears in the rail. ShareDialog no longer calls shareable HTML read-only.
close_reason: Enabled HTML comment composition after sharing while keeping suggestions unavailable.

title: Native: owner-side annotatable HTML render path
description:
Implement the spike's outcome so the owner's own local HTML file can host the annotation runtime.

Today App.svelte:3524 mounts HtmlViewer in path mode with no annotate/annotationEvents/onBridge, and HtmlViewer:87 gates annotating on content being defined, so the owner branch is doubly inert. This issue makes that branch capable of annotating; the NEXT issue decides when it is allowed to.

Covers: the HtmlViewer contract (path mode must be able to annotate, or the owner must be moved to whatever mode the spike chose), wiring annotationEvents and onBridge on the owner branch, and the bridge lifecycle on file switch — opening a second HTML file must dispose the first bridge, not leak it. Reuse the existing runtime and bridge unchanged; this is a plumbing change, not a redesign.
acceptance_criteria: With annotation enabled, opening a local HTML file in the native window boots the runtime inside the frame, the shell completes the handshake, and selecting text raises the Comment pill. Switching files disposes the previous bridge. Reviewer HTML annotation and markdown viewing are both unaffected.
notes: Validation finding: pair this with attn-z64t.9. Making the owner branch annotate without the reload fix produces a surface that loses all its highlights on every save of the watched file.
close_reason: Implemented native owner HTML annotation surface and bridge wiring.

title: Spike: get the annotation runtime into a locally rendered HTML file without breaking sub-resources
description:
Decide HOW the runtime reaches a document rendered from disk, then record it as an amendment. This blocks the native work and is the only genuinely open design question in the epic.

The naive move — switch local files from path mode to content mode so injectDocRuntime can splice — regresses rendering: srcdoc gives the frame an opaque origin and NO base URL, so relative sub-resources (img src=./chart.png, link href=style.css) stop resolving. Trading a correctly rendered document for annotation is not acceptable.

Candidates to evaluate, with a working prototype for whichever wins:
(a) Content mode plus an injected base href pointing at the file's directory. Cheapest if an opaque-origin srcdoc frame is permitted to load attn:// sub-resources — that is the thing to test first, because if it fails the option is dead.
(b) Inject at the attn:// protocol handler in Rust: byte-splice DOC_RUNTIME_SOURCE before the last closing body tag as the file is served. Preserves the base URL and every sub-resource, and Rust still never PARSES html. Costs ~21 KB in the binary (trivial against the 40 MiB gate) and changes the frame's origin from opaque to attn://localhost, which alters the security model — the handshake would gain a real checkable origin (an improvement) but the frame would no longer be origin-isolated from other attn:// content. Must be reasoned about explicitly, not assumed benign.
(c) Keep path mode and attach the runtime some other way.

Deliverable: a decision recorded in planning/collab/amendments.md and a note in html-annotation.md, plus whatever spike code proves it. Include what happens to the sandbox attribute and to the event.source handshake binding under the chosen option.
acceptance_criteria: A local HTML file with a relative image and a relative stylesheet renders correctly AND carries a booted annotation runtime, demonstrated by a prototype. The security consequences of the chosen option are written down, including the frame's resulting origin and how the shell verifies the handshake.
close_reason: Implemented native-path runtime injection with relative-resource regression coverage.

title: HTML commenting works wherever you open an HTML file (native owner + hosted app)
description: Commenting on HTML works today in exactly ONE place: a reviewer who received a shared HTML snapshot. Everywhere a person actually opens an HTML file it is absent, which reads as "the feature doesn't work". TWO CONCRETE FAILURES (both reproduced) 1. NATIVE, owner side. Opening a local .html renders it read-only with no comment affordance at all — no selection pill, no gutter pin, empty rail. Cause: App.svelte:3524 mounts `` with no `annotate`, no `annotationEvents`, no `onBridge`. `annotate=` is passed in exactly two places in the repo (App.svelte:3453 and BrowserReviewApp.svelte:1526), both reviewer-only branches. Compounding it, HtmlViewer:87 gates `annotating = annotate && content !== undefined`, and a local file renders in PATH mode (`src=attn://localhost`), so even passing `annotate` would be inert. 2. HOSTED, authoring app. Uploading an .html shows the "DOWNLOAD ONLY / This format is never executed here" card. Cause: `WorkspaceEntryKind` is 'markdown' | 'asset' (hosted/app/types.ts:21) — there is no HTML document concept. `kindForFile()` (import-files.ts:123) sends every non-markdown file to 'asset'; `toViewEntry()` (real-service.ts:606) renders an asset inline only if its media type is in an IMAGE allowlist, so text/html falls through to 'download-only'. The hosted authoring app does not import HtmlViewer at all. Publishing such an entry emits docType 'asset', so even sharing it yields a download card on the far side, not an annotatable document. DECISIONS TAKEN (owner, 2026-08-12) — these bound the epic * SHARE FIRST, same as markdown. Commenting requires a room + snapshot; that is already true for markdown (verified: composeAvailability returns `absent` with no room — compose-availability.ts:80). We are NOT introducing local-only annotations or a local room. So the acceptance bar is: share an HTML file, then annotate it from the surface you are on, exactly as markdown behaves. * COMMENT UX ONLY. No agent-facing API, no MCP surface, no agents replying. * PAGE SCRIPTS RUN. The annotation runtime requires allow-scripts, so "annotatable but scripts off" is not achievable as designed. Documents render with their scripts live inside the opaque-origin sandbox. Extends the posture already tracked in attn-kio6 to two more surfaces. EXPLICIT NON-GOALS * Local-only / unshared annotation. * Suggestions or agent-proposed edits on HTML (still a v1 non-goal; the daemon deliberately REJECTS html-anchored suggestions because the apply pipeline cannot resolve an HTML anchor against source bytes). * Live co-typing of HTML. * Editing HTML documents in the hosted app. THE ONE REAL TECHNICAL FORK (spike first — see the child) Getting the runtime into a LOCALLY rendered file is not simply "switch to content mode". Content mode renders via srcdoc on an opaque origin with no base URL, so a local document's relative sub-resources (``, ``) would stop loading — trading working rendering for annotation. That is a regression a real agent-authored report would hit immediately. Note this is NOT covered by html-annotation.md §8, whose sub-resource non-goal is about annotating INSIDE nested frames/shadow DOM. DONE MEANS A person can share an HTML file and then select text or an element and leave a comment that anchors, persists, and appears in the rail — from the native owner window, from the hosted authoring app, and (as today) from the reviewer surface — with the document still rendering correctly, sub-resources included.
acceptance_criteria: Share an HTML file, then select text or an element and leave a comment that anchors, persists across reopen, and appears in the rail — from (a) the native owner window viewing its own local file, (b) the hosted authoring app after uploading, (c) the reviewer surface as today. The document still renders correctly in every case, including relative sub-resources. Markdown commenting is unchanged on all three surfaces.
close_reason: HTML commenting now works across native owner, hosted author, and reviewer surfaces; validation and independent review complete.

title: Dialog content overflows horizontally: implicit grid column sizes to max-content
description:
The shared dialog body was 'grid gap-4 p-6' — one implicit column sized auto (minmax(auto,max-content)). Inside the ScrollArea that resolved to the widest child's max-content width instead of the dialog's, so a single unbreakable string (a font-mono project path in the share modal) laid every child out wider than the frame, and the frame's overflow-hidden CLIPPED it: 'Select visible' cut mid-word, file-type labels gone, the create button sliced. Measured live pre-fix: 542px column in a 446px content box, 32 elements up to 70px past the right edge.

Fix: grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)] on dialog-content-body so the track resolves against the dialog and children may shrink below min-content (which is what makes truncate/min-w-0 work). Plus min-w-0 on the share dialog's project-root row.

Affects all four dialogs sharing the primitive (Settings, Share, NamePrompt, ReviewExitConfirm). The mirror-image vertical bug was fixed and guarded in attn-11g4.1.1; that guard had no horizontal assertions, which is why this reached a user. Guard added to web/e2e/dialog-scroll.spec.ts and verified to fail without the fix.
close_reason: Fixed on angus/html-commenting: grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)] on the shared dialog body + min-w-0 on the share dialog's project-root row. Verified in the running app (542px→447.5px column, 32 overflowing children→0) and guarded by web/e2e/dialog-scroll.spec.ts, confirmed to fail without the fix.

title: Block surfaces are lit panels on a matte page; make them recessed
description:
Reported: "The frontmatter, code block and table background colors are too stark against the background... we want to aim for a Kindle type reading experience in both light and dark mode."
