One token drives all three: --code-block is used by pre, inline code, tables (DESIGN.md line 183 — "a table and a code block are the same class of object") and the frontmatter card (prosemirror.css:838).

CURRENT
  Paper: page 0.905, block 0.972  →  the block is 0.067 LIGHTER than the page
  Ink:   page 0.148, block 0.19   →  0.042 lighter, correct direction, too loud

The Paper case is the reported one and it is a direction error, not a magnitude error. Paper is the lightest thing a reading surface has; anything brighter than it reads as emissive, which is precisely the opposite of the e-ink feel being asked for. It also contradicts the block's own inset shadow, which says "pressed in" while the tone says "lifted".

PROPOSED — blocks step toward the foreground, one step, and a nested block takes one more:

  Paper   page 0.905  →  block oklch(0.885 0.010 78)   (-0.020)
                      →  nested oklch(0.865 0.010 78)  (-0.040)
  Ink     page 0.148  →  block oklch(0.176 0.014 256)  (+0.028)
                      →  nested oklch(0.204 0.014 256) (+0.056)

Both are ~2-3% steps, which is the Kindle register: present enough to bound the block, quiet enough that the eye never stops on the edge. The existing hairline border and inset shadow do the rest of the work, and they finally agree with the tone.

NESTED CASE, easy to miss: base.css:333 drops inline code inside a table cell to --background so it stays recessed against the cell. That rule inverts the moment the block goes darker than the page — the chip would become the lightest thing in the table. It needs to become the second step above, not the page value.

SYNTAX HIGHLIGHTING is the real risk. Shiki github-light is tuned for a white ground; moving the code surface from 0.972 to 0.885 costs every token some contrast. Sweep the token colours actually in use against the new surface and confirm AA; if a token family fails, the fix is the theme choice or an override, not abandoning the surface change.

OUT OF SCOPE: --surface-raised / --surface-raised-2 (0.94 / 0.965 on Paper). Those back genuinely floating objects — review cards, dialogs, popovers — which are above the page and carry lift shadows, so lighter-than-page is correct for them. This issue is about blocks embedded IN the reading column.
acceptance_criteria:
Code blocks, tables and frontmatter cards read as recessed into the page in both themes. Nothing on Paper is lighter than the page background.

Inline code nested inside a table cell still reads as a chip, stepping further toward the foreground rather than back toward the page.

Syntax highlighting clears AA on the new code surface, verified against the token colours actually rendered, not assumed. Checked on desktop and web, both themes.
close_reason:
--code-block moved to oklch(0.885 0.010 78) Paper / oklch(0.176 0.014 256) Ink, and a new --code-block-nested (0.865 / 0.204) gives a block-inside-a-block its second step. base.css's nested-chip rule moved off --background, which was a step toward the ink only while the block was lighter than the page and inverted silently the moment it moved. One token still drives pre, inline code, tables and the frontmatter card.

SYNTAX HIGHLIGHTING was the real cost and it was NOT pre-existing as first assumed. gate-35 had chosen vitesse-light precisely because it cleared AA on the OLD near-white ground; recessing the surface stranded that choice. Measured on the new ground: comments 1.76:1, punctuation 2.15:1, variables 2.69:1, strings 3.08:1, keywords 3.67:1 — and several vitesse tokens cannot reach 4.5:1 on ANY background (its comment grey tops out at 2.34:1 against pure white), so there was no headroom to tune. Switched to github-light-high-contrast / github-dark-high-contrast, which cleared every family except the light comment at 3.79:1; that one is closed by a shiki colorReplacements patch (#66707b -> #58616B, 4.68:1) applied at tokenize time, so no !important override and no per-token CSS hook is needed. Every rendered token family now clears AA in both themes.

title: Links: accent tone, and the underline the contrast maths makes non-optional
description:
Reported: "Links are not clearly separated in text. They should be the primary orange/blue color and the underline should appear on hover."

The colour half is right and is the fix for the reported symptom. The underline half does not survive contact with the palette, and the arithmetic is worth stating because it is not a matter of taste.

WCAG has TWO requirements for a link inside body text, and they pull in opposite directions:
  (a) the link must clear 4.5:1 against the page (it is body-size text);
  (b) if colour is its only at-rest distinction, it must ALSO clear 3:1 against the surrounding body text (technique G183).

Relative luminance from OKLCH L via Y = ((L*+16)/116)^3, contrast = (Y1+0.05)/(Y2+0.05):

  PAPER   page 0.905 (Y .774) · body 0.14 (Y .0173)
    --primary 0.48 (Y .168):  vs page 3.78:1  FAILS (a)   vs body 3.24:1  passes (b)
    L 0.42     (Y .125):      vs page 4.71:1  passes (a)  vs body 2.60:1  FAILS (b)

  INK     page 0.148 (Y .017) · body 0.87 (Y .700)
    --primary 0.72 (Y .437):  vs page 8.0:1   passes (a)  vs body 1.54:1  FAILS (b) badly

There is no lightness that satisfies both on either theme. Paper is squeezed from both ends; Ink cannot get close, because the body text is already near the top of the range and any link legible on a near-black page lands close to it.

So the rest-state underline is not a stylistic preference here — it is the only way to ship coloured links that pass AA. It is also the better answer to what was actually asked ("not clearly separated in text"): an underline separates a link at a glance in a way a hue shift inside a wall of serif text does not, and it is the print and Kindle convention besides.

PROPOSED, pending the owner's call:
  - rest:  the accent tone per theme (Paper terracotta, Ink steel blue) + a hairline underline at --link-underline weight, offset 2px
  - hover: --primary-hover + the underline thickens to 1px (the state change stays visible)
  - visited: keep a distinct token, but bring it into the accent family rather than the current neutral brown
  - focus-visible: unchanged, the existing ring

If the owner prefers underline-on-hover-only despite the above, the honest fallback is to keep the underline off at rest and accept that links are AA-failing on Paper and colour-only in Ink — that is a deliberate, recorded exception, not something to discover later in an audit.

ONE PENCIL RULE. DESIGN.md reserves the accent for "primary action, current selection, and focus", plus a closed two-item enumeration of labelling exceptions. A hyperlink IS an action, so this needs no third exception — but the rule should name links explicitly, or someone will later read terracotta links as a violation and "fix" them back to the muted brown.

Applies to the desktop app and the web app: base.css owns the a rules for the native and hosted-desktop entries; check hosted/review and the landing for their own link styling.
acceptance_criteria:
A link inside running prose is identifiable as a link without hovering it, on both themes, and the treatment passes WCAG AA for body text against the page. Hover produces a visible state change rather than being the moment the link first announces itself.

Whichever way the underline decision goes, the outcome is recorded: either the rest-state underline ships, or DESIGN.md records the AA exception explicitly with these numbers. No silent failure.

DESIGN.md's One Pencil Rule names links under 'action' so the accent on a link cannot later be mistaken for a violation. Applied on desktop and web; contrast verified with computed values from the running app, not from the token file.
close_reason: Links now carry the accent per theme (Paper oklch(0.48 0.14 28), Ink oklch(0.72 0.10 220)) plus a hairline rest-state underline at --link-underline, thickening to 2px on hover with --link-hover. Split chrome from prose deliberately: the bare 'a' rule keeps the no-rest-underline treatment for nav rows, breadcrumbs and buttons-as-links, while '.attn-doc a' owns prose. text-decoration-skip-ink: none so a descender cannot interrupt a hairline rule and read as a rendering fault. Measured on screen: link 5.3:1 on the page in Paper, 8.18:1 in Ink — both clear AA, and the underline carries the distinction that colour provably cannot (see the epic's maths). DESIGN.md's One Pencil Rule now names links under 'action' and records why the underline may not be removed for tidiness.

title: Reading surface colour: one ink for prose, legible links, and Kindle-calm block surfaces
description:
Two reported problems, one system. Both live in the same tokens and the same three stylesheets, and both need the same contrast sweep to verify, so they are one epic rather than two passes over the same files.

MEASURED, not inferred. Computed styles pulled from the running app for every prose element, both themes:

  element        Paper L   Ink L     source
  h1/p/li/td     0.14      0.87      --foreground
  link           0.38      0.74      --link
  blockquote     0.32      0.66      --muted-foreground
  th             0.32      0.66      --muted-foreground
  page bg        0.905     0.148     --background
  code/table/fm  0.972     0.19      --code-block

PROBLEM 1 — PROSE IS NOT ONE INK. Three elements opt out of --foreground. Links sit 0.24 lighter than body on Paper in the same warm hue, so on a link-dense document they read as faded text rather than as links — which is exactly what was reported. Blockquotes are greyed although a blockquote is still prose; the left bar and indent already carry that distinction, so the grey only costs legibility. The th eyebrow is the one defensible case: it is a small-caps label, chrome not prose, and it should stay muted.

PROBLEM 2 — THE PAGE IS NOT THE LIGHTEST SURFACE. On Paper, code blocks, tables and frontmatter cards render at L 0.972 against a 0.905 page — the block is LIGHTER than the sheet it sits on. Nothing in a physical reading surface is brighter than the paper, so the eye reads those blocks as backlit panels, which is the "too stark" complaint.

DESIGN.md CONTRADICTS ITSELF HERE, and that is worth fixing as part of this. The Elevation section says chrome recedes by going darker, and the Flat-Until-Lifted Rule names the code block as something "genuinely pressed into" the page, carrying an INSET shadow. But line 183 calls --code-block "the raised surface" and gives it a value lighter than the page. The block currently wears a recessed shadow and a raised tone at the same time.

THE RULE THAT RESOLVES BOTH: block surfaces step TOWARD the foreground, never away from it. On Paper the foreground is dark, so a block goes darker; in Ink the foreground is light, so it goes lighter. Both read as "more ink here". Ink already obeys this — only its magnitude is too loud. Paper inverts it. A nested block (inline code inside a table cell) takes one further step in the same direction, which also fixes base.css:333 — that rule drops nested code to --background to keep it recessed, and it inverts the moment --code-block goes darker than the page.

Scope is the desktop app AND the web app: App.svelte (both shells), hosted /app, hosted /review. tokens.css and base.css are shared by the native and hosted-desktop entries, so most of this lands once.
acceptance_criteria:
Running prose renders in one ink. Body, headings, list items, table cells, blockquotes and links all read as the same text colour except where a deliberate, documented exception applies (table header eyebrows stay muted).

Links are unmistakably links at a glance without being a second text colour: the accent tone plus a rest-state underline, both verified against WCAG (see the child issue — colour alone provably cannot satisfy both requirements on this palette).

Code blocks, tables and frontmatter cards read as pressed into the page, not lit on top of it, in both Paper and Ink. Nothing in Paper is lighter than the page. Syntax highlighting still clears AA on the new code surface.

DESIGN.md no longer describes --code-block as raised while shipping it with an inset shadow, and the elevation rule is stated once in terms every future surface can follow. Verified visually in both themes on desktop and web.
close_reason: All five children complete and verified on screen in both themes. Prose is one ink; links are the accent with a load-bearing rest underline; code, tables and frontmatter are recessed insets rather than lit panels; the syntax theme was re-chosen to survive the new ground; DESIGN.md states one elevation rule that predicts the whole system instead of two rules that contradicted each other.

title: Composer entry points swallow the click when they cannot open
acceptance_criteria:
Highlighting text in a room and invoking Comment never results in nothing happening. Each non-obvious refusal — no snapshot yet, file not part of the share, grant tier lacks suggest — is distinguishable and stated in words the user can act on.

Transient and structural refusals are told apart: a snapshot in flight reads as pending, a file outside the share reads as unavailable. Covered by a test that asserts no reachable path from a text selection inside a room to a silent no-op.
close_reason: New pure module review/compose-availability.ts resolves ready/pending/blocked/absent once; the toolbar, both keyboard shortcuts and both composers all spend it. Found a third silent site beyond the two in the issue: refreshSelectionToolbar cleared toolbarSelection entirely when no snapshot resolved, so no control appeared at all — that is the most literal form of the reported 'nothing appears'. The toolbar now renders whenever there is a review context, disables the unavailable action, and states the reason as visible text (role=status), not only a title. Transient (share landing, snapshot unhydrated) reads as pending; structural (file not shared, grant tier lacks suggest) reads as blocked, tier checked first so it never shows a spinner leading nowhere. The bare 'localGrantTier !== suggest' return is gone.

title: Mock share publishes no snapshot, so the browser dev loop can never comment
description:
Reported: 'Everything seems to work EXCEPT I can't actually make comments — I highlight text but nothing appears.' In a browser tab on / with a folder picked and a share completed.

ROOT CAUSE, traced end to end:

1. mock-ipc.ts handleReviewShare (~:429) emits share_ready then status. It never calls emitSnapshot. reviewStore.snapshots stays empty.
2. App.svelte ownerFileIdForPath (:892) resolves a path to a FileId by scanning reviewStore.snapshots for a matching ownerDisplayPath. Empty snapshots means it always returns null.
3. The owner file-sync effect (:706-714) therefore calls reviewStore.setCurrentFile(null) on every activePath change. currentFileId is pinned at null. (Note store.svelte.ts:875 would otherwise adopt a fileId from the first inbound comment event — this effect clears it straight back.)
4. App.svelte resolveActiveSnapshotForCompose (:1089) returns null when there is no snapshot for (roomId, currentFileId).
5. openCommentComposer (:1106) hits 'if (!snapshot || !snapshot.anchorIndex) return;' and returns. No composer, no error, no log.

Same class of gap as attn-bw2h.6 (mock-ipc missing half of the daemon's reply) one layer deeper: that issue restored share_ready so the sheet could complete; this is the snapshot that share_ready implies.

FIX. handleReviewShare must publish a snapshot per shared markdown file, the way the real ReviewManager does, before or alongside the status it already emits. The snapshot needs:

- ownerDisplayPath set to the path actually shared, so ownerFileIdForPath matches. A folder share must publish one snapshot per markdown file under it, not one for the folder (mirrors task test:folder-share on native).
- content: the real markdown. local-file-source.ts already holds the picked bytes for the session — take them from there rather than inventing sample text, or the anchors will not match what is on screen.
- anchorIndex: build it with buildCanonicalAnchorIndex (web/src/lib/review/browser-anchor-index.ts:24), the same function browser-snapshot-publisher.ts uses. Do NOT hand-roll a mock index. App.svelte's anchor-resolution effect (:1296) requires both a real anchorIndex and a string content, and the resolver maps each anchor's authored baseHash onto the current document — a synthetic index produces cards that resolve to nothing.
- baseHash consistent with that content, so the resolver takes the base-hash-match path.

Check the ordering comment already in handleReviewShare: share_ready goes first because it carries the room. The snapshot follows the same reasoning — the room must exist before a snapshot can be scoped to it.
acceptance_criteria:
In an ordinary browser tab on the Vite dev server: pick a folder, Share for review, highlight text in the document. The comment composer opens. Submitting it renders a margin card AND an inline decoration positioned on the highlighted range, not at the top of the document.

A folder share publishes one snapshot per markdown file; switching files in the sidebar keeps commenting working on each. reviewStore.currentFileId is non-null for any shared file that is on screen.
notes:
Validation pass, two confirmations and one addition:

CONFIRMED the ownership path works once a snapshot exists: applyShareReady (store.svelte.ts:797-799) sets role: 'owner' on the room, collabRoleFor (room-ui.ts:54) returns 'owner' from that, so the file-sync effect at App.svelte:706 runs. And a snapshot whose content is a string passes isRenderableReviewSnapshot (snapshot-kind.ts:11) with docType 'markdown' or undefined. No extra wiring needed beyond publishing the snapshot itself.

ADDITION: mockEventMeta (mock-ipc.ts:383) hardcodes snapshotId: MOCK_SNAPSHOT_ID on every event it mints. Once this issue publishes real per-file snapshots with their own ids, that meta field becomes a dangling reference. Thread scoping is unaffected (selectors read anchor.snapshotId, which the composer fills from the real snapshot), and the only other consumer is the signable-meta builder in browser-crypto.ts:534 — but align it anyway: have the mock event echo the snapshotId of the snapshot the anchor targets, so nothing downstream ever sees an id that was never published.
close_reason: handleReviewShare now calls publishMockSnapshots after ShareReady + status: one snapshot per shared markdown file, real bytes from local-file-source (new localMarkdown export), contentHash for baseHash, and buildCanonicalAnchorIndex for the index — the same hasher and canonical Rust/comrak indexer the hosted publisher uses, not a hand-rolled one. Path selection extracted to mock-share-snapshot.ts (pure, unit-tested: selection precedence, folder coverage, markdown-only, de-dup, root containment, stable FileIds, content-addressed SnapshotIds). mockEventMeta/mockReviewEvent now take the snapshotId the anchor actually targets so no event names an unpublished snapshot. Verified in a real browser tab: snapshot lands with content+anchorIndex+ownerDisplayPath+baseHash, currentFileId becomes non-null, and the full highlight→comment→margin card round trip works with the inline decoration on the right range.

title: Browser App.svelte: comment round-trip repair, shell-aware chrome, and header cluster polish
description:
Seven issues reported from a session in a BROWSER TAB on / — the native App.svelte frontend served by Vite (npm run dev / task dev's server), with a project folder opened through the file picker. No daemon, mock IPC.

Establishing the surface first, because it was misread once already and the memory note two-web-surfaces.md exists for exactly this: the tree in the report is missing ios-experience.html, landing-v2.html and prototype.html, which DO exist in planning/web-authoring/. local-file-source.ts is 'deliberately markdown-only'. So this is App.svelte in a browser, not the hosted /app (which sets showOutline={false} and would not render the FILES/OUTLINE tabs visible in the report).

One through-line explains the two biggest items: App.svelte assumes a daemon behind it and a native window shell around it, and neither holds in a browser tab.

- NO DAEMON. The report was 'sharing doesn't work' and narrowed on questioning to: the share itself completes, but highlighting text produces nothing at all. mock-ipc's handleReviewShare emits share_ready + status and never publishes a snapshot, so there is no file identity for the composer to anchor to and the click is swallowed in silence.
- NO NATIVE SHELL. App.svelte never passes showWindowDragRegion, so Sidebar.svelte defaults it true and reserves 46px to clear traffic lights that do not exist in a browser; the header reserves another 6.5rem when there is no sidebar. That dead corner is what item 4 of the report is actually about.

The rest is header and sidebar refinement: uneven spacing in the action cluster (caused by ReviewBar wrappers that survive their empty children), a bordered ShareChip that breaks the convention header-icon-states.test.ts already asserts, the wrong glyph on the comments toggle, and a filter that hides its own box until focused.

SCOPE (decided with the reporter): App.svelte only, covering BOTH shells — browser and desktop wry. The hosted /app owner header and the browser reviewer header carry the same grammar and will drift; that reconciliation is filed separately rather than folded in here.
acceptance_criteria:
In a browser tab on the Vite dev server, with a folder picked: Share for review completes, highlighting text opens the comment composer, and a submitted comment renders as a margin card with its inline decoration. A composer that genuinely cannot open says why instead of swallowing the click — on desktop too.

The brand sits in the freed top-left corner in the browser with no reserved traffic-light space, and is unchanged in the header on desktop. The header action cluster is evenly spaced with no dead gaps from empty slots. The lightning bolt is a borderless ghost at rest like its neighbours, promoting to the pill only while its popover is open. The comments toggle uses the panel-right glyph pair. The sidebar filter draws its box at rest, with focus still distinguishable.
close_reason: All eight children complete. The reported comment failure is fixed at the root (mock share publishes real snapshots) and made non-silent everywhere (compose-availability). Chrome is shell-aware, the header cluster is even and consistent, and the sidebar filter reads as a control. Verified in a real browser tab and a real desktop window; 116 unit test files and 13 Playwright tests green. Scoped to App.svelte per the reporter; hosted-header reconciliation is filed as attn-o17v.

title: Accordion reveal strands in WKWebView — frontmatter card will not open or close
description:
REGRESSION from attn-vlmz.3.3 (rebuilding the frontmatter card on the shared accordion). Found in the visual pass for attn-bw2h. The frontmatter card cannot be reliably opened OR closed in the desktop app.

The accordion reveals with `grid-template-rows: 0fr -> 1fr` under `transition-[grid-template-rows]`. In WKWebView that transition STRANDS: `data-state` flips correctly on the trigger, item and panel, but the computed `grid-template-rows` does not follow, in EITHER direction.

Measured in the built binary:
- data-state="open", class `data-[state=open]:grid-rows-[1fr]` present, rule generated in the bundle with the correct selector and higher specificity (0,2,0 vs 0,1,0) and later source order -> computed `grid-template-rows: 0px`, panel height 0, content (102px) clipped to nothing.
- Poking ANY inline style on the panel forced a reflow and it snapped to 102px, which is the tell.
- Three clean toggles afterwards: state closed/open/closed while the computed value stayed 101.546875px throughout. Stuck open.

So the panel's rendered size is decoupled from its state in both directions.

THIS VIOLATES THE TRUTH RULE, which DESIGN.md states behaviourally: "Pixels always equal state: no user-visible fact ... may depend on an animation completing... animation is enhancement, never the carrier of state. Occluded windows freeze the animation clock, so anything less soft-locks the app." A disclosure whose open-ness IS the transition's end value is exactly the prohibited shape. This is not a WKWebView quirk to work around; it is the rule catching a design that should not have shipped.

WHY IT WAS MISSED: the accordion's verification was Chromium-only (its own report says no test mounts the Svelte components and the NodeView path was exercised against a DOM stub, plus a Tailwind class-generation probe). The class generation was never the problem. This is the third documented instance of a WKWebView transition/animation stranding in this codebase, after the dialog `animationend` failure modes recorded in dialog-content.svelte and the scroll-area `transition-[color]` theme-strand.

FIX DIRECTION (do not just lengthen the duration): make the open state not depend on a transition completing. The reveal may animate as ENHANCEMENT, but the resting size must be set by state alone. Note the reduced-motion path already does exactly this (`motion-reduce:transition-none`), so a correct fix likely generalises that. Both consumers must be fixed together: the Svelte wrapper components and the imperative `createAccordionDom` path used by the NodeView.
acceptance_criteria: The frontmatter card opens and closes reliably in the built desktop app across repeated toggles; the panel's resting size is determined by data-state alone, never by a transition's end value; any animation is enhancement only; both the Svelte and imperative NodeView consumers behave identically; verified in the real binary, not only in Chromium.
notes: FIXED AND VERIFIED in the built binary: 5 consecutive toggles, rendered size follows state every time (open 102px / closed 0px, alternating). Before: stranded at 0px while data-state=open, then stuck at 101.5px across three toggles in BOTH directions. Fix removes the transition from the size path entirely (hidden / data-[state=open]:block), so state alone determines visibility — the Truth Rule's 'instant' alternative rather than an animation that can strand.

title: Share for review never completes on the local web build
description:
Reported: "Share for review on the local web doesn't seem to work here." Screenshot shows the sheet stuck on "Creating the encrypted room and minting invite links…" with all three tiers reading "Preparing view/comment/suggest link…".

REGRESSION-ADJACENT, and the screenshot is diagnostic in a way worth stating: the pending UI showing at all is attn-11g4.1.2 working correctly — before that change this state was an unlabelled freeze. So the loading state is right and the MINT underneath it is what never completes.

Two distinct things to establish, in this order:

1. WHY THE TIMEOUT DID NOT FIRE. `MINT_TIMEOUT_MS` is 15s and guards `phase === 'minting'`, which is exactly the phase shown. Either the screenshot was taken inside 15s, or the guard is not covering this path. If a mint can hang past its own deadline the fix is the deadline, not just the mint — attn-vlmz.1.2 established that no pending state may outlive its timeout, and this would be a second hole in that invariant.

2. WHY THE MINT HANGS. The native build and the hosted browser build take different transports. `scripts/build.sh debug` bakes ATTN_DEFAULT_RELAY_URL=https://relay-staging.attn.sh, while the local web loop expects either staging via proxy or a local relay on :8787 (see CLAUDE.md "Local hosted share loop"). Establish which relay the local web build actually reached, and whether the request failed, was refused, or never left.

Note attn-vlmz.1 verified minting end-to-end on the NATIVE stack against a local relay, and it worked. So this is specific to the web build's transport or origin configuration, not to the share pipeline as a whole — which narrows it considerably.

Reproduce with the documented local loop before changing anything: relay via `cd relay && npm run dev`, app via `cd web && npm run dev:browser:shares`.
acceptance_criteria: Share for review mints and shows all three tier links on the local web build; a mint that cannot complete surfaces an explicit error within its deadline instead of a permanent pending state; the timeout gap, if real, is closed for every phase that can show pending UI.
notes: VERIFIED end to end. Ran e2e/native-share.spec.ts against the raw dev loop: 3/3 pass, including 'the mint completes and offers three genuinely distinct tier links' — the exact failure reported. Also pinned: a mint that never answers resolves to an explicit error inside its deadline, and retry re-arms that deadline. Two corrections to my framing of this issue: the 15s timeout gap was NOT real (measured 15,056ms), and the HOSTED build mints fine (real 201s, three distinct tier secrets). The failing path was the raw browser dev loop, where mock-ipc had no share_ready kind and so could not produce an invite at all — zero network requests, no transport.

title: User's chosen avatar colour is ignored unless they are the room owner
description:
Reported: "The color I choose for my avatar as the user is not being respected either."

Cause found. `reviewStore.colorFor()` (web/src/lib/review/store.svelte.ts:505-513) resolves a declared colour as:

    this.participantColors[participantId]
      ?? (participantId === this.ownerParticipantId && this.activeRoom?.role === 'owner'
            ? userProfile.color
            : null)

so the local user's picked colour is consulted ONLY when they are the owner participant AND the active room's role is `owner`. Every other case — and any case where `ownerParticipantId` has not resolved yet — falls through to `hashParticipantColor(participantId)`, a deterministic hash that ignores the pick entirely.

Two things to establish before fixing:
1. Is the user's picked colour ever propagated into `participantColors` for their own id (i.e. announced into the room), or is the self-fallback the only path? If it is never announced, other peers see the hash too, and the picker is cosmetic-only for everyone but the picker.
2. Is the narrow owner-only condition load-bearing, or defensive? The fix is probably "self is self regardless of role", but confirm rather than widening a security-adjacent branch by assumption.

The picker is at NamePrompt (the swatch row in the identity dialog) and persists via userProfile.color.
acceptance_criteria: A user's picked colour appears on their own avatar and accent wherever they author, in any room role; it is announced to peers so they see the same colour; the deterministic hash remains the fallback only for participants who never declared one.
notes: VERIFIED by code + tests; peer half needs two windows. Peers DO see the picked colour — confirmed on both transports with file:line evidence (native effective_color() in all four announce paths + ReannounceIdentity into already-live rooms; hosted declaredColorEntry in join + announceProfile). SECOND BUG FIXED: a colourless announce could not CLEAR an earlier one, so switching back to Auto propagated nowhere, including to yourself. The agent also caught its own test being vacuous — fixture colour collided with hashParticipantColor('p_me'), so 3 assertions passed against the buggy code; fixed and guarded permanently.

title: Accent strip is 2px shorter than the card — absolute offsets resolve against the padding box
description:
REGRESSION from attn-11g4.4 (straightening the accent edge). Reported: "the left hand border isn't as tall as the right hand side of the comment element (seems like the top and bottom border height are missing from the left hand border)." That reading is exactly right.

Cause: ReviewMarginCard.svelte:705-710 pins the strip with `position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0; left: 0`. Absolute offsets resolve against the containing block's PADDING box, and the card carries `border: 1px solid`. So the strip spans (card height - 2px) and sits 1px inside the top and bottom edges, while the card's own right border runs the full height. The previous inset box-shadow did not show this because an inset shadow paints across the padding box of a border-box element, reaching the border's inner edge on all sides at once.

The fix must keep everything attn-11g4.4 established: square ends (border-radius 0), 3px width, --rmc-accent with its kind/state overrides, isolation:isolate, and no overflow:hidden on the card. Candidates: negative insets (top/bottom/left: -1px) so the strip covers the border, or moving the strip to the border box. Whichever is chosen, state in a comment WHY the offsets are not zero, or the next person will "tidy" them back.

Check it against the card's 6px radius: the strip's square ends already sit slightly proud at the corners (a known, accepted ~3px x 0.4px artifact from attn-11g4.4). Extending to the border must not make that materially worse.
acceptance_criteria: The accent strip is exactly flush with the card's top and bottom outer edges at every card state; square ends, 3px width, author/kind/state colours and isolation all preserved; verified at 2x in Paper and Ink.
notes: VERIFIED in the built binary, both themes: card height 96px, strip spans -1px to -1px against a 1px border = 96px painted, border-radius 0, isolation:isolate intact, colour resolving to the participant hue. left:0 is deliberate (1px border, then 3px accent) and now stated as a decision in the comment — left:-1px would cost 6px of corner overhang vs the 1px this costs.

title: Review card polish, margin connector removal, avatar identity, and local-web share repair

Eight issues reported from a session on the built desktop app plus the local web build, after the attn-11g4 / attn-vlmz wave.

Three of these are REGRESSIONS FROM THAT WAVE and are called out as such in their children — the accent strip's height, and the share-mint hang on local web. Owning that explicitly so nobody re-derives whether they are new.

The rest split into: review-card information design (the kind badge carries no information the header does not already imply, while the timestamp is buried), a margin connector nobody wants, an identity bug where the user's chosen avatar colour is ignored, and two places that should carry the primary accent and do not.

title: HTML annotation: pre-merge sign-off + hardening follow-ups (attn-61t)

The implementation epic attn-61t is CLOSED and a post-hoc adversarial review (3 independent reviewers over the full diff) confirmed the architecture; the quick fixes it surfaced are already committed on the branch (byte-cap truncation for CJK/emoji, surrogate-safe offset mapping, last-</body> injection + double-inject guard, inbound HtmlAnchor validation, HTML-suggestion rejection, hydrateSnapshot annotation carry-through, hosted-side local resolution verdicts, composer snapshot-identity capture). What remains needs a human or a design decision, not more code review.

title: Table serializer silently destroys data: inline marks stripped, escaped pipes corrupt the table
description:
Two PRE-EXISTING serializer defects found while capturing a byte-identity baseline for attn-11g4.8. Neither was caused by that work; both are silent data loss on save, which makes them more severe than anything in either UI epic.

1. INLINE MARKS STRIPPED INSIDE TABLE CELLS. Round-tripping a table through markdownParser -> markdownSerializer loses formatting in cells: backtick-code becomes plain text, bold becomes plain text, and links lose their target entirely. A user who writes a table with a link in it, opens the file in attn, and saves, gets a file with the link destroyed.

2. ESCAPED PIPE CORRUPTS THE TABLE. A cell containing an escaped pipe serializes as a BARE pipe, which markdown then reads as a column delimiter, so the table gains a phantom column and the row structure breaks on the next read. This is worse than losing formatting: it changes the document's shape.

Root cause is in the table serializer at web/src/lib/schema.ts (~:648), which reads attrs.align and cell CONTENT and discards mark information.

OPEN QUESTION to resolve first (asked of the agent that found it): is the mark loss serializer-only, or does the parser also fail to produce marks inside cells? Does a bold cell render bold in the editor and lose it on save, or was it never bold to begin with? Serializer-only means live data loss on every save of an existing file and is P1; parser-side means the feature never worked and is a lower-priority gap.
acceptance_criteria: A table containing inline code, bold, italics and links round-trips byte-exact through parse then serialize; a cell containing an escaped pipe round-trips without gaining a column; regression tests cover all of the above; the fix does not disturb the byte-identity established for plain tables in attn-11g4.8.
notes:
DIAGNOSIS COMPLETE — SERIALIZER ONLY, and the severity is higher than first filed.

The parser is FINE. Measured against the real parser, a cell containing bold/code/link/em/strikethrough produces every mark correctly, INCLUDING the link's href. A control run proves the same serializer handles those exact marks perfectly in a paragraph. The loss is entirely in the table path. So it IS bold in the editor and loses it on save — the worse of the two possibilities, i.e. live data loss on every save rather than a feature that never worked.

ROOT CAUSE 1 (marks), schema.ts:767-779 in renderTableRow:
  const cellSerializer = new MarkdownSerializer(markdownSerializer.nodes, markdownSerializer.marks);
  const text = cellSerializer.serialize(cell).trim().replace(/\n/g, ' ');
MarkdownSerializer.serialize() runs renderContent, which walks children as BLOCKS and calls each node's own serializer. Mark delimiters are only ever emitted by renderInline. A table_cell holds inline*, so every mark is silently dropped on the way out. Fix: render cell content via state.renderInline(cell). Also removes a MarkdownSerializer allocated per cell.

ROOT CAUSE 2 (escaped pipe) — same function, DIFFERENT cause, needs its own fix. The parser correctly resolves "x \| y" to the literal text "x | y"; the serializer then writes that bare | into a pipe-delimited row. Generic markdown escaping cannot catch it because | only needs escaping inside a table, which is context state.text() does not have. It must be escaped where the cell is joined.

SEVERITY — TWO SAVES TO UNRECOVERABLE CONTENT LOSS:
  save 1: "| x | y | keep |"   (pipe unescaped -> 3 cells in a 2-column table)
  save 2: "| x | y |"          (markdown-it truncates to the header's column count)
"keep" is gone permanently. Not just layout corruption — content destruction.

AND THE USER NEVER HAS TO TOUCH THE TABLE. serializeAccepted() (Editor.svelte:169-176) serializes the WHOLE document, so any save rewrites the entire file. Opening a doc and editing one paragraph flattens every formatted table in it.
FIXED AND INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. Re-ran the 10-table byte-identity baseline from attn-11g4.8: 8 of 10 byte-identical, and the ONLY two that changed are the two bug cases, both going from lossy to identity round-trips.

Fix 1 (marks): renderTableRow now wraps the cell's content in a paragraph inside a doc before serializing. That is the whole trick — serialize() runs renderContent which walks children as blocks, so handing it the cell rendered inline children through the text serializer and never emitted a mark delimiter; routing through a paragraph reaches the paragraph serializer, whose body is renderInline. Public API only (MarkdownSerializerState's constructor and out are @internal). The per-cell MarkdownSerializer allocation is gone.

Fix 2 (pipes): escapeCellPipes escapes every | in the FULLY RENDERED cell string. The library's escapeExtraCharacters option would have been wrong — it applies inside esc(), and two paths bypass esc() entirely: inline code (the code mark carries escape:false) and link destinations (escaped only for parens and quotes). GFM resolves cell-level backslash-pipe before inline parsing, so it is correct inside a code span.

Independently verified by me from inside the module graph: marks / escaped-pipes / plain / prose-pipe all cycle1=IDENTICAL and cycle2-stable=YES. The prose case confirms the escape is correctly scoped to the cell renderer and does not leak into ordinary text.

31 tests in table-serializer.test.ts. Every pipe case asserts TWO save cycles, because a single cycle passes while the document is already broken. One case was corrected mid-flight rather than forced: a pipe in a link destination serializes as %7C, which is markdown-it percent-encoding at parse time (a link in a plain paragraph normalizes identically) — table-independent URL normalization, not loss, converging after one save.

title: Verify HTML annotation in a running app + run the dual-instance E2E
description:
attn-61t shipped with no interactive verification. The runtime and the shell bridge are covered by 12 real-browser Playwright tests, and everything typechecks, but the shell wiring was never exercised in a running app.

Specifically unverified:
- Margin card placement against live frame geometry (cards are positioned from rects the frame reports over postMessage; the push-down collision layout has only ever run on ProseMirror coords).

- The rail toggle / mobile sheet for an annotatable HTML doc.
