title: Add canonical workspace manifest, asset snapshots, and browser Rust anchor index
description:
## Objective

Define and implement the missing canonical native/browser workspace snapshot protocol required by attn-7xl.4.3: versioned manifests, arbitrary binary asset payloads, stable entry identities, and the exact Rust/comrak anchor index in browser-owned Markdown snapshots.

## Constraints

- Additive coordinated native+browser protocol; never a web-only shape.
- Preserve existing Markdown/HTML canonical JSON bytes.
- Normalized root-relative paths only; no OPFS/local paths.
- Relay/R2 remain content-blind.
- Browser must use the canonical Rust indexer (WASM/shared crate), not a TypeScript approximation.
design: Use a docType-tagged SnapshotPlaintext union. Add asset payloads with unpadded base64url bytes + mediaType, and workspace_manifest with sorted manifest entries {fileId,snapshotId,path,kind,mediaType?,byteLength,contentHash}. Publish entries first and the manifest last; advance the sealed share publication pointer only after all durable ACKs. Extract/reuse the Rust comrak anchor builder for the browser through WASM.
acceptance_criteria: Rust and browser canonical vectors match byte-for-byte for Markdown, HTML, asset, and workspace_manifest payloads; nested paths and arbitrary binary bytes round-trip browser↔native; browser Markdown carries the exact Rust-built AnchorIndex; old Markdown/HTML bytes remain unchanged; tamper/path/media/length/hash checks fail closed; mailbox and R2 paths stay content-blind.
notes: Approach: preserve existing markdown/html canonical JSON by keeping the Rust SnapshotPlaintext struct shape compatible while adding validated optional fields/docType variants for asset and workspace_manifest; mirror it as a strict TS union. Publish normalized, path-sorted entry snapshots first and a signed manifest snapshot last; persist stable FileId mappings + manifest pointer under the sealed workspace share capability; mark published only after every durable ACK. Expose the exact existing src/review/anchors/index.rs implementation to the browser through a small wasm-pack crate that compiles the same source via a compatible module shim, then dynamically load it from the publisher (never a TS approximation or landing/app static import). Files: new crates/attn-anchor-wasm/** + generated web loader/package; Rust src/review/model.rs, bootstrap.rs, manager.rs and focused tests/vectors; web types.ts, browser-session.ts, browser-snapshot-publisher.ts/tests, browser-workspace-share.ts/tests. Test plan: old markdown/html canonical bytes unchanged; Rust/browser full-byte vectors for markdown/html/asset/manifest; invalid UTF-8/arbitrary binary/NUL; strict normalized paths/sort/duplicates/media/hash/length/tamper; exact Rust WASM AnchorIndex parity; mailbox/R2 ordering/retry/content blindness; native/browser hydration. Baseline: cargo check -p attn exit 0; cargo nextest baseline external relay quota failure at three_peer_comment_converges_async after 823 pass; npm check/test exit 0 (58 files).
close_reason: Canonical workspace manifest/assets and exact Rust/WASM anchor protocol implemented, interoperably validated, crash-safe, and security-reviewed.

title: Implement attn review verdicts --wait (block on verdict stream)
description:
Block until every listed suggestion (default: all own pending) has a verdict; exit 0 with the JSON verdict map, non-zero on --timeout. Park on the inbound verdict envelope stream (WS/DataChannel push already flows through the transport) — wait on a condition, never poll.

## Files
- src/cli_review.rs (--wait, --for <id,...>, --timeout <dur>)
- src/review/manager.rs (verdict subscription surface for the CLI/daemon boundary)

## Approach
Register interest in the target suggestion set, drain current state first (verdicts may already be complete), then await import-pipeline notifications. Timeout path exits non-zero with partial map on stderr/JSON. This is the agent gate: submit* -> verdicts --wait -> branch.

## Verification
- cargo build
- cargo test (wait resolves on already-complete set without blocking; resolves on late-arriving verdict; times out non-zero)
- Smoke: dual-instance — reviewer runs verdicts --wait in background, owner accepts, wait returns 0 with the map

## Plan Reference
- planning/sharing/README.md (Workstream D)
notes: Approach: add a tokio::watch verdict revision signal to ReviewManager; subscribe before reading persisted verdicts, snapshot the default target as all own pending suggestions (or use explicit --for ids), return immediately if complete, otherwise await watch::Receiver::changed with an optional deadline. Notify only after imported SuggestionAccepted/SuggestionRejected events (already persisted by InboundPipeline). Extend daemon socket with a typed wait request/response and run wait on a per-connection handler so other daemon commands remain responsive. CLI adds --wait, --for comma-list, --timeout duration; wait implies JSON; timeout prints partial JSON to stderr and exits non-zero. Files: src/review/manager.rs, src/daemon.rs, src/cli_review.rs. Tests: already-complete returns immediately; late persisted verdict wakes without polling; timeout returns partial state; CLI duration/options; concurrent socket responsiveness.
close_reason: Implemented and validated event-driven verdict waiting with fixed own-pending/explicit target sets, race-free subscribe-before-drain watch notifications, typed daemon streaming boundary, timeout partial JSON/non-zero exit, and responsive concurrent socket handling. Tests: 21 verdict-focused executions pass; cargo build/fmt/clippy pass; real relay dual-daemon smoke proved block-before-accept and wake-on-import with matching resulting_hash; release binary 31.08 MiB under 32 MiB.

title: Sharing v3: durable links, notifications, permission tiers, acceptance gate
description:
Make sharing a real category on top of the v2 review protocol: share URLs that keep resolving (durable shares), an async notification loop (native + browser Web Push), sender-controlled permission tiers (view/comment/suggest), and a first-class acceptance gate so agents block until the author has ruled on every suggestion. Live co-editing is explicitly out of scope; the collaboration verb is suggest.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] A share URL resolves for 90+ days (owner-renewed), survives room expiry, and is owner-revocable
- [ ] View-only links are cryptographically enforced by the relay; comment/suggest tiers enforced at import
- [ ] Comments arriving while away produce native (daemon) and browser (Web Push) notifications, relay staying content-blind
- [ ] An agent can submit suggestions from a worktree diff and block on `attn review verdicts --wait` until the owner rules on all of them

## Architecture
- Rooms stay ephemeral (decision #8); durability comes from a small relay-side share indirection holding the current roomId + latest encrypted snapshot
- Capability = which keys the URL carries: read keys vs write-admission key split in the HKDF tree (amends decision #2)
- Web Push is a content-free ping; the service worker decrypts locally via the remembered-room capability (decision #13)
- Owner-accepts-everything is the invariant; agents submit, humans decide (unchanged from v2)

## Plan Reference
- planning/sharing/README.md
- planning/collab/amendments.md (16 locked v2 decisions this plan amends/preserves)
notes: All Sharing v3 workstreams complete and independently reviewed: acceptance gate, cryptographic view/comment/suggest tiers, durable share lifecycle, native async loop, and content-blind browser Web Push. Real production-boundary native/browser/relay E2Es pass. Follow-up multi-room native WS stall tracked separately as attn-eaw.

notes: Approach: browser-workspace-lease.ts WorkspaceLeaseManager over the existing workspace_leases store + WorkspaceStore fencing checks (2.3). acquire(): single readwrite IDB tx (serialized across tabs) — grants when absent/expired/same-holder, bumps fencingToken on takeover, returns null when another live holder owns it (caller enters read-only). heartbeat(): extends expiresAt only for exact holder+token, else StorageConflictError. release(): deletes only if owned. BroadcastChannel 'attn-workspace-lease' advisory notifications (injectable factory; never decides correctness). Tests: fresh grant, live-holder denial, expiry takeover fences old holder's store writes, heartbeat extend/conflict, release/reacquire token monotonicity, concurrent acquire race yields one winner, channel events.
close_reason: Fenced cross-tab writer leases landed (browser-workspace-lease.ts): WorkspaceLeaseManager decides ownership via serialized IDB readwrite transactions — acquire grants on absent/expired/released/same-holder and bumps the fencing token on takeover (returns null while another holder is live, so secondary tabs stay read-only); heartbeat extends only for the exact holder+token, else StorageConflictError; release writes an expired tombstone preserving the token counter so fencing tokens are monotonic and the releasing holder is immediately fenced. BroadcastChannel notifications are advisory only (injectable, never authoritative). Combined with 2.3's mutation fencing, a suspended zombie tab cannot write after losing its lease. description:

## Implementation notes

## Source

planning/web-authoring/01-storage-foundation.md
acceptance_criteria: Normal Markdown workspaces work without OPFS; successful OPFS writes are integrity-checked; crashes cannot expose plaintext or lose the last committed revision.
notes: Approach: SealedBody gains 'idb-large' fallback variant (validator caps: idb<=512KiB inline, idb-large<=MAX_BODY+tag). WorkspaceStore takes {filesystem, inlineThresholdBytes} (BrowserStorage.workspaces passes its OPFS-backed SealedBlobFileSystem). Seal routing: sealed>threshold && fs -> OPFS via write-ahead gc-intent (gc record committed first, file written to opaque sha256-derived path, read-back verified, revision commit tx deletes intent); any OPFS failure falls back to idb-large + best-effort file delete. openBody supports opfs (length check + AEAD auth) and idb-large. sweepGc() deletes orphaned files then intents. deleteWorkspace deletes the workspace OPFS prefix. Tests with in-memory fault-injectable filesystem: routing, corrupt-file fail-closed, absent-OPFS fallback, write-failure fallback, crash-orphan sweep, threshold config, rename/delete of opfs bodies.
close_reason: Encrypted OPFS tier + IDB fallback landed: sealed bodies over a configurable threshold route to OPFS at opaque sha256-derived paths (no workspace/revision id leakage) behind a write-ahead GC intent (intent committed first, file written + read-back verified, revision commit tx clears the intent); any OPFS absence/failure falls back to encrypted IndexedDB (inline 'idb' under the 512KiB cap, new 'idb-large' variant above it) so no operation ever blocks on OPFS. sweepGc() deletes orphaned files/intents and workspace prefixes; live committed files survive sweeps; rename/delete retire OPFS bodies through the ledger; deleteWorkspace records a durable prefix-removal intent then executes it. BrowserStorage.workspaces now passes its OPFS-backed filesystem. title: Implement atomic workspace transactions
description:
## Objective

Add crash-safe create, rename, delete, select, immutable revision commit, and head-advance APIs with monotonic timestamps and fencing conflict checks.

## Implementation notes

## Source

acceptance_criteria: Multi-record operations are atomic, immutable history is preserved, stale writers cannot advance heads, and errors leave a recoverable committed state.
notes: Approach: new browser-workspace-store.ts (WorkspaceStore, exposed as BrowserStorage.workspaces getter) + browser-idb.ts shared helpers (requestValue/transactionDone/isConstraintError). Seal-outside-transaction design: WebCrypto cannot be awaited inside an IDB tx, so commit paths pre-seal with a tentative clock and retry (bounded) if the workspace clock moved; final write is one atomic multi-store tx (workspaces+entries+revisions+gc) enforcing head expectation, path uniqueness (store keys + unique history index), strictly-increasing per-workspace clock, clamped monotonic wall timestamps, and optional lease fencing checks (full lease lifecycle lands in 2.6). Rename re-seals the head at the new path (AAD binds path) and GC-queues old revisions; delete tombstones + GC-queues; deleteWorkspace crypto-erases key first. OPFS bodies deferred to 2.4 (loader throws typed error). Immutable history via [workspaceId,path,clock] unique index; idempotent commits dedupe by revisionId+bodyHash.
close_reason: Atomic workspace transactions landed (browser-workspace-store.ts, exposed as BrowserStorage.workspaces): createWorkspace (one-click: workspace+entry+revision in one tx; orphan-key retry), createEntry (path uniqueness, tombstone revive, entry cap), commitRevision (optimistic expectedHead, idempotent revisionId replay, conflict on id/content mismatch), renameEntry (re-seals head at new path since AAD binds path; retires old revisions; selection follows), deleteEntry (tombstone + revision retirement + selection clear), selectEntry, deleteWorkspace (crypto-erases key first). Seal-outside-tx design with bounded clock-race retries since WebCrypto cannot run inside an IDB tx; per-workspace clock strictly increases; wall timestamps clamped monotonic; optional lease fencing checks (lifecycle in 2.6); OPFS bodies typed-error until 2.4. IDB helpers extracted to browser-idb.ts. Validation: 13 new cases covering atomicity, idempotency, conflicts, aborted tx leaving prior head intact, backwards wall clock, fencing; 47/47 unit files, svelte-check 0, bundle gate green.

title: Relay: prune stale persisted per-device rate buckets
description: DurableObjectRateLimit persists one rate_v2:<device>:<minute> row per active device/minute and documents alarm cleanup, but RoomDO alarm never imports or prunes RATE_KEY_PREFIX/LEGACY_RATE_KEY_PREFIX. title: Relay: bound env_idx idempotency tombstone growth
description: Signal FIFO and owner-ACK deletion must retain env_idx tombstones so timed-out POST retries cannot resurrect, recharge, or rebroadcast deleted ciphertext. However live envelope_count/bytes debit frees capacity while each unique envelopeId leaves durable metadata until room cleanup; a long-lived admitted peer can rotate unique signal/event IDs and grow tombstones far beyond policy.maxEvents despite per-request rate limits. Add an explicit bounded tombstone/lifetime-event budget or compact authenticated dedupe structure, account its storage, expire safely without breaking retry semantics, and add sustained-rotation cost/cap regressions. Services must remain content-blind.
notes: Paused after research/baseline only; no source edits. Reprioritized to hosted web-first vertical slice and Cloudflare staging per user direction. Existing design notes remain valid for later implementation.

title: Relay: encode opaque identifiers before composing storage keys

Crafted opaque IDs containing ':' or NUL can alias keys, break parsing, or mix accounting/routing buckets. Define a canonical key-safe encoding (for example base64url UTF-8 or length-prefix segments), migrate/dual-read existing rows safely, restrict new wire identifiers if protocol-compatible, and add collision/control-character regressions without exposing content.

title: Relay: make inline/R2 byte accounting atomic and exact

title: Relay: durable per-IP quota + global byte ceiling on room creation
description:
Anonymous room creation is only bounded by in-memory per-isolate rate limits (relay/src/rate-limit.ts:55-60), which reset on cold start and don't coordinate across isolates/colos. Per-room caps (25 MiB, 500 events, 24h TTL) bound each room, but nothing durably bounds the aggregate: a determined actor can create-and-fill rooms toward a steady-state of hundreds of GB per IP within the 24h TTL window.

What needs to be done:
1. Durable per-IP quota — a small quota DO keyed by IP (or /24) consulted at POST /v2/rooms/:roomId: max N concurrent live rooms and M bytes/day per IP. Decrement on room expiry/delete.
2. Global circuit breaker — track total live rooms / total bytes across the namespace with an env-var ceiling; flip room creation to 503 when exceeded so the failure mode is 'service degraded' not 'surprise bill'.
3. Keep anonymous defaults tight (24h TTL, 25 MiB); registration later just raises policy limits — the tiering seam already exists.

Context: relay/src/room-do.ts:459-668 (room create), relay/src/index.ts:284-289 (create rate limit), planning/collab/relay-spec.md cost strategy ('no unbounded rooms').
notes:
Approach: add a singleton SQLite QuotaDO that atomically reserves the full HARD_MAX_ROOM_BYTES for each first-created room, enforcing per-source live-room and rolling-24h allocation limits plus global live-room/reserved-byte circuit breakers without observing content. Worker derives an HMAC source bucket only from CF-Connecting-IP and overwrites a private DO header; RoomDO acquires after owner signature+PoW, stores a generation lease, and idempotently releases it after explicit delete or alarm expiry. Rejoins/read/delete stay available when global admission is closed. Files: relay/src/{quota-do,quota,index,env,room-do}.ts, relay/wrangler.toml, relay tests, relay/spec docs. Tests: QuotaDO atomic boundary/idempotency/rolling-window/release tests; Worker first-create/rejoin/source/global/fail-closed integration; full relay typecheck+296-test baseline regression suite. Conservative invariant: quota counts reserved ciphertext capacity, not plaintext or content; services still cannot decrypt user data.
Completed: durable singleton SQLite QuotaDO reserves 25 MiB capacity per generation; source HMAC (/32 IPv4, /64 IPv6), per-source live/rolling-byte limits, global room/byte circuit breakers, confirmed leases, serialized RoomDO mutations, generation-bound one-shot R2 uploads, cleanup tombstone retries, bounded metadata, and separate production/staging R2 buckets. Validation 2026-07-09: npm run typecheck passed; full relay suite 22 files / 324 tests passed; real headless Chromium via Playwright passed health=200, 8 creates=201, ninth=429 ATTN_SOURCE_ROOM_QUOTA with retryAfterMs=60000, authenticated rejoin=200. Independent security audit found no attn-tdj blocker; remaining exact-accounting and reservation-lifecycle hardening are tracked in attn-8h5 and attn-64x.
close_reason: Implemented durable source quotas and global capacity circuit breakers with fail-closed confirmed leases, cleanup retention, and comprehensive regression/browser validation (324 tests plus Playwright Chromium E2E).

title: Onboarding: user display name (prompt on first share/join, default from git)
description:

(2) Frontend: profile state from init; NamePrompt modal on first share/join; edit-later affordance; prefer Participant.display_name in peer/author resolution. notes: CORE SHIPPED (commit 531ebaa on branch editorial-ux-and-collab-sync; NOT yet pushed to main). title: Connection badge shows Offline though WebRTC is connected (live_direct dropped when owner is on local doc)
description:
SYMPTOM: In a 2-party GUI share (owner + reviewer), the connection badge shows 'Offline' even though the WebRTC DataChannel is fully connected and carrying collab data. This is almost certainly the source of the user-reported 'sync feels broken / WebRTC isn't working' perception — WebRTC IS primary and connected; the badge just doesn't show it.

EVIDENCE (test:webrtc:live + temporary tracing): the DataChannel connects in ~100ms on localhost (create_offer -> badge-eval connected=1 = 100ms). The Rust manager correctly computes all_live (peers=1, transports=1, connected=1) and emits ReviewUpdate::ConnectionChanged{connection:'live_direct'}. Co-typing edits and a review comment both propagate. Only the badge is wrong (data-state stays 'offline'). So the bug is purely frontend.

ROOT CAUSE: web/src/lib/review/store.svelte.ts applyConnection() updates the active badge (this.connection) ONLY when currentRoomId === payload.roomId (early-returns otherwise). The OWNER, by design (attn-0wa), stays on its LOCAL doc rather than flipping to the shared-room view, so currentRoomId is not the shared room; the 'live_direct' update is recorded on the per-room record via upsertRoom but never reaches this.connection, so the global badge stays at its 'offline' default. (Reviewer also showed offline in test:webrtc:live — confirm whether its currentRoomId is set by the raw review_join IPC path vs the UI join used by the editorial E2E.)

RECOMMENDED FIX: the connection badge should reflect the connection state of the room the user is actually participating in / sharing, independent of which doc the editor is showing. Options: (a) when the owner shares, treat the shared room as the badge's room even while viewing the local doc; (b) have the badge read the per-room connection (upsertRoom already stores it) for the active share rather than only this.connection gated on currentRoomId. Decide the desired UX for 'owner viewing local doc while sharing'. Add a badge assertion to scripts/test-editorial-e2e.sh and make scripts/test-webrtc-live-e2e.sh green.

NOTE: functionally non-blocking (collab converges, WebRTC is primary), but high perceived-severity — it makes working WebRTC look broken.
close_reason: Fixed in d2fbe17 (on main). applyConnection now keeps status.connection in sync with this.connection, so the ConnectionBadge no longer reads a stale 'offline'. Verified: test:webrtc:live 7→9/9 (owner+reviewer badges flip to live_direct), editorial E2E 13/0/0, svelte-check 0 errors/0 warnings.

title: Faithful no-TURN partition: block peer UDP so ICE fails (validates attn-7qv)
description: The attn-orf 'partition' scenario applies iptables DROP between agent container IPs, but the WebRTC DataChannel still forms (connected=2) — ICE finds a path the rule doesn't cover (likely srflx via host-gateway, or an iptables-nft backend mismatch in debian-slim). Result: relay-only fallback is never exercised, so attn-7qv's per-peer routing is unvalidated. Make the partition truly sever the peer-to-peer path: default-DROP all egress/ingress, ALLOW only the relay (host.docker.internal:8787 TCP for WS+outbox) and loopback; verify direct UDP between agents is dead (e.g. ICE never reaches Connected). Then assert collab + comments STILL converge across owner/rvB/rvC via relay only. That run is the real no-TURN symmetric-NAT repro and the validation gate for attn-7qv.
close_reason: Done: partition now blocks ALL UDP (path-independent), with a no-live_direct faithfulness assert. Mesh provably can't form; relay-only convergence confirmed.

title: No TURN server: WebRTC mesh fails across symmetric NAT (cross-machine desync root cause)
description: STUN-only, no TURN (webrtc.rs DEFAULT_STUN_SERVER only; security-review.md + relay-spec.md confirm 'no TURN server stood up / STUN only'). Symmetric-NAT peer-pairs can't form direct DataChannels -> partial WebRTC mesh across real networks -> asymmetric drops in both co-typing and comments. User confirms desync is across-machines for both. Fix: stand up a TURN server (coturn or a managed TURN), plumb TURN URLs+short-lived credentials into WebRtcConfig.ice_servers(), and add ice_transport_policy handling. This is the real NAT-traversal fix.
close_reason: User constraint: NO TURN, ever. NAT traversal for symmetric-NAT peers must be solved via a reliable per-peer relay data-fallback instead (attn-7qv), not TURN.

title: Docker topology matrix harness (NAT / loss / partition / relay-only)
description: Compose: relay container + N headless-agent containers + a coordinator. Use network namespaces + tc netem/iptables to exercise NAT traversal, packet loss/latency, partition+reconnect, and relay-only fallback (block UDP to force WS). Assert events.jsonl + doc convergence across all peers per topology. Depends on T3.
notes: NOW CONVERGES 4/4 in baseline AND partition (commit f60cde1). Two fixes were needed, BOTH unrelated to the transport: (1) re-entrant mutex deadlock in the headless agent — handle_line held current_room across manager.submit (MutexGuard in match scrutinee lives the whole block), and submit's synchronous EventImported sink re-locks the same mutex -> deadlock after the first comment, starving all later commands incl. collab; (2) control channel: docker -i stdin AND bind-mounted FIFO/file all drop rapid writes on Docker Desktop (FUSE attr-cache staleness / no streaming) — replaced with a CONTAINER-LOCAL file the agent polls (ATTN_AGENT_CMD_FILE) that the harness appends to via docker exec. Verified collab is WebRTC-primary: sender routes channels=true relay=false, peers receive Collab over the DataChannel. The earlier owner-Share-hang is gone with these fixes. REMAINING GAP: the 'partition' scenario does NOT actually sever the mesh (connected=2 even under iptables DROP of inter-agent IPs — ICE finds a path around it), so relay-only fallback is NOT yet exercised. See follow-up bead for a faithful UDP/peer-path block.
close_reason: Harness built, trustworthy, and converges: baseline (WebRTC mesh) + faithful partition (UDP blackout, relay-only) both 4/4. Reliable container-local control channel; deadlock root-caused+fixed. NAT/loss profiles remain as future netem work but the core partition/relay-only matrix is proven.

title: Fix: fan review events across the WebRTC mesh (parity with send_collab)
description: FINDING (attn-sls): review events already converge to all peers via the relay in all modes on localhost, so this is NOT a drop-fix. It remains valid as the user's stated intent ('as much over WebRTC as possible; WS mostly for signaling'): optionally route review events over the live_webrtc mesh (parity with send_collab) to cut relay cost/latency, with relay as the fallback when the mesh is incomplete. Re-prioritize after the topology-layer repro (attn-orf) shows whether mesh peers actually drop events under partition/NAT.
close_reason: Landed in 32b2dd7; validated in the Docker harness — review-event Envelopes (kind=Event) are delivered over the WebRTC DataChannel to all connected peers (inbound Signal/Event confirmed), with the relay/outbox still covering un-meshed peers.

title: Deterministic in-process mesh-convergence test (reproduce review-event drop)
description: Build a CI-friendly, no-UDP harness: in-process mesh bus + injected mock WebRtcSender/MailboxSender (selector already supports handle injection) driving N ReviewManager peers. Assert that BOTH a collab step AND a review event from reviewerB converge to reviewerC. The review-event assertion FAILS today (red test reproducing the bug); collab passes. Lock the mock-relay deliverableTo contract: event->all subscribers, signal target=null->all, signal target=X->X only.
notes: DONE: tests/review_sync_convergence.rs landed. 3-peer, real Miniflare relay (gated by ATTN_SKIP_CONFORMANCE/wrangler), no UDP. Asserts reviewerB comment converges to owner+reviewerC in live/hybrid/async. ALL PASS -> rules out the relay-mediated review-event layer as the cause of asymmetric loss. Reusable as a regression guard and as the harness skeleton for topology fault-injection.
close_reason: Deterministic in-process convergence harness built and passing; relay-mediated review-event path proven sound on localhost in all modes. Bug localized away from this layer.

title: Bulletproof collab sync testing + fix asymmetric review-event loss
description: Multi-user (3+) collab drops review events (comments/suggestions) asymmetrically: a non-owner reviewer's comment reaches the owner but not other reviewers. Root cause: review events route through selector::send_envelopes over a SINGLE webrtc arm (no mesh fan-out), the owner never re-fans inbound events (manager.rs forward_transport_event:2543), and Live mode keeps no relay WS subscription (mailbox=None) so relay broadcast can't cover the gap. Co-typing is unaffected because send_collab fans across the live_webrtc mesh map. Intent: WebRTC carries data to all peers; WS is for signaling. Deliver a layered, deterministic test harness (in-process mesh-convergence first, then headless-agent + Docker topology matrix) and fix the fan-out.
notes: ITEM 1 (top priority): cross-machine sync drop. Conflict-resolution LOGIC is solid (real OT co-typing, three-way suggestion merge, anchor remap — all tested on localhost), but on a real network the no-TURN partial mesh + send_collab's all-or-nothing 'skip relay when mesh complete' (manager.rs:1186) means OT steps AND suggestion/comment delivery can silently DROP for un-meshable peers. This is what makes the rest feel broken. Pieces: attn-7qv (P0 per-peer relay-fallback fix), attn-orf (Docker symmetric-NAT repro/guard), attn-woc (events over mesh).
close_reason: EPIC complete. All children closed: attn-8zd (headless agent), attn-orf (topology harness), attn-7qv (per-peer relay fallback, VALIDATED), attn-ms7 (faithful partition), attn-woc (mesh event fan-out). Collab is WebRTC-primary with a proven no-TURN relay fallback; the agent deadlock that masked it is fixed. Cross-topology convergence demonstrated in Docker (baseline mesh + UDP-blackout relay-only, both 4/4).

title: Inbound envelope pipeline (decrypt + verify + import)
description: Per ServerFrame::Envelope from the WS stream: look up the per-kind key (eventKey | snapshotKey | signalKey) from room state, AES-256-GCM decrypt, verify Ed25519 signature against the deviceId's publicSigningKey from the cached /devices roster, dedupe by EventId (against ~/.attn/reviews/rooms/<roomId>/events.jsonl ledger), append to events.jsonl, update the persistent sync cursor. On success emit ReviewUpdate::EventImported into the ReviewManager event loop.
acceptance_criteria:
- For each ServerFrame::Envelope: select key by envelope.kind; decrypt (AES-256-GCM, nonce per crypto-spec §Nonce Discipline) — failure → ReviewUpdate::DecryptFailed and continue (do not crash, do not advance cursor)
- Ed25519 verify plaintext signature against device.publicSigningKey from cached /devices snapshot; signature failure → drop + ReviewUpdate::SignatureInvalid (do not advance cursor for that envelope)
- Dedupe by EventId: if already present in events.jsonl skip the append (but still advance the seq cursor)
- Append the canonical event bytes to events.jsonl (append-only, fsync per batch)
- Update last_seen_seq AFTER successful append (so a crash mid-write replays cleanly)
- Emit ReviewUpdate::EventImported{event} to the consumer (Phase 4 UI / ReviewManager)
- Cached /devices roster auto-refreshed when an envelope arrives signed by an unknown deviceId (issue GET /devices and retry verify once)
- Tests: happy path, wrong key, wrong sig, duplicate EventId, unknown device triggers refresh + verify

title: Outbox processor (~/.attn/reviews/rooms/<roomId>/outbox.jsonl)
description: Persistent outbox that survives crashes. Each line in outbox.jsonl is a queued MailboxEnvelope plus state metadata (attempts, last_error, status: pending|in_flight|sent). Processor reads pending entries, mints a PoW token from the Phase 0a token pool, batches up to 32, POSTs to /v2/rooms/:roomId/envelopes, and on success marks them sent (compaction sweeps sent lines out periodically). Backoff on 429/507/ATTN_POW_*. EnvelopeId is deterministic (see crypto-spec) so retries are server-side idempotent.
acceptance_criteria:
- ~/.attn/reviews/rooms/<roomId>/outbox.jsonl created on first send; append-only with periodic compaction of sent entries
- Each line: serde JSON {envelope, attempts, last_error?, status, queued_at}
- Processor task per room: read pending → mint PoW (use Phase 0a token pool) → batch up to 32 → POST → on 2xx mark sent
- Backoff: 429 honors Retry-After header; 507 ATTN_ROOM_EVENT_CAP/STORAGE_FULL → exponential backoff with cap (e.g., 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 30s); ATTN_POW_* → mint fresh token immediately (token reuse failure)
- Crash safety: status:in_flight entries are reset to pending on startup so they re-send; deterministic envelopeId guarantees server dedupe

title: Rate limiting (per-IP, per-device, anti-enumeration)
description: Two-tier rate limiting. Worker edge (before DO): per-IP 600/min sliding window using Cloudflare's rate-limiting binding or a KV-backed sliding window, and an anti-enumeration counter that returns 429 after 30 unknown rooms in 5 minutes from one IP. Per-device 120/min in DO storage (sliding window over rate:<deviceId>:<bucket>) checked after admission. All 429 responses include retryAfterMs in body and Retry-After header.
acceptance_criteria:
- Edge per-IP: 600 requests/min sliding window across all rooms; over → 429 ATTN_RATE_LIMITED with retryAfterMs
- Edge anti-enum: 30 unknown rooms (404 ATTN_ROOM_NOT_FOUND triggers) from one IP in 5 min → 429 ATTN_ANTI_ENUMERATION; the unknown-room counter is keyed by IP, not roomId, so the attacker cannot tell which roomId tripped it
- DO per-device: 120 requests/min sliding window over rate:<deviceId>:<minute-bucket> entries; over → 429 ATTN_RATE_LIMITED
- 429 responses set Retry-After header (seconds, rounded up) AND body {error:{code, retryAfterMs}}
- Edge limits checked before the request crosses to the DO (cost protection)
- Per-device limits checked after admission so they're attributable

title: Alarms: idle + hard-max TTL + pow-prune
description: DO alarms drive room TTL cleanup. Cloudflare DO supports only one pending alarm at a time, so always schedule at min(hard_max_at, last_event_at + idleTimeoutMs, next_pow_prune_at). On fire, determine which deadline tripped and act: idle/hard-max → close all WS with 4002 (room expired), wipe DO storage, schedule R2 cleanup; pow-prune → delete pow_seen entries past expiresAt+10min. Every WS connect calls cleanup_check() if now is within 1h of expires_at (decision #9). Hard-max defaults: 24h, or 7d when policy.longSession=true (decision #8). Idle default: 1h.
acceptance_criteria:
- alarm() handler reads all candidate deadlines (hard_max_at, last_event_at+idleTimeoutMs, pow_prune_at) and reschedules at the next earliest after acting on any that have fired
- Idle/hard-max fire: broadcast close 4002 with reason 'room_expired', deleteAll() DO storage, enqueue R2 prefix delete, set tombstone so further requests 410 ATTN_ROOM_EXPIRED for 24h
- pow-prune fire: scan meta:pow_seen:* and delete entries where extracted expiresAt+10min < now
- POST /envelopes updates last_event_at and reschedules the alarm
- Every WS upgrade calls cleanup_check() — if now within 1h of expires_at, run the same scan and reschedule
- hard_max_at computed at room creation: created + (longSession ? 7d : 24h), clamped by policy.expiresAt
- Tests: idle expiry path, hard-max expiry path, longSession 7-day cap, single-alarm scheduling correctness when multiple deadlines compete, cleanup_check on WS connect, pow_seen prune

title: POST + GET /v2/rooms/:roomId/blobs — R2 spillover
description: When kind==snapshot_blob and ciphertextBytes > 1 MiB, /envelopes is rejected and the client must use the blob flow. Client uploads ciphertext directly, then re-POSTs /envelopes with the same envelopeId and a small BlobRef payload referencing the R2 key. GET /v2/rooms/:roomId/blobs/:envelopeId returns a 5-min presigned GET URL.

title: POST /v2/rooms/:roomId/envelopes — batched ingest
description: Accept up to 32 envelopes per HTTP request (decision #7). Each envelope is validated end-to-end: ciphertextBytes equals base64url-decoded ciphertext length; size against policy.max{Event|Snapshot}Bytes by kind; deviceId and authorId are registered in the room. Single PoW token covers the whole batch. On any cap overflow (envelope_count > policy.maxEvents OR bytes_used + delta > policy.maxRoomBytes) the whole batch fails with 507. Idempotent on envelopeId. Signal envelopes use sub-caps with FIFO eviction. On success, allocates serverSeq, updates counters, reschedules idle alarm.
acceptance_criteria:
- Batch cap 32: 33+ envelopes → 400 ATTN_BATCH_TOO_LARGE before any work
- Single Attn-PoW token verified once for the whole HTTP request (resource binds METHOD + PATH, not per-envelope)
- Per envelope: ciphertextBytes === base64url_decoded.length else 400 ATTN_ENVELOPE_SIZE_MISMATCH; kind-specific size cap against policy.max{Event|Snapshot}Bytes else 413 ATTN_ENVELOPE_TOO_LARGE; deviceId + authorId registered else 403 ATTN_UNKNOWN_DEVICE
- serverSeq allocated atomically per envelope (monotonic, per relay-spec §serverSeq Allocation)
- Idempotency: existing envelopeId returns its stored serverSeq with no state change
- Whole-batch overflow: 507 ATTN_ROOM_EVENT_CAP or ATTN_ROOM_STORAGE_FULL (no partial commit)
- Signal envelopes: maxSignalEnvelopes=64 per (authorId, target.deviceId), FIFO-evict oldest in DO storage
- Updates meta:envelope_count, meta:bytes_used, meta:last_event_at; reschedules idle alarm
- Broadcasts envelope frames to subscribed WS sessions (hibernation-safe)
- Response: {accepted:[{envelopeId, serverSeq}], serverSeq:<max>}
- Tests: batch over cap, mixed kinds, idempotent retry, room-full, signal eviction, PoW reuse across batch
notes: Spec: planning/collab/relay-spec.md §POST /v2/rooms/:roomId/envelopes (218-269), §serverSeq Allocation (499-512), §Caps (535-555). amendments.md decisions #7 (batch cap + single PoW) and #5 (WS-only delivery: this endpoint feeds the WS broadcast, no HTTP GET pull).

title: DataChannel arm of Transport trait
description: Implement WebRTCTransport against the Transport trait defined in Phase 3b. The crucial property (decision #14, amendments.md §Phase 4): the DataChannel envelope FORMAT is identical to mailbox envelopes — same AEAD under eventKey/snapshotKey, same routing, same import path. No plaintext on the wire (decision #14) — snapshot bytes are application-encrypted, never relying on DTLS for confidentiality.
Trait abstraction allows a single ReviewManager codepath to consume both transports interchangeably.
notes: Specs: planning/collab/amendments.md §Phase 4 + Decision #14. Files: src/review/transport/webrtc.rs (new), src/review/transport.rs (trait). description: relay/src/pow.ts: verify the Attn-PoW header on every write endpoint (POST /devices, POST /envelopes, POST /acks, POST /blobs, DELETE). Token is 8 colon-separated fields, v2 format. Validation order per crypto-spec.md §Server Validation. Replay protection via meta:pow_seen:<expiresAt>:<hash> DO storage entries; a scheduled alarm prunes entries past expiresAt+10min. No client type is exempt (decision #6); default difficulty 16 bits, hard floor 12.
acceptance_criteria:
- Parse the 8-field v2 token; reject unknown version
- Validation in order: parse → v==v2 → difficulty>=max(policy.powBits,12) → expiresAt within 5-min window (not past, not >5min future) → resource matches (roomId, deviceId, base64url(SHA-256(METHOD + space + PATH))[:8]) → leading-zero bits in SHA-256(token bytes) → not in pow_seen replay set
- On success: insert meta:pow_seen:<expiresAt>:<hash> with TTL
- Errors map to ATTN_POW_INVALID (parse/format), ATTN_POW_INSUFFICIENT_DIFFICULTY, ATTN_POW_EXPIRED, ATTN_POW_RESOURCE_MISMATCH, ATTN_POW_REPLAYED — all 403
- Single PoW token per HTTP request — for batch /envelopes the same token covers the whole batch (decision #7)
- Alarm-driven prune loop removes pow_seen entries with expiresAt+10min < now
- Unit tests use vectors from crypto-spec.md §Test Vectors

title: A share with no explicit selection sends none of its images
description:
attn-udu8 publishes the images a shared document references, but only when the share carries an EXPLICIT file selection. Without one a reviewer sees placeholder cards and no frontend change can help, because the bytes were never sent.

The chain, in src/review/bootstrap.rs share_selected:
- record_local_share_selection is called only when has_explicit_selection; otherwise record_local_share is used and no selected_paths are stored.
- selected_share_wire_path returns None for any path absent from record.selected_paths.
- publish_asset_snapshot therefore fails with 'asset has no portable share path', logged and skipped (an image is deliberately never fatal to a share).
- No workspace manifest is published either, and documents fall back to an absolute ownerDisplayPath.

So the CLI path (attn review share <path>, and the legacy share(path) wrapper that passes an empty selection) silently produces a share whose images cannot travel. The native Share dialog always sends a selection, which is why this was invisible during testing — every live verification of attn-udu8 went through the dialog.

Worth deciding rather than patching blind: either the share flow always records a selection (making wire paths universal, which would also give folder-shares a manifest), or the no-selection path is documented as not carrying assets and the daemon says so once per share instead of once per skipped image.
acceptance_criteria: Either a share created without an explicit selection carries its referenced images, or it logs a single clear statement that assets are not included on this path and the limitation is documented. A test covers whichever behavior is chosen.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #17 (draft): snapshot authorship generalized beyond the manifest; wire paths mint for shares with no curated list. Verified live plus mutation-checked forgery tests.

title: dev-collab offers exactly one invite paste, with no retry

title: Markdown image rendering: resolve relative image srcs in the native viewer
description: Images referenced in markdown (e.g. ![diagram](./diagram.png)) never render in the native viewer. The ProseMirror image node emits the raw markdown src verbatim, which resolves against the document origin (attn://app or the Vite dev server) instead of the markdown file's directory, so relative and local-absolute srcs 404. Only https:/data: URLs render. The attn://localhost/<abs-path> protocol handler (src/main.rs) already serves local files with correct MIME — nothing rewrites markdown image srcs to use it.
design: Plan: (1) repro fixture tests/fixtures/images.md + sibling PNG; (2) pure resolver resolveImageSrc(docPath, src) in web/src/lib/markdown-layer.ts — pass through https:/http:/data:/attn: untouched, resolve relative + local-absolute paths against the doc's directory to attn://localhost/<encoded-abs-path>; (3) built-in image nodeView in Editor.svelte using the resolver for the DISPLAYED src only — node.attrs.src stays as-written so serialization round-trips; (4) new optional Editor prop (resolveAssetUrl) bound by App.svelte to the active tab's path; hosted /app passes nothing (workspace-relative images there are a separate follow-up); (5) graceful broken-image placeholder (alt + filename, paper/ink language) instead of the platform glyph; (6) unit tests for resolver edge cases + extend scripts/test-e2e.sh to assert img src is attn://localhost and naturalWidth > 0. No Rust changes expected; security posture unchanged.

title: Desk: stale #join intent reopens the join panel after Back from a workspace
description: web/hosted/app/main.ts:66 computes joinIntent once at boot (route.view === 'home' && location.hash === '#join') and AppShell passes it through to DeskHome (AppShell.svelte ~L697). DeskHome initializes let joinOpen = $state(joinIntent) at mount. DeskHome lives in the {:else} branch, so opening a workspace unmounts it and Back remounts it, re-reading the stale true — even though closeJoin() already replaceState'd the URL to /app. Repro: load /app#join, Cancel, open a workspace, press Back → join panel is open again with no #join in the URL.

Option (a) is simplest and also keeps openJoin's pushState('/app#join') coherent with reload. Same check for newIntent at AppShell L88 — verify it is already consumed once and does not re-fire.

title: [P2] DeskHome: Enter-to-open must not pre-empt focused buttons/links
description:
Where: web/src/hosted/app/DeskHome.svelte:100-108 (Enter handler), gated by `typingInField` (232-236) which only recognises INPUT/TEXTAREA/contentEditable.

Bug: after an ArrowDown sets `selectedIndex >= 0`, Enter on ANY non-text focus target (New / Import / Delete / Rename / Storage buttons, the row <a class=row-open> links, menu items) is preventDefault'ed and opens the *selected* workspace instead of activating the focused control. Keyboard-only and screen-reader users lose button activation entirely until selection is cleared; Tab → Delete → Enter silently opens a workspace.

Fix: narrow the Enter gate to when focus is on the desk navigation surface itself — i.e. `event.target === filterInput`, or the focused element is document.body / the desk root container / the selected row element (whatever receives focus when arrows move; verify with `moveSelection`). Concretely: return early if `(event.target as HTMLElement).closest('button, a, [role=button], [role=menuitem], select, summary')` matches and it isn't the selected row. Keep the attn-a9f7.1.1 promise intact: on a cold desk, ↓ then Enter (focus on body or filter) still opens. If arrow keys move DOM focus to the row, prefer making the row itself the Enter target and drop the global handler for that case.

Tests: vitest + @testing-library/svelte (or the project's existing component-test approach — see web/src/hosted/app/*.test.ts and tests under web/src/lib/review for precedent): (a) ↓ then Enter with focus on body opens selected workspace; (b) ↓, focus the Delete button of row 0, Enter → delete-confirm state entered, no openWorkspace call; (c) Enter in filter input still opens selection.
acceptance_criteria: Focused buttons/links on the desk activate normally on Enter even when a row is selected. ↓ + Enter on a cold desk still opens the selected workspace. Three tests above pass.
close_reason: deskEnterOpensSelection() in web/src/hosted/app/desk-keys.ts: Enter belongs to the desk only when focus is not on/inside an interactive control (tag, href-bearing <a>, ARIA role, contenteditable); the filter input is the explicit exception. Arrow and '/' gates keep typingInField. 20 cases in desk-keys.test.ts including a pre-fix contrast assertion.

title: [P2] Encode workspace id and file-path segments in every /app/w URL writer; round-trip with parseAppRoute
description:
Where (all raw template writes of /app/w/…):
- web/src/hosted/app/AppShell.svelte:142, 153, 223, 289-290, 330, 409
- web/src/hosted/app/DeskHome.svelte:472 (row <a href>)
- web/src/hosted/app/EditorShell.svelte:813, 932, 947, 2537, 2555

Bug: `normalizeEntryPath` (web/src/lib/hosted/entry-path.ts) accepts names like `draft#1.md`, `plan?.md`, `a b.md`, `50%.md`. Interpolating them raw into history.pushState/replaceState, location.assign, and anchors gives `#`/`?`/`%` URL semantics; `parseAppRoute` (web/src/lib/hosted/routes.ts:75) decodes per-segment via `decodeRouteSegment`, so the parser already expects encoded segments — the writers just don't produce them. Reload or a copied deep link then opens the wrong/missing file (and a bare `%` can make decodeURIComponent throw → route undefined → 404).

Fix: add `appWorkspaceUrl(workspaceId: string, filePath?: string): string` to web/src/lib/hosted/routes.ts that splits filePath on '/' and `encodeURIComponent`s each segment (and the workspace id), and replace every writer above with it. Grep `/app/w/` afterwards — the only remaining literal should be the `prefix` in parseAppRoute. Check `decodeRouteSegment` handles malformed percent sequences without throwing (wrap or verify) and that a literal `%2F` inside a segment does not get re-split into a path separator after decode (reject or keep as-is — pick the safer: reject, consistent with entry-path rules).

Tests: web/src/lib/hosted/routes.test.ts — property-style round-trip: for paths with '#', '?', '%', space, unicode, nested dirs, `parseAppRoute(new URL(appWorkspaceUrl(id,p), 'https://x').pathname)` returns {workspaceId:id, filePath:p}. Add a malformed-percent case (`/app/w/ws/%E0%A4%A`) → undefined, no throw.
acceptance_criteria: A single helper builds every /app/w URL; no raw template literal remains outside routes.ts. Round-trip tests pass for the listed special characters. Importing a file named `draft#1.md`, reloading, and sharing the URL all reopen the same document (manual check in npm run dev:browser).
close_reason: appWorkspaceUrl() in web/src/lib/hosted/routes.ts encodes workspace id + each path segment; all 12 raw /app/w writers in AppShell/DeskHome/EditorShell replaced. parseAppRoute already decoded per segment and rejected malformed/encoded-separator input. 12 round-trip paths + 6 edge cases in routes.test.ts.

title: Round every square-cornered border in the web app to the shadcn scale
description:
Owner, with a screenshot of `/open`: "anywhere there is a non-rounded border in the web app, change to have rounded borders for elements like this. can be subtle. Use the shadcn default".

## The scale was already right; the rules just did not use it

`--radius: 0.625rem` in tokens.css IS shadcn's default, and DESIGN.md's `rounded` scale (6 / 8 / 10 / 14 / pill) is shadcn's own ladder written out. Nothing needed inventing — a set of hand-authored panels in `app-shell.css` and `landing.css` simply never declared a radius at all, so they inherited the browser's square corners while every shadcn-derived component beside them was round. `.drop-zone` in the screenshot was one of eighteen.

Part of why: `chrome.css` only declared `--radius-md` and `--radius-lg` (attn-n01r.42 added those two when it found the hosted routes consuming radii that were never defined — undefined custom properties fail silently, no error, no lint, no visual alarm). `--radius-sm` and `--radius-xl` were still missing, so hosted CSS could not name every step and reached for pixel literals or nothing. All four are declared now.

## What changed

**app-shell.css (15):** `.drop-zone` `.quick-actions` `.degraded-banner` `.writing-sheet` `.asset-preview` `.review-card` `.status-box` `.confirm-clear` `.asset-image` `.share-progress`/`.share-ready-head` at `--radius-lg`; `.review-delivery-status` `.link-box` `.share-entry-list` `.share-choice-grid > label`/`.share-ttl-options label` `.share-tier-picker label` at `--radius-md`.

**landing.css (3):** `.stage-label` at md; `.entry-strip` and `.surfaces` at lg.

**Also normalised:** `.open-prompt` was 14px and `/open`'s `.drop-zone` was about to become 10px — two drop wells for the same act on two pages, in two shapes. Both are `--radius-lg` now.

## Three judgement calls worth recording

1. **md for the small controls, not lg.** 10px on a 28px-high box reads as a pill rather than a rounded rectangle. The owner asked for subtle.
2. **Single-side rules stay square.** A radius on one border edge does nothing anyway, and the hairlines under the desk title and the sidebar project row are RULES, not boxes — rounding them would be a category error.
3. **`overflow: hidden` where dividers are grid gap.** `.quick-actions`, `.entry-strip` and `.surfaces` draw their hairline dividers as `gap: 1px` showing the parent's own background, so the cells have no radius of their own. Without clipping, the square cell backgrounds paint straight over the corners the parent just rounded.

The review margin card's accent strip stays square-ended, and its card must still never gain `overflow: hidden` — that exception is already documented in DESIGN.md two bullets above the new rule, and the new rule points at it so nobody "fixes" it later.

## Verification

STATIC: re-scanned every stylesheet for rules with a full `border` shorthand and no radius. Every remaining hit is `border: 0` — no visible box.

RUNTIME: walked 11 routes x 2 themes, checking every element in the DOM with four non-zero border widths and a zero top-left radius. **Zero remain.** The native app is untouched: the only shared-file candidates in `app.css` (`.sidebar-project-trigger`, `.sidebar-view-tab`, `.sidebar-filter-input`) all carry `border: 0` and needed nothing.

Tailwind markup was checked too — every `border-*` utility in the Svelte components is single-side or `border-0`, and shadcn ships its own `rounded-*`.

GATES: svelte-check 0/0 · npm test 127/0 · build:browser green · route bundles + icon budgets clean.
acceptance_criteria: No element with a full border renders square corners on any hosted route in either theme; containers use --radius-lg and inner controls --radius-md; single-side rules unchanged; the native app unaffected; DESIGN.md records the rule.
close_reason: 97 e2e passed / 4 failed, all four the pre-existing attn-gccz set — no new failures. Static + runtime audits both clean: zero square-cornered full-border elements across 11 routes x 2 themes.

title: "Saved review" should read "comments" — and doing so exposed a duplicate control
description:
Owner: copy needs to say "comments", not "saved review".

"Saved review" named a STORAGE STATE rather than the thing on screen, and no other surface in the product used it — ReviewBar's own rail toggle has said "Show/Hide comments" all along.

FIXED across the header toggle ("Comments" / "Hide comments"), the rail placeholder label and heading, the empty/failed copy, the `aria-controls`/`id` pair (`comments-margin`), the component's own comments, and the e2e assertions.

A DUPLICATE CONTROL SURFACED WHILE DOING IT and is also fixed. The header toggle rendered on `reviewHistoryAvailable && railMode === 'hidden'`, while ReviewBar renders its rail toggle on `hasActiveRoom`. Both conditions can hold at once, and both buttons use the same panel-right glyph pair — so after the rename, sharing a document with the rail hidden would have put two identical buttons labelled "Show comments" in one header, opening two different things. The header toggle is now gated on `reviewStore.currentRoomId === null`, which is the same value ReviewBar's `hasActiveRoom` reads, so exactly one comments control exists at a time.

title: Ordered list markers stayed muted while bullets carried the accent
description:
Owner screenshot: an ordered list whose numerals were `--muted-foreground` while the bullets beside them carried the accent.

That split was never argued for — it just recorded what base.css happened to do — and it means a document mixing the two list kinds colours the same typographic mark two ways, implying a distinction that does not exist.

FIXED: `.attn-doc ol > li::marker` takes `color-mix(in oklch, var(--primary) 80%, transparent)`, identical to the bullets. Sizes still differ by glyph (bullets 0.85em, numerals 0.9em) because a numeral carries shape a dot does not and stops being legible past single digits if shrunk further.

DESIGN.md's third labelling exception now reads "List markers, ordered and unordered", with the extension and its reason recorded. Also corrected the stale "two enumerated labelling exceptions" line further down, left behind when attn-08fa.1 made it three.

VERIFIED in a real browser, both themes: ol::marker and ul::marker both compute `oklch(0.48 0.14 28 / 0.8)` in Paper and `oklch(0.72 0.1 220 / 0.8)` in Ink.

title: Hosted reviewer drops undecryptable snapshots silently — no console, no UI surface
description:
Found while fixing the compressed-R2 decrypt bug (ca118da). When snapshot
hydration fails in the hosted reviewer, every failure mode is invisible:

- resolveBrowserR2Snapshot throws -> browser-session catches, and when
  snapshotContent is already non-null it only sets state.authoringError,
  which no surface renders prominently; when the blob merely fails to parse,
  the id goes to invalidSnapshotBlobIds and NOTHING is emitted -- no
  console.error, no UI state, no telemetry.
- Net effect: the blob downloads with 200s, then the file simply never
  appears in the "Shared with you" list. The reviewer cannot distinguish
  "owner didn't share it" from "my client failed to decrypt it".

This cost four instrumented E2E runs to localize a real protocol bug; a
reviewer in the field would have had nothing to report but "the file isn't
there".

Wanted: a visible per-file failure state (e.g. a row rendered in an error
state with retry) or at minimum a console.error + a degraded-banner surface,
for BOTH the R2-resolve catch and the parse-failure/invalidSnapshotBlobIds
path in web/src/lib/review/browser-session.ts.

title: Repair owner file-delete confirmation semantics and focus
description:
The owner file-delete confirmation declares `role="alertdialog"` but does not implement the complete contract; Svelte reports the missing tabindex and the component maintains custom keyboard/focus behavior beside an existing shared dialog system.

Choose one honest model. Prefer the shared dialog primitive with a labelled modal, safe initial focus, Escape, focus containment, and restoration to the invoking file action. If the confirmation remains inline, remove dialog semantics and announce the confirmation appropriately. Preserve the selected file path through navigation races and keep destructive copy specific.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `./node_modules/.bin/svelte-check --tsconfig ./tsconfig.json` from `web/`.
2. Observe the accessibility warning at the owner file-delete confirmation in `EditorShell.svelte`.
3. Inspect the `role="alertdialog"` container and confirm it lacks the declared role’s complete focus/modal contract.
design: Use /impeccable harden. Prefer the established shared dialog primitive unless a verified inline confirmation is simpler and semantically honest.

title: Decide: autosave on desktop, or per-surface copy
description: Owner decision, and everything else in this epic waits on it. Option A brings autosave to desktop local editing so the copy is true everywhere; option B keeps each surface saying what is true of it. See the epic for the evidence. Record the choice and the reasoning on this issue before any code moves.
acceptance_criteria: The choice is recorded with its reasoning, and the sibling issues are scoped to match it.
notes:
DECISION (owner, 2026-08-08): **Option A — bring autosave to desktop.**

Reasoning:

1. The requested copy implies it. The ask was 'relabel the chip Changes autosaved, as long as this is correct to say'. Option B answers the letter of the ask by refusing it. A is the only option that ends with the requested sentence on screen.

2. The two surfaces were already supposed to be one product. Hosted /app has had a real AutosaveController since attn-7xl.3.3; desktop asking for a keystroke is not a deliberate difference, it is the older half of the app. Per-surface copy would have codified an accident.

3. What made the desktop dirty state load-bearing was that it was the ONLY thing standing between the user and lost work. That is a bad job for a status chip. Under A the dirty state still means something real — work not yet on disk — it is just short-lived, and it acquires a second, sharper job: it is the ONLY signal when autosave is deliberately held back (see below).

Scope decisions taken while implementing A:

- Reuse of hosted/app/autosave.ts was considered and REJECTED. Its contract is `commit: (text) => Promise<void>` and its entire discipline is that 'Saved' only ever follows a durable commit. The native save path is `editSave()` in web/src/lib/ipc.ts — a fire-and-forget `window.ipc.postMessage`, no ack, no promise. Adopting the controller would mean wrapping a void send in Promise.resolve(), which reports 'saved' when the message is QUEUED, not when bytes reach disk — keeping the shape of the durability guarantee while voiding it. A native module (web/src/lib/native-autosave.ts) matches the transport it actually has.

- Autosave is HELD, never fired, while the active file has a pending external-change/conflict (App.svelte's deferredReloadMtimeByPath). Autosaving over a file that changed on disk underneath the user is data loss, and it is the one case where the timer must lose to the human. This is also what keeps ⌘S meaningful after autosave exists: it is now the explicit 'my version wins' resolution of a disk conflict (Escape/cancel is 'the disk wins'), plus an immediate flush.

- The old collab-only 1.5s debounce (App.svelte:1061) is REPLACED, not supplemented — one timer, one file, no double-write.

COPY consequence for attn-yzsa.2: 'Saved on this device' was doing two jobs in one literal — save state AND the local-first claim. They are split. The chip (both surfaces) reports save state: 'Changes autosaved'. The local-first claim keeps its existing dedicated homes: the hosted AppHeader persistence badge ('On this device') and the landing Hero ('Saved on this device'), both untouched, plus the native chip's hover title which says 'Changes autosaved on this device'.
IMPLEMENTED as decided (2026-08-08). Landed exactly the scope above:

- NEW web/src/lib/native-autosave.ts — pure policy (`resolveAutosaveGate`) + injectable clock (`NativeAutosave`, 1.2s quiet period / 8s ceiling, `schedule`+`now` injected). Sibling to hosted/app/autosave.ts, NOT a reuse, for the fire-and-forget-transport reason recorded above.
- NEW web/src/lib/native-autosave.test.ts — 22 cases incl. gate ordering, held-vs-off, gate-asked-at-fire-time, ceiling, re-entrant commit, and source assertions that App.svelte spends the decision.
- Editor.svelte gained `onDocChange` (fires per doc-changing transaction while editable). `onDirtyChange` alone was not usable: it only fires on the clean->dirty EDGE, so a debounce hung off it measures from the FIRST keystroke of a burst, i.e. a ceiling wearing a debounce's name.
- App.svelte: one controller. `collabSaveTimer` deleted; `handleCollabDocChange` now calls the same `noteChange()`. Flush on file switch (openPathNow, before activePath moves) and on pagehide/visibilitychange+unmount. `saveEdits` cancels the clock; `cancelEdit` cancels it too (otherwise a revert is undone 1.2s later by a timer holding the discarded text).
- `deferredReloadMtimeByPath`/`NoticeByPath` converted to SvelteMap/SvelteSet — the hold is now render-visible, and a plain Map mutation would never invalidate the derived.

DISK-LEVEL VERIFICATION (real binary, isolated ATTN_HOME, copy of tests/fixtures/basic.md, no ~/.attn touched):
1. Typed via a real PM transaction, no keystroke: chip 'Saving…' -> file unchanged at 300ms -> written by 2.3s, typed text present on disk, chip back to 'Changes autosaved'.
2. Held: made the buffer dirty then overwrote the file externally inside the debounce. 4s later the external content was byte-identical (untouched), chip data-autosave='held', label 'Unsaved changes · file changed on disk'.
3. Cmd+S resolved it: buffer version won, chip re-armed, and the next edit autosaved again.
4. Ceiling: a change every 0.4s for 12s (quiet period never arrives) produced a disk write at t+8s mid-burst, then the trailing flush; buffer and disk agreed exactly afterwards.
VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY by the parent session, not taken on the implementing agent's report. Built the web bundle before cargo (build.rs returns early on a prebuilt web/dist/index.html, so a cargo-only build would have tested a stale frontend and produced a plausible false pass), then drove the real daemon on an isolated ATTN_HOME over a copy of tests/fixtures/basic.md:

  1. AUTOSAVE WRITES. Typed into the ProseMirror via the --eval bridge with NO keystroke sent. File hash moved a0df657f3589 -> 815416d4d2eb and the token appeared on disk. Chip went dirty -> saved, title 'Changes autosaved on this device'.
  2. DISK-CONFLICT GUARD HOLDS. Typed (buffer dirty), had an external writer append to the file, then kept typing to provoke the timer. The external line survived and the window's edit did NOT reach disk. Chip stayed dirty with the full explanatory title.
  3. THE COPY'S PROMISE IS TRUE. That title says 'save to keep yours'. flush() deliberately respects the gate, so I checked whether the sentence was writing a cheque the code would not honour — it is not: ⌘S routes to App's own saveEdits() rather than through the module, so dispatching it in the held state wrote the window's version and cleared the chip to saved.

117 unit test files green, svelte-check at its 6-error pre-existing baseline.
close_reason: Option A chosen and implemented: autosave now runs on desktop local editing, so 'Changes autosaved' is true on both surfaces rather than true on one and a lie on the other.

title: Save-state copy: make "Changes autosaved" true before saying it
description:
Reported: change the save chip's tooltip to "Changes autosaved", "as long as this is correct to say".

It is correct on one surface and false on the other, so the copy change cannot simply be applied.

WEB (hosted /app) — TRUE. hosted/app/autosave.ts is a real AutosaveController: 1.2s debounce after the last keystroke, 8s ceiling under continuous typing, commits serialized, and its own comment records the discipline that "Saved" only ever follows a durable commit. "Changes autosaved" describes this accurately.

DESKTOP (App.svelte) — FALSE TODAY. There are exactly two save paths:
  1. Mod-s in the editor keymap (Editor.svelte:444) — an explicit, manual save.
  2. A 1.5s debounce in App.svelte:1061, guarded by `collabActive && collabRole === 'owner'` — it exists so a live co-typing session is not lost on close, and it does not run outside a review room.

So a person editing a local file with no room open has no autosave at all. That is why the chip has an "Unsaved changes" state and an --amber-deep dirty glyph in the first place: on desktop, dirty is a real and persistent condition the user must resolve with a keystroke. Relabelling it "Changes autosaved" would be the most direct kind of lie a status region can tell — it reports where the user's work lives, and DESIGN.md's One Pencil Rule carve-out (attn-bw2h.8) grants it the accent precisely because that is "the product's entire claim in one glyph".

THE DECISION THIS EPIC EXISTS TO MAKE, and it is the owner's:

  A. Make it true — bring autosave to desktop local editing, then the copy is
     accurate everywhere and the two surfaces finally behave alike. This is the
     better product answer and the one the requested copy implies. It is also
     the larger change: it writes to the user's file on a timer, so it needs a
     considered debounce, an explicit relationship with the existing dirty
     state, and a decision about whether Cmd+S remains meaningful.

  B. Say what is true on each surface — hosted says "Changes autosaved", desktop
     keeps "Saved on this device". Cheap and honest, but the two surfaces then
     describe the same chip differently, which is the drift this request was
     trying to close.

Recommend A, with B as the interim if A is not wanted now.

Note that "Saved on this device" is doing a second job beyond save state: it is the local-first, nothing-left-your-machine claim, and it appears in the hosted landing Hero and in the hosted SaveState union as a literal. Whatever replaces it must keep that claim somewhere, or the product quietly stops saying the thing it is built on.
acceptance_criteria:
The save chip says the same thing on desktop and web, and what it says is true on both.

If autosave comes to desktop: editing a local file with no review room persists without a keystroke, the dirty state still means something real, and the relationship with Cmd+S is deliberate rather than vestigial.

The local-first claim currently carried by "Saved on this device" still has a home in the UI. The hosted SaveState union, the landing Hero, and the native chip agree on vocabulary.
close_reason: Both children complete and verified on a real daemon writing a real file: autosave persists without a keystroke, the disk-conflict guard refuses to overwrite a newer file, and ⌘S still overrides that hold exactly as the chip's copy promises.

title: Contrast sweep and a committed probe for the reading palette
description:
Every value in this epic is a contrast claim, and contrast claims are the kind that look right in a token file and fail on screen. attn-bw2h.12 is an open audit about exactly this class of problem: affordances that degrade into plausible-looking placeholders.

Sweep the reading surface in BOTH themes on BOTH surfaces (desktop app, web app), reading COMPUTED styles from the running app rather than the token source:

  - body prose on the page                       AA 4.5:1
  - blockquote prose                             AA 4.5:1, and equal to body ink
  - link vs page                                 AA 4.5:1
  - link vs surrounding body text                3:1, or the rest-state underline is present
  - table cell text on the new table surface     AA 4.5:1
  - th eyebrow on the new table surface          AA 4.5:1 at its size, or 3:1 if it qualifies as large
  - inline code on the new code surface          AA 4.5:1
  - inline code nested in a table cell           AA 4.5:1, and still visibly a chip
  - every shiki token family in use, both themes AA 4.5:1
  - frontmatter card label and values            AA 4.5:1

The probe used to diagnose this is worth keeping rather than rebuilding: drive the app with the existing Playwright config, load a fixture exercising every prose construct, flip data-theme, and dump getComputedStyle for each element. A committed version of that becomes the regression guard for the whole palette, not just this change.

Also confirm by eye, because AA is a floor and not the goal here: the blocks should read as quiet insets at a normal reading distance, not as bordered slabs. Screenshot both themes on both surfaces.
acceptance_criteria:
Every pairing listed passes its threshold in Paper and Ink, on desktop and web, measured from computed styles in the running app.

A committed probe reproduces the sweep on demand so the next palette change cannot regress it silently. Screenshots of both themes on both surfaces attached, and the blocks read as quiet insets by eye, not only by number.
close_reason:
web/e2e/reading-palette.spec.ts committed, with tests/fixtures/reading-palette.md exercising headings, prose, links in prose and in list items and in table cells, blockquote, table with th/td, inline code on the page and nested in a cell, a fenced code block, and frontmatter.

Measures what a reader sees rather than what the token file says. Colours resolve through a 1x1 CANVAS so the browser performs its own oklch->sRGB conversion (hand-rolling that in the test would let test and browser disagree about the very thing under test), and backgrounds resolve UP the tree with alpha compositing, since prose elements are transparent and measuring against rgba(0,0,0,0) would pass everything. Block surfaces resolve DOWN instead — a fix found the hard way, because a code block is a transparent wrapper around the pre that carries the fill, so the upward walk sailed past it and measured block and page as identical.

8 tests, both themes: AA per element against its own surface, prose-is-one-ink, links-not-colour-alone, and the two-tier direction rule including the nested step. Every rendered shiki token family is swept too. The suite PRINTS the full sweep, so DESIGN.md's quoted ratios can be refreshed without rebuilding the rig, and it asserts that required constructs were actually found — a selector matching nothing was otherwise a silent pass. All 21 Playwright tests green (13 pre-existing + 8 new); 116 unit test files green; svelte-check back at its 6-error pre-existing baseline. Screenshots of both themes captured.

title: Make DESIGN.md state one elevation rule, and stop calling the code block raised
description:
The token changes in this epic are only half-true until DESIGN.md agrees with them, and one of the statements it makes today is already false.

CONTRADICTION TO RESOLVE. Line 183 calls --code-block "the raised surface". The Elevation section describes chrome receding by going a step darker, and the Flat-Until-Lifted Rule lists the code block among things "genuinely pressed into" the page, carrying an inset shadow. So the same object is documented as raised and as pressed-in, and ships with a recessed shadow over a raised tone. That is why nobody caught the Paper value being lighter than the page: the doc licensed it.

WHAT TO WRITE INSTEAD — one rule that covers every future surface:

  A surface embedded IN the reading column steps toward the FOREGROUND: darker on
  Paper, lighter in Ink. Both mean "more ink here". A surface floating ABOVE the
  page (card, dialog, popover, menu) may step away from it, and earns a lift
  shadow when it does. Nothing on Paper is lighter than the page.

That formulation also explains the values already in the system rather than fighting them: sidebar and panel-surface recede on Paper and lift in Ink because they are chrome planes; review cards and dialogs are lighter on Paper because they genuinely float. Only the reading-column blocks were on the wrong side of it.

ALSO UPDATE
  - the colors block in the DESIGN.md frontmatter (code-block value)
  - the One Pencil Rule, naming links under "action" (see attn-evme.1)
  - .impeccable/design.json if it mirrors these tokens

Do this LAST, once the values from attn-evme.1 and .3 are settled and verified, so the doc records what shipped rather than what was proposed.
acceptance_criteria:
DESIGN.md describes embedded and floating surfaces with one rule that predicts every value currently in the system, and no longer calls --code-block raised while it carries an inset shadow.

The frontmatter colors block, the One Pencil Rule's treatment of links, and .impeccable/design.json all match what shipped.
notes:
CORRECTION to the close reason above: I wrote that no .impeccable/design.json exists in this repo. That was wrong — it does exist (24KB, generated 2026-08-07). The grep that told me otherwise ran with the working directory inside web/, so it was looking in the wrong place, and I did not re-check before recording it.

What is actually true: the sidecar's colorMeta covers 20 colours (primary, paper-bg, ink, the review and participant hues, panel-surface, panel-border, rail-chip-surface) and does NOT include link, code-block or code-block-nested. So it is not holding stale VALUES for anything this epic changed — it is stale only in the sense that DESIGN.md is now newer than it, which the impeccable hook reports.

Deliberately NOT refreshed here. Regenerating the sidecar is '/impeccable document', which rewrites DESIGN.md from the code, and DESIGN.md is exactly what this issue just hand-authored (the Two-Tier Surface Rule, the corrected Code Block entry, the re-measured frontmatter-key ratios). Running it as a side effect of this epic would risk overwriting that prose with generated text. The skill's own rule applies: drift is reported, not repaired as a side effect. Flagged to the owner instead.
close_reason:
Added The Two-Tier Surface Rule: embedded surfaces (code, tables, frontmatter, inputs) step toward the foreground — darker on Paper, lighter in Ink, both meaning 'more ink here' — and carry the pressed inset; floating surfaces (cards, dialogs, popovers) may step away and earn a lift. Plus the line that makes Paper unambiguous: nothing on Paper is lighter than the page. Written as descriptive rather than aspirational, so it predicts the values already in the system (chrome planes, review cards) instead of fighting them.

Corrected the Code Block entry, which called the token 'the raised surface' while the Flat-Until-Lifted Rule listed the same object as pressed-in with an inset shadow — the contradiction that licensed a panel brighter than the paper. Documented --code-block-nested. Updated the frontmatter colors block (code-block, code-block-nested, link). Re-measured the frontmatter-key accent exception, which the surface move changed: 6.47:1 -> 4.97:1 in Paper, 7.67:1 -> 7.85:1 in Ink, and flagged that Paper now clears the floor by under half a step so it is the first pairing to re-check if the tier moves again. No .impeccable/design.json exists in this repo, so nothing to mirror.

title: Blockquote prose is greyed although it is still prose
description:
Reported: "It looks like there is some color inconsistency here for text... All text should be the same color."

Measured on the running app. Blockquote prose renders at --muted-foreground: L 0.32 on Paper against a 0.14 body, L 0.66 in Ink against 0.87. It is the only block of running prose in the document that is not body ink.

A blockquote is prose. It is quoted prose, and it is already marked as such twice over — a 2.5px accent bar on the left edge and the indent that comes with it. Greying the text is a third signal doing the same job, and unlike the other two it is paid for in legibility: quoted passages are frequently the part of a document a reviewer reads most carefully.

The fix is to drop the colour override and let the bar and indent carry the distinction. base.css:340 for the static render, and check the ProseMirror path for an equivalent.

NOT IN SCOPE, deliberately: the th eyebrow also uses --muted-foreground, and should keep it. It is a 0.7em uppercase small-caps label at 0.06em tracking — chrome describing the table, not prose inside it — and it belongs to the same label family the sidebar and rail use. Muting a label is a hierarchy decision; muting prose is a legibility cost. Say so in a comment so the two are not "made consistent" later by someone reading only the token.
acceptance_criteria:
Blockquote body text renders at --foreground in both themes, on the static render and in the editor. The quote remains unmistakably a quote via its left bar and indent.

The th eyebrow still uses --muted-foreground, with a comment recording why prose and label diverge here on purpose.
close_reason: Blockquote colour override dropped; it inherits body ink rather than re-declaring, so a quote inside a review card or any other surface still inherits that surface's foreground. Measured 15.02:1 in Paper and 13.33:1 in Ink — identical to body prose, which is the point. The th eyebrow deliberately keeps --muted-foreground with a comment recording that prose and label diverge on purpose, so the next person does not 'make it consistent'.

title: Verify the whole epic in a running browser tab and desktop window
description:
Every item in this epic was reported from a running app, and two of them (attn-64iy.1, attn-64iy.5) are invisible to a unit test by construction: one is a mock-transport gap that only shows up when a real folder is picked, the other differs BY SHELL and so cannot be checked from one environment.

Precedent for making this its own issue rather than trusting the per-issue ACs: attn-bw2h.6 was closed only after being run end to end against the raw dev loop, and its notes record two corrections to the original diagnosis that no amount of reading the code had produced.

BROWSER (npm run dev in web/, open the served URL in Chrome, pick planning/web-authoring through the file picker):
- Share for review completes; highlight text; composer opens; submit; card lands in the margin with its inline decoration on the right range.
- Switch files in the sidebar and comment on a second file.
- Brand sits in the top-left corner above the project label with no dead strip above it, and stays put while the file list scrolls.
- Header cluster spacing is even; the lightning bolt is borderless at rest and pills when its popover opens; the comments toggle shows the panel-right glyphs; the filter draws its box.
- Close the last file so the sidebar disappears — the brand falls back into the header.

DESKTOP (task dev ATTN_PATH=planning/web-authoring):
- Traffic lights still have their corner, the drag strip still works, the brand is still in the header.
- The header changes from .3, .4 and .6 are present here too, since they are not shell-specific.
- Commenting still works against the real daemon — attn-64iy.1 touches mock-ipc only, but .2 changes the composer entry points that both shells share.
