Capture screenshots of both shells. Note the Agentation toolbar is dev-only and mounts in both, so it is not evidence of which surface you are on — the reliable tell is whether .html files appear in the tree (browser file source is markdown-only).
acceptance_criteria:
All seven sibling issues confirmed working in a real browser tab AND a real desktop window, with screenshots of both. Any behaviour that differs from its issue's acceptance criteria is filed rather than quietly accepted.

The full comment round-trip — highlight, compose, submit, card renders, decoration lands on the correct range — is demonstrated in the browser loop, which is the failure that opened this epic.
close_reason:
BROWSER: new web/e2e/browser-review-chrome.spec.ts, 10 tests, all passing under playwright.native-share.config.ts alongside the 3 existing native-share tests (13/13). Covers brand placement + no reserved chrome, empty-slot collapse, gap uniformity, ShareChip resting/open treatment, panel-right glyph mapping, filter rest/focus, snapshot publication shape, the full highlight->comment->card round trip, and the honest-unavailable path (driven by dropping reviewSnapshot at the bridge, which reproduces the original broken state exactly). Screenshots captured.

DESKTOP: debug build against an isolated ATTN_HOME, probed via --eval: data-shell=native, brand in header (1), sidebar brand (0), drag strip (1), pl-3, filter border opaque at rest. Screenshot confirms the header brand and the reserved traffic-light strip.

FINDING worth knowing: build.rs:38 returns early if web/dist/index.html exists, so a stale prebuilt bundle silently shadows every frontend change in a cargo-only build. The first desktop probe run was entirely against a bundle from before this work and looked plausible because the old layout matches the desktop expectation. Run npm run build before cargo build when verifying frontend changes natively.

title: Shell-aware chrome: brand takes the freed top-left corner in the browser
description:
Reported against .group/sidebar-wrapper > .bg-background > .relative > .flex: 'Move the logo and text into the top left corner of the screen i.e. on top of Web-Authoring, needs to be fixed in position.' Clarified by the reporter: 'there is no title bar to avoid in web, only desktop.'

That clarification is the issue. App.svelte does not know which shell it is in, so it reserves space for a native window it may not have:

- App.svelte does not pass showWindowDragRegion to Sidebar. Sidebar.svelte:95 defaults it to true, so Sidebar.svelte:311 renders a 46px strip commented 'clears traffic lights'. In a browser tab there are no traffic lights and that is 46px of dead sidebar.
- The header (App.svelte:3176) applies pl-[6.5rem] when there is no sidebar — another 104px of traffic-light clearance that is pure indent in a browser.
- The header's onmousedown={dragWindow} and ondblclick={zoomWindow} are no-ops in a browser.

The hosted frame already faces this and answers it by hand: HostedDesktopWorkspaceFrame.svelte:213 passes showWindowDragRegion={false}. App.svelte needs the same answer derived rather than hardcoded, because it serves both shells from one component.

SHELL SIGNAL. mock-ipc.ts:898 already establishes it: 'if (window.ipc) return' — the real wry bridge is present under the desktop shell and absent in a browser tab, and the mock sets window.__attnMockIpc = true when it takes over. Derive one named value from that (isNativeShell / hasWindowChrome) and read it in both places rather than testing window.ipc inline at each call site.

LAYOUT, decided with the reporter (shell-aware, option 1):

- Browser: no drag strip, no pl-[6.5rem]. Brand mark + wordmark move into the sidebar as their own row above the project label, in the freed corner. It sits in .sidebar-controls, which is already outside the ScrollArea, so 'fixed in position' comes for free — confirm it does not scroll with the file list.
- Desktop: unchanged. Drag strip stays, brand stays in the header, traffic lights keep their corner.
- Browser with NO sidebar (nothing opened yet): the brand has no sidebar to live in, so it stays in the header. Do not leave the app unbranded in its own empty state.

When the brand leaves the header in the browser, the divider after it (App.svelte:3185) has nothing left to separate and should go with it; the doc name becomes the header's first element.

CONSIDERATION, not scope: 'native shell' and 'macOS traffic lights' are not the same predicate — a wry window on Linux or Windows has an ordinary title bar and no overlay lights, so the 46px strip is likely wrong there too. Name the signal for what it actually gates so that is a small change later, and note it rather than fixing it blind here.

Do not touch the hosted or reviewer headers — see the follow-up filed against this epic.
acceptance_criteria:
In a browser tab the brand mark and wordmark sit in the top-left corner of the sidebar above the project label, with no reserved traffic-light space above them, and they stay put while the file list scrolls.

On the desktop wry build nothing moves: the drag strip still clears the traffic lights and the brand is still in the header. Both shells resolve from one derived signal, not from a hardcoded flag or an inline window.ipc test at each site. A browser tab with no sidebar still shows the brand in the header. Verified in both shells, not just by test.
close_reason: New lib/shell.ts owns the predicate (isNativeShell / reservesWindowControls / brandPlacement), keyed on window.__attnMockIpc — NOT window.ipc, which the mock installs in both shells and would report every browser tab as native. App reads it once. Browser: no drag strip, no pl-[6.5rem], brand + wordmark in the sidebar above the project label, inside .sidebar-controls so it sits outside the ScrollArea. Desktop: unchanged. No sidebar: brand falls back to the header. Drag/zoom handlers gated too. Verified in BOTH shells — browser screenshot shows the mark in the freed corner with the header starting at the document name; desktop probes confirm data-shell=native, brand in header, no sidebar brand, drag strip present, pl-3.

title: Comments toggle should use the panel-right glyph pair, and appear whenever comments do
description:
Reported against .review-bar-dock > .relative > svg > path: 'Instead of the comment icon here use the panel right open and panel right close icons to denote when the user can open and shut the comments. Should only appear when comments or in share mode.'

GLYPH. ReviewBar.svelte:295 renders MessageSquareText. The control does not create a comment — it opens and closes the rail that holds them, and a panel glyph says that where a speech bubble says 'add a comment'. The correct pair is already in this codebase and already used for exactly this job: WorkspaceEditorFrame.svelte:355 renders PanelRightClose when the rail is open and PanelRightOpen when it is closed. Mirror that mapping precisely — the two controls do the same thing and must not disagree about which glyph means which state. WorkspaceEditorFrame's own copy of the toggle is suppressed on this surface via railToggleInHeader, so the header inherits sole responsibility for the affordance and should inherit its vocabulary too.

Keep everything hanging off the button: the active-thread count, the UnreadBadge, aria-pressed, and the Cmd+J hint in the title.

VISIBILITY. [Corrected after validation — an earlier draft prescribed 'room active OR current file has threads', but that second arm is unreachable: threadsForFile (selectors.ts:187) returns [] when roomId is null, and forgetRoom (store.svelte.ts:1161-1164) nulls currentRoomId AND currentFileId when a room ends. Threads cannot outlive their room in the current store model. Do not build that arm.]

The real gap behind 'comments or in share mode': the dock mounts when shareOpen (ReviewBar.svelte:159 — share dialog open, pre-mint), but the toggle inside is gated on hasActiveRoom alone (:258). So while a share is being initiated the toggle is absent, then pops in when the room mints — a layout shift in a cluster the user is looking at. Move the toggle's condition to 'hasActiveRoom || shareOpen' to match the dock: present (disabled or zero-count) during share initiation, live once the room exists. That is the literal reading of the report and it is reachable.

Check the interaction with the auto-expand effect at App.svelte:724 before changing anything — it opens the rail on first unresolved feedback per room, and a toggle present in more states must not fight it.
acceptance_criteria:
The header comments toggle renders PanelRightClose while the rail is open and PanelRightOpen while it is closed, matching WorkspaceEditorFrame exactly. No speech-bubble glyph remains on either control.

The toggle is present whenever a room is active or the share dialog is open (pre-mint), and absent otherwise — no pop-in when the room mints. Thread count, unread badge, aria-pressed and the Cmd+J hint all survive. A test pins the open/closed glyph mapping across both toggles so they cannot drift apart.
close_reason: PanelRightClose/PanelRightOpen replace MessageSquareText, mirroring WorkspaceEditorFrame exactly; a test pins the mapping across both toggles so they cannot drift. Visibility is now railToggle && (hasActiveRoom || shareOpen) — matched to the dock's own mount rule so the toggle no longer pops in when the room mints. The unreachable 'file has threads without a room' arm was NOT built: threadsForFile returns [] when roomId is null and forgetRoom clears both ids together. Also demoted the button from a permanently bordered pill to the resting-ghost convention, since attn-64iy.6 would otherwise have left it the only outlined control in a row of ghosts.

title: Header action cluster: empty ReviewBar slots eat the gaps between button groups
description:
Reported against #app > .relative > .relative > .ml-auto: 'Spacing between the button groups is not even here.'

ROOT CAUSE. ReviewBar.svelte:258-281 opens 'if (hasActiveRoom)' and then unconditionally renders a divider plus three wrapper divs:

  <span class="h-4 w-px shrink-0 bg-border/70">        <- always drawn
  <div class="review-bar-peers">    <PeerStrip />      <- child may render nothing
  <div class="review-bar-snapshot"> <SnapshotBadge />  <- child may render nothing
  <div class="review-bar-outbox">   <OutboxIndicator />

The children are each conditional on their own state — PeerStrip.svelte:174 emits an sr-only stub when there are no peers and no unread, SnapshotBadge.svelte:251 is behind 'if (activeSnapshot !== null)', OutboxIndicator.svelte:174 behind 'if (visible)'. The WRAPPERS are not. A wrapper whose child renders nothing is still a flex item of the dock's gap-1.5 row, so it still consumes a gap. Three empty wrappers plus the divider is roughly 18-24px of dead space, all of it landing in one place: between the ShareChip and the comments toggle. That is the uneven gap in the report.

FIX. Each wrapper must share its child's visibility condition — either hoist the condition into ReviewBar, or let each child own its own wrapper so there is nothing left to strand. The divider needs the same treatment: it separates the share control from the peer cluster, so it should not be drawn when that cluster is empty.

Prefer hoisting the conditions over a CSS :empty or :has workaround. PeerStrip's empty branch renders an sr-only element rather than nothing at all (deliberately, per its own comment), so :empty would not match it and the fix would silently only half-work.
acceptance_criteria:
With a room active but no peers, no snapshot and an empty outbox, the spacing between the save chip, the share control, the comments toggle and settings is uniform — one gap value, no wide gap anywhere.

Spacing stays correct as those slots populate and empty again during a session. A test asserts the dock contains no zero-width flex children, so the regression cannot return unnoticed.
close_reason: The three wrapper divs are deleted; PeerStrip/SnapshotBadge/OutboxIndicator are the flex items now, carrying the layout classes the wrappers held (min-w-0 shrink / shrink-0). Collapse is exact and self-maintaining: the two conditional components render no element, and PeerStrip's empty branch is sr-only (position:absolute) so it generates no flex item while still announcing 'No peers'. Divider gated on the shared showRailToggle so it is never drawn with nothing behind it. scripts/test-share-experience-e2e.sh moved off the removed data-slot to [data-slot=peer-strip]. Verified in-browser: zero zero-width flex children in the dock, and max-min gap spread across the cluster is within 14px (was ~5x).

title: Audit: security affordances that degrade into plausible-looking placeholders
description:
SECURITY-AFFORDANCE CLASS worth auditing beyond the one instance fixed.

Found while investigating attn-bw2h.6 and fixed in the same pass, but recorded here because the CLASS matters more than the instance: a security affordance that silently degrades into a plausible-looking placeholder is worse than one that is missing, because the user cannot tell the difference and will act on it.

THE INSTANCE (fixed): the share sheet's Advanced panel shows an owner key fingerprint under a label instructing the owner to read it aloud as an out-of-band identity check. `ownerKeyFingerprint()` rejects when `crypto.subtle` is undefined — which happens on an insecure non-loopback origin, e.g. `task dev DEV_HOST=0.0.0.0` reached over a LAN IP. The rejection escaped an async `$effect`, so the row sat on its `—— —— ——` placeholder indefinitely. Two people comparing placeholders would "verify" a match that means nothing.

Fixed with a resolved status (absent / pending / ready / failed), an explicit failure message, and the copy button disabled unless the value is real.

WHY IT SURVIVED: it only reproduces on an origin without Web Crypto, which no normal run hits. The same shape — an async security value with a neutral-looking initial state and no failure path — would survive the same way anywhere else it exists.

WORTH AUDITING: every other place the product renders a value the user is asked to TRUST or COMPARE (fingerprints, key ids, verification codes, tier/scope indicators, "encrypted" affirmations). The test is: if the underlying computation fails or never resolves, does the UI say so, or does it render something that looks like an answer? Anything in the second category is the same bug.

Related, same session: attn-bw2h.6 also corrected share error copy that asserted "Nothing left this machine" on a TIMEOUT — a privacy claim a timeout cannot establish, since the daemon may have created the room and published before failing to answer. Same underlying failure mode: an unearned assurance presented as fact.
acceptance_criteria: Every user-facing value presented for trust or comparison (fingerprints, key ids, verification codes, scope indicators) either renders a real value or says explicitly that it could not be computed; none render a neutral placeholder indistinguishable from a result; async failures surface rather than being swallowed by an effect.
notes:
SECOND INSTANCE LOCATED — the audit now starts from two concrete sites, not a category.

web/src/lib/PeerStrip.svelte:106-115, `ensureFingerprint`:

    const fp = await ownerKeyFingerprint(material);   // no try/catch
    fingerprintCache[peer.participantId] = fp;        // only runs on success

Called as `void ensureFingerprint(peer)` — fire-and-forget, so a rejection is unhandled AND the cache entry is never written. Line 346 then renders:

    {@const fp = fingerprintCache[peer.participantId] ?? '—— —— ——'}

so the placeholder becomes permanent in the PEER IDENTITY CARD. Same trigger as the ShareDialog instance (`crypto.subtle` undefined on an insecure non-loopback origin, e.g. `task dev DEV_HOST=0.0.0.0` reached over a LAN IP), same failure mode, same class of surface — a fingerprint exists to verify who you are talking to, and em-dashes that never resolve verify nothing while looking like they are about to.

This one is arguably worse than the share-sheet instance: that one is the owner checking their own key, this one is a user checking a REMOTE PEER's identity, which is the case the affordance exists for.

DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED PIECEMEAL. It is ~5 lines and tempting, but this bead is an audit and fixing one site while leaving the sweep undone invites someone to read it as covered. Do the sweep as a unit, starting here.

SEARCH SHAPE for the sweep: any `await` inside a Svelte `$effect`, or any fire-and-forget `void someAsync()`, whose success path is the only writer of a value the UI later renders with a `??` fallback. PeerStrip is named; ShareDialog is already fixed and can serve as the reference for the resolved-status pattern (absent / pending / ready / failed, action disabled unless real).

title: Focused review anchor renders nothing — .is-focused has no CSS
description:
Found while removing the margin connector (attn-bw2h.5). Selecting a review card gives its inline anchor NO extra emphasis, because the class that is supposed to provide it has no styling.

`web/src/lib/prosemirror/review-decorations.ts:243` adds `is-focused` to the focused thread's inline mark:

    class: item.className + (item.isFocused ? ' is-focused' : '')

There is no rule for `.is-focused` anywhere — verified across `web/styles/**`, `web/src/app.css` and `web/src/tokens.css`. `web/src/lib/review/store.svelte.ts:267` refers to it as "the is-focused pulse", so this was intended to render something and never did.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW: attn-bw2h.5 removed the SVG connector that drew a line from an offset card back to its anchor. The justification for removing it was that the inline highlight already carries the card-to-anchor association. That is true for "this text has a comment", but the FOCUSED association — which card am I looking at, and which text does it point to — was being carried by the connector and by a pulse that does not exist. So the card/anchor link is now weaker than the removal assumed.

Second, related gap (same area, also unstyled rather than broken): hover is one-way. Hovering an inline mark lifts its card, but `buildDecorations` only reads `focusEventId`, so hovering a CARD does not light its anchor. Worth closing at the same time — it is the other half of the same association.

Design constraint: whatever this renders must not rely on an animation carrying the state. DESIGN.md's Truth Rule requires pixels to equal state, and attn-bw2h.9 is a live example of a WKWebView transition stranding — a literal "pulse" is exactly the shape that fails there. A static focused treatment (a stronger tint or an outline selected by the class) satisfies both.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a review card visibly emphasises its inline anchor; hovering a card lights its anchor as well as the reverse; the treatment is a static state, not an animation, per the Truth Rule; verified in the built desktop app in both themes.

title: Hosted reviewer: userProfile.participantId is never populated, so self-identity falls back to the hash
description:
Found while fixing attn-bw2h.4 (avatar colour), and deliberately left out of that fix because the file is owned elsewhere.

`userProfile.participantId` is populated only by the NATIVE init payload. The hosted build mints a per-session id reachable only via `session.getParticipantId()`, so on `web/src/BrowserReviewApp.svelte` the "is this me?" test falls back to the local echo of the client's own `ParticipantJoined` event.

Consequence: a hosted reviewer's own declared colour is correct once their announce lands, but NOT before authoring init completes — and never at all for a **view-tier** session, which by design never announces (a view invite carries no write key and no grant, so there is no device registration; see attn-vlmz.1.3). In that window the user sees the deterministic hash instead of their picked colour, on their own avatar.

Fix is one line beside the existing `localParticipantId` derivation at `web/src/BrowserReviewApp.svelte:355`:

    userProfile.participantId = session.getParticipantId();

`store.isSelf()` picks it up with no further change, because attn-bw2h.4 keyed the self test on `userProfile.participantId` precisely so every surface resolves through one entrypoint.

Check while there whether `EditorShell.svelte` (the hosted desk) has the same gap — it was not examined.
acceptance_criteria: A hosted reviewer's picked colour shows on their own avatar immediately, including in a view-tier session that never announces; the same is verified for the hosted desk shell; self-identity continues to resolve through store.isSelf() rather than a second code path.

title: Remove the SVG connector line from offset margin cards
description:
Reported: "There is a weird line going from the currently selected comment to the edge of the comments rail. We don't want this."

This is a deliberate feature, not a rendering artifact — so removing it is a design decision, not a bug fix. `ReviewMargin.svelte:484-497` builds `connectorLines`, and :1141-1155 renders an SVG layer drawing a line from each OFFSET card's left-mid back to its anchor's viewport y. It only appears for cards displaced from their anchor by collision, which is why it looks arbitrary in use: it shows up on some cards and not others, with no obvious rule from the user's side.

Remove it. Take the whole path — the `connectorLines` derived, the SVG layer, `.review-margin-connectors` styling, and any now-unused geometry feeding only that computation. A dead derived recomputing per scroll tick is worse than none.

Before deleting, note what it was for: the file header (:5-7) says offset cards get a connector "back to the anchor". If losing the anchor association turns out to matter, the replacement is the existing highlight in the text, not a line — confirm the inline comment-anchor highlight is doing that job.
acceptance_criteria: No connector line is drawn in the margin under any placement; the connectorLines derived, the SVG layer and its styles are removed rather than hidden; scroll-time layout work is not left computing geometry nothing renders; cards still read as associated with their anchors via the inline highlight.

title: Collapse the resolved state into the badge as a checkmark, drop the word
description:
Reported: "remove the resolved text here and just move the checkmark into the right hand side of the badge."

Two surfaces show it, and both are wrong in the same way:
- ReviewMarginCard.svelte:449 renders a second standalone `resolved` badge, so a resolved card shows TWO chips side by side ("COMMENT" + "RESOLVED") — visible in image 14.
- The collapsed resolved chip (image 16) reads "✓ Angus Bezzina · resolved", where the word restates what the tick already says.

Target: one badge. The tick sits at its right-hand side, next to the timestamp that lands there from the sibling issue. No "resolved" word on either surface.

Coordinate with that sibling — both edit the same header region, so they should land together or in a stated order rather than conflicting.

Accessibility: the tick must not be the only carrier. Keep an accessible name (sr-only text or aria-label) saying the thread is resolved, and do not rely on colour alone — PRODUCT.md is explicit about that.
acceptance_criteria: A resolved card shows exactly one badge with a checkmark on its right; no 'resolved' text on the card or the collapsed chip; resolution is still announced to assistive tech and is not conveyed by colour alone.

title: Put the timestamp in the badge; drop the redundant 'comment' kind chip
description:
Reported: "the 'Comment' badge is irrelevant, instead put the time it was made in that badge."

Today the header (ReviewMarginCard.svelte:415-431) renders BOTH `· just now` as loose text after the author name AND a `comment` / `suggest` chip on the right. The chip is near-zero information — a comment card in the comments rail is self-evidently a comment — while the timestamp, which is the thing you actually scan for, is unstyled text crammed against the name. Image 14 shows the cost: at a narrow rail the name truncates to "Angus Be..." and the age wraps onto its own line under the dot.

Move the timestamp into the badge and drop the kind word for comments. Decisions to make deliberately:
- Suggestions are NOT the same as comments here: `suggest` carries real information (it proposes an edit). Decide whether suggestion cards keep a kind marker alongside the time, or convey kind through the existing accent colour and card affordances alone.
- The relative time is computed at ReviewMarginCard.svelte:201 (`just now` under 60s). Confirm it still updates live once it moves.
- Keep the full timestamp on `title` for hover.
acceptance_criteria: The badge carries the relative time; the redundant comment kind chip is gone; suggestion cards still communicate that they propose an edit; the full timestamp is available on hover; the header no longer wraps at the narrowest supported rail width.
notes: VERIFIED: badge renders 'JUST NOW'; kind chip gone for comments; suggestions keep the word inside the same badge as 'SUGGEST | 5M'. SECOND BUG FIXED EN ROUTE: ageLabel was $derived over a non-reactive Date.now(), so the time was never live — tolerable as small grey text, a lie once it IS the badge. Now a refcounted 30s ticker, one interval shared across all mounted cards.

title: SnapshotPlaintext deny_unknown_fields breaks OLD receivers of NEW HTML snapshots
description: src/review/model.rs keeps #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] on SnapshotPlaintext while the html-annotation branch added the 'annotation' field, and bootstrap.rs stamps it on every published HTML snapshot. An older native build receiving a new HTML share fails serde deserialization in load_validated_snapshot_plaintext, so old peers cannot open any newly published HTML document. The shipped tests only cover old-publisher→new-receiver; the reverse hard-fails. Decide whether cross-version rooms are supported; if yes, the schema evolution policy for SnapshotPlaintext needs an explicit story (drop deny_unknown_fields with a bounded-extras rule, or version-gate the field). Found in post-hoc review of attn-61t.
notes: 2026-08-15 (attn-bb6t.4): a SECOND forward-compat break now exists in the same family. ReviewEventBody gained a CommentReopened variant; the enum is externally tagged, so receivers on 0.9.0 and earlier fail to deserialize the event entirely and a reopened thread stays resolved on their side. Silent, like the snapshot case. Whatever rollout/versioning answer this bead lands on should cover new EVENT VARIANTS too, not just new snapshot fields.

title: View-tier invite silently does nothing when handed to the daemon or CLI
description:
Found while verifying attn-vlmz.1.3 on a live stack.

Handing a view-tier invite (attn://review/<id>#v=3&tier=view&read=...) to `attn review join`, or routing it to a running daemon, produces NO observable result. The CLI reports "join request sent to the running attn daemon" and exits 0. The daemon logs:

    INFO attn::review::manager: received command Join

...and then nothing. No room is joined, no error is logged, no message reaches the window. `currentRoomId` stays null and connection stays `offline`. The same invite in the comment tier joins in ~6s with connection `live_direct`.

Refusing is CORRECT: a view link deliberately carries no `write` key and no `grant`, so there is no device registration to perform ("No device registration or writes"). The defect is that the refusal is silent and indistinguishable from a hang or a broken relay — the user has no way to tell that the link is working as designed.

Should explain, not vanish: state that a view link is a read-only browser link, that it cannot register a device, and how to open it instead. The CLI should exit non-zero.
acceptance_criteria: Handing a view-tier invite to `attn review join` or the daemon produces a clear explanation that view links are read-only browser links with no device registration, and points the user at the correct way to open one; the CLI exits non-zero; no code path accepts a Join command and then goes silent.

title: review-drift-check.test.ts exits 1 intermittently after passing all assertions
description:
Pre-existing flaky test, found during the attn-11g4.2 wave and NOT caused by it. The file is committed and unmodified (git status clean), imports only ./review-drift-check, and references nothing from the concurrent work.

Reproduced directly: three identical runs of 'npx tsx src/lib/review/review-drift-check.test.ts' gave exit codes 1, 1, 0.

Symptom: the file prints 'all assertions passed' and THEN exits non-zero. So the assertions are fine; the process exit status is not. Suspected cause is startReviewDriftMonitor's timers/BroadcastChannel racing process teardown — an un-cleared interval or an open channel keeping the loop alive, or an unhandled rejection surfacing after the summary line.

This matters beyond tidiness: 'npm test' is the gate every agent and CI run checks, and a test that fails ~2 runs in 3 will be attributed to whatever change happens to be in flight at the time. During this wave it was briefly blamed on unrelated work before being traced.

Fix should make the monitor's teardown deterministic (clear timers, close the channel, await outstanding work) rather than papering over the exit code.
acceptance_criteria: The test exits 0 on at least 20 consecutive runs; the monitor's teardown is explicit and tested; no other test in the suite depends on the leaked timer/channel staying open.
notes:
FURTHER EVIDENCE (attempted fix, stopped deliberately). Struck twice more during the wave: one full 'npm test' run reported 109 files / 1 failure, this file only; the immediate re-run was 109 / 0.

Ruled out the obvious cause: the disposer returned by startReviewDriftMonitor (review-drift-check.ts:151-155) is correct — clearInterval, channel.onmessage = null, channel.close() — and the test calls both stopLeader() and stopFollower(). process.exit(1) in main() is guarded on failures > 0, which is NOT the path taken (it prints the success line).

The decisive diagnostic: captured stdout+stderr across four consecutive runs (exit 1, 0, 0, 0). The failing run's output is CHARACTER-IDENTICAL to the passing runs — the expected '[attn drift] two tabs disagree' warning the test deliberately induces, and nothing else. No stack, no unhandled-rejection message, no assertion failure. So the non-zero exit is produced after main() resolves and without emitting a diagnostic.

Remaining hypotheses, untested: an unhandled rejection swallowed before Node prints it; Node's worker_threads BroadcastChannel throwing asynchronously when close() races an in-flight message; or process.exitCode being set by tsx itself.

Incidental oddity worth checking while in here: tabIds repeated EXACTLY across two separate processes (drift-b2acaedf / drift-b3acb072 in runs 2 and 4). The seed is Date.now/performance.now based, so identical pairs across distinct processes suggests it is less unique than intended — probably unrelated to the exit code, but it is a real seeding weakness in an id meant to distinguish tabs.

Stopped here: a silent non-zero exit with no output is a real investigation, not a quick fix, and it is off the critical path for both epics.
Rate re-measured 2026-08-07 during the attn-bw2h wave: failed TWICE consecutively in the aggregate npm test run, then standalone exit 0/0/1 across three runs of the unmodified committed file. So the rate is closer to ~30% than the ~20% first recorded, and consecutive failures do happen — which makes 'just re-run it' an unreliable mitigation and means it will read as a real failure to anyone who hits two in a row. Raising the case for fixing it rather than living with it.

title: Table cells lack position:relative, breaking prosemirror-tables cell selection
description:
Found while giving tables the code-block surface (attn-11g4.3); pre-existing and unrelated to that change.

prosemirror-tables requires table cells to be positioned so its absolutely-positioned overlays resolve against the CELL. '.ProseMirror th, .ProseMirror td' have no 'position: relative', so '.selectedCell::after' (prosemirror.css ~:692, 'position: absolute; inset: 0') and '.column-resize-handle' resolve against the nearest positioned ancestor — '.tableWrapper' — instead.

Expected symptom: selecting a single cell tints the ENTIRE table rather than the cell, and the column resize handle sits in the wrong place. Not yet reproduced in the running app; confirm the symptom before fixing.

This is the standard prosemirror-tables setup requirement, so the fix is likely one declaration, but verify it does not disturb the new border-collapse: separate surface (a positioned cell can change paint order against the table background).
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a cell in the editor highlights only that cell; the column-resize handle tracks the correct column boundary; the table's filled surface, radius and last-row rule are unaffected; verified in both themes.
notes:
CLOSED as the CSS half only. The issue's predicted symptom ('selecting a cell tints the entire table') is NOT REAL and cannot occur — see the blocker filed above. Verified against prosemirror-tables v1.8.5's own style/tables.css, which requires 'position: relative' on td/th (missing here, now added, editor-only), plus box-sizing:border-box (already covered by the global reset) and vertical-align:top (deliberately NOT adopted — our cells are middle-aligned and nobody asked to change that).

The mechanism in the issue was right: .column-resize-handle is a widget decoration inserted INSIDE the cell (index.js:2566-2571) and .selectedCell::after is a pseudo of the cell, so with no positioned cell both resolve against .tableWrapper (prosemirror.css:144). But no overlay is ever created, because the schema NaN-poisons TableMap first.

This change is therefore invisible today. Landed anyway because it is a genuine upstream-documented requirement and the overlays would otherwise render against the wrapper the moment the schema is fixed.

PAINT-ORDER ANALYSIS vs the new table surface: safe, and the two decisions turned out coupled. Cells carry NO background (the deliberate choice in attn-11g4.3), so positioning them lifts nothing into the positioned-descendants phase that could cover the panel. Had the header row been tinted, position:relative would now paint that fill over the table's own border and radius. Also: under 'border-collapse: collapse' the effect of position on a cell is UNDEFINED per CSS 2.1 s17.6.2 and engines have historically ignored it — attn-11g4.3's move to 'separate' is what makes this legal at all.

SIDE EFFECT, flagged not fixed (app.css not owned): .attn-remote-view-marker (collab presence, app.css:1006) is absolute with inset-inline-start:-1.4rem. app.css:994 positions its parent only for p/h1-h6/blockquote/pre/code/li — td/th are absent — so today a presence marker in a cell resolves against .tableWrapper and paints at the table's top-left gutter. After this change it resolves against the cell: clipped by overflow-x:auto in column 1, overlapping neighbouring text in columns 2+. Arguably more correct, possibly worse-looking. Only visible in a live collab session with a remote cursor in a cell.

title: Invert the content-measure allowlist to opt-out
description:
Surfaced while fixing attn-vlmz.3.1. The shared content column is applied by a hand-maintained opt-IN allowlist in two places (prosemirror.css '.ProseMirror > :is(...)' and base.css 'article.attn-doc > :is(...)'). Every element not named in it silently escapes the measure and misaligns.

Evidence this is systemic, not a one-off: fixing the reported frontmatter card required also adding .math-container, which was escaping identically and had NOT been reported — found only because the list was audited. The editor's blast radius is exactly one entry per top-level NodeView (currently mermaid, math, frontmatter) and grows by one every time a NodeView is added.

Worse on the viewer side: comrak passes raw HTML blocks straight through, so an author writing <div>, <details>, <figure> or <aside> in their markdown puts an arbitrary element directly under article.attn-doc, outside the measure. No allowlist can ever cover that.

Proposed durable fix: invert to 'article.attn-doc > * { max-width: var(--content-measure); margin-inline: auto }' with explicit opt-outs for the wrappers that need the min() clamp (.prose-scroll-x, .code-block, .tableWrapper carry 'max-width: min(100%, var(--content-measure))' and must keep it) and for hr (deliberately an 8rem flourish).

SHORTHAND TRAP to carry over: an allowlist entry alone is not always sufficient. .ProseMirror .frontmatter-card ties the allowlist on specificity (0,2,0) and comes later in the file, and its 'margin: 0 0 1.5rem' shorthand carries an implicit 'margin-inline: 0' that beat 'margin-inline: auto'. It had to be changed to 'margin-block'. Any inversion must sweep for margin shorthands on block children.
acceptance_criteria: Document blocks are inside the content measure by default in both the editor and the read-only viewer, including raw HTML blocks passed through by comrak; the min()-clamped wrappers and hr keep their current behaviour; adding a new NodeView requires no stylesheet change to stay aligned; verified at 960px and 660px content measures.

title: Persist rail width and update the width assertions
description:
Store the chosen width so it survives a restart. Preferences already have a durable home: src/prefs.rs holds theme and typeset in prefs.json under the daemon's runtime namespace and stamps values before first paint — extend that rather than adding a second mechanism. Note the Rust side normalises unknown values, so a width needs range clamping there too.

Add a double-click-to-reset and keyboard resize for accessibility.

REQUIRED: scripts/test-review-e2e.sh:389 and :413 assert offsetWidth is exactly 48 and exactly 320. Update them to reset to default first or to assert against the stored width — do not delete the coverage.
acceptance_criteria: Rail width survives a daemon restart; out-of-range or corrupt stored values clamp to the default; double-click resets; keyboard resize works; the review E2E suite passes with its width assertions intact and meaningful.
notes:
VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY (report still pending). Rust: RAIL_WIDTH_DEFAULT/MIN/MAX = 320/260/640 in prefs.rs, normalize_rail_width() range-checks, #[serde(default)] for forward compat. main.rs carries exactly the two authorised lines (let rail_width + "railWidth" in the init payload) with a comment explaining why this one is NOT stamped pre-paint like theme/typeset — the rail only exists inside a review room, so there is no first frame for a wrong width to flash on.

E2E rewrite is STRONGER than what it replaced, not weaker:
- resets via the product's own path (dispatches dblclick on the handle) before asserting 320, so the reset affordance is itself exercised rather than reached around;
- line 433 asserts offsetWidth === r.dataset.defaultWidth, so the test cannot pass merely because script and component share a hardcoded literal — an explicit anti-tautology guard;
- new assertions for the 260 min clamp, keyboard-resize increments, and aria-valuenow === offsetWidth so the ARIA value cannot drift from reality.

A11Y: role=separator + tabindex=0 + aria-orientation + aria-valuenow/min/max all present. The two svelte-check warnings this produced were suppressed with a NARROW two-rule svelte-ignore on that single element — the correct call, since Svelte's linter does not model a focusable separator (the ARIA splitter pattern) as interactive. Warnings are back to the pre-existing baseline of 1.

OPEN DESIGN NOTE: normalize_rail_width falls back to RAIL_WIDTH_DEFAULT rather than clamping to the nearest bound. That matches normalize_typeset's discipline in the same file, but for a numeric range clamping preserves intent better (a stored 700 -> 640 beats snapping to 320). Worth revisiting if the bounds ever move.

title: Add the drag handle and resize interaction
description:
Put a grab affordance on the rail's left border (a pill or hairline that thickens on hover), and implement pointer-drag resizing with a live-updating width.

Enforce a sensible minimum (cards must stay legible — the expanded default is 320px) and a maximum tied to keeping the document readable. Use pointer events so it works with trackpad and touch, set the right cursor, and make sure dragging does not select document text.

The rail is a docked panel with its own surface now, so the handle sits on a real edge.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging the left edge resizes the rail live; min and max are enforced; no text selection or scroll jank while dragging; the cursor changes on hover; works with a trackpad; margin cards reflow correctly at every width.

title: Show an explicit loading state while the share room mints
description:
Between the previous step and the link step there is a stall with no feedback. The phase machine already models it (ShareDialog.svelte:117, 'minting'), so this is a presentation gap.

Give minting a real loading state — spinner or progress affordance with a plain-English line about what is happening (creating the room, minting invite links). Reuse whatever the app already uses for pending work rather than inventing a spinner.

Related: the tier-link skeleton is a separate concern and its stuck-forever failure is filed under the web epic as attn-vlmz.1.2. Keep the two consistent; the same dialog serves both builds.
acceptance_criteria: The wait between steps shows a labelled loading state within 100ms; the state clears on ready and on error; the dialog does not resize when it clears; honours prefers-reduced-motion.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED. Reused the existing pending idiom rather than adding a spinner: the native shell's pulsing dot (animate-pulse), already used at ShareDialog.svelte:479 and App.svelte:2998. Pulling in the hosted .share-spinner or components/ui/skeleton would have introduced a third idiom into one dialog.

Three surfaces now carry the state: Dialog.Description reads 'Creating the encrypted room and minting invite links...' during minting; the primary card's minting row is role=status aria-live=polite; the three tier placeholders read 'Preparing view/comment/suggest link...' in a role=status group, no longer named like finished controls. Within 100ms is satisfied because phase='minting' is set synchronously in startMint() before the await.

Reduced motion: the global block neutralises animate-pulse, which is fine ONLY because the meaning now lives in text and live regions rather than the animation — noted in a code comment so nobody 'fixes' it by adding a motion-independent spinner.

HEIGHT-JUMP BUG FIXED en route: share-ready-files ('Reviewers receive') was gated on isReady, so the dialog grew a whole section the instant ShareReady landed — exactly what the dialog-content.svelte comment claims does not happen. Now renders from minting onward (selection is already known), identical content across the transition.

title: Make the comments rail resizable with a drag handle
description:
The right-hand comments rail is a fixed width today: RAIL_WIDTH_PX in web/src/lib/review/rail-mode.ts is a literal Record ({hidden: 0, collapsed: 48, expanded: 320}) consumed by WorkspaceEditorFrame as an inline style. Users want to drag it wider.

Design note: the rail was just converted from a transparent floating margin to a docked painted panel with a hairline left border, so it now has a real edge for a handle to live on.

WATCH OUT — scripts/test-review-e2e.sh:389 and :413 assert offsetWidth is EXACTLY 48 and EXACTLY 320. A persisted custom width will break those unless they are updated to reset or assert against the stored value.
acceptance_criteria: The rail can be dragged from its left edge with a visible handle/pill; a minimum and maximum are enforced; the chosen width persists across restarts; keyboard resize and a double-click reset exist; the review E2E width assertions are updated rather than deleted.

title: Write the threat model and choose a sanitisation approach for embedded markup
description:
Before any parser flag changes, decide what is allowed and prove the boundary.

Inputs are not trusted: documents are authored by agents and received from peers over shares. In the hosted build the app origin holds room secrets, so injected script is a direct compromise, not a cosmetic bug.

Cover: SVG only or general HTML; sanitiser choice (DOMPurify vs an explicit allowlist); where sanitisation runs (parse time vs render time vs both); how the native build differs from hosted; and how the original source survives a round trip so sanitising never rewrites the user's file.
acceptance_criteria: A written threat model and decision record; an explicit tag/attribute allowlist; a chosen sanitiser with justification; a documented answer for round-tripping unsanitised source.
notes:
COMPLETE. Deny-by-default allowlist sanitiser, verified at the claimed lines: svg-sanitizer.ts:254 'const keep = ALLOWED_ELEMENTS.has(tag)', :310 'if (!keep) return null', :456 'if (!ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES.has(rawName)) return null' — attributes are never examined on a dropped element. All six bypass classes answered by name in the record's section 6: mXSS (parse once, build DOM directly, sanitised result NEVER re-serialised or re-parsed, guarded by a test grepping both modules for innerHTML/outerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML/document.write); namespace (createElementNS(SVG_NS) unconditionally, xmlns* dropped, foreignObject/math/annotation-xml dropped WITH SUBTREE rather than unwrapped); use/xlink:href (only on <use>, only ^#[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$, checked AFTER entity decoding, rewritten into the block's own id space); SMIL (no animation element allowlisted, so nothing can rewrite a validated attribute); <style> element (dropped with subtree — the one case CSP would not have caught on either build); entity/DTD (any '<!' other than '<!--' rejects the whole block).

The agent WITHDREW its binary-size argument against DOMPurify once the no-CSP finding inverted the cost/benefit, and hardened instead: an independent post-build DOM audit (embedded-svg-view.ts:64) that re-checks the CONSTRUCTED DOM against the same tables plus namespace, /^on/i and URL schemes, so parser and audit must fail together; plus the innerHTML regression test. DOMPurify (RETURN_DOM_FRAGMENT) and hosted-only-with-native-disabled remain recorded as open fallbacks.

KEY SECURITY FINDING recorded in the threat model and worth acting on independently: the native app shell has NO Content-Security-Policy. The only CSP in src/main.rs (:816) is gated on .html/.htm files served to the sandboxed HtmlViewer iframe. The hosted build has a real policy with no unsafe-inline. So native — the build that also exposes the window.__attn__ IPC bridge — is the weaker target.

title: Decide and build the shared accordion primitive
description:
There is no accordion in web/src/lib/components/ui/ — the closest existing primitive is `collapsible` (bits-ui). Decide between adopting collapsible and adding a real accordion (bits-ui ships one), and record the reasoning.

The consumer is awkward and should be weighed in the decision: the frontmatter card is a ProseMirror NodeView built with imperative document.createElement, so a Svelte primitive means either mounting a component inside the NodeView or extracting the accordion's behaviour and styling into something a NodeView can use directly.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded with its rationale; the chosen primitive exists in components/ui with the app's focus, keyboard, and reduced-motion conventions; the approach for using it from a ProseMirror NodeView is proven.

title: Bring the frontmatter card inside the shared content measure
description:
Root cause is known. styles/prosemirror.css:103 applies `max-width: var(--content-measure); margin-inline: auto` to an explicit element list:
  `.ProseMirror > :is(p, h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6, ul, ol, dl, blockquote, pre, table, .mermaid-container)`
The frontmatter card renders as `<details class="frontmatter-card">` and is absent from that list, so it ignores the column entirely.

base.css carries the same list for the read-only viewer (`article.attn-doc > :is(...)`) and needs the same addition.

While here, audit the list for other NodeView-rendered blocks that escape it — an allowlist that must be hand-updated per node type is the actual defect.
acceptance_criteria: The frontmatter card shares its left and right edges with surrounding prose in editor and viewer, at every typeset including manuscript (660px) and editorial (960px); any other block found escaping the measure is fixed or filed.
notes: IMPLEMENTED (pending visual verification). .frontmatter-card added to BOTH measure allowlists: prosemirror.css:113 (.ProseMirror > :is(...)) and base.css:123 (article.attn-doc > :is(...)). AUDIT RESULT: .math-container was ALSO escaping the content measure and has been added to both lists — same class of bug, not reported by the user, found only because the allowlist was audited. This confirms the underlying defect: a hand-maintained per-node-type allowlist silently omits every new NodeView. Worth a follow-up to invert it (opt-out rather than opt-in) so future NodeViews are aligned by default.

title: Apply the shared surface-plane system to the hosted app
description:
With both elements identified, give them backgrounds drawn from the shared token set rather than ad-hoc values.

Reuse the system the native app now uses: chrome planes recessed onto the sidebar's plane (--panel-surface behind --panel-border), the document as a lighter sheet between them, and floating cards above on --review-card-surface. Verify in Paper and Ink; light and dark need opposite lightness moves.
acceptance_criteria: Both surfaces are visibly distinct from their neighbours in both themes; values come from shared tokens; no regression to the document reading surface; screenshots before/after in both themes.
notes:
TARGETS (from attn-vlmz.2.1):
1. HEADER — App.svelte:3165-3167. Swap bg-background/border-border for --panel-surface/--panel-border, matching .right-rail (WorkspaceEditorFrame.svelte:129-136) and the sidebar. tokens.css:110-117 already argues for this: the panel value was chosen so 'with both edges recessed equally the document reads as a lit sheet between two rails'. The header currently sits ON the paper, which is the one remaining gap in that story.
   DO ALL THREE HEADERS TOGETHER: the same grammar is duplicated at HostedDesktopWorkspaceFrame.svelte:228-230 (data-slot=owner-header) and BrowserReviewApp.svelte:1249, deliberately unified per the ruling recorded at HostedDesktopWorkspaceFrame.svelte:224. Changing only the native one forks that decision. Doing all three also delivers the hosted half of this feature.
2. DROP CARD — OpenLocalFiles.svelte:127-129. DECISION: recess to --panel-surface so it reads as a well you drop INTO, which suits a drop target better than a raised card; keep the dashed edge for the drop affordance. The alternative (--review-card-surface, an object resting on the paper) is defensible and is a one-token change if it looks wrong.
   BLOCKED-ISH: OpenLocalFiles.svelte is untracked and was authored by a separate concurrent workstream.

title: Identify the two flagged surfaces in source before restyling
description:
Run the hosted build, locate `#app > .relative > .relative` and `#bits-c2 > #bits-1 > .flex > .flex` in the live DOM, and record which components render them. The second is a bits-ui portal — the id is generated per mount, so only a runtime check is reliable.

Record findings on this issue before any CSS is written; the styling task depends on it.
acceptance_criteria: Both selectors are mapped to a named component and file path, recorded in this issue, with a screenshot of each highlighted.
notes:
MAPPED — both selectors resolved with certainty from recorded agentation session data (fullPath, cssClasses, boundingBox, computedStyles), then reproduced live and confirmed (stored boundingBox 434x259 at x=533 reproduced exactly).

PREMISE CORRECTION: this feedback is against the NATIVE frontend, not the hosted build. The reporter was on web/index.html -> src/main.ts -> App.svelte, i.e. what plain 'npm run dev' serves at /. 'npm run dev:browser' has vite root web/hosted and serves the marketing Landing at /, with the hosted desk at /app rendering AppShell -> EditorShell (div.editor-shell, never main.relative). Verified independently: the annotated element carries pl-[6.5rem] + data-slot=native-header, markup that exists in exactly one file in the repo (App.svelte:3166).

1) '#app > .relative > .relative' — AMBIGUOUS, matches two elements live (header.relative and div#bits-c1.relative). fullPath settles it: header[data-slot=native-header], App.svelte nativeHeader() snippet, element at :3165-3167. It is the top chrome bar. Background is bg-background = oklch(0.905 0.01 78), IDENTICAL to the paper; only a border-b hairline separates them, which is exactly why the top of the window reads as undifferentiated.

2) '#bits-c2 > #bits-1 > .flex > .flex' — NOT a portal (no dialog was open). #bits-c1/#bits-c2 are the bits-ui ScrollArea root and viewport (scroll-area.svelte:55/:61); #bits-1 is its inner content wrapper. The target is the dashed empty-state drop-zone card in OpenLocalFiles.svelte:127-129, inside [data-slot=empty-workspace]. Background: none, fully transparent, 1px dashed border only.

Screenshots with the element outlined are in the session scratchpad (surface-1-native-header.png, surface-2-drop-card.png).

title: Render inline SVG and HTML safely in documents
description:
A document containing raw SVG renders as literal escaped text in a paragraph — the reporter saw `<svg preserveAspectRatio="xMinYMin meet"...` as body copy.

Root cause: web/src/lib/schema.ts:387 constructs the parser as `MarkdownIt('default', { html: false })`, so all raw HTML is escaped by design.

This is SECURITY-SENSITIVE and must not be a one-line flag flip. attn renders agent-authored documents and documents received from peers over a share; in the hosted build a malicious shared document that can inject markup is an XSS vector against the reviewer's origin, which also holds room secrets. Any solution needs sanitisation, an explicit allowlist, and a serializer that round-trips the original source.
acceptance_criteria: SVG in a markdown document renders as an image in both the native and hosted builds; script, event-handler attributes, foreignObject, and external references are stripped; the original markdown round-trips byte-exact; the sanitiser has direct unit tests including known SVG XSS payloads; the threat model is written down.

title: Frontmatter card: align to the content column and build it on a shared accordion
description:
Two defects in the folded frontmatter card (web/src/lib/prosemirror/frontmatter-nodeview.ts):

1. ALIGNMENT — root cause found. styles/prosemirror.css:103 caps and centres the content column with
     `.ProseMirror > :is(p, h1..h6, ul, ol, dl, blockquote, pre, table, .mermaid-container)`
   `.frontmatter-card` is a <details> element and is NOT in that list, so it escapes the measure and sits out of alignment with every other block.

2. COMPONENT — the card is hand-rolled imperative DOM (document.createElement('details'/'summary')) with its own chevron span and rotate transform. It shares nothing with the rest of the app. Note there is currently NO accordion primitive in web/src/lib/components/ui/ — the nearest is `collapsible` (bits-ui). Deciding between adopting collapsible and adding a real accordion is part of this work.

Constraint: this is a ProseMirror NodeView, so mounting a Svelte component inside it is non-trivial and needs an explicit approach.
acceptance_criteria: The frontmatter card shares the same left and right edges as surrounding prose at every typeset; its open/close behaviour and chevron come from one shared primitive used elsewhere in the app; the raw YAML still round-trips byte-exact through the node's value attr.

title: Differentiate hosted surfaces so panes and overlays read as distinct planes
description:
Two elements were flagged as needing a differentiated background:
  - `#app > .relative > .relative`
  - `#bits-c2 > #bits-1 > .flex > .flex`

bits-ui ids are generated per mount, so the second cannot be mapped to source statically — it must be identified at runtime before anything is restyled.

The native app has just been given a surface system for exactly this problem (chrome planes vs document sheet, using --panel-surface / --panel-border on the sidebar plane, with cards floating above on --review-card-surface). The hosted build should adopt the same system rather than inventing per-element colours.
acceptance_criteria: Both flagged elements are identified in source and documented; both carry a background that is visibly distinct from their neighbours in Paper and Ink; the treatment reuses the shared surface tokens rather than one-off values.
notes: SCOPE CORRECTED after attn-vlmz.2.1: the two flagged surfaces are in the NATIVE frontend (App.svelte, OpenLocalFiles.svelte), not the hosted build. The epic title says 'Hosted web app' because the reporter said 'web version' — they were running the native frontend in a browser tab via 'npm run dev'. Features .1/.3/.4 are unaffected (they are genuinely shared or hosted); only this feature's file targets change.

title: app-shell.css uses 11 distinct border-radius values with no documented scale
description:
Same pathology the type ramp had, one property over. attn-n01r.8 found app-shell.css had drifted to 33 distinct font sizes because no documented step fit, and fixed it by writing a nine-step ramp into DESIGN.md and snapping every value to it. Radius never got that treatment.

MEASURED in web/src/hosted/app/app-shell.css after snapping the two singletons the design hook flagged:
  8px x13 · 50% x10 · 6px x11 · 999px x6 · 2px x3 · var(--radius-md) x2 · var(--radius-lg) x2
  12px x2 · 14px x2 · 10px x1 · '14px 14px 0 0' x1 · inherit x1 · 0 x1

Eleven distinct non-trivial values, four of them used once or twice, and two tokens (--radius-md/--radius-lg from chrome.css) used only twice between them while raw px is used ~40 times. 8px and 6px sit one step apart doing the same job on the same kind of element.

DESIGN.md documents radii only per-component and incompletely: micro 2px (line 208, 'the mark family for inline review marks, focus rings, and accent bars'), review margin card 10px (241), chip 10px (245), tree rows 9px (250), insertion mark 2px (255). There is no scale, so 6px/8px/12px/14px are unfalsifiable — which is exactly why they multiplied.

WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED: choosing the scale is a design decision with visible consequence on nearly every element of the desk and editor, and it arrived at the end of a 48-commit branch that is about to be smoke-tested. Reshaping every corner unreviewed is not a hook-cleanup task. The two values the hook actually named (4px on .folio-filter kbd, 5px on .file) were snapped to 6px, since both were singletons in a file already using 6px eleven times.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, to be argued not assumed: a four-step scale (2 micro / 6 control / 10 card / 999 pill) plus 50% for avatars, with 8/12/14 folded into their nearest step and the raw px replaced by tokens so DESIGN.md and the CSS cannot drift again. Landing.css should be measured the same way before committing to the numbers.

Note the design-system-radius hook findings currently compare against .impeccable/design.json, which is dated Aug 3 and predates the Aug 5 DESIGN.md work; refresh the sidecar before trusting them.

title: Landing review demo: color-contrast violation on the reviewer avatar after the visitor joins
description:
PRE-EXISTING on main — NOT introduced by the attn-n01r epic. Verified by checking out main and running the same spec there; it fails identically.

FAILING TEST: web/e2e/landing-review-demo.spec.ts:36 'landing demo shows agent feedback and lets the visitor join the review'. Its trailing axe run (wcag2a/2aa/21a/21aa) reports:
  id: color-contrast, impact: serious, target: span[data-author-kind="reviewer"]
This is the only failure in the 91-test routes suite; the other 89 pass (1 skipped).

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED:
- The element is .rmc-avatar in web/src/lib/ReviewMarginCard.svelte:417 — a 16px circle, aria-hidden, glyph in var(--monogram) (oklch(1 0 0), white in both themes) over an inline background-color from reviewStore.colorFor(authorId).
- It does NOT reproduce on initial load: axe on /app?surface=landing-review-demo&autoplay=0 reports zero violations. It only appears after the visitor selects text, comments, and joins — so it is the freshly-created 'You' card.
- The palette is not the cause. Measured white against all nine PARTICIPANT_PALETTE swatches plus AGENT_COLOR: 5.07:1 (berry) to 20.54:1 (clay). Every one passes 4.5:1.
- The demo's VISITOR_ID participant declares no color, so colorFor falls through userProfile.color (defaults null) to hashParticipantColor — which always returns a palette swatch.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: the actual failing foreground/background pair. My attempt to reproduce the join in a probe spec did not drive the ProseMirror selection correctly, so I never read the computed colors off the failing node. I am deliberately NOT recording a mechanism I did not measure. The next step is to take the real test, insert a getComputedStyle read on span[data-author-kind='reviewer'] just before the axe call, and print color/backgroundColor/fontSize — the pair will name the bug immediately.

One hypothesis worth testing first, unverified: that the inline background-color is momentarily unset for a locally-authored card whose author is not yet resolved in the roster, leaving white-on-card (~1.1:1).

SCOPE NOTE: ReviewMarginCard is shared with the native app, so a palette or token change here is cross-surface and should not be made casually.

title: 'New workspace' on the desk sometimes reopens an existing empty workspace with no feedback
description:
Split out of attn-n01r.6 rather than folded into it, because it changes a documented behaviour.

`AppShell.svelte:71-88` scans for a workspace named 'Untitled' with `assetCount 0`,
`markdownCount <= 1` and an empty body, and reuses it instead of creating. The guard exists for a
good reason (attn-cjn): a bookmarked `/app#new` or a back-button revisit should not grow the desk by
one empty workspace every time.

But `AppShell.svelte:100-108` routes the DESK BUTTON through the same `createAndOpen()`, so a control
labelled "New workspace" sometimes reopens an old one and says nothing about it.

MEASURED: clicking "+ New workspace" on an untouched Untitled workspace returned
`/app/w/XikIfzW835EqJETFvOKa0w/untitled.md` — byte-identical to the previous click — and the desk row
count stayed at 3 across a fourth click.

RECOMMENDED: scope the idempotency guard to the `#new` URL intent, and always create from the desk
button. The guard then does exactly the job it was written for and the button tells the truth.
The alternative — keeping reuse and saying "Reopening your empty draft" — is honest but worse: it
explains a behaviour nobody asked for.

Note the naming fix in attn-n01r.6 reduces the sting: a reused workspace that has since been typed
into now carries its own heading as a name, so it is at least identifiable. The button still lies
about what the click did.
close_reason:
Fixed by scoping the guard to the intent it was written for.

createAndOpen() now takes an explicit  flag:
  /app#new URL intent  -> true   (attn-cjn's idempotency, unchanged)
  desk button onCreate -> false  (always creates)

The guard exists so a bookmarked /app#new or a back-button revisit does not grow the desk. It was
also running for the desk's 'New workspace' button, so a control with that label sometimes reopened
an old workspace and said nothing about it.

VERIFIED: clicking the desk button three times now returns three distinct workspace ids
  6--dqGYSj1wiAgiVHzXwYQ / xq-GfTd-eytsWflyO-co2Q / IImq-6GZDIRyvjzhPdPJFg
and the desk lists 3 rows. Previously it returned the same id every time and the row count never
moved.

NOT PROPERLY VERIFIED — the /app#new idempotency itself. My probe navigated to '/app/#new' and both
runs produced a null id, so the 'same id' result was vacuous rather than a pass. The code path is
unchanged (that call site now passes  explicitly, which is the behaviour it already had), so I
have no reason to think it regressed — but I did not actually exercise it and I am not claiming
otherwise. Worth covering in the routes e2e alongside the budgets added for .41, since it is exactly
the kind of URL-intent behaviour that regresses silently.

97/97 test files; svelte-check 0 errors.

title: Route-bundle gate now measures the wire, not just the module graph
description:
Closes the second half of attn-n01r.41: the gate that reported green while ~600 KB of the graph it
guards shipped to the desk.

TWO CHANGES.

1. **Runtime script budgets, in e2e/hosted-routes.spec.ts.** A static-manifest gate structurally
   cannot see an awaited `import()` — Vite records that graph under `chunk.dynamicImports`, which the
   walk does not traverse. Only measuring what the browser fetches can. Added:
   - a per-route script-byte budget, asserted from actual `content-length` on script responses:
       `/`     110 KB   (measured ~72 KB)
       `/app`  500 KB   (measured ~414 KB)
     Headroom is deliberate but small — these should fail on a regression, not absorb one.
   - a desk equivalent of the landing's forbidden-chunk check (`FORBIDDEN_ON_DESK`), asserting the
     desk fetches no prosemirror / mermaid / katex / schema / BrowserReviewApp chunk at all.

2. **The static gate now states only what it verified.** It printed 'route bundle boundaries hold:
   landing/app never preload editor or crypto chunks', which reads as a guarantee about what ships.
   It now prints 'static route graphs clean: no editor or crypto chunks statically reachable' plus an
   explicit note that dynamic-import graphs are not checked here and that the wire is covered by the
   budgets above.

Why both: the static walk is genuinely useful and correct about the module graph — it should keep
running. The failure was that its success message claimed more than its method could support, and a
gate that overstates itself is worse than no gate, because it converts an unnoticed regression into a
documented guarantee.

VERIFIED: `node web/scripts/check-route-bundles.mjs` passes and prints the honest message. The e2e
budgets could not be executed here (the routes config boots `wrangler dev`), but the numbers they
assert are the ones measured throughout attn-n01r.41 with the same content-length method.
close_reason:
Done in the same change that filed it — see the description for the full rationale.

VERIFIED: node web/scripts/check-route-bundles.mjs passes and now prints
  'static route graphs clean: no editor or crypto chunks statically reachable'
  '  note: dynamic-import graphs are NOT checked here — see the script budgets in e2e/hosted-routes.spec.ts'
instead of the previous 'route bundle boundaries hold', which claimed more than the method supports.

The e2e budgets type-check and are wired into the existing routes suite. They could not be executed
in this environment (playwright.routes.config.ts boots `wrangler dev`), but the thresholds are the
numbers measured repeatedly throughout attn-n01r.41 using the same content-length method — / at ~72 KB
against a 110 KB budget, /app at ~414 KB against 500 KB.

Anyone running `npm run test:e2e:routes` will exercise them for real. If the desk regresses past
500 KB the assertion names the actual figure, which is the diagnostic the old gate could not give.

title: Collab and review-drift tests flake under the parallel runner; pass in isolation
description:
Two collab/review test files fail intermittently under the parallel runner and pass reliably in
isolation. Seen repeatedly across this session:

  src/lib/review/review-drift-check.test.ts       — flaked before any attn-n01r change was made
  src/lib/review/browser-local-collab.test.ts     — flaked after, on "published room authority stays
                                                    live for local follower tabs / headless published
                                                    edit commits once"

Evidence:
- `npx tsx src/lib/review/browser-local-collab.test.ts` -> 11/11 passed, three runs in a row.
- `npm run test:unit` -> alternates: one run fails browser-local-collab, the next fails
  review-drift-check, the next passes 97/97 clean.
- review-drift-check was already flaking early in the session, before any source change.

WHY IT NEEDS A LOOK RATHER THAN A SHRUG: attn-n01r.41 deferred several imports onto their call sites
(`await import('../schema')` inside LocalCollabHub.commitNow and loadSeed, and
`await import('../prosemirror/collab-controller')` in browser-session). Each adds a microtask before
work that was previously synchronous. The commit-ordering contract itself is preserved — commitNow
still registers its promise in `inflightCommits` synchronously, which is what close() awaits — but a
test asserting "commits once" by counting within a fixed number of ticks would become more sensitive
to scheduling, not less.

So the honest read is: probably a pre-existing timing dependency in these tests, plausibly made
easier to hit. Both are true statements and only measurement separates them.

Worth doing:
1. Run browser-local-collab.test.ts N times against the commit BEFORE attn-n01r.41's first pass and
   after it, and compare failure rates. That settles cause in one experiment.
2. If the tests are counting commits by tick rather than by awaiting the recorded promises, fix the
   assertion to await `inflightCommits` — the contract the implementation actually offers.
3. A flaky collab test is worse than a failing one: it trains people to re-run.
close_reason:
Root-caused by experiment, and it was my regression — not a pre-existing flake.

I filed this suspecting the deferred imports had 'sensitised' an already-timing-dependent test, and
noted the experiment that would settle it. I ran it.

  browser-local-collab.test.ts, in isolation, 20 runs each:
    BEFORE the deferred import (9d65236^)   0/20 failed
    AFTER  the deferred import (HEAD)       3/20 failed
    AFTER  this fix                         0/20 failed

Not the parallel runner, not pre-existing:  inside commitNow added a tick
before the commit was issued, and 'headless published edit commits once' is timing-dependent on it.
close()'s contract was never violated — the promise was still registered synchronously — which is
exactly why it read as safe and why only measurement caught it.

FIX: prime the module in loadSeed, which is async and always runs before any commit, into a
module-scoped . commitNow reads the cached reference and serializes synchronously, as
it originally did. The desk still never loads the module — verified after the fix, /app ships
414.1 KB of script with 0 ProseMirror/schema chunks, unchanged from before.

Note the honest shape of this: the earlier reasoning ('close() awaits inflightCommits, so registering
synchronously is sufficient') was correct about the contract and insufficient as a safety argument.
The contract held; the test still broke, because the test measures issue timing rather than
completion. Correct-about-the-invariant is not the same as safe-to-change.

REMAINING, separate and genuinely pre-existing: review-drift-check.test.ts also flakes under the
parallel runner. It was flaking early in this session before any attn-n01r change, and it passes
standalone. Not caused here, and not investigated — worth its own look, since a flaky test trains
people to re-run.

Full suite: 97/97 clean. svelte-check 0 errors.

title: Landing has no breakpoint between 680 and 1180px; type and tracks go ragged across the band
description:
Split out of attn-n01r.24 when the badge-collision half was fixed. What remains is composition work
that wants a design decision, not a mechanical change — which is why it did not ship with the fix.

`landing.css` still contains exactly two media queries: `max-width: 1180px` and `max-width: 680px`.
Between 681 and 1180 every multi-column grid keeps its desktop track count while the container loses
up to 500px.

Measured track widths across the band:

  .entry-strip (3 cols)   768: 278/223/223   1024: 377/302/302   1180: 437/350/350
  .steps (3 cols)         768: 241 x3        1024: 326 x3        1180: 378 x3
  .surfaces (2 cols)      768: 361/361       1024: 489 x2        1180: 567 x2
  .share-proof            768: 395/280       1024: 582/349       1180: 680/408

Three consequences:

1. **`.surface h3` is a flat 41.6px across the entire range** — no `clamp()`, unlike the h1 and the
   chapter h2 which both clamp. So "Your private desk" runs 41.6px type inside a 290px content box at
   768px: it breaks to two lines, and the mono list item "→ Existing files stay where they are"
   orphans "are" onto its own line.

2. **The entry cards show the same pressure** — "Import workspace" wraps to two lines while its
   neighbours do not, leaving ragged body-copy baselines across the strip.

3. **`.hero-lede` is capped at `max-width: 610px`** and never grows, so at 1024 the hero column is
   922px and the lede stops 312px short of the h1's edge — a visibly ragged right margin with a large
   empty right half.

Recommended: add a ~900px breakpoint dropping `.entry-strip` and `.steps` to 2 columns and
`.surfaces` to 1; add `clamp()` to `.surface h3` and `.entry-title`; let `.hero-lede` grow with its
column or cap it in `ch` against the measure rather than a fixed px.

Note the 200%-text work (attn-n01r.23) already converted these grids to `minmax(0, …)` and made the
nav wrap, so the band no longer *overflows* — it is now a proportion and rhythm problem rather than a
breakage one.

Suggested command: /impeccable adapt
close_reason:
Fixed. The band has a tier, and the type in it scales.

ADDED a 980px breakpoint — .entry-strip and .steps drop to 2 columns, .surfaces and .share-proof to 1.
MEASURED grid tracks:
        BEFORE (desktop counts held all the way down)   AFTER
  768   entry 278/223/223 · steps 241x3 · surfaces 361/361   entry 363/363 · steps 362/362 · surfaces 721
  900   —                                                    entry 429/429 · steps 428/428 · surfaces 853
  1024  entry 377/302/302 · steps 326x3 · surfaces 489x2      unchanged (desktop tier resumes)
  1180  entry 437/350/350                                     unchanged
Zero horizontal overflow at every width.

.surface h3 NOW CLAMPS — clamp(1.9rem, 3.2vw, 2.6rem). It was a flat 41.6px across the whole range
while its container shed 500px, so 'Your private desk' broke to two lines inside a 290px box at 768
while its neighbour stayed on one.
MEASURED: 30px @768 -> 33 @1024 -> 38 @1180 -> 42 @1440. .entry-title clamps on the same principle.

.hero-lede CAPPED IN ch, NOT px — max-width: 62ch. The finding offered either growing it with the
column or capping it against the measure; I took the measure. Growing it to the hero column's 922px
at 1024 would produce a 100+ character line, which trades a ragged right margin for an unreadable
one. 62ch is the readable cap and it now scales with the type rather than sitting at a fixed 610px.

title: Blocked/quota states hide the primary actions from keyboard users with no reason exposed
description:
When storage is blocked or under quota pressure, the desk disables its primary actions and tells a keyboard or screen-reader user nothing about why.

  DeskHome.svelte:135, 146 — measured: `disabled` true, `aria-disabled` null, `title` null.

Because the controls use the `disabled` attribute rather than `aria-disabled`, they are removed from the tab order entirely. A keyboard user never encounters "New workspace" or "Import workspace" at all — the primary actions simply are not there, with no explanation of their absence.

The banner above them does not fill the gap: `DegradedBanner.svelte:42` uses `role="status"`, a *polite* live region that is rendered at page load rather than announced as a change. A polite region present at first paint announces nothing.

Fix:
- Use `aria-disabled="true"` plus a click guard instead of `disabled`, so the controls stay focusable and discoverable.
- Add `aria-describedby` pointing at the reason.
- Promote the banner to `role="alert"` for the quota-pressure and blocked modes specifically, so the state change is announced.

Two related gaps from the same pass:
- **No status announcement for rename or delete.** There is no `aria-live` region anywhere on the desk; deleting a workspace removes a row silently. WCAG 4.1.3 (AA).
- **Cancel and "Delete workspace" are visually near-identical** in the confirm dialog — both `.button`, same 46px height, same border, same fill, differing only by one step of the same hue in text colour. On a destructive, irreversible confirmation, the two options should not be near-twins.

Worth preserving, and unusual: the degraded-state vocabulary itself (`DegradedBanner.svelte`, `AppHeader.svelte:14-27`, `StoragePage.svelte:65-103`) is genuinely thorough — five distinct persistence modes with specific, honest, non-alarmist copy, all reachable via `?shell=` for testing. `DegradedBanner.svelte:50-53` even documents a real prior fix where dead `<button>`s became working links on the "back up before you lose data" prompt. The states are well modelled; only their announcement is missing.

Suggested command: /impeccable harden
close_reason:
Fixed the blocking half; two smaller items are called out below.

THE PRIMARY ACTIONS STAY REACHABLE — New workspace and Import workspace used the 
attribute, which removes an element from the tab order entirely, so a keyboard user in a blocked
storage profile never encountered the desk's two primary actions and was never told why they were
missing. They now use aria-disabled with a click guard, so they keep their place in the tab order and
are announced as unavailable.

THE REASON IS NOW STATED — added a role='alert' explanation the buttons point at via
aria-describedby: what is wrong, and what to check. The DegradedBanner above uses role='status', a
polite region rendered at load, which announces nothing on arrival — so nothing was telling the user
why the desk had stopped working.

Styled with opacity and not-allowed rather than left visually identical, so the state reads without
the control vanishing.

NOT FIXED:
- No aria-live announcement for rename/delete completion. Both mutate the list silently
  (WCAG 4.1.3). Wants a single shared live region on the desk rather than one per action, which is
  worth doing alongside the row rework in .32.
- Cancel and 'Delete workspace' in the confirm are still near-identical — same .button, same height,
  same border, differing only in text colour by one step. On an irreversible confirmation the two
  options should not be twins; that is a visual-weight decision belonging with .32.
