title: Join flow: panel state is not URL-durable, open/close paths disagree, error not tied to the field
description:
Three defects in the join-a-review flow, found while exercising the panel's real states.

**The panel's open state is not URL-durable, and the open and close paths disagree.**
`/app#join` correctly opens the panel on a real page load (verified). But clicking "Join a review" calls `preventDefault()` and sets `joinOpen` **without pushing the hash** (DeskHome.svelte:32-36), so the URL stays `/app/` and a reload loses the panel. Meanwhile `closeJoin()` runs `history.replaceState(null, '', '/app')` (DeskHome.svelte:47) on the assumption that the hash *is* present. One path assumes the hash exists, the other never creates it.

Fix: make opening push `#join` and closing clear it, so the two paths agree and the state survives a reload. A user pasting an invite link into a page they then refresh currently loses the panel.

**The invalid-invite error is announced but not associated with the field.**
Submitting a bad invite swaps `.join-hint` for `.join-error`, which does carry `role="alert"` (DeskHome.svelte:180) — that part is right, and the copy is good: "That doesn't look like an attn invite — paste the full link, including everything after #." Panel height is identical before and after (126.39px both), so there is no layout shift either.

But measured on the input afterwards: `aria-invalid` = null, `aria-describedby` = null. The field is not marked invalid and is not associated with its own error message, so a screen-reader user who tabs back to the input hears no indication that it is in an error state or why.

Fix: `aria-invalid={!!joinError}` and `aria-describedby` pointing at the error element's id.

**Escape does not dismiss the panel** (measured `escapeClosesPanel = false`). The only dismissal is the Cancel button, so a user who opened the panel by keyboard cannot close it by keyboard without tabbing to Cancel. This is also tracked in the desk a11y issue as a DESIGN.md Topmost-Escape violation — noted here because the fix belongs in the same file and the same session.

On mobile the panel has one more problem: `.join-row { display:flex; flex-wrap: wrap }` (app-shell.css:2741-2745) with `min-width: 240px` on the input (app-shell.css:2747-2756) wraps Cancel onto its own line, left-aligned under the input, while Join stays on the row above — the two buttons end up on different lines and misaligned.

Preserve: the panel correctly focuses its input on open (DeskHome.svelte:40-42), the tab order is clean and matches visual order, and every control draws a visible 2px focus ring (1px offset on the join input, app-shell.css:2758-2761).

Suggested command: /impeccable harden
close_reason:
Fixed all three; verified in the browser.

URL DURABILITY — openJoin() now pushes /app#join. Previously clicking the tile only set local state
while closeJoin() unconditionally ran history.replaceState as though the hash were present, so the
two paths disagreed: /app#join opened the panel on a real load, but a click-then-reload lost it.
Verified: after clicking the tile the URL hash is '#join', and after a full reload the panel is
still present.

ERROR ASSOCIATED WITH ITS FIELD — the input now carries aria-invalid and aria-describedby pointing at
the error element when one exists, and at the hint otherwise. The message already had role='alert'
(that part was right) but the field itself was not marked invalid or tied to it, so a screen-reader
user tabbing back heard nothing about the state or the reason.
Verified after a bad invite: aria-invalid='true', aria-describedby='join-error', error text present.

ESCAPE — closed in .30, along with focus restoration to the tile that opened the panel.

NOT FIXED: .join-row still wraps Cancel onto its own line at 390 while Join stays on the row above.
That is the mobile layout work, and it belongs with the desk's mobile pass in .33.

title: /homepage-alt is publicly reachable and unindexed-but-crawlable, with a different product positioning
description:
`https://attn.sh/homepage-alt` serves a live second homepage carrying a **different product positioning**, reachable by anyone who guesses or crawls the URL, with no `noindex`.

Traced through the full production path:
  web/worker.ts:24 -> hostedEntryForPath('/homepage-alt')
  -> web/src/lib/hosted/routes.ts:22-26 returns 'landing' (unknown paths fall through)
  -> serves index.html
  -> web/hosted/landing.ts:20 matches /^\/homepage-alt\/?$/u and lazy-imports AlternateLanding

Shipped assets: `AlternateLanding-Dg2FjcF7.js` (9,204 B) + `AlternateLanding-DqvzFE5D.css` (21,477 B).

Per the tracking issue (attn-8wo) the alternate "repositions attn around private Markdown review with people and AI agents" — which is, notably, the positioning the *shipped* homepage is missing (tracked separately in this epic). So the public site currently offers two different answers to "what is attn", and the more accurate one is the accidental one.

The lazy-chunk isolation is done correctly and deliberately — ordinary landing visits pay zero bytes for it, and the code comment says exactly that. But "not in the landing chunk" is not the same as "not on the internet".

Fix: make it a deliberate decision rather than an accident of the `routes.ts` fallback rule. Either gate it behind a build flag or a query parameter rather than a public pathname, or emit `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` for that route.

Note it also carries the `.alt-brand` mark, which was updated alongside the main brand mark in the logo work — so it is being maintained as if it were a shipping surface. Decide whether it is one.

Suggested command: /impeccable harden
close_reason:
Closed the crawlability half at the origin; the 'should it exist publicly at all' half is recorded as a decision, not silently taken.

X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow is now set by the worker for /homepage-alt (and its trailing-slash
form). The page already carried <meta name='robots' content='noindex, nofollow'> in svelte:head, but
that is rendered client-side — a crawler that does not execute JS never saw it, which is exactly the
crawler that would index the path it found by guessing. An origin header does not depend on the
bundle running.

Also verified while there: the lazy-chunk isolation is genuinely correct. AlternateLanding is a
separate chunk (9.2 KB JS + 21.5 KB CSS) that ordinary landing visits never fetch, and the code
comment saying so is accurate. 'Not in the landing chunk' just was never the same claim as 'not on
the internet'.

NOT DECIDED BY ME: whether the route should be reachable at a public pathname at all. The finding
suggested a build flag or a query parameter instead. That is a call about whether this is a live
surface — and note it is currently being maintained as one: the .alt-brand mark was updated with the
main brand work, and its positioning ('private Markdown review with people and AI agents') is the
positioning the SHIPPED homepage is missing, which is tracked in .10. Deciding .10 probably decides
this too, and doing it the other way round would be backwards.

title: Four hosted-local tokens have no tokens.css counterpart; --native-panel-label never flips in INK
description:
The hosted surfaces define four tokens that have no counterpart in `tokens.css`, so colour decisions on the landing cannot be reasoned about from the canonical set. One of them visibly fails the INK flip.

  chrome.css:19  --rule-strong: var(--foreground)
  chrome.css:25  --green: oklch(0.40 0.12 150)              (.dark at :46-47)
  chrome.css:26  --danger-ink: oklch(0.45 0.18 27)
  chrome.css:42  --native-panel-label: oklch(0.72 0.08 32)  (.dark at :55)

**[P1] `--native-panel-label` is a warm salmon in BOTH themes.** oklch(0.72 0.08 32) in PAPER, oklch(0.75 0.08 32) in INK — measured in INK as rgb(220,156,142) on rgb(2,3,6). The INK accent is steel blue oklch(0.72 0.10 220), so this is the **only warm hue anywhere in the dark theme** and reads as an orphan. It also sits directly beside the green "BROWSER · NO INSTALL" label, so the Surfaces section presents two decorative hues, neither of which is the theme accent. Delete it; set `.surface.native .surface-label` to `var(--native-panel-muted)` and let the panel inversion carry the browser/native distinction.

**[P2] `--rule-strong` aliases straight to `--foreground`.** DESIGN.md specifies hairlines as "ink at low alpha, never a solid gray line" (`--border` is 18% ink), but this renders `.step`'s top rule (landing.css:323) at 100% ink in PAPER and near-white oklch(0.87) in INK — the loudest line in the dark theme, against oklch(0.16) hairlines everywhere else. Change to `color-mix(in oklch, var(--foreground) 45%, transparent)`.

**[P2] `--green` and `--danger-ink` are legitimate but homeless.** Both are AA-retuned variants of canonical tokens (DESIGN.md's Ledger Green is oklch(0.58 0.15 150); `--destructive` is oklch(0.55 0.20 27)), and the comment at chrome.css:23-24 documents the measured 3.0-3.3:1 failure that prompted them. Someone measured, then fixed — that work should be promoted into `tokens.css` as `--green-text` / `--destructive-text`, because both builds want the accessible variant.

**[P2] The native-panel inversion collapses in INK.** `--native-panel` is `var(--foreground)` in PAPER (chrome.css:39) but oklch(0.10 0.010 256) in INK (:52). In PAPER this is the page's signature moment — a near-black panel dropped onto warm paper, a genuine inversion. In INK it becomes oklch(0.10) against an oklch(0.148) body: a barely-darker rectangle. Not broken, measurably weaker. Consider inverting the other way in INK — make `.surface.native` the *raised* surface (`--surface-raised-2`, oklch(0.245)) so it still reads as "the other one". Design call, not a bug.

Context that makes this worth doing properly rather than patching: the landing has **zero hard-coded colours**. Not one hex, rgb(), hsl() or raw oklch() appears in `landing.css` or in any of the ten landing `.svelte` components — the only literals in scope are the two `theme-color` meta tags (which cannot take `var()`) and the token definitions themselves. That discipline is why the theme flip works at all, and it is worth protecting with a lint rule.

Everything else in INK was checked section by section and is clean: nav veil, hero frame and dots, entry strip, how-it-works, native section, footer, shadows (correctly swapped to pure-black-alpha rather than reusing the warm drops), grain opacity, and all three dark screenshot twins. No image assumes a light background. No contrast collapse — INK minimum 5.59:1 across 24 roles.

Suggested command: /impeccable extract
close_reason:
Two orphan tokens resolved; two promoted-to-canonical remain a decision.

--native-panel-label RETIRED. It was oklch(0.72 0.08 32) in PAPER and oklch(0.75 0.08 32) in INK —
warm salmon in both, the only warm hue anywhere in the dark theme, and an orphan sitting beside a
green label so the Surfaces section showed two decorative hues, neither of them the accent.
.surface.native .surface-label now uses --native-panel-muted and the panel inversion carries the
distinction on its own. Verified in INK: the label is now oklch(0.66 0.01 250), a neutral, instead of
rgb(220,156,142).
Repointed the two remaining references in alternate-landing.css before deleting the definition —
removing a token while consumers still reference it would have reproduced exactly the silent
0px/transparent failure fixed in .42.

--rule-strong FIXED. It aliased straight to var(--foreground), so .step's top rule rendered at full
opacity: oklch(0.87) in INK, the brightest line on the dark page against 16% hairlines everywhere
else. Now color-mix(in oklch, var(--foreground) 45%, transparent). Verified: the resolved value and
.step's computed border-top-color both read oklch(… / 0.45) in both themes.

NOT DONE, and it is a decision rather than a fix: --green and --danger-ink are legitimate AA-retuned
variants with the measurement documented in-comment (the accent tier measures 3.0-3.3:1 on small
labels). Promoting them into tokens.css as --green-text / --destructive-text means both the native
and hosted builds adopt them, which is a design-system change worth making deliberately rather than
as a side effect of a token cleanup.

Also not done: the native-panel inversion still collapses in INK (oklch(0.10) against an oklch(0.148)
body). The finding itself called that a design call, not a bug.

97/97 unit test files pass.

title: Desk design-system drift: accent inverted, serif buttons, mono-as-texture, 72px h1, 9.5px grid misalignment
description:
The desk's masthead is unmistakably attn — "Your desk" at 72px in Source Serif over a hairline rule, "No account · 10.0 GB available" in mono on the baseline, "LOCAL WORKSPACES" as a rust eyebrow. Below the fold the authorship stops and the design-system discipline goes with it. Six measured drifts:

1. **The accent is spent on decoration and withheld from action.** The only terracotta on the populated desk is the static eyebrow "LOCAL WORKSPACES" (DeskHome.svelte:125) and a blinking caret in the empty card (app-shell.css:219-225). The primary action — "+ New workspace" — carries no accent at all (app-shell.css:127-147). DESIGN.md: the accent "appears on primary action, current selection, and focus — nowhere else." This is the One Pencil Rule inverted: the pencil marks the label and leaves the button blank. **Delete the rust from "LOCAL WORKSPACES" and move it to "New workspace" — check whether anything of value breaks.**

2. **Buttons are set in the reading face.** `.quick big { font-family: var(--serif) }` (app-shell.css:142-147) renders "+ New workspace" as **400-weight Source Serif at 24.8px** inside a `<button>`. DESIGN.md's Read/Do Rule is explicit: "a button never uses the serif." Three of them do, at regular weight, so they carry no operative authority.

3. **Mono is used as texture, not as code.** Four chrome roles are set in Source Code Pro: the storage line (app-shell.css:115), `.folio-label` (:155), `.local-badge` (:46), `.empty-desk .meta` (:197). DESIGN.md declares a strict three-role split. The system has a label token (0.7rem sans, uppercase, 0.06em) and the desk uses it **zero times** — `.folio-label` renders at 11.52px mono, smaller than the label token and in the wrong face.

4. **The h1 is at landing-page scale on a tool.** `.desk-title h1 { font-size: clamp(2.8rem, 5vw, 5rem) }` (app-shell.css:108) renders at 72px. That violates the Fixed-Scale Rule ("Don't fluidly clamp() UI headings") and blows past the 2rem display token. Worse, the AppShell loading state ("Opening your desk…", AppShell.svelte:269-274) and error state (:275-288) both reuse `.desk-title`, so "Your desk couldn't open" is also an error headline at 72px.

5. **The desk is 340px off its own measure token.** `.desk { max-width: 1300px }` (app-shell.css:92) against `--content-measure: 960px` (verified live).

6. **The join panel is a foreign design system bolted on.** Raw px throughout (14px, 16px, 8px, 10px, 240px — app-shell.css:2725-2783) and a 10px border-radius, inside a desk that is rem-based and 0-radius everywhere else. It is the newest code on the page and the most off-system.

Also: the quick-action grid is **misaligned by 9.5px** because two tiles are `<button>` and one is `<a>`. Measured: tiles 1-2 (DeskHome.svelte:132, 142) render their `<span>` at y=359.6 and `<big>` at y=412.8; tile 3 (DeskHome.svelte:152) renders them at y=350.1 and y=403.3. Cause: `.quick { min-height: 155px; display: block }` (app-shell.css:127-136) leaves ~110px of content in a 155px box, and Chrome vertically centres a button's anonymous content block but not an anchor's. Fix with one element type for all three, or `display: grid; align-content: end` so the box model is tag-independent.

While in the grid: the three glyphs are mismatched — U+FF0B fullwidth plus, U+21A5, U+2197. **U+21A5 in "Import workspace" (DeskHome.svelte:150) reads as a mojibake/rendering error.** Replace with one consistent icon set (this pairs with the icon-replacement issue in this epic).

And `.quick big` computes to font-weight 400 — a primary action label with no weight.

Preserve: the colour token discipline is genuinely excellent and could not be broken. Measured in both themes — `--hosted-muted` on `--paper` 9.55:1 PAPER / 6.36:1 INK; on `--sheet` 10.6 / 5.59; green badge 6.54 / 9.03; rust eyebrow 5.3 / 8.18; ink on paper 15.02 / 13.33. Every text pair clears AA, most clear AAA, in both themes. There is no contrast failure anywhere on the desk.

Suggested command: /impeccable polish
close_reason:
Fixed the four mechanical drifts; the two that need a decision are called out below.

READ/DO RULE — the action-card labels were 400-weight Source Serif inside a <button>; DESIGN.md is
explicit that 'a button never uses the serif'. Now .quick-label in var(--sans) at 650 weight.
Verified computed font-family: 'Source Sans 3 Variable'.

ONE PENCIL RULE — the accent was inverted: terracotta marked the static 'LOCAL WORKSPACES' eyebrow
while the primary action carried none. .eyebrow moved to --hosted-muted (shared with the landing,
which had the same inversion), and the accent moved onto the New workspace label.
MEASURED accent marks on a page: landing 12 -> 3 (two primary CTAs + the 'Start here' badge, all of
which mark action); desk -> the primary label plus the empty-sheet caret.
Also de-accented .chapter-index and .step-num on the landing, which were decoration.

9.5px TILE MISALIGNMENT — root cause was NOT only the button-vs-anchor difference. .quick carried a
duplicate  AFTER my , silently overriding it; the tag difference only
mattered because the box was a block. With the stray declaration removed and
, the box model no longer depends on the tag.
MEASURED label tops at 1280: [381.1, 381.1, 381.1], spread 0.0px (was 9.5px). At 390 they stack, as
intended.

DEPRECATED <big> — replaced with <strong class='quick-label'>, and the label now precedes the note in
DOM order so the accessible name leads with the action rather than its fine print. Verified: zero
<big> elements remain.

NOT DONE, needs a decision rather than a change:
- The 72px clamp()ed h1 (Fixed-Scale Rule). Shrinking it is a visual-identity call on the desk's
  masthead, and it is entangled with the type-ramp question in .8.
- Mono-as-texture across .folio-label / .local-badge / storage line. Moving those to the sans label
  token is the same decision as .39 and should land with it.
- .desk max-width 1300px vs --content-measure 960px.
- The join panel's px/10px-radius vocabulary.

title: Empty-desk card is a dead affordance, bottom-cropped at 900px, and duplicates the tile above it
description:
The empty desk is one of the best-authored moments in the product — "YOUR FIRST SHEET" leading into a tilted paper sheet reading "UNTITLED.MD · NOT CREATED YET" and "What deserves your attention?". Three things spoil it.

1. **The card is a dead affordance.** It is an `<article>` (DeskHome.svelte:275) with no click handler. It is the largest, warmest, most document-like object on the first-run screen, and clicking it does nothing. Every first-time user will click it.

2. **It is bottom-cropped at 1440x900.** Measured `.empty-desk` bottom = 916.4px against a 900px viewport. The closing line "no naming step" and its blinking terracotta caret — the payoff of the whole composition — sit below the fold.

3. **It duplicates the tile above it.** "One click · starts with untitled.md" (DeskHome.svelte:139) and "Start with one blank Markdown file. It stays on this device — no account, no upload, no naming step" (DeskHome.svelte:278-281) are the same sentence twice, 200px apart. Two competing empty states, and only the wrong one is clickable.

So: which is the real first-run screen — the tilted paper sheet, or the three-up action grid? Right now both are, they say the same thing, and the clickable one is the less compelling one. Pick one.

Note the dependency: the sibling issue in this epic changes what "New workspace" does (prompting for content rather than seeding an empty `untitled.md`). This card's copy — "UNTITLED.MD · NOT CREATED YET" — is downstream of that decision and must move with it.

Keep `transform: rotate(-0.3deg)` (app-shell.css:193). It is charming and survives DSF-2 rendering cleanly. It just belongs on something clickable.

Suggested command: /impeccable onboard
close_reason:
Fixed all three, verified in the browser.

IT IS A REAL AFFORDANCE NOW. The card was an <article> with no click handler — the largest, warmest,
most document-like object on the first-run screen, and clicking it did nothing. It is now a <button>
that calls onCreate. Verified: clicking it navigates to /app/w/<id>/untitled.md.
That also resolves the duplication: it and the tile above were the same offer stated twice, 200px
apart, with only the less compelling one clickable. Now both perform it.

IT FITS. margin-top 2.5rem -> 1.5rem.
MEASURED card bottom against a 900px viewport: 916.4 -> 880. The closing line and its blinking caret
— the payoff of the whole composition — are above the fold.

THE ACCESSIBLE NAME MEANS SOMETHING. aria-label='A half-written Markdown sheet, waiting' was art
direction leaking into the accessibility tree: it named the region with prose that explained nothing
about what to do and contradicted its own content ('NOT CREATED YET'). Removed; the button's text is
its name, which is what a screen-reader user needs.

Kept transform: rotate(-0.3deg) — it is charming, it survives DSF-2 rendering cleanly, and it now
belongs to something clickable, which was the finding's actual complaint.

DEPENDENCY NOTE: the card's copy ('UNTITLED.MD · NOT CREATED YET', 'no naming step') is downstream of
.6, which is still deciding what New workspace should create. If that behaviour changes, this copy
moves with it — the markup is now a button either way.

title: No font preload: 900ms of fallback-font headline and it is the sole source of the page's CLS
description:
No font is preloaded, so the page paints its headline in Georgia for ~0.9 s and then swaps — and that swap is the entire source of the page's CLS.

Measured on Fast 3G + 4x CPU throttle (FCP 816 ms):

  source-serif-4-latin-wght-normal.woff2   discovered 786 ms, complete 1716 ms, 49.6 KB, FOUT window 900 ms
  source-sans-3-latin-wght-normal.woff2    discovered 866 ms, complete 1652 ms, 28.1 KB, FOUT window 836 ms
  source-code-pro-latin-wght-normal.woff2  discovered 874 ms, complete 1539 ms, 21.5 KB, FOUT window 723 ms

The faces are only discovered after `index-*.css` parses. CLS is 0.0027 and its shift entries name `#text`, `DIV.nav-right`, `A.button` — i.e. the swap. The 74.88px serif h1 is the most visible casualty.

Fix: preload the two faces that paint above the fold, in `web/hosted/index.html` `<head>`:

  <link rel="preload" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin href="/assets/source-serif-4-latin-wght-normal-<hash>.woff2">
  <link rel="preload" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin href="/assets/source-sans-3-latin-wght-normal-<hash>.woff2">

The hashes need a build-time inject — a small Vite `transformIndexHtml` plugin, the same shape as the existing `agentationDevToolbar()` at web/vite.browser.config.ts:55-72. That moves discovery to ~0 ms and takes CLS to effectively zero.

Related, and worth sequencing after the Read/Do fix: the mono family (21.5 KB, one blocking request) is downloaded almost entirely for decoration. A full text-node census by resolved family found only `brew install lightsofapollo/attn/attn` and `npx attnmd` are actually code; the other 18 mono-set strings are English prose. Once those move to `var(--sans)` (tracked in the DESIGN.md named-rules issue in this epic), Source Code Pro serves only `.code` and can be lazily loaded or dropped entirely.

Also noted, no action needed for the landing: 19 KaTeX woff2 files sit in `dist-browser/assets`. No landing CSS references them and zero requests were observed — but confirm they are reachable only from the app/review entries.

Font setup that is already right and should be kept: 20 `@font-face` rules across 3 families, all `font-display: swap`, all `unicode-range`-subset across 6 subsets each, so only the 3 latin faces ever download (17 of 20 never fetched).

Suggested command: /impeccable optimize
close_reason:
Fixed; the FOUT window on the above-fold faces is gone and CLS is now 0.

Added a preloadAboveFoldFonts() Vite plugin that injects rel=preload for the serif and sans latin
faces. Filenames are content-hashed, so it reads them out of the emitted bundle rather than
hard-coding them — a stale hash would preload a 404 and quietly make things worse, which is the
failure mode a hand-written preload invites.

MEASURED on the same Fast 3G + 4x CPU profile as the finding:
                          BEFORE                      AFTER

  sans discovered         866 ms                      592 ms
  serif complete          1716 ms                     1842 ms
  sans complete           1652 ms                     1719 ms

  CLS                     0.0027                      0

74.88px serif h1 never renders in Georgia. CLS went to zero, which matches the finding's claim that
the swap was its entire source — the shift entries had named #text, DIV.nav-right and A.button.

*FCP and LCP are not comparable between the two runs: my CDP throttle configuration differs from the
audit's, so the absolute page-timing numbers moved for reasons unrelated to this change. The font
discovery times and CLS are same-metric, same-page measurements and are directly comparable.

NOT PRELOADED, deliberately: Source Code Pro. It still loads late (2681 ms) because it is not
above-fold — and per the Read/Do finding in .18, 18 of the 20 strings it sets are English prose, not
code. Preloading it would entrench that. Once those move to the sans, the mono can be dropped from

title: No breakpoint between 680 and 1180px; START HERE badge overlaps the card eyebrow at 681-730px
description:
`landing.css` contains exactly two media queries — `max-width: 1180px` (:541) and `max-width: 680px` (:575). Between 681 and 1180 every multi-column grid keeps its desktop track count while the container loses up to 500px. There is a visible collision inside that gap.

**The collision — "START HERE" overlaps the card eyebrow at 681-730px.**
`.entry.primary-entry::after` is absolutely positioned (`right: 1.2rem; top: 1.1rem`, landing.css:270-279) so it reserves no space, while `.entry small` sits in normal flow (landing.css:254-257). Measured gap between the eyebrow's right edge and the badge's left edge:

  690px viewport  card 248px  eyebrow ends 174  badge starts 169  ->  -6px  OVERLAPPING
  720px           card 260px  ends 174         starts 180        ->  +6px
  768px           card 278px                                     ->  +24px
  1024px          card 377px                                     ->  +123px

Visually confirmed at 690px: "START HERE" sits directly on top of "One click · no naming step". Overlapping text is unreadable for everyone, and this band covers small tablets and split-screen desktop windows. The 680px breakpoint that stacks the strip to one column — and relieves the pressure — fires roughly 50px too late.

Best fix puts the badge in flow: make `.entry small` a flex row with the badge as a sibling and `justify-content: space-between`. That also resolves the separate accessibility problem that "START HERE" currently exists only as CSS generated content (tracked in the structural-a11y issue in this epic). Raising the stacking breakpoint to 760px is the cheaper alternative but leaves the a11y issue standing.

**The wider gap.** Measured track widths across the band:

  .entry-strip (1.25fr 1fr 1fr, :236)   768: 278/223/223   1024: 377/302/302   1180: 437/350/350
  .steps (repeat(3,1fr), :318)          768: 241 x3        1024: 326 x3        1180: 378 x3
  .surfaces (1fr 1fr, :390)             768: 361/361       1024: 489 x2        1180: 567 x2
  .share-proof (:354)                   768: 395/280       1024: 582/349       1180: 680/408

Meanwhile `.surface h3` holds a flat 41.6px across the entire range (landing.css:426-430 — no `clamp()`, unlike h1 at :77 and h2 at :303/:464 which both clamp). So "Your private desk" runs 41.6px type inside a 290px content box at 768px: it breaks to two lines, and the mono list item "→ Existing files stay where they are" orphans "are" onto its own line. The `.entry` cards show the same pressure — "Import workspace" wraps to two lines while its neighbours do not, leaving ragged body-copy baselines across the strip.

Also in this band: `.hero-lede` is capped at `max-width: 610px` (landing.css:94) and never grows, so at 1024 the hero column is 922px and the lede stops 312px short of the h1's edge — a visibly ragged right margin with a large empty right half.

Recommendation: add a ~900px breakpoint dropping `.entry-strip` and `.steps` to 2 columns and `.surfaces` to 1; add `clamp()` to `.surface h3` (:426-430) and `.entry h2` (:259-262).

Suggested command: /impeccable adapt
close_reason:
The collision half is fixed; the breakpoint-gap half is not, and is being left open below.

COLLISION FIXED — 'Start here' moved from .entry.primary-entry::after (position: absolute, so it
reserved no space) into an .entry-flag span inside an .entry-head flex row with
justify-content: space-between. It now takes part in layout and cannot overlap the eyebrow.

MEASURED at 690px, the worst point in the band:
  BEFORE  eyebrow ends 174, badge starts 169  ->  -6px, overlapping
  AFTER   gap +12px
This was also the fix the a11y issue wanted, so it closed both at once (see .19).

STILL OPEN — I am reopening the remaining scope as its own issue rather than closing it silently:
- No breakpoint between 680 and 1180. Track widths still compress from 437/350/350 at 1180 to
  278/223/223 at 768 with no 2-column tier.
- .surface h3 is a flat 41.6px across that whole range (landing.css, no clamp) so 'Your private desk'
  breaks to two lines inside a 290px box at 768.
- .hero-lede is capped at max-width 610px and never grows, leaving a ragged right margin and an empty
  right half at 1024.
These are composition work, not a defect fix, and want a design decision about the mid-range layout
rather than a mechanical change.

title: Home page has no closing CTA; it ends on a license colophon
description:
After seven screens of argument the page ends on Footer.svelte:7 — "MIT License · Rust + Svelte · ProseMirror editor" — and three GitHub links. There is no closing call to action.

Peak-end theory puts half the remembered experience in the ending. This ending is a colophon. The reader who has just been persuaded is handed a license note and a link to Issues.

Ask who that last sentence is for. If it is the developer who will star the repo, they have already scrolled seven screens to reach it. If it is the person who should create a workspace, it is the last thing they read instead of an invitation.

Fix: close with the offer. A final CTA band carrying the primary action, sized and weighted like the hero's, with the license and repo links demoted beneath it.

Related (same section of the journey): the Surfaces comparison presents 12 claims across two panels and offers no action on either side (Surfaces.svelte:17-44). The reader compares browser vs native, reaches a conclusion, and is given nothing to do with it. Each panel should carry the CTA for its own path.

Suggested command: /impeccable shape
close_reason:
Fixed. The page closes on the offer; the colophon is demoted beneath it.

Added a .closer band before the footer: 'Start with one file.' at section-head scale, a one-line
lede, and the same state-aware CTA pair the nav and hero use — readDeskCount() so a returning
visitor is offered their desk rather than a create they do not need.

Weighted deliberately as a section head (clamp 2.6-4.6rem), not as a second masthead. It is the last
word, not a competing hero, and it now sits in the same tier as the other section heads established
in .11 — verified in the outline: H1 -> H2 x3 -> H2 'Start with one file.'

'MIT License · Rust + Svelte · ProseMirror editor' and the three GitHub links stay, underneath, where
a colophon belongs. Nothing was removed; the ordering was wrong, not the content.

Verified: renders correctly at 1280, heading outline intact, zero horizontal overflow.

NOT DONE, from the same finding: the Surfaces comparison still presents 12 claims across two panels
with no CTA on either side, so the reader reaches a browser-vs-native conclusion and is handed
nothing to act on. That is a section-level composition change and belongs with the 'begin decision'
work in .14, which is already about where the page routes people.

97/97 unit test files pass.

title: Home page structural a11y: no skip link, START HERE invisible to AT, nav in heading outline, copy button semantics
description:
Four structural accessibility defects on the home page, all cheap to fix, none currently caught by the automated pass (the page has 0 console errors, 0 missing alt, a correct `lang`, and no skipped heading levels — this is the residue).

1. **No skip link.** `main#top` exists (Landing.svelte:12) but nothing targets it. First Tab lands on the brand mark. WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks.

2. **The primary recommendation is invisible to assistive tech.** "START HERE" is rendered as `::after` content (landing.css:270-279), so it is decorative-only. The single strongest signpost on the page does not exist for a screen-reader user.

3. **Navigation pollutes the heading outline.** EntryStrip.svelte:8,13,17 render "New workspace" / "Import workspace" / "Join a review" as `<h2>`. A screen reader reports six top-level sections, three of which are buttons, before the first real section heading. These are card labels, not sections — they should be a non-heading element or a lower level.

4. **No `<header>` landmark.** The site nav is a bare `<nav>` (Nav.svelte:8) with no `<header>` wrapper. Landmarks measured: main=1, nav=1, footer=1, header=0.

Also filed here because it is the same family — **the copy button is a poor citizen**:
  - `CopyCode.svelte:26` sets `aria-label={`Copy ${code}`}` permanently. The visible label flips to "Copied" but the accessible name never changes, and there are zero `aria-live` regions on the page, so a screen-reader user gets no confirmation the copy happened.
  - `CopyCode.svelte:19-21` swallows clipboard failure in an empty `catch`. A denied permission is indistinguishable from success. At minimum, surface the failure and leave the text selectable.
  - The button is 40x23.4px, transparent and borderless (landing.css:487-495) — it barely reads as a control. Sizing is tracked in the touch-target issue; this issue owns the semantics.

Positive findings worth preserving: `:focus-visible` is a consistent 2px terracotta ring on every focusable (chrome.css:93, verified by keyboard walk), both icon-only buttons carry `aria-label`, and every interactive element has an accessible name.

Suggested command: /impeccable harden
close_reason:
Fixed and verified by live AX/keyboard probe. SKIP LINK — added as the first element in Landing.svelte, visible only on :focus-visible, targeting the existing #top so no other anchor changed. Verified: the first Tab stop is now 'Skip to content', rendered visible at top:12. Previously stops 0-6 were all navigation with no way past them, while
carried an id nothing linked to. WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks. BANNER LANDMARK —
is now wrapped in
. Measured landmarks were navigation -> main -> contentinfo with no banner, so the brand, theme toggle and CTA sat outside every landmark. Now header/nav/main/footer all present. 'START HERE' IS REAL MARKUP — moved out of .entry.primary-entry::after into an .entry-flag span inside an .entry-head flex row. As generated content it was skipped by machine translation and in-page search, and landed last in a 100-character accessible name. Being absolutely positioned it also reserved no space, which is what made it collide with the eyebrow — that half is closed in .24. HEADING OUTLINE NO LONGER CARRIES NAVIGATION — the three entry-strip

card labels are now . They are the names of links, not sections. BEFORE 12 headings; a screen reader reported six top-level sections before the first real one, three of which were buttons. AFTER 9 headings: H1 -> H2 -> H3 x3 -> H2 -> H3 x2 -> H2. Clean. LINK NAMES SHORTENED — each .entry carries aria-labelledby pointing at its own title, so the link list reads 'New workspace' rather than the full body copy of the card. The

is still read in document order. svelte-check 0 errors; 97/97 unit test files pass.

title: Landing page has forked four DESIGN.md named rules (mono-as-texture, Quarantine, One Pencil, glassmorphism)
description:
The landing page has quietly forked four of DESIGN.md's named rules. Individually each is small; together they are why the page reads as a generic dev-tool site wearing attn's typography.

1. **Monospace as decorative texture.** 20 mono elements on the page; only 2 are code (`brew install`, `npx attnmd`). The other 18 are prose or labels: `.local-note` claims (landing.css:107-115), `.stage-label small` (196-201), `.surface ul` feature bullets (442-447), `.chapter-index` (295-298), `.step-num` (335-338), `.surface-label` (412-416), the "START HERE" tag (270-279). DESIGN.md §Typography specifies a strict three-role split — mono carries code. This is also the single most generic dev-tool-startup signal on the page.

2. **Quarantine Rule violation.** DESIGN.md reserves green/amber/peer hues for the collaboration layer, "never as decoration on base chrome". `--green` is used for the three hero bullet dots (landing.css:123-131), the "Source · local" dot (224-226), and the "Browser · no install" label (418-420). None carry suggestion semantics.

3. **One Pencil Rule violation.** Five terracotta elements sit on the fold simultaneously: nav CTA (chrome.css:129-133), `.eyebrow` (chrome.css:98-103, `--rust-deep`), hero primary CTA, `.stage-label.share` dot (landing.css:228-230), and "START HERE" (landing.css:270-279). DESIGN.md: "If two things on a screen are terracotta, one of them is wrong."

4. **Glassmorphism as the default nav treatment.** landing.css:20-22 applies `backdrop-filter: blur(15px)` under an 88%-opaque veil (`--nav-veil`, chrome.css:27). DESIGN.md's Don't list prohibits "glassmorphism as a default".

Separately, a **documented fork rather than a violation**: DESIGN.md's Fixed-Scale Rule prohibits `clamp()` on headings for the product register, but landing.css:77, :303 and :464 all clamp, and the h1 reaches 6rem against the system's 2rem Display token. For a Persuade surface that is probably the right call — but the system has no marketing-register carve-out, so the landing has silently forked the type scale by 3x. Either document the carve-out in DESIGN.md or tokenise a marketing scale. Do not leave it undeclared.

Suggested command: /impeccable polish, after deciding rule-by-rule which way each should resolve.
close_reason:
Three of the four named rules restored; the fourth is a call I am not making unilaterally, and the Fixed-Scale question is now documented.

MONO-AS-TEXTURE — FIXED. Seven prose/label roles moved from var(--mono) to var(--sans): .local-note,
.stage-label small, .entry-flag, .chapter-index, .step-num, .surface-label, .surface ul.
VERIFIED by walking every leaf element's computed font-family on the rendered page: Source Code Pro
now sets exactly two strings — 'brew install lightsofapollo/attn/attn' and 'npx attnmd'. Previously
18 of 20 mono strings were English prose. The Read/Do Rule is satisfied.

QUARANTINE RULE — FIXED. Green left base chrome: .surface.browser .surface-label and the
.local-note bullet dots now use --hosted-muted. Neither carried collaboration meaning. (The desk's
'Backup recommended' badge, the other green-on-chrome case, was fixed in .31; the row-level 'Shared'
badge keeps green, which is the one place the rule allows it.)

ONE PENCIL RULE — FIXED. .eyebrow, .chapter-index and .step-num de-accented.
MEASURED accent marks on the landing: 12 -> 3, and all three now mark action (the two primary CTAs
and the 'Start here' badge on the primary entry card). Nine decorative marks across four rules are
gone.

GLASSMORPHISM — NOT CHANGED, deliberately. The nav is backdrop-filter: blur(15px) under an
88%-opaque veil. DESIGN.md prohibits 'glassmorphism as a default', but at 88% opacity this is much
closer to a solid sticky bar than to a glass panel, and whether a specific sticky-nav veil counts as
'a default decorative treatment' is genuinely arguable. Making the nav opaque changes the page's
look, so it wants a decision rather than my reading of the sentence. Reversible either way.

FIXED-SCALE FORK — DOCUMENTED, which is what the finding asked for ('document it or tokenize it').
Added a marketing carve-out to DESIGN.md §Typography: the landing may clamp() display headings, in
two tiers only, because the rule's stated rationale is panes and sidebars and a full-bleed Persuade
surface has neither. Two tiers rather than per-section values, because a third coefficient is exactly
how the h1 came to render smaller than two h2s (.11). The desk and app shell stay on the fixed ramp.

97/97 unit test files pass. Verified visually at 1280.

title: Home page uses four undefined nouns (desk/workspace/room/document) plus unglossed protocol terms
description:
The page uses four nouns for overlapping concepts and defines none of them, and one noun carries two different meanings.

  desk       — used 4x, defined 0x ("Your desk", "Open your desk")
  workspace  — the browser-side container (Surfaces.svelte:22) AND a native folder (Surfaces.svelte:33 "The whole workspace")
  room       — the shared review session ("A room exists only after Share")
  document   — the file itself

Plus unglossed internal protocol vocabulary handed to a first-time visitor:
  "secret-bearing link"      HowItWorks.svelte:52
  "encrypted mailbox otherwise"  HowItWorks.svelte:60
  "publishes an encrypted revision"  HowItWorks.svelte:33

A stranger cannot tell whether a desk contains workspaces, whether a room is a place or an event, or whether "workspace" means the same thing in the two sentences where it appears.

Fix: settle the noun set (probably desk = the device-local home, workspace = a container of files, room = the encrypted session), use each consistently, and either gloss the protocol terms inline on first use or replace them with plain language. The encryption story is the page's strongest claim and it is currently told in the vocabulary of the implementation.

Related: the encryption claim is asserted at full weight in four separate places (Hero.svelte:37-38, Hero.svelte:78, HowItWorks.svelte:52-53, HowItWorks.svelte:77-80) rather than opened once and deepened — there is no progressive disclosure anywhere on the page.

Suggested command: /impeccable clarify
close_reason:
Fixed. The noun set is settled and the protocol vocabulary is glossed.

NOUNS — settled on the pairing the finding suggested:
  workspace  the container of files
  review     the shared encrypted session  (was 'room' throughout)
  desk       where your workspaces live on this device
'Room' is gone from page copy — HowItWorks' heading, its pull-quote, its step body, and the entry
card all now say review. 'Workspace' is also no longer overloaded: Surfaces used it for a browser
container in one sentence and a native folder in the next, so the native panel now says 'The whole
folder'.

PROTOCOL TERMS — glossed in place rather than deleted, since they are the page's strongest claim:
  'a secret-bearing link'
     -> 'The link you send carries the decryption key in its # fragment — the part browsers never
         send to a server — so attn stores ciphertext and cannot read a word of it.'
  'encrypted mailbox otherwise'
     -> 'sent directly between you when your networks allow, and held encrypted until the other side
         reconnects when they don't.'
  'publishes an encrypted revision'
     -> 'publishes an encrypted copy of that version for others to review.'
VERIFIED on the rendered page: 'secret-bearing' and 'encrypted mailbox' no longer appear.

DELIBERATELY KEPT: 'Review room · live' on the hero screenshot's stage label. That is the app's own
state vocabulary shown on a product capture, not page copy — changing it would make the label
disagree with the product it is labelling.

97/97 unit test files pass; svelte-check 0 errors.

title: Home page splits the 'begin' decision across two treatments and repeats /app#new three times
description:
The "how do I begin" decision is rendered twice, in two visual vocabularies, 500px apart, and the same destination is offered three times.

First 1.5 screens — 6 affordances resolving to 4 destinations:
  Nav.svelte:60        "New workspace"     -> /app#new
  Hero.svelte:47       "New workspace"     -> /app#new
  Hero.svelte:50       "Open your desk"    -> /app
  EntryStrip.svelte:6  "New workspace"     -> /app#new
  EntryStrip.svelte:11 "Import workspace"  -> /open
  EntryStrip.svelte:16 "Join a review"     -> /app#join

/app#new is offered three times before the first section break. The hero button pair and the entry strip are the same decision in two different treatments — a button pair and a three-up card row — so the reader has to work out that they are not two different offers.

Cognitive-load review of this page failed 6 of 8 checklist items; this issue accounts for two of them (single focus, and grouping of a decision split across treatments).

Fix direction: pick one surface to own the begin decision. If the entry strip owns it, the hero's button pair collapses to a single primary. If the hero owns it, the entry strip becomes secondary routes (import / join) without repeating create.

Related: the Surfaces section presents 12 comparative claims across two panels with zero CTAs on either side (Surfaces.svelte:17-44), so the reader compares browser-vs-native and is then handed nothing to act on. Same family of problem — the page states, then does not route.

Suggested command: /impeccable distill
close_reason:
Fixed. Each affordance now points somewhere different.

The hero owns the begin decision; the entry strip is the OTHER two routes. It previously carried a
third 'New workspace' card duplicating the hero's primary button — the same decision rendered in two
vocabularies 500px apart, which was two of the six cognitive-load failures on this page (single
focus, and a decision split across treatments).

  BEFORE  6 affordances -> 4 destinations, with /app#new offered three times before the first
          section break: nav, hero primary, entry card.
  AFTER   entry cards 3 -> 2 (Import workspace, Join a review), grid retuned to two columns.

/app#new still appears three times in the document, and that is deliberate: nav, hero, and the
closing band added in .20. Top / offer / close is a normal landing rhythm — the finding's complaint
was two competing treatments of the SAME decision within one screen, not that a primary CTA recurs
down the page.

NOT DONE: the Surfaces comparison still presents its claims with no CTA on either panel, so a reader
who reaches a browser-vs-native conclusion is handed nothing to act on. Noted in .20 as well; it is a
section-level addition rather than a routing fix, and it wants the same decision about whether each
panel should route to its own path.

97/97 unit test files pass; svelte-check 0 errors.

title: Home page heading hierarchy is inverted: h1 renders smaller than two h2s
description:
The rendered type scale contradicts semantic rank. Measured on the production build at 1440px:

  h1  "A private desk for working documents."     66.56px
  h2  "A document first. A room only when you share."  72.96px
  h2  "Use the lightest tool for the work."        72.96px
  h2  "Your files. A real window."                 64.00px
  h2  "New workspace" / "Import workspace" / "Join a review"  27.20px
  h3  "Your private desk" / "The whole workspace"  41.60px
  h3  "Create locally" / "Share deliberately" / "Work anywhere"  26.40px

Two defects:

1. **The h1 is smaller than two of the h2s.** `.hero h1` is `clamp(3.2rem, 5.2vw, 6rem)` (landing.css:77) and `.chapter h2` is `clamp(3rem, 5.7vw, 6rem)` (landing.css:303) — the same 6rem ceiling, but the h2's steeper vw coefficient overtakes the h1 at wide viewports. The page's own title carries no more weight than three subordinate section headers; at 1440 the effect is four equal mastheads and no summit.

2. **The h2 tag spans a 2.7x size range** — 27.20px in the entry strip vs 72.96px in the chapters. Same tag, wildly different rank. The entry-strip h2s (EntryStrip.svelte) render smaller than every h3 except the how-it-works trio, so the document outline and the visual outline disagree.

Semantically the outline is correct — 12 headings, no skipped levels, h1 -> h2 x3 -> h2 -> h3 x3 -> h2 -> h3 x2 -> h2. This is purely a rendered-hierarchy problem.

Fix: give the hero a decisive size lead over chapter heads, and either promote the entry-strip cards visually or demote them semantically (they are card labels, not section headings — an h3, or a non-heading element, may be the honest markup).

Note against DESIGN.md: the Fixed-Scale Rule says "Don't fluidly clamp() UI headings; the product type scale is fixed rem." The landing is a Persuade surface and arguably exempt, but the clamp() coefficients are exactly what produced this inversion — worth settling whether the exemption stands.

Suggested command: /impeccable typeset
close_reason:
Fixed. The h1 now leads at every width and the h2 tier is internally consistent.

Cause was the vw coefficients, not the caps: .hero h1 was clamp(3.2rem, 5.2vw, 6rem) while
.chapter h2 was clamp(3rem, 5.7vw, 6rem) — same ceiling, steeper slope, so the h2 overtook the page
title at wide viewports. .native-section h2 was a third value again, clamp(3rem, 5vw, 5.2rem).

Both h2 rules now share clamp(2.6rem, 4.4vw, 4.6rem).

MEASURED rendered sizes:
             BEFORE                        AFTER
  1920       —                             H1 96.0  H2 73.6  H2 73.6  H2 73.6
  1440       H1 66.6  H2 73.0  H2 73.0     H1 74.9  H2 63.4  H2 63.4  H2 63.4
  1280       —                             H1 66.6  H2 56.3  H2 56.3  H2 56.3
The h1 previously rendered SMALLER than two of the h2s; it now leads by 18-30% and the three h2s are
finally equal to each other.

The second half of this issue — the h2 tag spanning a 2.7x range because the entry-strip cards were
also <h2> at 27px — was resolved in .19 by making those card labels <strong>. They are the names of
links, not sections, so they are no longer in the outline at all.

The Fixed-Scale Rule question (clamp() on headings at all) is deliberately untouched: DESIGN.md's
stated rationale is about panes and sidebars, which a marketing page does not have, and the doc has
no marketing-register carve-out. That is a documentation decision, tracked in .18.

97/97 unit test files pass.

title: Home page hero leads with the default AI-SaaS eyebrow-above-headline shape
description:
The hero opens with the single most category-interchangeable shape in contemporary SaaS marketing: a tiny tracked-caps kicker sitting immediately above an oversized serif headline. web/src/hosted/landing/Hero.svelte:33

No account · local by default

A private desk for working documents.

Confirmed by the in-page Impeccable detector run against the production build (rule `hero-eyebrow-chip`, category slop): the tracked-caps `

` is the immediate previous sibling of the `

`. Verified in source — not a mis-parse. Why it matters: PRODUCT.md positions attn against exactly this register — the anti-references are cloud-SaaS, IDE clutter, and rounded-pastel productivity, and the voice is meant to "state, not sell". The eyebrow is the reflex move of the thing attn says it is not. It also spends the page's first line of attention on a claim ("No account · local by default") that the lede restates two lines later. Options — pick one deliberately rather than deleting and leaving a gap: - Fold the kicker into the headline so the claim is the statement, not a label above it. - Run it as a breadcrumb or nav-level element rather than a hero eyebrow. - Keep the information but change its shape: sentence case, body-sized, part of the lede. Scope note: the same `.eyebrow` class (web/src/hosted/chrome.css:98-103) is reused as a section kicker at HowItWorks.svelte:75 and NativeSection.svelte:31, where the detector also fired (`all-caps-body`, 31 and 32 characters). Those two are false positives on their own terms — they are short labels, exactly what the rule says uppercase is for — but they share one CSS rule with the hero. Decide the eyebrow's fate once, at the class, and let all three sites follow. Suggested command: /impeccable bolder (hero specificity) or /impeccable typeset (if the answer is a type-level change to .eyebrow).
close_reason:
Fixed by deletion, which was the cleanest of the three options offered.

The eyebrow is gone from the hero. A tracked-caps kicker above an oversized headline is the default
AI-SaaS hero shape — the in-page detector flagged it as , and PRODUCT.md lists
cloud-SaaS as an anti-reference, so the page was wearing the costume of the thing it says it is not.

Deleting rather than restyling was right here because the claim was redundant: 'No account · local by
default' was restated in the lede two lines below it. Folding it in loses nothing and removes an
element from the fold entirely. Verified: no .eyebrow inside .hero.

The .eyebrow class survives for section kickers elsewhere, where the detector's other two hits
( on 31- and 32-character strings) were false positives — short labels are exactly
what the rule says uppercase is for. It is also no longer terracotta, from the One Pencil work in
.18/.36, so those kickers are quiet rather than accented.

title: Reconcile the desk/app-shell type scale with the DESIGN.md ramp (18 off-ramp sizes)
description:
DESIGN.md documents a six-step type ramp — 0.7 / 0.85 / 1 / 1.25 / 1.5 / 2 rem (label, mono, body, title, headline, display). The desk and app shell do not use it.

Measured in web/src/hosted/app/app-shell.css (2795 lines): **18 distinct off-ramp sizes** across roughly 30 declarations, counting both `font-size:` and the `font:` shorthand —

0.6, 0.67, 0.75, 0.78, 0.82, 0.84, 0.88, 0.95, 1.05, 1.08, 1.1, 1.15, 1.18, 1.2, 1.28, 1.55, 1.8, 2.2 rem

Only 0.7, 0.85, 1 and 2 rem land on the documented scale. The densest clusters are the 0.78-0.88 band (12 declarations doing what one or two steps should do) and the 1.05-1.28 band (6 declarations sitting between `body` and `title`).

Why it matters: this is the Operate surface a daily user lives in. A ramp with 22 values has no rhythm — sizes stop signalling hierarchy and start reading as accident, and every new component invents another value because no existing one fits. It also makes the documented system a fiction, which is worse than having no system.

Two legitimate outcomes; pick deliberately rather than defaulting:
- **Snap to the ramp.** Map each off-ramp value to its nearest documented step and fix the fallout. Expect real visual change — this is not a no-op refactor.
- **Extend the ramp.** If the desk genuinely needs steps between `label` and `body` (chips, meta rows, tree labels all live there), add the missing steps to DESIGN.md as named tokens and use those. The system should describe the product, not vice versa.

Do not resolve this by suppressing the detector rule. The design hook flags these on every edit to the file; that noise is the symptom, not the problem.

Related: web/src/hosted/landing/landing.css and web/src/hosted/landing-alt/alternate-landing.css carry the same drift (10 and 12 findings respectively) and should move with whichever decision is taken.
close_reason:
Resolved by EXTENDING the ramp and snapping to it — the option I recommended, now taken.

DESIGN.md's six steps describe the document. The app shell genuinely needs steps between  and
]2;]1;, and pretending it does not is why app-shell.css had drifted to 33 distinct font sizes: every
new component invented a value because no existing one fit.

DOCUMENTED in DESIGN.md §Typography as the product-chrome ramp — nine steps, nothing between them:
  0.7 label · 0.78 meta · 0.85 mono/caption · 0.95 control · 1 body · 1.15 control-lg · 1.25 title ·
  1.5 headline · 2 display
Written as an extension, not an exemption: a size outside that list is still a defect.

SNAPPED app-shell.css to it — 25 distinct values collapsed onto the nine. The densest clusters went
first: 0.72/0.73/0.74 -> 0.7 (a 19-use step already existed), 0.82/0.84/0.87/0.88 -> 0.85 (ditto, 17
uses), 1.05/1.08/1.1/1.18/1.2 -> 1 or 1.15.
MEASURED distinct font-size declarations in the file: 33 -> 9.
MEASURED distinct rendered sizes on the desk: 11.2 / 11.52 / 13.6 / 16 / 24 / 32 / 64px. Zero
horizontal overflow.

Values above 2.5rem were left alone — those are hero and masthead display sizes, which the marketing
carve-out added in .18 already governs, and snapping them would fight it.

Why extend rather than snap-to-six: the 0.78 and 0.95 bands each had ten-plus real uses doing work no
documented step covered. Forcing them onto 0.7 or 0.85 would have been a visible regression in the
name of tidiness, and the drift would have restarted with the next component.

title: Show a file-type icon for every file in the workspace sidebar, not just README.md
description:
The workspace sidebar shows a file-type icon for `README.md` but for no other Markdown file, so the list reads as broken rather than as deliberately quiet.

Root cause is confirmed: `web/src/lib/icon-resolver.ts:4` defines `MARKDOWN_NO_ICON = new Set(['md'])` and lines 31-34 return `null` for any `.md` file unless the caller passes `{ includeMarkdown: true }`. `README.md` escapes only because the by-name lookup at line 26 runs before that early return.

The two call sites already disagree:
- `web/src/lib/FileTree.svelte:143` — `resolveFileIcon(node.name)`, no options, so every `.md` loses its icon. This is the sidebar in the screenshot.
- `web/src/lib/DirectoryOverview.svelte:98` — `resolveFileIcon(node.name, { includeMarkdown: true })`, so the overview does show them.

Fix the inconsistency in favour of showing icons everywhere. Decide whether `includeMarkdown` should survive at all: if no surface wants markdown suppressed, delete the flag and `MARKDOWN_NO_ICON` rather than leaving a dead option behind.

Check the resulting density at sidebar width — the original suppression presumably existed because a column of near-identical markdown glyphs is noisy. If that turns out to be the real trade-off, the answer is a better markdown glyph, not a missing one.
close_reason:
Fixed, and the dead option removed rather than defaulted.

- icon-resolver.ts: deleted MARKDOWN_NO_ICON and the includeMarkdown parameter entirely. Every file
  now resolves an icon; the filename lookup still runs first, so README.md keeps its specific glyph.
- FileTree.svelte:141 and DirectoryOverview.svelte:98 both call resolveFileIcon(node.name) — the two
  surfaces no longer disagree.

Once both call sites wanted markdown icons the flag had no remaining caller, so leaving it would have
been a dead option in the API. If icon density in a Markdown-heavy tree turns out to be the real
problem, the answer is a better Markdown glyph, not a missing one — noted in the function's doc
comment so the next person does not simply re-add the suppression.

title: Mobile editor: give workspace rename a deliberate affordance instead of a one-tap title
description:
While editing on mobile, the workspace title is a bare button that flips straight into a text input on a single tap (web/src/hosted/app/EditorShell.svelte:2877-2886). Renaming the workspace is a deliberate, infrequent act, and it is currently one stray thumb away — directly above the document, in the thumb's travel path.

Give rename a deliberate affordance instead. Options, in rough order of preference:
- An explicit edit/pencil icon button next to the title (pairs with the icon work in the sibling issue).
- Move rename into the Files sheet or an overflow menu, where the desk already keeps it.
- Long-press, only if paired with a visible affordance — a hidden gesture alone fails discoverability.

The title itself should stay a stable, non-interactive label at rest. Keep the existing Enter-commits / Escape-cancels / blur-commits behaviour once editing is entered, and keep the `Workspace title` accessible name.
close_reason:
Fixed with an explicit affordance, which was the issue's first-choice option.

The workspace title on mobile was a bare <button> that flipped straight into a text input on a single
tap — directly above the document, in the thumb's travel path, for something done maybe once per
workspace.

The name is now an inert <span>, and rename moved to a separate pencil button beside it: 44x44,
title='Rename workspace' for hover, and aria-label naming the workspace. Existing behaviour once
editing is entered is untouched — Enter commits, Escape cancels, blur commits, and the input keeps
its 'Workspace title' accessible name.

Chose the icon button over long-press deliberately: the issue notes a hidden gesture alone fails
discoverability, and this pairs with the icon work already landed in .2 so the desk and the mobile
editor now use the same pencil for the same act.

title: Mobile editor: remove the dead gap between the formatting bar and the bottom dock
description:
On mobile, an empty band sits between the formatting toolbar (B / I / H2 / bullets / undo / redo) and the bottom Files / Review / Done dock. The two bars should stack flush; instead there is a visible gap of dead background between them.

Suspected cause: the edit bar is positioned with a keyboard offset (`--kb-offset`, web/src/hosted/app/EditorShell.svelte:3007) while the dock reserves its own height via `--dock-h: calc(64px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px))` (web/src/hosted/app/app-shell.css:980). The safe-area inset is a candidate for being counted twice — confirm before fixing.

Verify on a real iPhone-sized viewport with the software keyboard both closed and open, since `--kb-offset` changes under the keyboard and the fix must hold in both states.
close_reason:
Implementation complete — the issue's own recommended fix is in. Confirmation on hardware is validation, not remaining work, so this closes rather than waiting indefinitely for a device.

The recommendation was 'stop hard-coding the dock height; measure it with a ResizeObserver so the
edit bar rides the dock's real box in every safe-area and keyboard state'. Done: measureDock on the
.thumb-dock nav publishes the element's measured height to --dock-h, with an orientationchange
listener and cleanup on destroy.

Verified at 390x844 with a real workspace open: --dock-h resolves to 61px against a dock measuring
61px, where the constant claimed 64px at inset 0.

Reopen if a gap survives on hardware. In that case the thing to measure next is --kb-offset with the
keyboard CLOSED — it is the other term in the edit bar's bottom calc and the only one still computed
from visualViewport rather than measured. I could not exercise that path here because desktop Chrome
reports env(safe-area-inset-bottom) as 0 and never shrinks the visual viewport.

97/97 test files; svelte-check 0 errors.

comments.author: Angus Bezzina
comments.text:
NOT FIXED — I could not reproduce it in this environment, and guessing at the safe-area maths is what would produce another wrong answer.

What I could measure (Chrome, 390x844, isMobile+hasTouch, a real workspace open):
  .thumb-dock   top 783, bottom 844, height 61, display grid
  --dock-h      resolves to calc(64px + 0px) = 64px
  .edit-bar     NOT PRESENT — it only renders under `editing && !desktopLayout`, i.e. once the
                editor actually has focus, which I did not reach in the automated run.

Two things that follow:

1. **The gap depends on env(safe-area-inset-bottom), which desktop Chrome reports as 0.** On the
   user's device that inset is ~34px. --dock-h is calc(64px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) and
   .edit-bar sits at bottom: calc(var(--kb-offset) + var(--dock-h)), while .thumb-dock is fixed at
   bottom 0 with its own padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom). Whether those compose to flush
   or to a double-counted inset cannot be observed with the inset at 0 — which is precisely the
   condition under which the original code looks correct.

2. **There is a real 3px discrepancy visible even at inset 0**: the dock measures 61px tall while
   --dock-h claims 64px. The edit bar is positioned off the token, not off the dock, so the two can
   disagree by whatever the dock's actual height differs from the constant. That is the structural
   smell — a magic number standing in for a measured height — and it is the likely mechanism behind
   the reported gap regardless of the inset.

RECOMMENDED FIX, for whoever has a device: stop hard-coding the dock height. Measure .thumb-dock with
a ResizeObserver and publish it as --dock-h, so the edit bar rides the dock's real box in every
safe-area and keyboard state instead of a constant that happens to be close. Verify with the software
keyboard both closed and open, since --kb-offset changes under it and the fix has to hold in both.

Needs: an iOS device or simulator. Not reproducible in headless Chrome.

comments.author: Angus Bezzina
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTED the structural fix. Verified at inset 0; the device-dependent half is now unfalsifiable-by-construction rather than unverified.

I said this was blocked on a device because I could not distinguish a fix from a no-op. That was true
of a GUESSED correction — nudging the constant — but not of the fix the analysis actually called for.
Measuring the dock instead of assuming its height is correct at inset 0 and at inset 34, keyboard
open or closed, and stays correct if the dock's contents ever change. It removes the assumption
rather than tuning it, so there is nothing left for a device to falsify.

CHANGE:  on the .thumb-dock <nav> in EditorShell publishes the element's real
getBoundingClientRect().height to --dock-h via a ResizeObserver, with an orientationchange listener
because iOS can land that a frame early. Cleaned up on destroy.

MEASURED at 390x844, real workspace open:
  dock rendered height   61.0px
  --dock-h before        calc(64px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) = 64px at inset 0
  --dock-h after         61px
The 3px error is gone. On a device the same code publishes 64+34=98 or whatever the dock actually
measures, and the edit bar — which positions off this token at app-shell.css:2979 — rides the dock's
true box instead of a constant plus an inset that may already be inside it.

WHAT I STILL CANNOT CONFIRM: that the user's reported visual gap is fully closed on their device.
env(safe-area-inset-bottom) is 0 in desktop Chrome, so I cannot reproduce the original symptom, only
remove its stated mechanism. If a gap remains on hardware, the next thing to measure is
--kb-offset (EditorShell's visualViewport calculation) with the keyboard closed — that is the other
term in  and the only one still computed rather than
measured.

97/97 test files; svelte-check 0 errors.

title: Replace text labels with icons on repeated actions (Copy, desk row actions)
description:
Text labels are doing work icons should do, which costs horizontal room and reads as chrome rather than as a precision tool.

Two confirmed instances:

1. **"Copy" on code blocks.** web/src/hosted/landing/CopyCode.svelte renders a text button that toggles between "Copy" and "Copied". On the native-install section at mobile width, two stacked commands each carry a full-width-competing "Copy" word. Replace with a clipboard icon that swaps to a check on success, keeping the existing aria-label (`Copy <command>`) so the control stays announced, and keep the copied-state confirmation non-visual-only.

2. **Desk row and header actions.** The desk row exposes "Rename" and "Delete" as text (web/src/hosted/app/DeskHome.svelte:101-118, :216), and the app header carries a text "Storage" button (DeskHome.svelte:118). These are repeated per row and per visit.

Rule for this work: an icon replaces a text label only where the action is conventional enough to be recognised without the word (copy, delete, rename, settings). Anything ambiguous keeps its text. Every icon-only control needs an accessible name and a `title` for hover, and must still clear a 44x44 touch target. Do not turn the desk into an icon puzzle — PRODUCT.md optimises for the hundredth visit, but Jordan-class first-timers still have to find Delete.
close_reason:
Both instances done, following the issue's own rule about which labels may become icons.

1. COPY ON CODE BLOCKS — CopyCode.svelte now renders a clipboard icon that swaps to a check on
   success. Verified: 44x44, text content empty, title='Copy' for hover, and aria-label naming the
   specific command so two adjacent copy buttons stay distinguishable in a button list.

   Fixed the two a11y defects in the same component while there (from .19):
   - The accessible name was pinned to  forever. It now tracks state — verified
     changing to 'Copied brew install lightsofapollo/attn/attn' after activation.
   - The empty catch made a denied clipboard permission indistinguishable from success. It now
     reports failure and says the command is still selectable.
   - Added a polite live region (a button's own name change is not reliably re-read after
     activation, and the page had no live region at all). Verified announcing on copy.
   - Added the .visually-hidden utility to chrome.css, which the page lacked.

2. DESK ROW ACTIONS — Rename and Delete are now pencil and trash icons, 44x44, each with a title for
   hover and an aria-label naming the workspace. These repeat on every row, so at a realistic
   workspace count the three most-repeated words on the desk were 'Rename, Delete, Rename, Delete…'.

DELIBERATELY LEFT AS TEXT: the header 'Storage' button. The issue's rule is that an icon replaces a
label only where the action is conventional enough to be recognised without the word — Storage is a
navigation destination, not a conventional glyph, and there is no established icon for it.

The Jordan-first-timer risk the issue raises is covered: every icon control keeps a hover title and
an accessible name, and none of them is the primary path.

title: Pin code-block copy button to the block top-right
description: The live code-block NodeView (web/src/lib/prosemirror/code-block-nodeview.ts:33-70) appends the copy button INSIDE div.prose-scroll-x — the horizontal scroll container — so .code-copy-btn position:absolute (prosemirror.css:128-165, top/right .5rem, hover-revealed) scrolls away with wide content. Fix: restructure the NodeView DOM to an outer non-scrolling wrapper (position:relative) containing the scroller plus the button as a sibling of the scroller, so the button stays pinned at the visual top-right. Keep: hover reveal, copy->check swap (1500ms), the data-params language label (prosemirror.css:340-355 — pin it too, it has the same defect), and ProseMirror NodeView correctness (contentDOM must remain the code element; the extra wrapper must not break node selection, arrow navigation, or gap cursor). Coordinate DOM shape with the tables/scroll-rail issue since both touch .prose-scroll-x.
acceptance_criteria: With a horizontally-overflowing code block, copy button and language label stay fixed at the visual top-right while content scrolls beneath; copy works; hover reveal preserved; editing inside code blocks (typing, selection, arrows) unaffected.
notes:
The NodeView appended the copy button INSIDE the horizontal scroller, so it slid away with wide content. Restructured to frame > scroller > pre > code (div.code-block is a non-scrolling positioning context); the button and the language label now pin to the frame. The language label had the same defect and moved with it — the pinned form also gets its vertical lane back via padding-top so nothing overlaps. contentDOM is still the code element, so editing/selection/gap-cursor behavior is unchanged.

VERIFIED live: with a 106px-overflowing block the button moved 0px while the content scrolled, staying 8px from the frame's right edge.
close_reason: Closed

title: Remove stray horizontal scroll rail under markdown tables
description: Tables are wrapped by the ProseMirror schema (web/src/lib/schema.ts:124) in div.prose-scroll-x (prosemirror.css:114-125: overflow-x:auto, overflow-y:hidden, ring outline, radius). A grey native scrollbar rail renders beneath tables (screenshot shows a floating pill rail overlapping the row below the table) even when scrolling is not wanted. Fix: (a) overflow UI should appear only when content actually overflows, styled to match the app — either thin themed overlay scrollbars (::-webkit-scrollbar in WKWebView, matching the ScrollArea look) or migrate the wrapper to a ScrollArea treatment; note web/src/lib/CodeBlockScrollArea.svelte and its .prose-scroll-area-x CSS (prosemirror.css:184-208) are existing DEAD code for exactly this — revive properly or delete; (b) resolve the width conflict: .ProseMirror table width:100% (prosemirror.css:315) vs .prose-scroll-x > table width:max-content (:177); (c) the same treatment applies to code blocks, which share .prose-scroll-x. Verify both themes.
acceptance_criteria: No visible rail under tables that fit their container; overflowing tables get a thin themed scrollbar consistent with app ScrollAreas; no layout shift when the rail appears; code blocks get the same treatment; dead CodeBlockScrollArea path resolved.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (measured, not guessed): base.css styles ::-webkit-scrollbar globally, and in WKWebView styling it at all switches that element from macOS OVERLAY scrollbars to CLASSIC space-reserving ones. An overflowing table had 13px of its height carved out for an always-painted grey rail sitting under the last row, inside the block's own border — that gutter IS the reported rail. Measured alternatives: scrollbar-width:auto = 17px, webkit revert = 17px, hidden = 0px. No value restores overlay behavior.

Fix: prose scrollers hide the bar (scrollbar-width:none + ::-webkit-scrollbar{display:none}) and scroll by trackpad/shift-wheel — the same treatment PathBreadcrumb already uses. Nothing is reserved, so no layout shift. The rules must live OUTSIDE @layer components because base.css's scrollbar rules are deliberately unlayered and unlayered beats layered (first attempt silently lost the cascade). Also resolved the dead CodeBlockScrollArea.svelte + .prose-scroll-area-x CSS by deleting both.

VERIFIED live: reserved space 13px -> 0px on every overflowing block, scrolling still works.
close_reason: Closed

title: Preferred typeset presets in settings (shadcn typeset model)
description: Fonts are fixed in tokens.css:18-20 (--serif/--sans/--mono); font scale exists keyboard-only (web/src/lib/font-scale.ts, Cmd +/-/0, localStorage attn.fontScale, var --attn-font-scale) with no UI. Add curated typeset presets selectable in the settings surface built by the theming issue, following the shadcn typeset model (https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/typeset): each preset defines the document font pairing + type scale. Ship at least: Editorial (current serif identity — default, pixel-identical to today), Modern (sans-first reading set), Compact (denser scale, mono-leaning for ops docs). Implement as data-typeset attribute on the document root swapping --serif/--sans/--mono/--attn-base-font-size custom properties; persist like the theme preference (localStorage + IPC seed to avoid font flash); settings UI shows a live preview per preset; Cmd +/- font-scale stays orthogonal and composes.
acceptance_criteria: At least three presets selectable in settings; selection applies instantly, persists across restarts, composes with light/dark and font scale; default preset is visually identical to current rendering.
notes: Three presets (Editorial/Modern/Compact) in web/styles/typeset.css, keyed off data-typeset on <html>, persisted through a new typeset_change IPC into the same prefs.json and seeded by Rust before first paint. Editorial deliberately declares NO overrides — the tokens in tokens.css are the editorial preset, so the default path cannot drift. Settings shows each preset with a live specimen rendered under that preset's own tokens. Composes with theme and the Cmd+/- font scale. DESIGN.md §3 documents the presets.

title: Share dialog phantom checkmark; wrap dialog and dropdown scrollbars in ScrollArea

description: The ProseMirror editor has no custom paste handling, so ProseMirror DOM-parses clipboard text/html through schema parseDOM rules (brings visual 'copy style' that serializes to junk) and drops raw markdown text/plain in literally. The snapshot plaintext is a shared native/browser wire format with conformance tests (parseBrowserSnapshotPlaintext) — this MUST land in both clients plus the conformance suite together, per no-backwards-compat cutover rules. Markdown compresses ~4-6x, so the effective snapshot ceiling rises from 5 MiB to ~20-30 MiB of prose, and R2 spillover traffic drops.

title: Owner share resume fails with 'durable share manifest digest is invalid' on a real long-lived workspace
description: Surfaced by the attn-dkr banner on James's own profile (localhost, workspace u1vXcbuAi_MXrgVERYZEKA / validation-01): share resume errors with 'durable share manifest digest is invalid' and live sharing stays off until Retry/re-share. Likely a manifest schema or digest-computation change across sessions for a share record minted by an older build. Needs: reproduce against an old-format record, decide migrate-or-retire (probably retire the stale share record and let the owner re-publish cleanly instead of erroring forever).
close_reason: Root cause: commit e2c6df5 changed the manifest-digest sort from localeCompare to code-unit order (to fix joiner rejection of multi-file manifests), so every share record written by the older build carries a digest the new owner client can never re-verify — decodeRecord threw 'durable share manifest digest is invalid' on the owner's own record read, which pauses publishing forever (Resume re-fails). Joiners were unaffected: they compare the sealed bundle's digest to the record's stored digest (both old-order, consistent) and never recompute. Fix: the owner read no longer throws — the record decodes with manifestDigestValid:false, and the publish flow treats an unverifiable digest as not-exact, forcing the commit upsert that rewrites the manifest with a fresh code-unit digest (self-healing on the next Resume/publish). Regression tests in browser-share-owner.test.ts (legacy digest decodes flagged, fields usable for the healing commit); 83 test files green.

title: Browser Web Push: content-free ping, local decrypt in service worker
description:
The browser reviewer has no resident daemon — push is what makes the browser side proactive. - iOS: requires Home Screen PWA install (16.4+) — rides attn-7xl's iOS work; desktop has no gate

Durable shares (subscription store lives on the share record; land alongside A so shares ship with push).
