- NEW SECURITY NOTE needing review: annotating requires allow-scripts, so hosted reviewers (today allowScripts=false) get page scripts enabled WHILE ANNOTATING. Frame stays opaque-origin so no app/file/storage reach. Read-only viewing keeps today's script-free rendering. See html-annotation.md §4.
close_reason:
All 9 phases closed on branch angus/html-commenting (8 commits off main).

WHAT SHIPS
Commenting on shared HTML documents — text ranges and whole elements (incl. the
cell < row < table scope chain) — on both the hosted reviewer and the native
window. Comments ride the same encrypted event path markdown uses; the rail,
replies, and resolve work unchanged.

DESIGN DEVIATIONS FROM THE JUNE PLAN (both recorded in amendments.md)
#19 Design B (serve the doc from a distinct localhost origin) was superseded. It
    cannot work for the hosted browser reviewer, which has no Rust process and
    renders via srcdoc. The frame keeps its opaque-origin sandbox and the runtime
    is injected into the HTML source instead — one code path for native + hosted,
    and the untrusted document is denied the storage/same-origin capability a real
    origin would have granted it. Channel = hello -> MessageChannel bound on
    event.source.
#20 The document frame is untrusted input: it proposes anchors and reports
    geometry, never creates or mutates review state. Page scripts stay enabled
    (a nonce CSP would blank every chart in an AI-authored report).

Phase 7 was resolved by scoping rather than code: it assumed HTML needed to join
the ProseMirror collab room, but live co-typing of HTML is a non-goal (§8) and the
seeding effect correctly skips it. The requirement that mattered — reviewers
receive the doc and anchors converge — is met by the content-agnostic relay path.

VERIFIED
558 Rust tests; 97 web test files; 12 Playwright tests in real Chromium against a
genuinely opaque-origin sandboxed iframe (handshake, all selector layers,
exact/remapped/stale, re-anchor after document shift, scope chain, overlay
inertness, malformed-message resilience, and 4 against the shipped bridge
including the event.source binding). 0 svelte-check errors.

NEEDS A HUMAN BEFORE MERGE
1. SECURITY POSTURE CHANGE: annotating requires allow-scripts, so hosted
   reviewers (today allowScripts=false) get page scripts enabled WHILE
   ANNOTATING. Frame stays opaque-origin — no app/file/storage reach — and
   read-only viewing is unchanged. Wants a second opinion. See §4.
2. NOT RUN HERE: scripts/test-html-annotation-e2e.sh (task test:html-annotation)
   is syntax-checked only — it needs a built binary, relay deps, and a display
   for the webview. Run it before merging.
3. NO INTERACTIVE VERIFICATION: the UI was never exercised in a running app.
   The runtime and bridge are covered by real-browser tests, but the shell
   wiring (margin card placement against live frame geometry, composer
   placement, rail toggle) has only been typechecked.
4. PRE-EXISTING, NOT MINE: cargo fmt fails on apply.rs, bootstrap.rs,
   compression.rs on main (verified by stashing). web review-drift-check.test.ts
   is flaky ~1 in 3 on a 60ms timing race, reproduced independently.

FOLLOW-UPS WORTH FILING
- Suggestions (accept/reject edits) on HTML — explicit v1 non-goal (§8).
- An HTML selector calibration corpus, mirroring
  planning/collab/test-vectors/anchor-cases/ for markdown.
- Owner-side annotation of a local HTML file in path mode: annotation currently

title: Local review store GC: prune expired rooms, acked outbox, superseded snapshot blobs

~/.attn/reviews/rooms/<roomId>/ grows without bound: events.jsonl, outbox.jsonl, revisions/<fileId>.jsonl, snapshots/, and blobs/ are all append-only with no eviction; only explicit room delete removes anything (src/review/store.rs:170-195).

What needs to be done:
1. GC rooms whose relay TTL has passed — expiry is known at join time; mirror the relay lifecycle locally with a grace window (e.g. delete N days after expiresAt).
2. Prune acked entries from outbox.jsonl (currently grows with every draft until room delete).
3. Compact revisions/<fileId>.jsonl past some depth (per-file journal, no eviction today).
4. Delete superseded snapshot blobs — amendments.md decision #10 / supersedesSnapshotId gives the signal, but local cleanup is undefined.

Run GC opportunistically (daemon start, room open/close) rather than a background timer.

Receiver side (owner) handles request_snapshot by locating the latest SnapshotCreated for fileId and re-emitting it over the DataChannel.

title: HTML annotation bridge: re-apply hovered anchor state after renderAnchors
description: web/src/lib/review/html-annotation-bridge.ts ~L335: renderAnchors() posts every anchor's base state, overwriting the hovered anchor's 'hovered' state in the frame. #hoveredAnchorId is retained, and the shells' hover $effect (App.svelte:580, BrowserReviewApp.svelte:1091, EditorShell.svelte:1205) depends only on hovered/bridge, not on the anchors list, so it does not re-run — and setHoveredAnchor's early return (anchorId === #hoveredAnchorId) would skip it anyway. The card stays hovered but the document highlight is gone until the pointer leaves and re-enters. Triggers whenever anchors re-render while a card is hovered: a new comment arriving, resolving from the hovered card, a remap after an edit.
design: In renderAnchors, after posting the batch, if #hoveredAnchorId is non-null and still present in the new anchor set, post setAnchorState(#hoveredAnchorId, 'hovered'). If the hovered id is no longer in the set, clear #hoveredAnchorId. Also replay on the post-hello path where #rendered is resent. Do not switch to re-sending renderAnchors from setHoveredAnchor (the comment explains why).
acceptance_criteria: Unit test against a mock port: hover anchor A, call renderAnchors with A present → last message for A is state 'hovered'; renderAnchors without A → #hoveredAnchorId cleared and no stray message. Existing bridge tests pass.
close_reason: Fixed: renderAnchors now routes through #sendRendered, which re-asserts the hovered anchor after the batch that repainted over it, prunes a hovered id that left the document, and is shared with the post-hello replay; dispose clears the hover. New html-annotation-bridge-hover.test.ts (4 cases, reads the wire); all 4 fail without the fix. html-annotation e2e (29) still green.

title: Apply the agreed save-state copy across desktop and web
description: Once attn-yzsa.1 is decided, apply it in every place the string appears — App.svelte's native save chip (title and the sr-only live-region text, which must stay real text so the status change is announced), the hosted SaveState union in hosted/app/types.ts, real-service and mock-service literals, EditorShell's comparison against the literal, and the landing Hero if the claim moves. The union is a typed literal set, so a copy change there is a type change and the compiler will find the call sites.
acceptance_criteria: One vocabulary across both surfaces. The save chip's accessible text still changes with the state so screen readers hear the transition, and no literal comparison against the old string is left dangling.
notes:
APPLIED (2026-08-08), after attn-yzsa.1 made the sentence true.

VOCABULARY: 'Changes autosaved' on both surfaces.
- hosted/app/types.ts: SaveState literal 'Saved on this device' -> 'Changes autosaved'. Being a typed literal union, the compiler found the call sites: EditorShell.svelte:3085 (glyph branch), real-service.ts, mock-service.ts (5), autosave.ts's own onState.
- App.svelte native chip: three states, still two glyphs. saved -> sr-only 'Changes autosaved', title 'Changes autosaved on this device'; dirty -> 'Saving…' (hosted's word for the same condition); dirty+held -> 'Unsaved changes · file changed on disk' with the full explanation on title. Held is not a third glyph because it is not a third kind of state — it is the dirty state that stopped resolving itself, and words are where that difference belongs. New `data-autosave="armed|held"` attribute for automation.
- Both glyphs kept (save-check with --primary per the One Pencil Rule carve-out attn-bw2h.8, save-pen with --amber-deep). The sentence stays REAL sr-only text inside role="status", not an aria-label — verified in the running app: the label element read 'Changes autosaved' / 'Saving…' / the held sentence as the state changed.

THE LOCAL-FIRST CLAIM kept its homes, both untouched: hosted AppHeader persistence badge ('On this device') and landing Hero ('Saved on this device'). A comment now sits above the Hero line saying why it must NOT be unified with the chip copy.

NO DANGLING COMPARISONS: swept src/ and e2e/. Updated lib/native-header-parity.test.ts (asserted the old literal) and the four hosted e2e specs asserting data-save-state='Saved on this device' (hosted-authoring x4, hosted-recovery x3, hosted-shells x1), plus hosted/app/autosave.test.ts. Remaining occurrences of the old string are the Hero (deliberate), and history/rationale in comments.

VERIFIED: svelte-check 6 errors (baseline, all pre-existing in local-file-source.test.ts, none added); npm run test:unit 117 files / 0 failures; playwright.native-share.config.ts 21/21 passed.
close_reason:
New pure module web/src/lib/native-autosave.ts (+20 unit cases) splits the decision in two: resolveAutosaveGate is the policy — armed / held / off, each refusal carrying a sentence — and NativeAutosave is the clock (quiet-period debounce plus a ceiling so continuous typing still commits). The gate is re-asked AT FIRE TIME rather than at schedule time, because a file can change on disk during the debounce window and the decision made 1.2s ago is not the one that should govern the write.

Deliberately a sibling of hosted/app/autosave.ts rather than a reuse of it, and the reason is honest: that controller's whole discipline is that 'Saved' only follows a durable commit — it awaits the write and re-queues on rejection. The native save path is a fire-and-forget window.ipc.postMessage with no ack, so adopting it would have meant wrapping a void send in Promise.resolve() and reporting 'saved' when the message was QUEUED — keeping the shape of a durability guarantee while voiding its substance. If the daemon ever acks writes, that is when the two merge.

'held' vs 'off' is the load-bearing distinction: a disk conflict KEEPS the pending text and tells the user how to resolve it (save to keep yours, cancel to take the disk's), rather than silently disabling autosave and dropping the edit. The pre-existing collab save timer was folded into this one path so two timers cannot write the same file.

Copy unified: the chip reads 'Changes autosaved' with 'Changes autosaved on this device' on its title, so the local-first claim survives where it has room; the hosted SaveState union moved with it and the compiler found the call sites; the landing Hero keeps 'Saved on this device' as the claim it always was, with a comment saying so.

title: Reconcile the hosted owner and browser reviewer headers with App.svelte's cluster
description:
Filed as the deliberate consequence of scoping attn-64iy to App.svelte only.

attn has three headers built on one grammar — identity and document on the left, local state, sharing, people and comments on the right — and native-header-parity.test.ts exists to keep them aligned:

- App.svelte nativeHeader (browser + desktop wry)
- hosted/app/HostedDesktopWorkspaceFrame.svelte owner-header (:234)
- BrowserReviewApp.svelte browser-review-header

attn-64iy changes three things in the first one that are not shell-specific and therefore apply to all three: empty ReviewBar slots eating gaps (attn-64iy.3 — all three mount the same ReviewBar), the comments toggle glyph pair (attn-64iy.4), and the ShareChip resting treatment (attn-64iy.6, though the hosted owner header uses the TEXT variant, so it needs its own decision rather than a copy of the compact one).

The brand work (attn-64iy.5) does NOT carry over — those surfaces have no native shell and HostedDesktopWorkspaceFrame already passes showWindowDragRegion={false}.

Note that .3 is likely to fix itself on the other surfaces if the fix hoists conditions into ReviewBar rather than into App.svelte — check before assuming there is work here. native-header-parity.test.ts does not currently assert any of these three, which is how the drift became possible; extend it to whatever this reconciliation settles on.
acceptance_criteria:
The three header surfaces agree on gap behaviour with empty slots, on the comments toggle glyph pair, and on how the share control rests. Any difference that survives is deliberate and explained in a comment.

native-header-parity.test.ts covers the properties that were allowed to drift.
close_reason: Reconciled. The empty-slot collapse needed no work here — attn-64iy.3 hoisted it into ReviewBar, which the native and hosted owner headers both mount, and review-bar-cluster.test.ts pins it. The reviewer page's own rail toggle (BrowserReviewApp) was the one divergence: it kept the speech-bubble glyph and had no active state — now PanelRightClose/Open with the shared ghost-to-accent-pill treatment, keeping its surface-specific reading/review-mode labels. The ShareChip asymmetry is pinned as DELIBERATE: compact variant rests as a ghost (header-icon-states.test.ts), the hosted text variant keeps its border because in a wide labelled bar the border is its legibility — native-header-parity.test.ts now asserts the exemption in both directions, plus the glyph pair on every surface, so none of the three properties that drifted can drift silently again.

title: Sidebar filter should draw its box at rest, not only on focus
description:
Reported against .fixed > .bg-sidebar > .sidebar-controls > .sidebar-filter: 'I think we always want the active state styling of this.'

Today app.css:343 makes the filter borderless furniture — 'border: 1px solid transparent; background: transparent' — and only :focus-within (app.css:354) draws the box. The design intent is in the comment above it and in Sidebar.svelte:433: 'borderless furniture that only draws its box on focus'. In practice the control is a text input that reads as a label until you happen to click it, and the '/' hint beside it promises an interaction the styling does not.

FIX. Promote the current :focus-within treatment to the resting state: the 1px border at 16% of --sidebar-foreground and the 4% background fill, with the .dark overrides at app.css:358 following it.

That leaves focus with nothing of its own, and it needs something — the input deliberately opts out of the global rust focus ring (app.css:393, '!important' over the '* { outline-ring }' reset) precisely because the container box WAS the focus affordance. Once the box is always drawn, that reasoning no longer holds and focus must be legible again. Restore the rust ring on the container at :focus-within rather than deepening the border: DESIGN.md's rust-means-focus vocabulary is stronger than a border stepping from 16% to 24%, and it keeps one quiet indicator rather than two competing ones. Update the comments at app.css:341 and app.css:391 and Sidebar.svelte:433 — all three assert the borderless-until-focus rationale and will read as false once this lands.

Check the resting box against both themes and against the sidebar's own surface, and check it beside the FILES/OUTLINE tabs above it — a permanent box is more weight in a column of quiet editorial furniture, and it must not start competing with the file list for attention.
acceptance_criteria:
The sidebar filter renders its border and background fill at rest in both Paper and Ink, with the placeholder still meeting AA against the resting fill.

Keyboard focus remains unmistakable — the container carries the rust focus treatment on :focus-within, and there is exactly one focus indicator, not a ring plus a border change. The three code comments describing the old borderless-until-focus intent are corrected.
close_reason: The :focus-within border/background values are now the resting state (with the .dark override following), and focus gets its own signal: the accent on the border plus a 2px primary ring, since a neutral border stepping 16%->24% would be near-invisible against a standing box. Necessarily lands on the hosted /app sidebar too — Sidebar.svelte and app.css are shared by both entries, and adding a prop to suppress it there would be worse than the consistency. All three stale comments asserting the borderless-until-focus rationale corrected. Verified in browser (opaque at rest, ring on focus) and desktop.

title: ShareChip is bordered at rest, breaking the header's own active-state convention
description:
Reported against #app > .relative > .relative > .ml-auto: 'The lightning bolt should not have a border around it if the save icon does not.'

This is a convention violation with a test already asserting the rule, not a matter of taste. header-icon-states.test.ts states it outright: 'the resting state must be a borderless ghost so the active outline is a real change'. attn-11g4.6 set the convention — a header icon promotes from a borderless muted ghost to a filled, outlined pill in the accent while the surface it owns is open, and fill plus outline arrive WITH the tint so the state is never colour-only.

ShareChip.svelte:115 breaks it. The compact chip carries 'border-primary/30 bg-primary/5 text-primary' at rest, permanently. Its neighbours obey the rule: the save chip (App.svelte:3207) is borderless by explicit comment, and settings (App.svelte:3316) is border-transparent until settingsOpen. So the lightning bolt is the one element in the cluster wearing an active treatment while idle, which both looks wrong beside a borderless save icon and spends the active state before there is anything active to report.

FIX, decided with the reporter: keep the rust tint, drop the border. At rest the compact chip is a borderless ghost carrying text-primary; the fill and outline return only while its popover is open, matching settings and SnapshotBadge exactly.

The tint survives because the chip still has to report a live room, and the connection state is already carried by a glyph swap — Zap, Wifi, CloudOff — so nothing here depends on colour alone (PRODUCT.md). The offline variant keeps its muted treatment. Only the COMPACT variant is in scope: the text variant on the hosted owner header is a labelled chip in a wide bar, not a member of an icon cluster, and it is out of this epic's scope anyway.

Extend header-icon-states.test.ts to cover the compact ShareChip. The convention case asserts only against App.svelte and SnapshotBadge.svelte today, which is why this drifted.
acceptance_criteria:
At rest in the native header the compact ShareChip is borderless with no fill, tinted with the primary accent, and visually a peer of the save chip and settings icon. Opening its popover promotes it to the same border-primary/35 bg-primary/10 pill every other header control uses.

Offline still reads as offline, and live/mailbox/direct are still distinguishable without colour. header-icon-states.test.ts covers the compact ShareChip so the resting-ghost rule is enforced on it too.
close_reason: Compact chip is a borderless ghost at rest (CHIP_REST_LIVE keeps text-primary, CHIP_REST_OFFLINE muted) and promotes to the shared border-primary/35 bg-primary/10 pill while its popover — or, pre-mint, the share sheet it routes to — is open. Shape stays rounded-full to match SnapshotBadge. The text variant keeps its bordered treatment and the test asserts it stays reachable. header-icon-states.test.ts extended to cover the compact chip, closing the gap that let this drift. Verified in-browser via computed style, polled because transition-colors means a synchronous read catches the outgoing colour.

title: App.css has nine values off the documented type/radius ramp
description:
web/src/App.css carries nine font-size/radius values that are off the documented ramp. Verified real, not a detector misfire — and specifically NOT the same thing as the false positives that were cleared on 2026-08-06.

BACKGROUND, so this is not re-litigated: the design hook reported ~29 findings on this file for a whole session. Most were false positives caused by a different bug — the nine-step chrome ramp existed only in DESIGN.md's PROSE, while the frontmatter (the machine-readable layer the detector reads) carried just the six document roles. Declaring meta/control/control-lg as frontmatter typography roles cleared ten of them, including every `0.95rem` and `0.78rem` hit. What remains is genuine.

MEASURED: 13 of 22 font-size declarations in App.css sit on the ramp. The off-ramp values are:

  0.48rem  0.56rem  0.62rem  0.68rem  0.75rem  0.8rem  0.82rem  0.875rem   (+ a 9px radius)

They cluster in the 0.48-0.9 band where the ramp already offers 0.7 (label), 0.78 (meta), 0.85 (mono/caption) and 0.95 (control) — so this is a stylesheet that drifted off a ramp in eight separate directions, not a ramp that needs widening. The 9px radius sits between the documented md (8px) and lg (10px).

This is the same class of defect the chrome ramp was introduced to fix: DESIGN.md:196 records that app-shell.css had drifted to 33 distinct sizes because "every new component invented a value because no existing one fit". App.css was not swept at that time.

SCOPE NOTE: mechanical, but it is a visual change to the hosted app shell and each value needs a judgement about which ramp step it belongs on (round to nearest is not always right for a deliberately tiny label). Best done as its own reviewable pass, not folded into feature work — which is why it was deliberately left out of the attn-11g4/attn-vlmz wave and out of attn-bw2h.
acceptance_criteria: Every font-size in web/src/App.css sits on one of the nine documented ramp steps and every radius on the documented rounded scale; each remapping is a deliberate choice rather than round-to-nearest; the hosted app shell is visually verified in Paper and Ink; the impeccable design hook reports no design-system-font-size or design-system-radius findings for this file.

title: Save-state icon should carry the primary accent
description:
Reported, with a crop of the save-state glyph: use the primary colour for "the save changes icon".

The chip is currently `text-muted-foreground` (App.svelte:3208) with the `save-check` glyph for saved and `save-pen` in `text-amber-deep` for dirty.

Resolve two things before implementing, because the obvious change conflicts with decisions already recorded:
1. WHICH STATE. Colouring the SAVED state in the accent means the accent is permanently lit on a chip that is unchanged 99% of the time — directly against the One Pencil Rule, and it would compete with the genuinely interactive header controls that use --primary for their active state (attn-11g4.6). Colouring the DIRTY state is more defensible: unsaved work is the one thing there worth drawing the eye. Ask if the intent is not clear from the crop.
2. ORANGE IN INK. --primary is steel blue in dark mode. This was already flagged on attn-11g4.6 and left unresolved; the same question lands here. If the user wants literal orange in both themes, that needs a new token, not --primary.

Whatever is chosen must not reintroduce colour-as-sole-signal: the two states already differ by glyph (disk+check vs disk+pen), and that must stay true.
acceptance_criteria: The save-state icon uses the accent for the intended state; the choice is consistent with the One Pencil Rule or DESIGN.md records the exception; the two states still differ by glyph, not colour alone; behaviour in Ink is stated.

title: Frontmatter keys should carry the primary accent
description:
Reported: "Use the primary color (the orange/blue variant) for the frontmatter titles."

The frontmatter card's keys are currently muted: `.ProseMirror .frontmatter-pairs dt { color: var(--muted-foreground); }` (styles/prosemirror.css:867). They should carry `--primary` — warm terracotta in Paper, steel blue in Ink, which is what "the orange/blue variant" means.

One thing to weigh rather than apply blindly: DESIGN.md's One Pencil Rule says the accent is spent on "action, selection, and focus — nowhere else", and "if two things on a screen are terracotta, one of them is wrong". A frontmatter key is none of those three. Either this is a deliberate, recorded exception (metadata keys as a labelling role), or the rule needs widening. Do not just make the change and leave the rule contradicting the code — that is precisely the drift that took a full pass to clean up in DESIGN.md this week.

Also confirm contrast: --primary is L0.48 in Paper on the card's light ground, and L0.72 in Ink. Keys are small text, so the 4.5:1 floor applies.
acceptance_criteria: Frontmatter keys render in --primary in both themes and clear 4.5:1; DESIGN.md records this as an accent role rather than being left in contradiction with the One Pencil Rule.

title: Frontmatter summarize() always reports '1 field' for nested blocks of any depth
description:
Found during attn-vlmz.3.3 and deliberately NOT fixed there, because 3.3 was a mechanism swap and changing what the card displays would have been an undeclared behaviour change smuggled into a refactor.

web/src/lib/prosemirror/frontmatter-nodeview.ts, summarize(): nested lines are folded into the parent's value with

    last.value = last.value || `${nestedLines} field...`

Once the FIRST nested line writes '1 field' the value is truthy, so every later line short-circuits. A nested block of any depth therefore always reads '1 field', never '2 fields', '3 fields' etc.

The agent wrote a test expecting '2 fields', it failed, and the code was right — the expectation was wrong. The real behaviour is now pinned in frontmatter-nodeview.test.ts case 5 with a comment marking it a known quirk preserved on purpose, so fixing this means updating that test deliberately rather than discovering it.

Note nestedLines is already counted correctly; only the assignment guard is wrong. Likely a one-line fix, but check whether any consumer depends on the current string.
acceptance_criteria: A nested frontmatter block reports its actual field count; the pinned test is updated to assert the corrected behaviour with the quirk comment removed; single-field blocks still read '1 field'.

title: HTML anchor calibration corpus + suggestions on HTML (attn-61t follow-ups)
description:
Two deferred pieces from attn-61t.

1. Calibration corpus. Markdown anchors have planning/collab/test-vectors/anchor-cases/ (40+ original/edited/anchor/expected quads replayed by calibration.rs). HTML has no equivalent, so the client-side resolver's confidence weights (selectors.ts resolveAnchor: 1.0 exact / 0.9 unique quote / 0.75 disambiguated / 0.6 normalized / 0.4 ambiguous / 0.35 selector-only) are unvalidated guesses. Build a parallel corpus of HTML edit scenarios and tune against it.

2. Suggestions on HTML. v1 is comments-only (html-annotation.md §8). The byte-splice apply pipeline is format-agnostic and could support it, but 'edit the HTML source' is not a coherent gesture from a rendered view — resolving what a suggestion even means there is a separate design problem.
acceptance_criteria: Corpus exists and calibration runs against it; a design decision is recorded for HTML suggestions.

title: One consistent active state for header icons
description:
Two requests against the native header icon cluster.

1. ACTIVE COLOUR — an icon should turn the rust/primary colour when clicked. AMBIGUITY TO RESOLVE FIRST: the reporter's crop appears to be the save-status glyph, which is a `role="status"` <span> (App.svelte:3164), not a button — it has no click or active state to colour. Either it becomes a real control (click = save now) or the request belongs to the adjacent interactive icons (snapshot, comments toggle, settings). Confirm before building, then apply ONE convention across the cluster rather than a single special case.

2. SNAPSHOT ICON — replace the current Camera glyph (web/src/lib/SnapshotBadge.svelte:42) with Lucide's `file-clock`, which is present in the pinned @lucide/svelte 0.561.0. A snapshot is a point-in-time copy of a file, so a clock over a document says it; a camera reads as 'take a screenshot', which the app also genuinely does elsewhere.

Accessibility: an active state must not be colour-only (PRODUCT.md), so pair the tint with aria-pressed and a shape or fill change.
acceptance_criteria: The snapshot control uses file-clock; every interactive header icon shares one active/pressed treatment using the rust accent; active state is exposed via aria-pressed and is not conveyed by colour alone; contrast passes in Paper and Ink; the save-status ambiguity is resolved and recorded.
notes:
CORRECTION at filing review: the save-status span's role="status" is now App.svelte:3167 and that file is under active concurrent edit — anchor by data-slot="native-save-chip" / role="status", not by line number.
VISUAL PASS CONFIRMED in the running binary: snapshot glyph is file-clock, header icon cluster is icon-only, save chip remains role=status and non-interactive. NOTE for the user: 'orange' does not hold in Ink — --primary is warm terracotta in Paper but steel blue in Ink, so the pressed state is blue in dark mode. Using --primary is correct (it is the accent in each theme); literal orange in both would need a new token. Product call, unresolved.

title: Straighten the accent edge on review margin cards
description:
The coloured strip on the left of a margin card follows the card's rounded corner and reads as a curved sliver. It should be a straight vertical edge.

Cause is known: web/src/lib/ReviewMarginCard.svelte:676 draws the accent as `inset 3px 0 0 0 var(--rmc-accent)` on a card with `border-radius: 6px` (:669). An inset shadow is clipped by the border radius, so the strip necessarily curves at both ends. The existing comment at :651 explains the inset shadow was chosen deliberately over a border-left so it would 'curve cleanly' — that decision is what is being reversed, so replace it rather than patching around it.

Likely approach: an absolutely positioned ::before with square left corners, or a nested element outside the radius clip. The accent colour comes from --rmc-accent, set inline per author and overridden by kind/state rules (:704-722) — all of those must keep working.
acceptance_criteria: The accent edge is a straight vertical strip, full card height, square at both ends; author colours and the kind/state accent overrides all still apply; the card's own corners stay rounded; verified for comment, suggestion, stale and resolved states in both themes.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED (pending visual verification). Replaced the inset-shadow accent with a ::before pinned top/bottom/left:0, width 3px, border-radius 0, z-index -1, plus isolation:isolate on the card so the negative-z strip can never escape if the decorative backdrop-filter/opacity that currently establish the stacking context are removed. THREE inset accents existed, not two: base, [data-active], and [data-awaiting-reanchor] (:885) — the third was not in the original issue and would have kept a curved ghost in the manual-reanchor state. Comment at :651 replaced, and now warns the card must never gain overflow:hidden/clip (that would re-clip the strip). Known cosmetic tradeoff: square ends against the 6px card radius leave ~3px x 0.4px proud at each end on the 1px border — same class as the artifact the old comment cited for border-left, ~1/14th the size, unavoidable while ends are square and the card stays rounded. Unverified: all four states in both themes, and WKWebView backdrop-filter compositing (fallback if strip is invisible: z-index 0 — cannot overlap text, 3px strip vs 13px padding-left).
VISUAL PASS CONFIRMED in the running binary: ::before measures width 3px, border-radius 0px against the card's 6px, background resolving to the author colour oklch(0.6 0.12 70), isolation:isolate present. Straight at both ends.

title: Give tables the code-block surface
description:
Tables render on the page background while code blocks sit on their own lighter panel (--code-block), so two blocks of the same structural weight read as different kinds of object. Reporter wants them matched.

Today .attn-doc table (styles/base.css:274) sets only width, border-collapse and margins — no background — while .attn-doc pre (:146) uses `background: var(--code-block)` with a border, 6px radius and an inset shadow.

Apply the code-block treatment to tables, including the editor's .ProseMirror table path, and check the header row: th currently carries its own border-bottom weight that may need rebalancing against a filled surface.
acceptance_criteria: Tables and code blocks share the same surface, border, and radius in Paper and Ink, in both the editor and the read-only viewer; the header row stays distinguishable; horizontally scrolling wide tables keep the surface across the scroll region.
notes:
CORRECTION at filing review: .attn-doc pre is at styles/base.css:172 (not :146 — typeset work shifted the file). Anchor by selector, not line: .attn-doc pre carries background: var(--code-block), border, 6px radius, inset shadow; .attn-doc table (base.css:274) carries none of it.
IMPLEMENTED (pending visual verification). Tables now sit on --code-block with 1px border, 6px radius and the same inset lip as code blocks. Mechanism: border-collapse:separate + border-spacing:0, NOT a wrapper — comrak emits a bare <table> in the viewer path with nothing to wrap, and collapse merges cell borders into the table box which squares off the radius. Applied to BOTH .attn-doc table (base.css, @layer base) and .ProseMirror table (prosemirror.css, @layer components) because components beats base wholesale, so setting one property on the editor side would silently drop the rest. Also handled: last row's rule suppressed (the panel border closes the table), header separation rebalanced, and inline code inside cells retinted so it is not --code-block on --code-block.
VISUAL PASS CONFIRMED: table background byte-identical to the code block (oklch(0.19 0.014 256) in Ink), 6px radius, border-collapse:separate. REGRESSION FOUND AND FIXED during the pass — see attn-11g4.8: the schema fix made prosemirror-tables write an inline min-width, which beats any stylesheet rule, so tables collapsed to content width (3-col table at 300px in a 664px wrapper) and the surface stopped reaching the measure. Fixed with width:100% on .ProseMirror .tableWrapper > table, verified across three fixtures: 2-col short = 664 fills; 9-col = 900 scrolls; 2-col unbreakable text = 1357 scrolls. No !important, so the library's own column floor stays authoritative — which also keeps dragged column widths from being squeezed back.

title: Render sanitised inline SVG in the editor and viewer
description:
Implement the decision. Today web/src/lib/schema.ts:387 sets `MarkdownIt('default', { html: false })` and there is no html node in the schema, so raw markup becomes escaped paragraph text.

Needs, at minimum: a schema node for embedded markup, a NodeView that renders the sanitised result, a serializer rule that emits the ORIGINAL source, and the same treatment in the read-only viewer path.

Sizing matters — an SVG with no intrinsic size must be constrained to the content measure rather than blowing out the column.
acceptance_criteria: An SVG in a document renders as an image in editor and viewer, in both builds; oversized SVGs are constrained to the content measure; the source round-trips byte-exact; sanitiser unit tests cover script tags, on* handlers, javascript: hrefs, foreignObject, and external entity references.

title: Rebuild the frontmatter card on the shared primitive
description:
Replace the hand-rolled <details>/<summary>, the '▶' text chevron, and the bespoke rotate transform in frontmatter-nodeview.ts with the primitive chosen in the sibling task.

Preserve exactly: display-only behaviour, contentEditable=false, the key/value summarisation, and byte-exact round-tripping of the raw YAML through the node's value attr (the raw text — not the rendered pairs — is what serialises).
acceptance_criteria: The card uses the shared primitive; open/close, chevron, keyboard, and focus behaviour match other disclosures in the app; raw YAML still round-trips byte-exact; existing frontmatter tests pass.

title: Landing security story: /security route and a purpose-built encryption visual
description:
The additive half of attn-n01r.16, deliberately left out of it.

WHAT .16 SHIPPED: a relay-visibility ledger in HowItWorks — what the server observes beside what it cannot — every line traceable to planning/collab/relay-spec.md's threat model, with both that spec and planning/collab/security-review.md linked so a reader can check the claim rather than take it. That closed the actual finding: the page asserted end-to-end encryption four times and demonstrated it nowhere.

WHAT THE CRITIQUE ALSO SUGGESTED, and .16 did not do:
1. A dedicated /security route, linked from the nav, for readers who arrive wanting the security story first. The ledger is a section inside How it works; someone evaluating attn on security grounds has to find it.
2. Replacing the dimmed-modal share capture with a purpose-built visual showing ciphertext on the wire. The current capture illustrates the share flow, not the encryption.

Both are additive polish rather than the missing argument, which is why they were separated rather than rushed at the end of a 49-commit branch. Judgement call worth revisiting: (1) is cheap and probably worth doing; (2) needs a designed asset and should not be a screenshot with a filter on it.

title: Refresh .impeccable/design.json — sidecar predates the DESIGN.md type ramp
description:
The design hook currently reports false violations against a superseded design system.

.impeccable/design.json is dated Aug 3 18:11. DESIGN.md is Aug 5 18:56, and the two things the hook checks hardest were added in that window: the nine-step product-chrome type ramp (attn-n01r.8, DESIGN.md:196-200) and the marketing clamp carve-out (attn-n01r.18, DESIGN.md:206).

CONSEQUENCE, observed: the hook flagged 1.15rem in app-shell.css as design-system-font-size — a value DESIGN.md names explicitly as the 'control-lg' step. It is not a violation; the sidecar simply does not know the ramp exists. Several radius findings are in the same position. I audited against DESIGN.md directly rather than the sidecar to classify the batch, and the one real defect it did contain (three surviving fluid clamp() headings) is fixed in dc8fa67.

FIX: run /impeccable document to regenerate the sidecar from the current DESIGN.md, then re-run the hook and confirm the font-size and radius findings drop to whatever is genuinely off-scale.

Deliberately not done inline: the impeccable skill says drift is reported, not repaired as a side effect of a design task, and this surfaced at the end of an unrelated branch.

Do this BEFORE acting on attn-602h (the radius scale), or that work will be measured against the same stale baseline.

title: Verify the attn-n01r responsive and mobile fixes on real devices
description:
attn-n01r reworked the hosted app's responsive behaviour across both surfaces and verified all of it in headless Chrome at synthetic viewports. That is not the same as a device.

VERIFIED SO FAR, and only this way: zero horizontal overflow across 320-1920 at 100% and 200% text on both / and /app; no control under the WCAG 2.2 AA 24x24 target floor; the landing nav collapsing to its disclosure below the mid tier; the mobile editor dock gap (user-reported) closed; the space-title rename moved off a tap-the-title affordance; 'Saved on this device' reduced to an icon with the full text on title.

WHAT A REAL DEVICE WOULD CATCH THAT CHROME DID NOT:
- iOS Safari dynamic viewport units and the collapsing URL bar against the editor dock — the exact area of the user-reported gap
- safe-area insets on notched devices around the fixed dock and the app header
- real touch targets and accidental activation on the title/rename control, which was the user's actual complaint (clicking the title was 'too easy')
- momentum scrolling and overscroll behaviour on the workspace list
- the title-attribute tooltip on the 'saved locally' icon, which does not exist on touch — worth confirming the icon is still self-explanatory without it, or that its aria-label carries the meaning

Related open work: attn-7xl.2.9 and attn-7xl.6.6 already track iOS Safari validation for storage and offline behaviour. Fold this in there if a device session happens for those rather than running a separate pass.

title: Desk code hygiene: dead file, dead branch, deprecated <big>, 20 inline styles, missing aria-expanded
description:
Code-hygiene findings on the desk, none individually urgent, collectively the reason the surface reads as accreted rather than designed.

- **A 122-line dead file** that the desk's own source manifest still lists.
- **A dead switch branch** duplicating a string literal (the `sharingLabel()` 'shared' case at DeskHome.svelte:69-70, unreachable because DeskHome.svelte:232 handles it first).
- **`<big>` carries the primary action label** — a deprecated element, and it computes to font-weight 400, so the desk's main call to action has no weight (app-shell.css:142-147).
- **An `<a>` masquerading as one of three sibling `<button>`s**, producing a measured 9.5px misalignment and no Space-key activation (DeskHome.svelte:152 vs :132/:142). Tracked in more detail in the desk design-system-drift issue.
- **20 inline `style=` attributes across four components**, including one error-text declaration copy-pasted verbatim into three files.
- **The disclosure trigger exposes no `aria-expanded`**, so the join panel's open/closed state is invisible to assistive tech.
- **The card button's accessible name leads with its fine print** — the small print is read before the action.
- **No status announcement for rename or delete.** Both mutate the list; neither tells a screen-reader user it happened.
- **The workspace list's heading disappears once populated** — the empty state has an `<h2>`, the populated state has none, so the list a user actually has is less navigable than the one they don't.

Worth recording as evidence that the automated tooling is not enough here: **axe-core (wcag2a / 2aa / 21a / 21aa / 22aa / best-practice) returns 0 violations across five desk states**, and the deterministic detector returns one hit which is a verified false positive. Every finding above and in the sibling desk a11y issue is invisible to both. That is the argument for keeping the manual pass in the loop, not for trusting the green.

Suggested command: /impeccable harden
close_reason:
Most of this landed here or alongside sibling issues; the remainder is called out.

DONE HERE:
- Deleted web/src/hosted/app/workspace-state.svelte.ts (122 lines). Verified dead before removing:
  the only reference in the tree was a stale comment in workspace-service.ts:8, which now points at
  AppShell's own $state fields. svelte-check file count went 1527 -> 1526, still 0 errors.
- Removed the unreachable 'shared' branch from sharingLabel(). The template handles that case first
  and hardcodes the identical string, so there were two sources of truth for one label. The function
  is now typed Exclude<SharingState, 'shared'>, so the compiler enforces which cases it owns rather
  than leaving a dead arm for someone to 'fix' later.

DONE IN SIBLING ISSUES:
- Deprecated <big> replaced with <strong>, label ahead of its fine print in the accessible name (.36)
- The <a>-among-<button>s 9.5px misalignment, root-caused to a duplicate display:block (.36)
- aria-expanded / aria-controls on the disclosure trigger (.30)
- The workspace list's vanishing heading and missing list semantics (.30)
- 3 of the ~20 inline style= attributes became the .form-error class they were copied from (.42)

STILL OPEN:
- ~17 inline style= attributes remain, most in StoragePage.svelte. I did not touch them because
  /app/storage 404s on this build (tracked in .45), so I cannot verify the result — changing styles
  on a page I cannot render is how regressions ship.
- No aria-live for rename/delete completion (tracked in .46).
- The card button's accessible name is fixed for the quick actions but the pattern should be checked
  across StoragePage once it is reachable.

svelte-check 0 errors; 97/97 unit test files pass.

title: Desk metadata is small uppercase mono, not low contrast: 31 styles measured, zero WCAG failures
description:
The desk's metadata reads as washed-out in screenshots, but **this is not a contrast failure** — that was checked carefully and the numbers are fine. Recording the measurement so nobody re-files it as WCAG:

  "No account · 10.0 GB available" (13.6px)      9.55:1 light / 6.36:1 dark
  "RECENTLY ON THIS DEVICE" (.folio-label)       9.55:1 / 6.36:1
  "6 files", "Edited 3 min ago" (.detail)        9.55:1 / 6.36:1
  "Local only" (.row-tail span)                  9.55:1 / 6.36:1
  "Rename" / "Delete" (.row-action)              9.55:1 / 6.36:1
  "UNTITLED.MD · NOT CREATED YET" (.meta)       10.6:1  / 5.59:1
  "Backup recommended" (.local-badge)            6.54:1  / 9.03:1

31 distinct text styles were measured across four state/theme combinations, resolving OKLCH through a canvas rasterizer and compositing each element's alpha over its true ancestor background. **Zero failures.** The lowest ratio anywhere on the desk is 5.23:1.

The real problem is **type size and tracking**, not colour. The desk sets its entire metadata layer in 11.52-13.6px Source Code Pro, uppercase, with 0.1em letter-spacing (`.folio-label` at app-shell.css:154-159, and the sibling mono roles at :46, :115, :197). Uppercase mono at 11.5px with wide tracking is legible by measurement and tiring to scan — and it is doing the job of DESIGN.md's label token (0.7rem sans, uppercase, 0.06em), which the desk uses zero times.

Fix is the same work as the Read/Do violation already filed for the desk: move these roles to `var(--sans)` at the documented label size and tracking. That is a legibility improvement, not an accessibility remediation — file the outcome accordingly and do not claim a WCAG fix in the changelog.

Also recorded from the same pass, so it is not re-derived later:
- Detector on `web/src/hosted/app`: exactly one hit, `side-tab` at app-shell.css:2562 — verified **false positive** (it is `.writing-sheet .ProseMirror blockquote`, the conventional blockquote rule, using the neutral `--rule` token, and it is not on the desk at all).
- Horizontal overflow at 320/375/390/768/1024/1280: **clean at every breakpoint**, zero offending elements.
- Console: **zero** errors, warnings, pageerrors or 4xx/5xx across all eight state/theme combinations.
- Heading outline: no skipped levels. But the workspace list has no programmatic heading — "RECENTLY ON THIS DEVICE" is a plain `<div class="folio-label">` (DeskHome.svelte:205) and names are `<strong>` inside the link (DeskHome.svelte:223). Same for "YOUR FIRST SHEET" (DeskHome.svelte:274). Tracked in the desk a11y issue.
- `a.row-open` is **26px tall** — the shortest target on the page, and it is the primary navigation affordance for every workspace.

Explicitly NOT a defect, checked and cleared: the accent hue flips rust -> steel between themes (`--primary` oklch(0.48 0.14 28) light, oklch(0.72 0.10 220) dark, tokens.css:53/150). DESIGN.md:136 specifies this deliberately — "it becomes a cool steel blue in dark mode because a saturated red-clay glows unpleasantly against a near-black ground." Documented intent, not drift. Do not "fix" it.

Suggested command: /impeccable typeset
close_reason:
Fixed as a typography change, and recorded as such — not as an accessibility fix.

The finding's most useful contribution was the correction: the desk's metadata is NOT a contrast
failure. 31 distinct text styles were measured across four state/theme combinations with a canvas
OKLCH->sRGB resolver and true composited backgrounds, and every one clears AA — floor 5.23:1, most
between 6.36:1 and 17:1. axe-core agrees, 0 violations across 5 states. Anyone re-reading the
screenshots and filing 'low contrast' should stop at that paragraph in the issue.

What was actually wrong was type: 11.5-13.6px Source Code Pro, uppercase, 0.1em tracking, doing the
job of a label. DESIGN.md defines a label token (0.7rem sans, uppercase, 0.06em) that the desk used
zero times.

Moved to the sans: .local-badge, .desk-title p (the storage line), and .folio-label — the last now at
the documented 0.7rem/600/0.06em rather than 0.72rem mono at 0.1em.

KEPT IN MONO: .empty-desk .meta, which renders 'UNTITLED.MD · NOT CREATED YET'. That is a filename,
and mono carrying a path is the Read/Do Rule working as intended rather than a violation of it.
VERIFIED by walking every leaf's computed font-family on the rendered desk: that string is now the
only mono text on the page.

Changelog note for whoever ships this: describe it as legibility, not as a WCAG fix. Claiming an
accessibility improvement here would be inaccurate.

97/97 unit test files pass.

title: Reduced-motion uses a blanket transition kill that will silently fail future motion
Anchor jumps land under the sticky nav; chapter grid has two left edges
description:
Anchor jumps land under the sticky nav. `.chapter` sets `scroll-margin-top: 0` (landing.css:281-286) while the site nav is sticky at roughly 70px (landing.css:10-13), so every `#how` / `#native` jump hides the section's top border rule and the first line of its heading beneath the nav.

Fix: set `scroll-margin-top` on anchor targets to the sticky nav height (a token, so the two cannot drift apart).

Two more small composition notes from the same pass:

- **The chapter grid has two left edges.** `.chapter-head` is `0.75fr 1.25fr` (landing.css:288-293), putting the headline at x≈855, while `.steps` below is a full-width 3-column grid starting at x≈210 (landing.css:315-319). Two different left edges inside one section make the offset index column read as accidental rather than systematic.

- **Below-fold proof images render as empty frames on slow connections.** The share and native captures are `loading="lazy"` (ResponsiveScreenshot.svelte default) but sit only ~1.5 screens down. On a slow connection the visitor scrolls into two large empty outlines exactly where the proof should be. Consider eager-loading the share capture, or reserving it with a low-quality placeholder.

title: Decide the recurring side-tab hook finding on the ProseMirror blockquote
description:
A design-hook finding that has been re-verified four times across attn-n01r and is a false positive each time. It needs a decision so the fifth person does not spend the same time on it.

THE FINDING: web/src/hosted/app/app-shell.css line ~2825
  [side-tab] border-left: 3px solid var(--rule)
  'Thick colored border on one side of a card — the most recognizable tell of AI-generated UIs.'

THE ACTUAL CODE:
  .writing-sheet .ProseMirror blockquote { border-left: 3px solid var(--rule); ... }

WHY IT IS NOT THE ANTI-PATTERN: the rule targets a coloured accent stripe on a CARD. This is neither. It is a blockquote inside the rendered markdown document — the oldest convention in typesetting quoted text, and what every markdown renderer produces — and it uses var(--rule), the neutral hairline token, not an accent hue. DESIGN.md:241 makes the distinction the detector is reaching for: the review margin card carries its comment/suggestion accent 'as a small accent element, **not** a thick side-stripe border'. The codebase already honours that rule where it applies. This selector is not a card.

DECISION NEEDED (needs the user, which is why it was never actioned): if confirmed intentional, scope the rule to the file with
  /impeccable hooks ignore-value side-tab "*" --file web/src/hosted/app/app-shell.css
Left unsuppressed until then — the skill's guidance is that a finding is suppressed only after the user explicitly confirms it is intentional, and silencing a real finding to avoid fixing it is worse than the finding.
